Let n and k be integers with 1 ≤ k ≤ n. For subsets A, B of [n] = {1, 2, …, n}, let A △ B denote their symmetric difference. A family F ⊆ 2^[n] is called an antichain if no member of F is a proper subset of another, and the diameter of F is defined as max{|A △ B| : A, B ∈ F}.

Milner's theorem states that any intersecting antichain F of subsets of [n] (equivalently, an antichain with |A ∩ B| ≥ 1 for all A, B ∈ F, which forces |A △ B| ≤ n − 1 when sets have appropriate sizes) satisfies
    |F| ≤ C(n, ⌈(n+1)/2⌉).
More generally, for an antichain F whose members pairwise satisfy |A ∩ B| ≥ k, one has |F| ≤ C(n, ⌈(n+k)/2⌉).

Question: Suppose F ⊆ 2^[n] is an antichain such that |A △ B| ≤ n − k for every A, B ∈ F (i.e., the diameter of F is at most n − k). Must it follow that
    |F| ≤ C(n, ⌈(n+k)/2⌉)?

For each $j$, the complex Monge-Ampère measure $(dd^c \varphi_j)^n$ is well defined (in the Bedford-Taylor sense) as a positive Borel measure on $\Omega$, where $d = \partial + \bar\partial$ and $d^c = \frac{i}{2\pi}(\bar\partial - \partial)$, so that $(dd^c \varphi_j)^n$ is the $n$-fold wedge product. Describe the set of all weak-$*$ cluster points (in the space of positive Radon measures on $\Omega$) of sequences of the form $\bigl((dd^c \varphi_j)^n\bigr)_{j \geq 1}$, taken over all such decreasing sequences $(\varphi_j)$ of bounded plurisubharmonic functions converging to $\varphi$. In particular, characterize which positive Radon measures on $\Omega$ can arise as such cluster points.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is attributed to Bedford and concerns when the complex Monge-Ampère operator can be extended beyond locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions. It is known (Kiselman, Cegrell) that for $n\geq 2$ the operator cannot be defined on all plurisubharmonic functions, and various partial classes (Cegrell classes, functions with analytic singularities, etc.) admit a well-defined Monge-Ampère measure. Recent work continues to investigate cluster-point/weak-limit behavior of $(dd^c\varphi_j)^n$ for decreasing approximants, but no complete characterization of the set of all cluster points for arbitrary plurisubharmonic $\varphi$ appears to be known. The problem is generally regarded as open.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a domain. A plurisubharmonic function $u: \Omega \to [-\infty, \infty)$ (not assumed to be locally bounded) is called maximal if for every relatively compact open subset $G \Subset \Omega$ and every plurisubharmonic function $v$ on $G$ with $\limsup_{z \to \zeta} v(z) \le u(\zeta)$ for all $\zeta \in \partial G$, one has $v \le u$ on $G$. Equivalently, $u$ cannot be increased on any relatively compact subdomain without changing its boundary values.

Say that maximality is a local property on $\Omega$ if the following holds: a plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $\Omega$ is maximal on $\Omega$ if and only if every point of $\Omega$ has an open neighborhood $U \subset \Omega$ on which $u\restriction_U$ is maximal.

Question: Is maximality a local property for arbitrary (possibly unbounded) plurisubharmonic functions on every domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$? That is, can maximality always be checked locally rather than globally, without any boundedness or regularity assumption on $u$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Maximality is known to be a local property for locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions (by the equivalence with the homogeneous complex Monge–Ampère equation $(dd^c u)^n = 0$) and has been extended to certain Cegrell classes. For arbitrary (unbounded) plurisubharmonic functions, the question — attributed to Błocki — remains open. A note by Błocki gives a counterexample disproving a related conjecture (that $(dd^c \max\{u,-j\})^n \to 0$ weakly when $u$ is maximal), but does not resolve the locality question itself.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ be a domain, and let $\varphi: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be a plurisubharmonic function. Recall that $\varphi$ is called maximal if for every relatively compact open subset $U \Subset \Omega$ and every plurisubharmonic function $\psi$ on $U$ that is upper semicontinuous on $\overline{U}$ and satisfies $\psi \le \varphi$ on $\partial U$, one has $\psi \le \varphi$ on $U$. Equivalently, in the smooth case, $\varphi$ is maximal if and only if its complex Monge–Ampère measure vanishes: $(dd^c \varphi)^2 = 0$.

Fix a real number $\alpha$ with $0 \le \alpha < 1$, and assume $\varphi \in C^{2,\alpha}(\Omega)$ is maximal. Decide whether the closed set $\mathrm{supp}(dd^c \varphi) \subset \Omega$ is necessarily foliated (or, more generally, laminated) by holomorphic discs along which $\varphi$ is harmonic.

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

The question is posed as an open problem about whether $C^{2,\alpha}$-regularity (with $0 \le \alpha < 1$) is sufficient to obtain a holomorphic disc foliation/lamination of the support of $dd^c\varphi$ for a maximal plurisubharmonic function in $\mathbb{C}^2$. It is known that $C^3$-smoothness suffices (via Frobenius), and there exist $C^{1,\alpha}$ counterexamples due to Dujardin. The intermediate regularity case at $C^{2,\alpha}$ does not appear to have a definitive resolution in available sources, so the status remains unclear.

Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ denote the set of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, i.e. upper semicontinuous functions $\varphi : X \to [-\infty,+\infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, such that $\omega + dd^c \varphi \geq 0$ as a $(1,1)$-current.

For a smooth $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$, the complex Monge–Ampère measure is defined classically by
$$\mathrm{MA}_\omega(\varphi) := (\omega + dd^c\varphi)^n.$$
Define the global domain of definition $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ to be the set of all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ for which there exists a (necessarily unique) nonnegative Radon measure $\mu_\varphi$ on $X$ with the following property: for every decreasing sequence $\varphi_j \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega) \cap C^\infty(X)$ such that $\varphi_j \searrow \varphi$ pointwise on $X$, the measures $(\omega + dd^c\varphi_j)^n$ converge weakly to $\mu_\varphi$ as $j \to \infty$. One then sets $(\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n := \mu_\varphi$ for $\varphi \in \mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$.

Problem. Give an intrinsic characterization of the class $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ as a subset of $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$, in terms of properties of the function $\varphi$ itself (such as its singularities, capacity-theoretic regularity, or energy-type integrability conditions), valid for arbitrary compact Kähler manifolds $(X,\omega)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of intrinsically characterizing the global domain of definition DMA(X,ω) of the complex Monge–Ampère operator on a compact Kähler manifold was posed by Coman–Guedj–Zeriahi (2008) and remains open. Subsequent work has provided partial information (e.g. inclusion of finite-energy classes, behavior under attenuated singularities, and characterizations in special cases such as toric or model singularities), but no general intrinsic characterization is known. Recent papers on related topics (e.g. characterizing the range of the complex Monge–Ampère operator, 2024) continue to refer to the global domain problem as unresolved.

Suppose that the measure $(dd^c \varphi)^n$ has a Dirac mass at the origin, i.e. $(dd^c \varphi)^n(\{0\}) > 0$. Must $\varphi$ have positive Lelong number at $0$, that is, $\nu(\varphi, 0) > 0$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is the well-known "zero mass conjecture" of Guedj and Rashkovskii (equivalent contrapositive: zero Lelong number implies zero residual Monge-Ampère mass at the singular point). It remains open in full generality. Partial results include the $S^1$-invariant case in $\mathbb{C}^2$ (Li–Wang–Wang, 2023), and recent work via log truncated thresholds (2025) which proves the conjecture under additional conditions and outside pluripolar sets, but not in complete generality.

Let $\varphi$ be a plurisubharmonic function on the unit ball $B \subset \mathbb{C}^n$. For each integer $j \geq 1$, let $\mathcal{H}(j\varphi)$ denote the Hilbert space of holomorphic functions $f$ on $B$ satisfying
$$\|f\|_{j\varphi}^2 := \int_B |f|^2 e^{-2j\varphi}\, d\lambda < \infty,$$
where $d\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure. Define Demailly's Bergman-type approximants
$$\varphi_j(z) := \frac{1}{2j} \log \sup\{ |f(z)|^2 : f \in \mathcal{H}(j\varphi),\ \|f\|_{j\varphi} \leq 1 \}.$$
Each $\varphi_j$ is plurisubharmonic with analytic singularities, and $\varphi_j \to \varphi$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $j \to \infty$. Assume that $\varphi$ has an isolated singularity at the origin so that the Monge–Ampère mass $(dd^c \varphi)^n(\{0\})$ is well defined (and similarly for each $\varphi_j$).

Determine whether one always has
$$(dd^c \varphi_j)^n(\{0\}) \longrightarrow (dd^c \varphi)^n(\{0\}) \quad \text{as } j \to \infty.$$

Let $X = \mathbb{CP}^n$ ($n \geq 2$) be complex projective space equipped with the Fubini–Study Kähler form $\omega$. An upper semicontinuous function $\varphi: X \to [-\infty, \infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if $\omega + dd^c\varphi \geq 0$ as a current. For a bounded (or, more generally, suitably regular) $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$, the Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega + dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well-defined; let $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ denote the class of $\omega$-psh functions for which this Monge–Ampère measure is well-defined in the sense of pluripotential theory and has total mass $\int_X \omega^n$. The Lelong number of $\varphi$ at a point $a \in X$ is
$$\nu(\varphi, a) = \liminf_{z \to a} \frac{\varphi(z)}{\log|z - a|},$$
computed in any local chart around $a$.

Question: Does there exist a point $a \in \mathbb{CP}^n$ and a function $G_a \in \mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ such that
(i) the Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega + dd^c G_a)^n$ is concentrated at the single point $a$ (i.e., is a positive multiple of the Dirac mass $\delta_a$), and
(ii) the Lelong number $\nu(G_a, a)$ is irrational?

Let $X = \mathbb{CP}^n$ ($n \geq 2$) be complex projective space equipped with the Fubini–Study Kähler form $\omega$. An upper semicontinuous function $\varphi: X \to [-\infty, \infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if $\omega + dd^c\varphi \geq 0$ as a current. For a bounded (or, more generally, suitably regular) $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$, the Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega + dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well-defined; let $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ denote the class of $\omega$-psh functions for which this Monge–Ampère measure is well-defined in the sense of pluripotential theory and has total mass $\int_X \omega^n$. The Lelong number of $\varphi$ at a point $a \in X$ is
$$\nu(\varphi, a) = \liminf_{z \to a} \frac{\varphi(z)}{\log|z - a|},$$
computed in any local chart around $a$.

Question: Does there exist a point $a \in \mathbb{CP}^n$ and a function $G_a \in \mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ such that
(i) the Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega + dd^c G_a)^n$ is concentrated at the single point $a$ (i.e., is a positive multiple of the Dirac mass $\delta_a$), and
(ii) the Lelong number $\nu(G_a, a)$ is irrational?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is attributed to Coman–Guedj and appears to remain open in dimension $n \geq 2$. In dimension one the Lelong number coincides with the Dirac mass and is therefore rational. Known constructions of quasi-psh Green functions with Monge–Ampère mass concentrated at a point produce rational Lelong numbers; no example with irrational Lelong number is known, and no proof of nonexistence has been published.

Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, and let $T$ and $S$ be cohomologous closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ (i.e. $\{T\}=\{S\}$ in $H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$). Write $T = \theta + dd^c \varphi$ and $S = \theta + dd^c \psi$ for a smooth representative $\theta$ and quasi-plurisubharmonic potentials $\varphi,\psi$. Say that $T$ is more singular than $S$ if $\varphi \le \psi + C$ for some constant $C$. Define the non-pluripolar self-product $\langle T^n\rangle$ as the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure of $T$, constructed by setting, for each $k$,
$$\langle T^k\rangle := \lim_{j\to\infty} \mathbf{1}_{\{\varphi > -j\}}(\theta + dd^c\max(\varphi,-j))^k$$
extended by zero across $\{\varphi = -\infty\}$, this limit being independent of the chosen potential and producing a closed positive current of bidegree $(k,k)$ that puts no mass on pluripolar sets.

Question: does the inequality
$$\int_X \langle T^n\rangle \;\le\; \int_X \langle S^n\rangle$$
hold whenever $T$ and $S$ are cohomologous and $T$ is more singular than $S$? More generally, does $\langle T^n\rangle \le \langle S^n\rangle$ as measures on $X$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The monotonicity conjecture of Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi for non-pluripolar products has been established. Witt Nyström proved monotonicity of non-pluripolar masses for cohomologous currents with one more singular than the other, and Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu (Analysis & PDE, 2018) extended monotonicity to currents in possibly different big cohomology classes, fully resolving the conjecture. Subsequent works (e.g., on log-concavity of volumes and integration-by-parts formulas) build on this resolution.

representations.normalized:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, where $\omega$ is a fixed Kähler form. Denote by $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ the set of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, i.e. upper semicontinuous functions $\varphi : X \to [-\infty,+\infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, such that $\omega + dd^c\varphi \ge 0$ in the sense of currents.

Let $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ denote the largest subset of $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ on which the complex Monge–Ampère operator
$$\mathrm{MA}(\varphi) := (\omega + dd^c\varphi)^n$$
can be defined as a positive Radon measure on $X$ in such a way that it is continuous under decreasing limits of bounded $\omega$-plurisubharmonic sequences. Let
$$\mathcal{E}(X,\omega) := \Bigl\{\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega) : \mathrm{MA}(\varphi) \text{ is well defined and } \int_X \mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = \int_X \omega^n\Bigr\}$$
be the class of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions of full Monge–Ampère mass. It is known that $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$ if and only if $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi)$ does not charge any pluripolar subset of $X$.

Question. Suppose $\varphi \in \mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ satisfies the weaker requirement that its Monge–Ampère measure $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi)$ does not charge the (possibly pluripolar) set $\{\varphi = -\infty\}$. Does it follow that $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$?

Let $\pi : X \to \mathbb{CP}^2$ be the blow-up of the complex projective plane at one point; then $X$ is a del Pezzo surface with positive first Chern class $c_1(X)$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega$ on $X$ representing $c_1(X)$, and let $V = \int_X \omega^2$. Let $D \subset X$ be a smooth anticanonical divisor (so $[D]$ represents $c_1(X)$ as a $(1,1)$-current of integration), and define the probability measure
$$\mu_D = \frac{\omega \wedge [D]}{V},$$
which is supported on $D$ and is therefore pluripolar in $X$.

Let $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ denote the set of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, and let $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ denote the domain of definition of the complex Monge–Ampère operator on $X$, that is, the largest subclass of $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ on which the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère operator
$$\mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = \frac{1}{V}(\omega + dd^c\varphi)^2$$
extends as a positive Radon measure satisfying the standard convergence and locality properties (in the sense of Cegrell's class extended to compact Kähler manifolds).

Question: Does there exist $\varphi_D \in \mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ such that
$$\mathrm{MA}(\varphi_D) = \mu_D ?$$

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $\mathrm{PSH}(\Omega) \cap L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ denote the cone of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega$. For $u \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega) \cap L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, the complex Monge–Ampère operator
$$ (dd^c u)^n = \underbrace{dd^c u \wedge \cdots \wedge dd^c u}_{n \text{ times}} $$
is well defined as a positive Radon measure on $\Omega$ (Bedford–Taylor). Let
$$ \mathcal{R}(\Omega) = \{(dd^c u)^n : u \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega) \cap L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)\} $$
be the range of this operator.

Question: Is there a characterization of $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$ purely in terms of a uniform integrability condition on the positive Radon measures on $\Omega$? More precisely, does there exist a family $\mathcal{F}$ of test functions (or weights) such that a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ belongs to $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$ if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ is uniformly integrable with respect to $\mu$?

Fix an integer m ≥ 1 and consider a complex parameter vector z = (V(2), V(4), …, V(2m)) ∈ C^m. For each integer n ≥ 1, let X_n^+(F_m) denote the family of admissible positive-step walks of length n with steps drawn from F_m = {2, 4, …, 2m}, i.e. finite sequences (k_1, k_2, …, k_N) with each k_j ∈ F_m ∪ (−F_m) such that all partial sums n + k_1 + k_2 + ⋯ + k_j (j = 1, …, N) are positive integers different from n, and with terminal partial sum equal to n (so the walk returns to n while staying in the admissible region).

To each walk x = (k_1, …, k_N) ∈ X_n^+(F_m) associate the weight
   h(x) = h_z,n(x) = ∏_{j=1}^{N} V(|k_j|) · ∏_{j=1}^{N-1} 1/(n^2 − (n + k_1 + ⋯ + k_j)^2),
where V(2k) is the corresponding component of z (and V(−2k) = V(2k) is interpreted via |k_j|).

Question. Is it true that for Lebesgue-almost every z ∈ C^m there exists a constant C(z) > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n,
   ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)|  ≤  C(z) · | ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x) | ?

$$\varphi\big|_{\partial \Omega} = 0 \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mu = (dd^c \varphi)^n \quad\text{in } \Omega \, ?$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The general continuous subsolution problem of Kołodziej remains open. Significant partial results exist: Kołodziej and Nguyen (2018, 2019) showed that if the modulus of continuity of the subsolution satisfies a Dini-type condition, or if the measure is dominated by capacity (e.g., has $L^p$ density for $p>1$, or is moderate), then a continuous solution exists. The Hölder continuous analogue has also been settled affirmatively. However, an unconditional positive answer with only continuity of the subsolution has not been established.

Denote by $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ the set of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, i.e. upper semicontinuous functions $\varphi: X \to [-\infty,\infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, such that $\omega + dd^c\varphi \ge 0$ as a current. For $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega) \cap L^\infty(X)$ the Monge-Ampère measure
$$\mathrm{MA}(\varphi) := (\omega + dd^c\varphi)^n$$
is a well-defined positive Radon measure on $X$ (in the sense of Bedford-Taylor).

Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $X$ which is locally dominated by Monge-Ampère measures of bounded plurisubharmonic functions, in the following sense: every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ (biholomorphic to an open set in $\mathbb{C}^n$) on which there exists a bounded plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $U$ such that $\mu|_U \le (dd^c u)^n$ as measures on $U$.

Determine whether there must exist $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega) \cap L^\infty(X)$ such that
$$\mu = (\omega + dd^c\varphi)^n.$$

This is known as Kołodziej's bounded subsolution conjecture on compact Kähler manifolds. A 2023 preprint by D.-V. Vu (arXiv:2304.07876, "Monge-Ampère measures of bounded potentials") announced a resolution implying Kołodziej's conjecture, but the paper was subsequently withdrawn. We could not find a definitive published proof, so the current status is unclear; partial results (e.g. Hölder/continuous analogues, non-pluripolar variants, and various special cases) are known.

Fix integers m ≥ 1 and consider parameters z = (V_1, V_2, …, V_m) ∈ C^m. For each integer n ≥ 1, let X_n^+ = X_n^+(F_m) denote the (combinatorially defined) finite index set of "positive" walks of weighted length n associated with the m-parameter family F_m (the index set arising in the eigenfunction expansions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials of m terms, so that each x ∈ X_n^+ is a finite sequence of admissible jumps and h(x) = h(x; z) is a rational function of z whose factors are products of the coordinates V_j and reciprocals of small denominators built from the jumps in x).

Define
  C(z) := sup_n  ( ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x; z)| ) / | ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x; z) |  ∈ [0, ∞],
the smallest (possibly infinite) constant for which the comparison inequality
  ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x; z)|  ≤  C(z) · | ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x; z) |
holds simultaneously for every n ≥ 1.

Let W := { z ∈ C^m : C(z) = ∞ } be the associated exceptional set. Determine the structure of W as a subset of C^m: in particular, decide whether W is a (countable union of) proper analytic / algebraic subvarieties of C^m, describe its dimension and irreducible components, and decide whether C^m \ W has full Lebesgue measure (i.e. whether the comparison inequality holds for almost every z ∈ C^m).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is posed as an open problem by Djakov and Mityagin (2012) concerning the structure of the exceptional set in C^m on which a comparison inequality between the absolute and signed sums over walk-type combinatorial objects fails. Subsequent literature on combinatorial identities of Djakov–Mityagin and on convergence/divergence of spectral decompositions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials addresses related identities and special cases (e.g. two-term potentials), but no source found resolves the description of the exceptional set W = {z : C(z) = ∞} in general. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold, and let $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ denote the set of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, i.e., upper semicontinuous functions $\varphi\colon X\to[-\infty,\infty)$, not identically $-\infty$, such that $\omega+dd^c\varphi\geq 0$ in the sense of currents. For a bounded $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$, the Monge–Ampère measure $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi):=(\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well defined (where $n=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}X$).

Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $X$. Consider the following two properties:

(i) There exists $\varepsilon_\mu>0$ such that for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$, the function $e^{-\varepsilon_\mu\varphi}$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$, and moreover the family $\{e^{-\varepsilon_\mu\varphi}:\varphi\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega),\ \sup_X\varphi=0\}$ is bounded in $L^1(\mu)$.

(ii) There exists a Hölder continuous $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ such that $\mu=\mathrm{MA}(\varphi)$.

Determine whether (i) and (ii) are equivalent.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The implication (ii) ⇒ (i) is well known, while the converse (i) ⇒ (ii) is the difficult direction. Existing characterizations of Monge–Ampère measures admitting Hölder continuous potentials (e.g., via Hölder continuous super-potentials, or via membership in suitable Sobolev/Besov spaces) give sufficient conditions but do not establish the full equivalence with the exponential integrability condition. No published source found that resolves this equivalence; it appears to remain open.

Let $n\ge 1$ and let $B\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ denote the open unit ball. Fix $p>1$. Let $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{B})$ be a plurisubharmonic function (i.e., the complex Hessian $(\varphi_{j\bar k})_{j,k=1}^n$ is positive semidefinite) such that $\varphi|_{\partial B}=0$, and write
$$\det(\varphi_{j\bar k}) = f.$$
It is known that there exists a constant $C=C(n,p)>0$, depending only on $n$ and $p$, such that
$$\|\varphi\|_{L^\infty(B)} \;\le\; C\,\|f\|_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}.$$
Provide a proof of this a priori estimate that uses only PDE techniques (such as maximum-principle/ABP-type arguments, auxiliary equations, and integral estimates), without recourse to pluripotential theory.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Błocki (2011) gave a PDE proof using the Alexandrov–Bakelman–Pucci maximum principle for $p>2$. A full PDE proof of the sharp $L^\infty$ estimate for all $p>1$ (and more general settings) was obtained by Guo, Phong and Tong in "On $L^\infty$ estimates for complex Monge–Ampère equations" (arXiv:2106.02224, 2021), using auxiliary Monge–Ampère equations and an ABP-type argument; this resolves the question.

Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $\omega$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ that is semi-positive (i.e., $\omega \ge 0$ pointwise as a Hermitian form) and big (i.e., the cohomology class $\{\omega\}$ contains a Kähler current; equivalently, $\int_X \omega^n > 0$ together with bigness of the class). Let $dV$ be a smooth volume form on $X$, and let $0 \le f \in L^p(X, dV)$ for some $p > 1$, normalized so that $\int_X f\, dV = \int_X \omega^n$.

Consider the degenerate complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$(\omega + dd^c \varphi)^n = f\, dV$$
for an $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ (i.e., $\varphi$ is upper semicontinuous and $\omega + dd^c\varphi \ge 0$ as a current), where the left-hand side is interpreted as the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure of $\varphi$, and $\varphi$ is normalized (e.g., $\sup_X \varphi = 0$).

Question: must every such solution $\varphi$ be Hölder continuous on all of $X$? That is, does there exist $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $C > 0$ (depending on the data) such that $|\varphi(x) - \varphi(y)| \le C\, d(x,y)^\alpha$ for all $x, y \in X$, where $d$ is the distance induced by a fixed Kähler metric on $X$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Known results establish Hölder continuity of $\varphi$ on the ample locus of $\{\omega\}$ when $\omega$ is semi-positive and big with $f \in L^p$, $p>1$ (Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi and subsequent work, including stability/Hölder regularity papers in big cohomology classes). However, global Hölder continuity on all of $X$ — including across the non-ample locus where $\omega$ degenerates — remains an open problem; recent literature continues to phrase Hölder regularity statements as holding on the ample locus rather than globally.

Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $S \subset X$ be a smooth totally real submanifold of maximal real dimension $n$ (so that at every $p \in S$, the real tangent space $T_pS$ satisfies $T_pS \cap J(T_pS) = \{0\}$, where $J$ is the complex structure on $X$). Let $\mu_S$ denote the normalized $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $S$, regarded as a probability measure on $X$. It is known that $S$ is non-pluripolar, and consequently there exists a unique $\omega$-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi_S$ in the finite-energy class $\mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$, normalized by $\sup_X \varphi_S = 0$, satisfying the complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$(\omega + dd^c \varphi_S)^n \;=\; \mu_S$$
in the sense of pluripotential theory. Determine the optimal regularity of the potential $\varphi_S$ (for instance, the largest Hölder exponent $\alpha \in (0,1]$, or higher regularity class, that $\varphi_S$ is guaranteed to belong to, and whether this exponent is sharp).

Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of dimension $n$ in the Fujiki class (i.e., bimeromorphic to a compact Kähler manifold). Let $\alpha \in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ be a big cohomology class, that is, $\alpha$ can be represented by a closed $(1,1)$-current that dominates a Hermitian form. The ample locus $\mathrm{Amp}(\alpha)$ is the largest Zariski open subset of $X$ on which some closed positive current with minimal singularities representing $\alpha$ has locally bounded local potentials. Closed positive $(1,1)$-currents in $\alpha$ admit a non-pluripolar self-intersection product $\langle T^n \rangle$, a positive Borel measure putting no mass on pluripolar sets, and a current $T$ in $\alpha$ is said to have full Monge–Ampère mass (finite energy) when $\int_X \langle T^n \rangle = \mathrm{vol}(\alpha)$.

Let $\mu$ be a smooth positive volume form on $X$ with $\int_X \mu = \mathrm{vol}(\alpha)$, and let $T$ be the unique closed positive $(1,1)$-current with full Monge–Ampère mass in $\alpha$ such that
$$\langle T^n \rangle = \mu.$$

Determine whether $T$ is smooth (i.e., has $C^\infty$ local potentials) on the ample locus $\mathrm{Amp}(\alpha)$.

Determine whether $T$ is smooth (i.e., has $C^\infty$ local potentials) on the ample locus $\mathrm{Amp}(\alpha)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The smoothness of T on the ample locus is established in the case where the class α is nef and big (Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Acta Math. 2010). For a general big class, only partial regularity (e.g., uniform Hölder regularity on the ample locus, and L^∞ bounds on local potentials) is known, and full C^∞ smoothness on Amp(α) for arbitrary big classes remains open.

A 2017 attempt by Dinew–Kołodziej (arXiv:1706.07392) to provide an analytic proof of Krylov's C^{1,1} estimates was withdrawn due to a mistake in the main argument. Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n \ge 3$, where $\omega$ is a smooth positive $(1,1)$-form. A function $\varphi: X \to \mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if $\varphi$ is upper semicontinuous, locally integrable, and $\omega + dd^c\varphi \ge 0$ in the sense of currents (where $d = \partial+\bar\partial$ and $d^c = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(\bar\partial-\partial)$, so that $dd^c = \tfrac{i}{\pi}\partial\bar\partial$). For a bounded $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$, the Bedford–Taylor–type product $(\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well defined as a positive Radon measure on $X$.

Give an intrinsic geometric/analytic characterization of those Hermitian forms $\omega$ on $X$ for which
$$\int_X (\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n \;=\; \int_X \omega^n$$
holds for every bounded $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$ on $X$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem, posed by Dinew and Kołodziej, asks for a characterization of Hermitian metrics for which the total Monge–Ampère mass is independent of the bounded ω-psh potential. Sufficient conditions (e.g. pluriclosed/SKT-type or stronger Kähler-like conditions, and balanced/Astheno-Kähler-related conditions ensuring $dd^c\omega^k=0$ for relevant $k$) are known to imply mass invariance, but a complete intrinsic characterization on general compact Hermitian manifolds of dimension ≥ 3 does not appear in the literature; recent works on pluripotential theory on Hermitian manifolds continue to treat this as an open problem.

$$T(X,\omega)\;=\;\inf\Bigl\{\int_X (\omega+dd^c\varphi)^n \;:\; \varphi\in C^\infty(X)\cap \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)\Bigr\}.$$
Determine whether there exists a compact Hermitian manifold $(X,\omega)$ for which $T(X,\omega)=0$, or prove that $T(X,\omega)>0$ for every compact Hermitian manifold.

Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n$, where $\omega$ is a smooth positive $(1,1)$-form (not assumed to be closed). A function $\varphi: X \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$) if $\varphi$ is upper semicontinuous, locally integrable, and satisfies $\omega + dd^c \varphi \geq 0$ as a current, where $d^c = \frac{i}{2\pi}(\bar\partial - \partial)$. For bounded $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions the Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega + dd^c \varphi)^n$ is defined in the sense of Bedford–Taylor. Define
$$\mathrm{cap}(X,\omega) \;=\; \inf\Big\{\int_X (\omega + dd^c \varphi)^n \;:\; \varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega),\; 0 \leq \varphi \leq 1 \Big\}.$$

(a) Relate the invariant $\mathrm{cap}(X,\omega)$ to the geometry of $(X,\omega)$.
(b) Determine whether $\mathrm{cap}(X,\omega)$ can be computed from geometric data of $(X,\omega)$.
(c) Determine how $\mathrm{cap}(X,\omega)$ behaves under smooth deformations of the Hermitian metric $\omega$.

representations.normalized:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n$. A function $u\in L^1(M)$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if $u$ is upper semicontinuous and $\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial u\ge 0$ as a current on $M$. For continuous $\omega$-psh functions, the complex Monge–Ampère measure $(\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial u)^n$ is well defined via Bedford–Taylor theory.

Fix $p>1$. Suppose $u,v$ are continuous $\omega$-psh functions on $M$, normalized by $\sup_M u=\sup_M v=0$, satisfying
$$(\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial u)^n = f\,\omega^n, \qquad (\omega+\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial v)^n = g\,\omega^n,$$
with $f,g\in L^p(M,\omega^n)$, $f,g\ge 0$, and $\int_M f\,\omega^n=\int_M g\,\omega^n=\int_M\omega^n$.

It is known that there exist constants $C>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, depending only on $(M,\omega)$, $p$, and an upper bound for $\|f\|_{L^p}+\|g\|_{L^p}$, such that, under the additional non-degeneracy assumption $f\ge c_0>0$ on $M$,
$$\|u-v\|_{L^\infty(M)} \le C\,\|f-g\|_{L^p}^{\alpha}.$$

Question: Does the same stability estimate
$$\|u-v\|_{L^\infty(M)} \le C\,\|f-g\|_{L^p}^{\alpha}$$
continue to hold without assuming the lower bound $f\ge c_0>0$? That is, can the strict positivity hypothesis on the right-hand side $f$ be removed?

Lu, Phung, and Tô (Ann. Inst. Fourier 71 (2021), 2019–2045; arXiv:2003.08417) established stability and Hölder regularity for complex Monge–Ampère equations on compact Hermitian manifolds with right-hand side in L^p, p>1, removing the non-degeneracy assumption for the equation of the form (ω+i∂∂̄u)^n = e^{u+F}ω^n. Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ (for instance $X=\mathbb{C}^n$ or a compact Kähler manifold with a fixed Kähler form $\omega$). A function $\varphi:X\to[-\infty,\infty)$ is called quasi-plurisubharmonic (quasi-psh) if it is locally the sum of a plurisubharmonic function and a smooth function; equivalently, $dd^c\varphi+\theta\geq 0$ for some smooth $(1,1)$-form $\theta$. The Lelong number of $\varphi$ at a point $x\in X$ is $\nu(\varphi,x)=\liminf_{z\to x}\varphi(z)/\log|z-x|$.

In complex dimension $n\leq 2$ the following desingularization statement is known: for every quasi-psh function $\varphi$ on $X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a finite composition of blow-ups with smooth centers $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ such that
$$\pi^*\varphi=\sum_{j} a_j\,\log|s_{E_j}|+\psi,$$
where the $E_j$ are exceptional prime divisors of $\pi$, $s_{E_j}$ are local defining sections of $E_j$, $a_j\geq 0$, and $\psi$ is a quasi-psh function on $\widetilde X$ all of whose Lelong numbers are bounded by $\varepsilon$.

Question: Does this desingularization property extend to every dimension $n\geq 3$? That is, given any quasi-psh function $\varphi$ on a complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, can one find a sequence of blow-ups along smooth centers after which $\pi^*\varphi$ decomposes as an explicit divisorial part plus a quasi-psh remainder with Lelong numbers $\leq\varepsilon$ everywhere?

A two-dimensional desingularization result for quasi-psh functions is due to Favre–Jonsson (valuative analysis on $\mathbb{C}^2$) and was used by Guedj. The status remains unclear from available evidence.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded hyperconvex domain, i.e., a bounded, connected, open set admitting a continuous, negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion function. Let $\delta_\Omega$ denote the diameter of $\Omega$. Recall Cegrell's class $\mathcal{F}(\Omega)$, consisting of all plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi : \Omega \to [-\infty, 0)$ such that there exists a decreasing sequence $\varphi_j \in \mathcal{E}_0(\Omega)$ (bounded plurisubharmonic functions with zero boundary values and finite total Monge–Ampère mass) decreasing to $\varphi$ with $\sup_j \int_\Omega (dd^c \varphi_j)^n < \infty$; for $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$ the complex Monge–Ampère measure $(dd^c\varphi)^n$ is well defined as a positive Radon measure of finite total mass.

For $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$, set
$$\lambda^n = \int_\Omega (dd^c \varphi)^n, \qquad \lambda > 0.$$
It is known that there exists a constant $c_n > 0$, depending only on $n$, such that for every $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$ and every $s > 0$,
$$\mathrm{Vol}(\{\varphi < -s\}) \le c_n\, \delta_\Omega^{2n} (1 + s\lambda^{-1})^{n-1} \exp(-2n s \lambda^{-1}).$$

Question. Does there exist a constant $c_n' > 0$, depending only on $n$, such that for every bounded hyperconvex $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$, every $\varphi \in \mathcal{F}(\Omega)$, and every $s > 0$,
$$\mathrm{Vol}(\{\varphi < -s\}) \le c_n'\, \delta_\Omega^{2n} \exp(-2n s \lambda^{-1})\, ?$$
That is, can the polynomial prefactor $(1 + s\lambda^{-1})^{n-1}$ be removed at the cost of changing the constant?

Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold which is either Kähler or, more generally, lies in the Fujiki class $\mathcal{C}$ (i.e., is bimeromorphic to a compact Kähler manifold). Let $\omega$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ which is semi-positive and big, meaning $\omega \geq 0$ pointwise and $\int_X \omega^n > 0$, where $n = \dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$.

A function $\varphi : X \to [-\infty, +\infty)$ is called $\omega$-plurisubharmonic ($\omega$-psh) if it is upper semicontinuous, locally integrable, and $\omega + dd^c \varphi \geq 0$ in the sense of currents. For an $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$, the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = (\omega + dd^c \varphi)^n$ is well defined, and $\varphi$ is said to have full Monge–Ampère mass if $\int_X \mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = \int_X \omega^n$. The finite-energy class $\mathcal{E}(X, \omega)$ consists of all $\omega$-psh functions with full Monge–Ampère mass.

Recall that the Lelong number of $\varphi$ at a point $x \in X$ is
$$\nu(\varphi, x) = \liminf_{z \to x} \frac{\varphi(z)}{\log |z - x|},$$
computed in any local holomorphic chart.

Question: Is it true that for every $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X, \omega)$, the Lelong number $\nu(\varphi, x)$ vanishes at every point $x \in X$?

For an $\omega$-psh function $\varphi$, the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = (\omega + dd^c \varphi)^n$ is well defined, and $\varphi$ is said to have full Monge–Ampère mass if $\int_X \mathrm{MA}(\varphi) = \int_X \omega^n$. The finite-energy class $\mathcal{E}(X, \omega)$ consists of all $\omega$-psh functions with full Monge–Ampère mass.

Recall that the Lelong number of $\varphi$ at a point $x \in X$ is
$$\nu(\varphi, x) = \liminf_{z \to x} \frac{\varphi(z)}{\log |z - x|},$$
computed in any local holomorphic chart.

Question: Is it true that for every $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X, \omega)$, the Lelong number $\nu(\varphi, x)$ vanishes at every point $x \in X$?

It is classically known (Guedj–Zeriahi) that on a compact Kähler manifold with $\omega$ a Kähler form, every $\varphi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\omega)$ has zero Lelong numbers everywhere. The question concerns the more general setting of a semi-positive big $(1,1)$-form on a Fujiki-class manifold. Web search did not return a definitive resolution of this generalized question; recent works on relative pluripotential theory and finite-energy classes in big cohomology classes discuss related results but do not appear to settle the question in this exact generality. Status appears unknown from available sources.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded pseudoconvex domain and let $\varphi : \Omega \to [-\infty, \infty)$ be a plurisubharmonic function (i.e., upper semicontinuous, not identically $-\infty$, and such that for every complex line $L$ the restriction $\varphi|_{\Omega \cap L}$ is subharmonic). Say that $\varphi$ admits a differential test from above at a point $z_0 \in \Omega$ if there exists a $C^2$ function $u$ defined in a neighborhood of $z_0$ such that $\varphi \le u$ near $z_0$ and $\varphi(z_0) = u(z_0)$. Let
$$N(\varphi) := \{ z_0 \in \Omega : \varphi \text{ admits no differential test from above at } z_0 \}.$$
It is known that $N(\varphi)$ has empty interior. Determine what further can be said about $N(\varphi)$; in particular, decide whether $N(\varphi)$ must have zero Lebesgue measure, and whether $N(\varphi)$ must have zero (Bedford–Taylor) pluricapacity.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $f \geq 0$ be a continuous function on $\Omega$. Consider the local complex Monge-Ampère equation
$$-(dd^c V)^n + f\, dV = 0,$$
where $dV$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\Omega$ and $(dd^c V)^n$ is the complex Monge-Ampère operator. Let $v: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous viscosity supersolution of this equation. Define the plurisubharmonic envelope of $v$ by
$$P(v)(z) := \sup\{u(z) : u \text{ plurisubharmonic on } \Omega,\ u \leq v \text{ on } \Omega\}.$$
Determine whether the upper semicontinuous regularization $P(v)^*$ is a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation, i.e. whether $P(v)$ is plurisubharmonic and satisfies
$$-(dd^c P(v))^n + f\, dV \leq 0$$
in the pluripotential sense on $\Omega$.

Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $\alpha_0 \in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ be a Kähler class. Let $S_0$ be a positive closed $(1,1)$-current representing $\alpha_0$, which may have nonzero Lelong numbers. By work of Di Nezza and Lu, there exists a maximal weak Kähler–Ricci flow $(\omega_t)_{0 < t < T_{\max}}$ starting from $S_0$, namely a family of positive closed $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ such that on a time-increasing family of Zariski open subsets $\Omega_t \subset X$ each $\omega_t$ is a smooth Kähler form satisfying the Kähler–Ricci flow equation
$$\frac{\partial \omega_t}{\partial t} = -\mathrm{Ric}(\omega_t),$$
with $\omega_t \to S_0$ as $t \to 0^+$ in the sense of currents.

Recall that a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $X$ has analytic singularities if locally
$$\varphi = \tfrac{c}{2}\log\Big(\sum_{j=1}^N |f_j|^2\Big) + \text{(smooth)}$$
for some constant $c > 0$ and holomorphic functions $f_1,\dots,f_N$; a positive closed $(1,1)$-current is said to have analytic singularities if its local potentials do.

Question: Does the family $(\omega_t)_{0 < t < T_{\max}}$ produce, as $t \to 0^+$, a family of approximating positive closed $(1,1)$-currents in the class $\alpha_0$ that have analytic singularities and converge to $S_0$? Equivalently, does the weak Kähler–Ricci flow regularize $S_0$ by currents with analytic singularities, in analogy with Demailly's regularization theorem?

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded smooth strictly pseudoconvex domain, and set $\Omega_T := (0,T) \times \Omega$ for some $T \in (0,\infty]$. Consider the complex Monge–Ampère flow
$$ (dd^c u_t)^n = e^{\partial_t u + F(t,z,u)}\, \mu(z)\, dt, \qquad (t,z) \in \Omega_T, $$
where, for each $t$, $u_t = u(t,\cdot)$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$, $dd^c$ is taken in the spatial variables, $F$ is a smooth function nondecreasing in the last argument, and $\mu$ is a smooth positive volume form on $\overline{\Omega}$. The flow is supplemented with a boundary condition on $(0,T) \times \partial\Omega$ and an initial condition $u(0,\cdot) = u_0$, where $u_0$ is plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$.

It is known that when $u_0$ is bounded, there exists a solution $u$ to this Cauchy–Dirichlet problem which is smooth on $\Omega_T$ and continuous up to $t = 0$ in an appropriate sense (instantaneous smoothing).

Question: Can such a complex Monge–Ampère flow be started from an arbitrary plurisubharmonic initial datum $u_0$ — in particular one that is not assumed to be bounded — in the sense of producing a (suitably weak) solution that is smooth for $t > 0$ and recovers $u_0$ as $t \to 0^+$?

Let $\{\omega_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a continuous family of smooth semi-positive $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ such that there exists a fixed semi-positive big $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ with $\omega_t \geq \theta$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. Let $F:[0,T]\times X\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous and nondecreasing in the last variable, and let $\mu(t,x)$ be a bounded continuous (non-negative) volume form on $[0,T]\times X$. Consider the degenerate parabolic complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$\bigl(\omega_t + dd^c\varphi_t\bigr)^n \;=\; e^{\dot{\varphi}_t + F(t,x,\varphi_t)}\,\mu(t,x) \qquad\text{on } [0,T]\times X,$$
where $\varphi_t(x)=\varphi(t,x)$ and $\dot\varphi_t = \partial_t\varphi$, and where solutions, subsolutions and supersolutions are understood in the viscosity sense (with $\omega_t+dd^c\varphi_t$ interpreted via the standard viscosity formulation for degenerate complex Monge–Ampère operators).

Suppose $u:[0,T]\times X\to\mathbb{R}$ is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution and $v:[0,T]\times X\to\mathbb{R}$ is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity supersolution of the above equation, and that $u(0,x)\le v(0,x)$ for every $x\in X$.

Question: Does it follow that $u(t,x)\le v(t,x)$ for every $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times X$?

Let $G \cong C_{n_1} \oplus \cdots \oplus C_{n_r}$ be a finite abelian group with $|G| \geq 3$ and $1 < n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_r$. Let $\mathcal{B}(G)$ denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over $G$, i.e., the monoid (under concatenation) of finite unordered sequences of elements of $G$ whose terms sum to $0$, with irreducible (atomic) elements being the minimal zero-sum sequences. For a nonzero, non-identity element $B \in \mathcal{B}(G)$, the set of lengths of $B$ is
$$\mathsf{L}(B) = \{k \in \mathbb{N} : B = U_1 \cdots U_k \text{ for some atoms } U_1, \ldots, U_k \in \mathcal{B}(G)\}.$$
For a finite set $L = \{\ell_0 < \ell_1 < \cdots < \ell_k\} \subset \mathbb{Z}$, define its set of distances
$$\Delta(L) = \{\ell_i - \ell_{i-1} : 1 \leq i \leq k\},$$
and set
$$\Delta(G) = \bigcup_{B \in \mathcal{B}(G)} \Delta(\mathsf{L}(B)).$$
Determine whether
$$\max \Delta(G) = \max\!\left\{\, n_r - 2,\ -1 + \sum_{i=1}^{r} \left\lfloor \tfrac{n_i}{2} \right\rfloor \,\right\}.$$

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|\ge 3$. By the structure theorem there are uniquely determined integers $1<n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ such that $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$; one calls $r(G)=r$ the rank of $G$ and $\exp(G)=n_r$ the exponent of $G$.

For a subset $G_0\subseteq G$, a sequence over $G_0$ is a finite unordered tuple of elements of $G_0$ (formally, an element of the free abelian monoid $\mathcal F(G_0)$ on $G_0$). A sequence $S=g_1\cdots g_\ell$ is called a zero-sum sequence if $g_1+\cdots+g_\ell=0$, and it is called a minimal zero-sum sequence if it is a zero-sum sequence and no proper nonempty subsequence of it is a zero-sum sequence. Let $\mathcal A(G_0)$ denote the set of minimal zero-sum sequences over $G_0$. For a zero-sum sequence $S$ over $G_0$, the set of lengths of $S$ is
$$\mathsf L(S)=\{k\in\mathbb N : S=U_1\cdots U_k \text{ with } U_1,\dots,U_k\in\mathcal A(G_0)\}.$$
Let $\mathcal L(G_0)=\{\mathsf L(S): S \text{ a zero-sum sequence over }G_0\}$. For a finite set $L=\{l_1<l_2<\cdots<l_k\}\subseteq\mathbb N$ define $\Delta(L)=\{l_{i+1}-l_i : 1\le i\le k-1\}$, and put
$$\Delta(G_0)=\bigcup_{L\in\mathcal L(G_0),\,|L|\ge 2}\Delta(L).$$
Define
$$\Delta^*(G)=\{\min\Delta(G_0) : G_0\subseteq G,\ \Delta(G_0)\neq\varnothing\}\subseteq\mathbb N.$$

Question: Does there exist a finite abelian group $G$ such that $\Delta^*(G)$ is an interval of $\mathbb N$ (i.e. $\Delta^*(G)=[\min\Delta^*(G),\max\Delta^*(G)]\cap\mathbb N$) and at the same time $\exp(G)\ge 2r(G)+2$?

Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with finite class group $G$. For an element $a \in H$, write $a = u_1 \cdots u_k$ as a product of atoms (irreducibles); the set of lengths of $a$ is
$$L(a) = \{ k \in \mathbb{N} : a = u_1 \cdots u_k \text{ with each } u_i \text{ an atom of } H \},$$
and the system of sets of lengths of $H$ is $\mathcal{L}(H) = \{ L(a) : a \in H \}$.

A non-empty subset $L \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ is called an almost arithmetic multiprogression (AAMP) with bound $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$, difference $d \in \mathbb{N}$, and period $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \{0, d, 2d, \dots\}$ with $0, d \in \mathcal{D}$, if there exist integers $y, \ell$ with
$$L = y + (L' \cup L^* \cup L'') \subseteq y + \mathcal{D} + d\mathbb{Z},$$
where $L^* = (\mathcal{D} + d\mathbb{Z}) \cap [0, \ell d]$ is the central part, and $L' \subseteq [-M, -1]$, $L'' \subseteq \ell d + [1, M]$ are bounded "end" perturbations.

The Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths asserts: for every Krull monoid $H$ with finite class group there exist $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and a finite non-empty set $\Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that every $L \in \mathcal{L}(H)$ is an AAMP with bound $M$ and difference $d \in \Delta^*$.

For a finite abelian group $G$, let $\mathcal{B}(G)$ denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over $G$, and write $\mathcal{L}(G) = \mathcal{L}(\mathcal{B}(G))$. Let $\mathsf{D}(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of $G$, i.e.\ the smallest $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$ has a non-empty zero-sum subsequence. Let
$$M^*(G) = \min\{M \in \mathbb{N}_0 : \exists \text{ finite } \Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N} \text{ with every } L \in \mathcal{L}(G) \text{ an AAMP with bound } M \text{ and difference } d \in \Delta^*\}.$$

Determine the rough order of magnitude of $M^*(G)$ as a function of $\mathsf{D}(G)$, as $G$ ranges over finite abelian groups.

A non-empty subset $L \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ is called an almost arithmetic multiprogression (AAMP) with bound $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$, difference $d \in \mathbb{N}$, and period $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \{0, d, 2d, \dots\}$ with $0, d \in \mathcal{D}$, if there exist integers $y, \ell$ with

where $L^* = (\mathcal{D} + d\mathbb{Z}) \cap [0, \ell d]$ is the central part, and $L' \subseteq [-M, -1]$, $L'' \subseteq \ell d + [1, M]$ are bounded "end" perturbations.

The Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths asserts: for every Krull monoid $H$ with finite class group there exist $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and a finite non-empty set $\Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that every $L \in \mathcal{L}(H)$ is an AAMP with bound $M$ and difference $d \in \Delta^*$.

For a finite abelian group $G$, let $\mathcal{B}(G)$ denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over $G$, and write $\mathcal{L}(G) = \mathcal{L}(\mathcal{B}(G))$. Let $\mathsf{D}(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of $G$, i.e.\ the smallest $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$ has a non-empty zero-sum subsequence. Let
$$M^*(G) = \min\{M \in \mathbb{N}_0 : \exists \text{ finite } \Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N} \text{ with every } L \in \mathcal{L}(G) \text{ an AAMP with bound } M \text{ and difference } d \in \Delta^*\}.$$

Determine the rough order of magnitude of $M^*(G)$ as a function of $\mathsf{D}(G)$, as $G$ ranges over finite abelian groups.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A web search did not turn up a published determination of the order of magnitude of the optimal bound in the Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths in terms of the Davenport constant. Surveys of factorization theory in Krull monoids continue to list quantitative refinements of the STSL bound as an open direction, and no source identified gives an asymptotic answer. Status appears to remain open.

Fix a field $\mathbb{K}$ and a nonzero scalar $q\in\mathbb{K}$ that is not a root of unity. For $X,Y$ in an associative algebra set $[X,Y]_q=qXY-q^{-1}YX$ and $[X,Y]=XY-YX$.

(1) The q-Onsager algebra $O_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebra with two generators $W_0,W_1$ and the q-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\rho\,[W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $\rho\in\mathbb{K}$ is a fixed scalar.

(2) The current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebra generated by an infinite family of generators $\{W_{-k},\,W_{k+1},\,G_{k+1},\,\tilde G_{k+1}\mid k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\}$ subject to the standard list of defining relations under which the first modes $W_0,W_1$ satisfy the q-Dolan–Grady relations above with the same parameter $\rho$.

(3) Let $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ be the quantum affine algebra with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i,q^{\pm h_i}$ ($i=0,1$). Fix scalars $k_\pm,\varepsilon_\pm\in\mathbb{K}$ with $\rho=(q+q^{-1})^2 k_+k_-$, and let $B$ be the left coideal subalgebra of $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ generated by
$$\mathcal{W}_0=k_+e_1+k_-q^{-1}f_1q^{h_1}+\varepsilon_+ q^{h_1},\qquad \mathcal{W}_1=k_-e_0+k_+q^{-1}f_0q^{h_0}+\varepsilon_- q^{h_0}.$$

Prove or disprove: the three algebras $\mathcal{A}_q$, $O_q$, and $B$ are mutually isomorphic as associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebras.

Subsequent work by Terwilliger and collaborators (notably "The alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra", arXiv:2103.03028, and "The q-Onsager algebra and its alternating central extension", arXiv:2106.14041, Comm. Math. Phys. 2021) clarified the relation: the current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q$ is the alternating central extension of $O_q$, with an algebra isomorphism $\langle W_0,W_1\rangle\subset\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q$ and a tensor-product factorization $\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q\otimes Z$ where $Z$ is a polynomial center. Thus $O_q$ embeds in $\mathcal{A}_q$ but the two are not isomorphic; $\mathcal{A}_q$ is strictly larger. The isomorphism of $O_q$ with the coideal subalgebra image is established in Baseilhac–Belliard and related work. Hence the conjecture as stated is partially resolved (with a negative answer for $\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q$ in the strict sense).

Setup. Let $q$ be a generic nonzero complex parameter and let $\varepsilon_+,\varepsilon_-$ be fixed nonzero scalars. Consider the quantum affine algebra $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i,q^{\pm h_i}$ ($i=0,1$) and standard relations.

(i) Augmented $q$-Onsager algebra $\mathcal{O}_q$. Define $\mathcal{O}_q$ as the unital associative algebra with generators $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ satisfying
- $[K_0,K_1]=0$,
- $K_0 Z_1 K_0^{-1}=q^{2}Z_1$, $K_0\widetilde Z_1K_0^{-1}=q^{-2}\widetilde Z_1$,
- $K_1 Z_1 K_1^{-1}=q^{-2}Z_1$, $K_1\widetilde Z_1K_1^{-1}=q^{2}\widetilde Z_1$,
- the higher $q$-Serre / $q$-commutator relations
$$[Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,\widetilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[Z_1,K_0K_1]\,K_0K_1,\qquad [\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[\widetilde Z_1,K_0K_1]\,K_0K_1,$$
with $\rho=-(q^2-q^{-2})^2$ and $[X,Y]_p:=XY-pYX$.

(ii) Coideal subalgebra $\mathcal{B}\subset U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the subalgebra generated by
$$\varepsilon_+ q^{h_1},\quad \varepsilon_- q^{h_0},\quad (q^2-q^{-2})(\varepsilon_+ q^{-1}e_0 q^{h_1}+\varepsilon_- f_1 q^{h_1+h_0}),\quad (q^2-q^{-2})(\varepsilon_- q^{-1}e_1 q^{h_0}+\varepsilon_+ f_0 q^{h_1+h_0}).$$

(iii) Current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$. Let $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ be the algebra obtained as the quotient of the reflection equation algebra for the $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ $R$-matrix by the diagonal/scalar reduction giving currents with modes $K_k,K_{k+1},Z_{k+1},\widetilde Z_{k+1}$ ($k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$), subject to the relations induced by the reflection equation.

Problem. Prove that there are algebra isomorphisms
$$\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}} \;\cong\; \mathcal{O}_q \;\cong\; \mathcal{B},$$
where the second isomorphism is induced by the assignment in (ii). Furthermore, find explicit polynomial formulas expressing the higher current modes $K_k,K_{k+1},Z_{k+1},\widetilde Z_{k+1}$ of $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ as noncommutative polynomials in the generators $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ of $\mathcal{O}_q$.

representations.normalized:
Let $A_q$ denote the $q$-Onsager algebra, defined as the unital associative algebra over $\mathbb{C}(q)$ generated by two elements $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho [W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho [W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho \in \mathbb{C}(q)$ is fixed.

For each integer $N \geq 1$, on every finite-dimensional irreducible $A_q$-module of "type 1" with diameter $N$, there exist $q$-analogues of Davies' relations: certain explicit polynomials of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0$ and $W_1$ act as zero on the module. Let $A_q^{[2N+1]}$ be the quotient of $A_q$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these universal polynomial relations.

For $N=1$, $A_q^{[3]}$ is isomorphic to the Askey–Wilson algebra $AW(3)$ of Zhedanov, and there is a known algebra homomorphism from $AW(3)$ into the double affine Hecke algebra (DAHA) of type $(C_1^\vee,C_1)$.

Question: For general $N \geq 2$, does there exist an algebra homomorphism from $A_q^{[2N+1]}$ into an algebra that naturally generalizes the double affine Hecke algebra of type $(C_1^\vee, C_1)$?

Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and $q\in\mathbb{F}^\times$ a nonzero scalar that is not a root of unity. The $q$-Onsager algebra $A_q$ is the associative $\mathbb{F}$-algebra with generators $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY-q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho = -(q^2-q^{-2})^2$.

For a fixed positive integer $N$, on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module certain polynomials of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0$ and $W_1$ are known to act as zero. Let $I_{2N+1}\subset A_q$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all such polynomial relations of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0,W_1$ that vanish on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module, and define
$$A_q^{[2N+1]} := A_q / I_{2N+1}.$$

Problem. Classify, up to isomorphism, all finite-dimensional irreducible $A_q^{[2N+1]}$-modules.

Setting. Let $q$ be a nonzero complex parameter that is not a root of unity. The $q$-Onsager algebra $A_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with two generators $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_0,W_1], \qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho = -(q-q^{-1})^2$.

Gasper–Rahman multivariable polynomials. Let $\{P_{n_1,\dots,n_k}(x_1,\dots,x_k)\}$ denote the family of multivariable orthogonal $q$-Racah polynomials of Gasper and Rahman (a multivariable extension of the Askey–Wilson/$q$-Racah scheme). Suppose that, viewed as elements built from $W_0, W_1$ via a fixed substitution, these polynomials yield a linear basis of $A_q$.

Quotient. For an integer $N \ge 1$, let $I_{2N+1} \subset A_q$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all polynomial relations in $W_0, W_1$ of total degree $2N+1$ that act as zero on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module of "level" $2N+1$, and set
$$A_q^{[2N+1]} := A_q / I_{2N+1}.$$

Problem.
(a) Classify, up to isomorphism, the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of $A_q^{[2N+1]}$.
(b) Carry out a detailed study of the finite-dimensional $A_q^{[2N+1]}$-modules naturally associated with the Gasper–Rahman multivariable polynomials: describe their structure, weights/eigenvalues of natural commuting subalgebras, decomposition into irreducibles, and the role played by the Gasper–Rahman polynomials as overlap coefficients between distinguished eigenbases.

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let g be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over k, and let X be a scheme of finite type over k. Let Γ be a finite group acting on X by scheme automorphisms and on g by Lie algebra automorphisms. The associated equivariant map algebra is

  M = M(X, g)^Γ = { f ∈ g ⊗_k 𝒪(X) : (id ⊗ γ*)·f = γ·f for all γ ∈ Γ },

with Lie bracket induced from that of g and pointwise multiplication on 𝒪(X). For an M-module V, let H^1(M, V) denote the first Chevalley–Eilenberg Lie algebra cohomology of M with coefficients in V, which classifies equivalence classes of abelian extensions / outer derivations valued in V.

Problem. Give an explicit description of H^1(M, V) for a general M-module V, in terms of invariants of (X, g, Γ) and of V. In particular:

(a) Specialize to the adjoint module M_ad = M (with action by the Lie bracket) and produce an explicit description of

  H^1(M, M_ad) = Der_k(M) / IDer(M),

the space of outer k-linear derivations of M (where IDer(M) denotes inner derivations).

(b) Extend the result beyond the previously known cases (such as multiloop algebras and locally finite modules) to a uniform statement covering arbitrary M-modules V and arbitrary equivariant map algebras M(X, g)^Γ with g semisimple.

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a positive integer $h$ and a finite subset $A\subseteq G$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA=\{a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\dots,a_h\in A\}\,. $$
For positive integers $m,h$, let
$$\rho(G,m,h)=\min\{|hA| : A\subseteq G,\ |A|=m\}\,. $$
Assume that $m\le p<hm-h+1$. Prove or disprove the following statement: under these hypotheses one has $\rho(G,m,h)=p$, and for every $m$-element subset $A\subseteq G$ the equality $|hA|=p$ holds if and only if $A$ is contained in a coset of some subgroup $H\le G$ of order $p$.

The conjecture appears in Bajnok's compendium of open problems on sumsets in finite abelian groups. Subsequent surveys (including recent ones in 2023–2025) continue to discuss direct and inverse problems for $\rho(G,m,h)$, but no source found in the search definitively establishes a full proof or disproof of the inverse characterization stated above. Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a subset $A \subseteq G$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA = \{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1, \ldots, a_h \in A\}.$$
For positive integers $m, h$ with $1 \le m \le |G|$, let
$$\rho(G, m, h) = \min\{|hA| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}.$$
Consider the boundary case in which $p = hm - h + 1$. In this regime two known families of $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ achieve the minimum value of $|hA|$:
(i) arithmetic progressions of length $m$ in $G$ (i.e., subsets of the form $\{a, a+d, a+2d, \ldots, a+(m-1)d\}$ for some $a, d \in G$);
(ii) $m$-element subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of $G$ of order $p$.

Problem: Classify completely all $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ for which $|hA|$ equals the minimum value $\rho(G, m, h)$ when $p = hm - h + 1$. In particular, determine all extremal configurations beyond the two families (i) and (ii).

Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting by Lie algebra automorphisms on $\mathfrak{g}$ and by scheme automorphisms on $X$. Form the equivariant map algebra
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma} = \{\,\alpha \in \mathfrak{g}\otimes_k \mathcal{O}(X) : (\gamma\cdot \alpha) = \alpha \text{ for all } \gamma\in\Gamma\,\},$$
viewed as a Lie algebra under the pointwise bracket, where $\Gamma$ acts diagonally on $\mathfrak{g}\otimes \mathcal{O}(X)$.

For an $M$-module $V$, let $H_*(M,V)$ denote the Chevalley–Eilenberg homology of $M$ with coefficients in $V$.

(a) Compute the homology groups $H_*(M,V)$ for general pairs $(M,V)$ of equivariant map algebras and modules; in particular, identify the structure of these homology groups in terms of the data $(\mathfrak{g}, X, \Gamma)$.

(b) Compute the abelianization $H_0(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}}) = M/[M,M]$, where $M_{\mathrm{ad}}$ denotes $M$ acting on itself by the adjoint action.

(c) Use (b) to characterize, in terms of $(\mathfrak{g}, X, \Gamma)$, exactly which equivariant map algebras $M$ are perfect (i.e. satisfy $[M,M] = M$).

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Partial results are known: the abelianization $H_0(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}}) = M/[M,M]$ has been computed in several cases, leading to classifications of perfect equivariant map algebras (work of Neher–Savage and collaborators). $$\hat{\rho}(G, m, h) = \min\{\, |h^{\wedge} A| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\,\}.$$
Assume $h < m \le p$. Prove or disprove:
$$\hat{\rho}(G, m, h) = \min\{\, p,\ hm - h^2 + 1\,\}.$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

For cyclic groups of prime order, the formula follows from the Dias da Silva–Hamidoune theorem (1994). For general finite abelian groups with $h<m\le p$ (smallest prime divisor of $|G|$), the equality is stated as a conjecture in Bajnok's work on restricted sumsets, and recent literature on critical numbers and restricted sumsets does not report a full proof for arbitrary finite abelian groups; only partial/related results and tight upper bounds are available. $$h^{\wedge} A \;=\; \{\, a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1, \ldots, a_h \in A \text{ are pairwise distinct}\,\}.$$
Fix integers $m \ge 4$ and $h$ with $2 \le h \le m-2$, and assume that $p > hm - h^2 + 1$. It is known that under these hypotheses every $m$-element subset $A \subseteq G$ satisfies $|h^{\wedge} A| \ge hm - h^2 + 1$. \begin{enumerate}

\item $A$ is an arithmetic progression in $G$, i.e., $A = \{a,\; a+d,\; a+2d,\; \ldots,\; a+(m-1)d\}$ for some $a, d \in G$.
\end{enumerate}

For a finite abelian group G and a positive integer h, define the restricted h-fold sumset of a subset A ⊆ G by
  h^∧ A = { a_1 + a_2 + ⋯ + a_h : a_1, …, a_h ∈ A, a_i ≠ a_j for i ≠ j },
and define the restricted h-critical number χ̂(G, h) to be the smallest positive integer m such that h^∧ A = G for every subset A ⊆ G with |A| = m (when such an m exists).

Take G = Z_n, the cyclic group of order n, and h = 3. Determine whether the following equalities hold for all n ≥ 16:

(1) If n has at least one prime divisor congruent to 2 (mod 3), and p denotes the smallest such prime divisor, then
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 3   if n = p,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 2   if n = 3p,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 1   otherwise.

(2) If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 (mod 3), then
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = ⌊n/3⌋ + 4   if 9 | n,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = ⌊n/3⌋ + 3   otherwise.

The corresponding inequalities "≥" are known to hold; the question is whether equality always holds.

Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the space of Dirichlet polynomials, i.e., finite sums $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ with complex coefficients $a_n$. For $1\le p<\infty$, the Hardy space $\mathcal H^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of $\mathscr{D}$ with respect to the norm
$$\|F\|_{\mathcal H^p}^p \;=\; \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt,$$
which, via the Bohr lift $n^{-s}\mapsto z^{\kappa(n)}$ (where $\kappa(n)$ is the multi-index of prime exponents of $n$), is isometrically identified with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional torus.

Fix a real number $L>0$. The question is the following:

For which $p\in[1,\infty)$ does there exist a constant $C_{p,L}>0$, depending only on $p$ and $L$, such that the inequality
$$\int_I \Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-1/2 - it}\Big|^p\,dt \;\le\; C_{p,L}\,\|F\|_{\mathcal H^p}^p$$
holds for every Dirichlet polynomial $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ (with $N\ge 1$ arbitrary and coefficients arbitrary) and for every interval $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ of length $L$ on the critical line $\operatorname{Re} s=1/2$?

Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the space of Dirichlet series $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$. For $0<p<\infty$, define the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series as the completion of the set of Dirichlet polynomials $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm

Every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ defines a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

A positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ is called a Carleson measure for $\mathcal{H}^p$ if there exists a constant $C>0$ such that
$$\int_{\mathbb{C}_{1/2}} |F(s)|^p\,d\mu(s) \;\le\; C\,\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}^p \qquad \text{for every } F\in\mathcal{H}^p.$$

Problem: For $0<p<2$, give an intrinsic geometric or capacitary characterization of all positive Borel measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ that are Carleson measures for $\mathcal{H}^p$.

Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD) processes at present-day high-energy hadron and nuclear colliders that probe partons carrying a small longitudinal momentum fraction x of their parent hadron and having transverse momentum k_T of the order of the saturation scale Q_s(x). Here "parton saturation" denotes the weakly coupled nonlinear QCD regime expected to set in when gluon densities at small x become so large that nonlinear effects (such as gluon recombination) balance linear BFKL-type growth, and Q_s(x) is the momentum scale separating the dense (k_T ≲ Q_s) from the dilute (k_T ≫ Q_s) regime, with Q_s(x) increasing as x decreases. The Color Glass Condensate (CGC) is the effective field theory implementation of this nonlinear saturation regime.

Question: Is it necessary, at currently accessible collider energies, to use the nonlinear CGC/saturation framework to describe QCD data in the kinematic region x ≪ 1, k_T ∼ Q_s(x)? Equivalently: can the relevant observables in this regime be adequately described instead by purely linear (collinear or k_T-factorized) gluon distributions supplemented by an ad hoc non-perturbative infrared cutoff, or does an adequate description of the data require properly incorporating the nonlinear dynamics at k_T ∼ Q_s(x)?

The task is to determine, on the basis of comparison with collider data, whether nonlinear saturation dynamics is unavoidable for a satisfactory phenomenological description, or whether linear-evolution descriptions with a tunable infrared cutoff suffice.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether nonlinear saturation/CGC dynamics is strictly necessary at current colliders, as opposed to linear gluon distributions with an ad hoc infrared cutoff, remains an active phenomenological question. Recent work (e.g. NLO CGC phenomenology with threshold resummation for forward hadron production at RHIC/LHC, and CMS observations of long-range two-particle correlations in p–Pb collisions) provides increasingly suggestive but not yet conclusive evidence for saturation. For $0<p<\infty$, let $\mathcal{H}^p$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series, defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm
$$\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T} |F(it)|^p \, dt\right)^{1/p}.$$
Equivalently, via Bohr's correspondence $n^{-s} \mapsto z^{\kappa(n)}$ (where $\kappa(n)$ is the multi-index of prime exponents of $n$), $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometrically identified with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional polytorus. Each $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ defines a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

Recall that a holomorphic function $f$ on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}$ is said to belong locally to the Nevanlinna class if for every relatively compact subdomain $U\Subset\Omega$ with smooth boundary,
$$\sup_{r}\int_{\partial U_r} \log^+ |f(z)|\, |dz| < \infty,$$
where $\{U_r\}$ is an exhaustion of $U$; equivalently, $\log^+|f|$ has a positive harmonic majorant on every relatively compact subdomain of $\Omega$.

Question: For every $p<2$ and every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$, does $F$ belong locally to the Nevanlinna class on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$?

For a real number $p\in[1,\infty)$, let $\mathcal{H}^p$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series defined as follows. For a Dirichlet polynomial $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$, set
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \lim_{T\to\infty}\Big(\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt\Big)^{1/p},$$
and define $\mathcal{H}^p$ as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials in this norm. Equivalently, via the Bohr lift $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}p_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots\mapsto z_1^{\alpha_1}z_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometrically isomorphic to the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus equipped with normalized Haar measure.

A Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of a Banach space $X$ is called unconditional if for every $x\in X$ with expansion $x=\sum_n c_n e_n$, the series converges unconditionally (equivalently, $\sum_n \varepsilon_n c_n e_n$ converges in $X$ for every choice of signs $\varepsilon_n\in\{-1,+1\}$).

Question: For every $p\in(1,\infty)$ with $p\neq 2$, does the Banach space $\mathcal{H}^p$ admit an unconditional Schauder basis?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series admits an unconditional basis for $p\in(1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$ appears to remain open. It is known that the canonical Dirichlet monomial basis $\{n^{-s}\}$ is unconditional in $\mathcal{H}^p$ only for $p=2$, but the existence of some other unconditional basis is unresolved. representations.normalized:
In the framework of small-$x$ QCD evolution for high-energy nuclear collisions, the running-coupling Balitsky–Kovchegov (rcBK) equation governs the nonlinear evolution of the dipole scattering amplitude $N(r,x)$ in the saturation regime, while DGLAP evolution governs the linear, leading-twist regime at large transverse momentum $p_T \gg Q_s(x)$, where $Q_s(x)$ is the saturation scale. The nuclear modification factor for proton–nucleus collisions is defined as
$$R_{pA}(p_T,y) = \frac{1}{A}\,\frac{d^2N_{pA}/dp_T\,dy}{d^2N_{pp}/dp_T\,dy},$$
which by collinear-factorization expectations should approach unity for $p_T \gg Q_s$. Current rcBK-based predictions, however, do not embed the DGLAP limit and yield $R_{pA}\to 1$ only at unrealistically large $p_T$, especially at forward rapidities where small-$x$ evolution has acted.

Determine, within QCD, the dynamics and rate of the transition from the nonlinear saturation regime to the high-$p_T$ leading-twist DGLAP regime. Specifically:

(i) Construct a small-$x$ evolution scheme for the unintegrated gluon distribution (or dipole amplitude) that simultaneously reduces to rcBK in the saturation regime ($p_T \lesssim Q_s$) and to DGLAP evolution in the leading-twist regime ($p_T \gg Q_s$), with a controlled matching at intermediate $p_T$.

(ii) Quantify, in this scheme, how rapidly $R_{pA}(p_T,y)\to 1$ as $p_T$ grows above $Q_s(x)$, identifying the parametric dependence of the transition scale on $x$ (or rapidity $y$), $A$, and the strong coupling $\alpha_s$.

(iii) Show that the resulting predictions are consistent with proton–nucleus collider data and, where available, electron–nucleus deep-inelastic scattering data.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent literature confirms that the precise matching between nonlinear (rcBK/JIMWLK) small-$x$ evolution and linear DGLAP leading-twist evolution remains phenomenologically unsettled: theoretical arguments only establish each framework in its asymptotic limit, and the intermediate-$(x,Q^2)$ kinematics relevant to $R_{pA}$ at the LHC is still unclear. Various DGLAP-improved saturation models (e.g., color-dipole DGLAP-improved fits) and unified evolution proposals exist, but no consensus solution embeds DGLAP into rcBK so that $R_{pA}\to 1$ at realistic $p_T$.

representations.normalized:
In the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory of small-x QCD, a large nucleus at high energy is characterized by a transverse-position-dependent gluon distribution and a local saturation scale Q_s(x, b), where x is the longitudinal momentum fraction and b is the transverse impact parameter relative to the nuclear center. A common phenomenological prescription is to model the nucleus as an ensemble of independent CGC sources distributed in the transverse plane according to a Woods–Saxon profile

  ρ(r) = ρ_0 / (1 + exp((r - R)/a)),

and to evolve the gluon density at each impact parameter b independently in x via small-x evolution equations (e.g., the JIMWLK or BK equations), with no transverse coupling between different b.

Determine, from first principles in QCD at high parton density:

(a) the correct functional dependence of the nuclear gluon density xG_A(x, b) and of the saturation scale Q_s,A(x, b) on the transverse impact parameter b in a large nucleus at small x;

(b) whether the prescription of treating the nucleus as a Woods–Saxon distribution of independent CGC sources with b-independent (locally evolved) small-x evolution provides a conceptually accurate description of the transverse structure of nuclei at small x, or whether non-trivial transverse correlations and/or coupling between different impact parameters during small-x evolution must be included for a correct description.

The impact-parameter dependence of the nuclear gluon density and saturation scale remains a central open non-perturbative input in CGC phenomenology. While impact-parameter dependent dipole and b-CGC models have been developed and refined, and exclusive processes at the future Electron-Ion Collider are being designed precisely to image the transverse small-x structure of nuclei, no first-principles determination has been established and the question of whether independent-b evolution of Woods–Saxon-distributed CGC sources is conceptually sufficient is still under active investigation.

The canonical system $\{n^{-s}\}$ is known to be a Schauder basis of $H^p$ for $1<p<\infty$ and only a Markushevich basis (not Schauder) for $H^1$; it is unconditional only when $p=2$. Let $\mathbb{D}^\infty = \{ z = (z_1, z_2, \ldots) : z_j \in \mathbb{C},\ |z_j| < 1 \text{ for all } j,\ \sup_j |z_j| < 1 \}$ be the infinite polydisc, and let $\mathbb{T}^\infty = \prod_{j=1}^\infty \{ |w_j| = 1 \}$ be the infinite-dimensional torus, equipped with the product Haar (Lebesgue) measure $m_\infty$. For $1 \le p \le \infty$, let $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ denote the Hardy space defined as the closure in $L^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty, m_\infty)$ of the analytic trigonometric polynomials (those whose Fourier coefficients are supported on multi-indices $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ with $\alpha_j \ge 0$ for all $j$). Each $f \in H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ corresponds to an analytic function $\widetilde{f}$ on $\mathbb{D}^\infty$ (defined for instance on $\bigcup_{0<r<1} r\,\mathbb{D}^\infty$ via its monomial expansion), and $f$ is recovered as a boundary value of $\widetilde{f}$.

For a point $w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty$, an "approach family" to $w$ is a family $\{A_w\}_{w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty}$ of subsets $A_w \subset \mathbb{D}^\infty$ accumulating at $w$ (e.g., the radial approach $\{rw : 0 < r < 1\}$, or some non-tangential analogue).

Problem. Determine general conditions on such an approach family $\{A_w\}_{w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty}$ — radial or non-tangential — under which a Fatou-type theorem holds: namely, for every $f \in H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ and for $m_\infty$-almost every $w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty$, the limit
$$\lim_{\substack{z \to w \\ z \in A_w}} \widetilde{f}(z)$$
exists and equals $f(w)$.
