The problem of identifying general radial or non-tangential approach regions yielding a.e. boundary limits for $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ functions remains a delicate one. Aleman, Olsen, and Saksman (Journal d'Analyse Mathématique, 2019) established several Fatou-type theorems for restricted modes of radial convergence and showed that the pointwise Fatou theorem fails in infinite dimensions without such restrictions even for bounded analytic functions. No comprehensive characterization of admissible radial/non-tangential approaches has been found in subsequent literature, so the problem appears to remain open in its general form, with only partial results.

representations.normalized:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the dynamics of hadrons probed at very small Bjorken-x is governed by a high-density system of gluons. In this regime, nonlinear gluon recombination effects balance linear gluon emission, leading to the phenomenon of parton saturation, characterized by a dynamically generated saturation scale Q_s(x) that grows as x decreases. When Q_s is large compared to Lambda_QCD, the strong coupling alpha_s(Q_s) is small, so the saturated gluon system can be described as a weakly coupled but highly nonlinear many-body system (e.g., via the Color Glass Condensate effective theory, the JIMWLK/BK evolution equations, and classical Yang-Mills fields as the relevant degrees of freedom). At the opposite extreme, when momentum scales approach Lambda_QCD, QCD becomes strongly coupled and exhibits color confinement, with hadrons rather than gluons as the appropriate degrees of freedom.

Provide a quantitative theoretical description of how QCD interpolates between these two regimes. Specifically:

(a) Determine how the small-x, high-density (saturation) description of hadronic matter, formulated in terms of weakly coupled nonlinear classical color fields, evolves into the confining regime of QCD as the saturation scale Q_s is decreased toward Lambda_QCD.

(b) In particular, characterize whether classical color fields remain the correct effective degrees of freedom throughout the transition, determine whether and how the QCD coupling should be taken to run with Q_s in this crossover, and describe the universality properties (if any) of observables in the transition region.

The strong coupling α_s(μ) of QCD depends on a renormalization scale μ via the QCD β-function, and in many small-x evolution equations (e.g., the Balitsky–Kovchegov and JIMWLK equations) the choice of the scale at which α_s is evaluated is not uniquely fixed by the leading-order formalism.\n\nDetermine whether, in the saturation regime at small x, the appropriate renormalization scale for the running QCD coupling is set by the saturation scale Q_s(x) itself. For a Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$, recall the following construction. By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, each integer $n\ge 1$ factors uniquely as $n=p_1^{\kappa_1}p_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots$ where $p_1<p_2<\cdots$ are the primes. The Bohr correspondence assigns to $f$ the formal power series $\mathcal{B}f(z)=\sum_n a_n z^{\kappa(n)}$ in infinitely many variables $z=(z_1,z_2,\dots)$, where $z^{\kappa(n)}=z_1^{\kappa_1}z_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots$. For $0<p<\infty$, the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm (quasi-norm when $0<p<1$)
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\int_{\mathbb{T}^\infty} |\mathcal{B}f(z)|^p\, dm_\infty(z)\right)^{1/p},$$
where $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ is the infinite-dimensional torus and $m_\infty$ is its normalized Haar measure. Equivalently (by the Birkhoff ergodic theorem), $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}^p = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T |f(it)|^p\,dt$ for Dirichlet polynomials.

For $1<p<\infty$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is a reflexive Banach space, but for $0<p\le 1$ — and especially in the non-locally-convex range $0<p<1$ — the structure of the topological dual is far less understood.

Problem. Describe the dual space $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ for $0<p<1$. That is, characterize all continuous linear functionals on $\mathcal{H}^p$ and provide an explicit, usable concrete representation of them (for instance, as a space of Dirichlet series or via pairings with such, together with a norm or quasi-norm equivalent to the dual norm).

Subsequent literature on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (e.g., works on linear space properties of $\mathcal{H}^p$, multipliers, and Volterra operators) continues to investigate functionals on $\mathcal{H}^p$ for $0<p\le 1$ — for instance establishing that $\varphi_\beta(s)=\sum n^{-\beta-s}$ defines a bounded functional on $\mathcal{H}^p$ when $\beta>1/p$ and not when $\beta<1/p$, and conjecturing the boundary case. However, no full description of $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ for $0<p<1$ appears in the literature; the problem is referenced as still open in recent surveys and papers.

representations.normalized:
Let $\mathbb{T}^\infty = \prod_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{T}$ denote the infinite-dimensional torus equipped with its normalized Haar measure. For a multi-index $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ (finitely supported integer sequences), let $z^\alpha = \prod_n z_n^{\alpha_n}$ denote the corresponding character. Define the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ as the closed subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ spanned by $\{z^\alpha : \alpha \ge 0\}$ (i.e., $\alpha_n \ge 0$ for all $n$), and let $P_+ : L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty) \to H^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ be the orthogonal Riesz projection. For an analytic symbol $\psi = \sum_{\alpha \ge 0} \hat\psi(\alpha) z^\alpha$, the (small) Hankel form is defined on finite analytic polynomials by
$$H_\psi(f,g) = \sum_{\alpha,\beta \ge 0} \hat\psi(\alpha+\beta)\, \hat f(\alpha)\, \hat g(\beta),$$
with norm $\|H_\psi\|$ as a bilinear form on $H^2 \times H^2$.

Nehari's classical theorem on $\mathbb{T}$ states that $H_\psi$ is bounded if and only if $\psi = P_+\varphi$ for some $\varphi \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T})$, with $\|H_\psi\| \asymp \inf\{\|\varphi\|_\infty : P_+\varphi = \psi\}$.

Problem: Formulate and establish the appropriate counterpart of Nehari's theorem on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$. Specifically, characterize intrinsically the space $P_+(L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty))$ — the Riesz projection of $L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ — and identify natural BMO-type spaces on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ that govern the boundedness of Hankel forms / small Hankel operators in this infinite-dimensional setting.

Searches indicate this remains an open problem. The classical Nehari theorem holds on finite polydisks $\mathbb{T}^d$ (Ferguson–Lacey for $d=2$, Lacey–Terwilleger for $d>2$), but the constants grow at least exponentially in the dimension (work building on Helson), which precludes a direct passage to $\mathbb{T}^\infty$. representations.normalized:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at high parton densities, hadrons and nuclei are dominated by gluons whose occupation numbers grow until nonlinear interactions balance gluon emission, producing a characteristic saturation momentum scale $Q_s$. In the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework, fast partons are treated as static color sources with random color charge density $\rho^a(x_\perp)$ governed by a weight functional $W_Y[\rho]$ (with rapidity $Y$ evolution given by the JIMWLK equation), while slower gluons are described by classical Yang–Mills fields $A^\mu_a$ obeying $[D_\mu, F^{\mu\nu}]_a = J^\nu_a$ sourced by $\rho^a$. Observables are computed as path integrals $\langle \mathcal{O}\rangle = \int \mathcal{D}\rho\, W_Y[\rho]\, \mathcal{O}[A_{\rm cl}[\rho]]$ together with quantum fluctuations on top of these classical solutions.

Determine whether classical color fields, in the sense above, remain the correct effective degrees of freedom for the strongly correlated many-gluon system of QCD in the saturation regime probed by proton–nucleus and electron–nucleus collisions. Concretely: identify a parametric regime (in terms of $Q_s$, $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$, the strong coupling $\alpha_s(Q_s)$, the atomic number $A$, and the rapidity $Y$) and an observable for which the leading-order classical-field description, supplemented by the standard small-$x$ quantum evolution, either (i) provides a controlled approximation to full QCD with quantifiable corrections, or (ii) demonstrably fails, requiring a different effective description (for instance, one in which the relevant degrees of freedom are not classical fields).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether classical color fields are the correct effective degrees of freedom in saturated QCD is conceptual and remains an active research direction. The CGC effective theory continues to be developed and tested phenomenologically at RHIC and the LHC, and is a central motivation for the Electron-Ion Collider, but no definitive proof of its validity (or its replacement) in the strongly correlated saturation regime has been established. The status is therefore best characterized as open.

representations.normalized:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD), at small Bjorken-x the gluon density inside a hadron grows rapidly and is conjectured to enter a non-linear regime, called parton saturation, characterized by a dynamically generated saturation scale Q_s(x,A) (depending on x and on the nuclear mass number A) at which non-linear gluon recombination balances linear BFKL-type growth, while the strong coupling α_s(Q_s) remains weak. In this regime the small-x gluon system is described as a strongly correlated many-body state, often modeled by classical Yang–Mills color fields (the Color Glass Condensate effective theory) with stochastic color sources.

Formulate and establish the universality properties of this saturation regime. Specifically:

(a) Identify and prove which observables (e.g., dipole scattering amplitudes, unintegrated gluon distributions, multi-parton correlators, n-point Wilson-line correlators) become universal functions of the single combination Q_s(x,A) times a transverse scale, independent of the specific hadronic target (proton vs. nucleus) and of details of the initial non-perturbative input.

(b) Determine the precise sense (geometric scaling, fixed points of the JIMWLK / Balitsky–Kovchegov non-linear evolution equations, scaling solutions of these renormalization-group equations) in which such universality holds, including the dependence on the running of α_s and on impact parameter.

(c) Specify which measurements in proton–nucleus (p+A) and electron–nucleus (e+A) collisions—such as forward single-inclusive hadron production, di-hadron azimuthal correlations, diffractive vector-meson production, inclusive and diffractive deep inelastic structure functions—can isolate and quantitatively test these universality predictions, distinguishing genuine saturation universality from leading-twist collinear-factorization expectations.

(d) Characterize how the saturation regime connects, as Q_s decreases, to the confinement regime, and whether classical color fields remain the correct effective degrees of freedom in that transition.
representations.original:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD), at small Bjorken-x the gluon density inside a hadron grows rapidly and is conjectured to enter a non-linear regime, called parton saturation, characterized by a dynamically generated saturation scale Q_s(x,A) (depending on x and on the nuclear mass number A) at which non-linear gluon recombination balances linear BFKL-type growth, while the strong coupling α_s(Q_s) remains weak. In this regime the small-x gluon system is described as a strongly correlated many-body state, often modeled by classical Yang–Mills color fields (the Color Glass Condensate effective theory) with stochastic color sources.

Formulate and establish the universality properties of this saturation regime. Specifically:

(a) Identify and prove which observables (e.g., dipole scattering amplitudes, unintegrated gluon distributions, multi-parton correlators, n-point Wilson-line correlators) become universal functions of the single combination Q_s(x,A) times a transverse scale, independent of the specific hadronic target (proton vs. nucleus) and of details of the initial non-perturbative input.

(b) Determine the precise sense (geometric scaling, fixed points of the JIMWLK / Balitsky–Kovchegov non-linear evolution equations, scaling solutions of these renormalization-group equations) in which such universality holds, including the dependence on the running of α_s and on impact parameter.

(c) Specify which measurements in proton–nucleus (p+A) and electron–nucleus (e+A) collisions—such as forward single-inclusive hadron production, di-hadron azimuthal correlations, diffractive vector-meson production, inclusive and diffractive deep inelastic structure functions—can isolate and quantitatively test these universality predictions, distinguishing genuine saturation universality from leading-twist collinear-factorization expectations.

(d) Characterize how the saturation regime connects, as Q_s decreases, to the confinement regime, and whether classical color fields remain the correct effective degrees of freedom in that transition.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The universality of the QCD saturation regime and its experimental exploration via p+A and e+A collisions remains an active open research direction. While partial universality results (geometric scaling, BK/JIMWLK fixed-point analyses, CGC factorization theorems for limited classes of observables) have been established, a complete characterization is unresolved and is a central scientific motivation for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), expected to begin operations in the early 2030s.

Let $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ denote the infinite-dimensional torus, equipped with its normalized Haar measure. For $f \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ with Fourier expansion $f(z) = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}} \hat{f}(\alpha) z^\alpha$ (where $\mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ denotes finitely supported integer multi-indices), the Riesz projection $P_+ f$ is defined by
$$P_+ f(z) = \sum_{\alpha \geq 0} \hat{f}(\alpha) z^\alpha,$$
the sum being taken over multi-indices with all nonnegative entries. Via the Bohr correspondence $z_j \leftrightarrow p_j^{-s}$ (where $p_j$ is the $j$-th prime), an analytic function on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ corresponds to a Dirichlet series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$.

Consider the Dirichlet series
$$\phi_0(s) = 1 + \sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{\log n}\, n^{-1/2 - s},$$
which is the analytic symbol of the multiplicative Hilbert matrix $\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{mn}\,\log(mn)}\bigr)_{m,n\geq 2}$.

Question: Does there exist a function $F \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ such that, under the Bohr correspondence, $\phi_0$ corresponds to the analytic projection $P_+ F$?

The problem was posed in connection with the multiplicative Hilbert matrix and its analytic symbol. $$S(r) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{2n}{(n^2 + r^2)^2}, \qquad r > 0.$$

$$\frac{1}{\,r^2 + \tfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{4r^2 + 1}{12(r^2 + a)}\,} \;<\; S(r) \;<\; \frac{1}{\,r^2 + \tfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{4r^2 + 1}{12(r^2 + b)}\,}$$
holds for every $r > 0$. (Necessary conditions $a \le 3/2$ and $b \ge 1/4$ are known.)

Let $\mathscr{H}^2$ denote the Hilbert space of Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$ with square-summable coefficients, equipped with the norm $\|f\|_{\mathscr{H}^2}^2=\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|^2$. By a theorem of Gordon and Hedenmalm, an analytic function $\varphi:\mathbb{C}_{1/2}\to\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ (where $\mathbb{C}_\theta=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>\theta\}$) induces a bounded composition operator $C_\varphi f = f\circ\varphi$ on $\mathscr{H}^2$ if and only if $\varphi$ admits a representation
$$\varphi(s) = c_0 s + \sum_{n=1}^\infty c_n n^{-s},$$
with $c_0\in\mathbb{N}_0$ a non-negative integer, the Dirichlet series $\sum_n c_n n^{-s}$ converges uniformly in $\mathbb{C}_\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and either (a) $c_0\geq 1$ and $\varphi$ maps $\mathbb{C}_0$ into $\mathbb{C}_0$, or (b) $c_0=0$ and $\varphi$ maps $\mathbb{C}_0$ into $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$.

Problem: Give a complete characterization of those symbols $\varphi$ in the Gordon–Hedenmalm class for which the composition operator $C_\varphi:\mathscr{H}^2\to\mathscr{H}^2$ is compact.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Brevig and Perfekt (Advances in Mathematics 385 (2021), 107775; arXiv:2005.05094) introduced a mean counting function for Dirichlet series and characterized the compact composition operators with Dirichlet series symbols on $\mathscr{H}^2$: $C_\varphi$ is compact iff the mean counting function of $\varphi$ satisfies a specified decay condition at the boundary of the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$. This resolves the characterization problem in the Gordon–Hedenmalm class.

Consider inclusive deep inelastic scattering of electrons off a nucleus A, e + A → e + X, whose total virtual-photon–nucleus cross section is determined by the two structure functions F2(x, Q^2) and FL(x, Q^2). These provide access, respectively, to the integrated quark and gluon distributions of the nucleus at small Bjorken x and photon virtuality Q^2.

Two theoretical descriptions are considered:

(i) A nonlinear small-x description in which the dipole–nucleus scattering amplitude evolves according to the running-coupling Balitsky–Kovchegov (rcBK) equation,
    ∂_Y N(r, Y) = ∫ d^2 r1 K_rc(r, r1, r2) [N(r1, Y) + N(r2, Y) − N(r, Y) − N(r1, Y) N(r2, Y)],
where r = r1 + r2, Y = ln(1/x), and K_rc is the Balitsky running-coupling kernel; this approach implements gluon saturation with a nuclear saturation scale Q_s,A^2(x).

(ii) A linear collinear-factorization description using the EPS09 nuclear parton distribution functions at next-to-leading order, in which F2 and FL are obtained from convolutions of nuclear quark and gluon PDFs with the standard DIS coefficient functions.

Assume that, at sufficiently small x and moderate Q^2, the rcBK framework correctly predicts the nuclear-to-proton ratios F2^A/F2^p (and the corresponding FL ratio), with saturation effects setting in at the rcBK-predicted values of Q_s,A^2(x).

Question. In the kinematic regime where the rcBK prediction implies the onset of saturation, can the linear EPS09 nuclear PDF framework be tuned, within its uncertainty bands, to simultaneously reproduce both the F2 and FL electron–nucleus data that are consistent with the rcBK prediction? If no choice of nuclear PDFs within the EPS09 (linear DGLAP) framework can describe F2 and FL simultaneously under these conditions, then the rcBK-based nonlinear description provides the unique consistent data description; determine whether such a simultaneous linear description is possible.

Consider inclusive deep inelastic scattering of electrons on nuclei (e+A DIS), in which the virtual-photon–nucleus cross section is decomposed into the inclusive structure function F_2(x,Q^2) and the longitudinal structure function F_L(x,Q^2), with x the Bjorken variable and Q^2 the photon virtuality. At small x, two competing theoretical descriptions of QCD evolution are available: (i) linear evolution, governed by DGLAP and/or BFKL equations, in which gluon densities grow without bound; and (ii) nonlinear evolution, governed by equations of the Balitsky–Kovchegov / JIMWLK type, which include gluon recombination and lead to saturation of the gluon density at a scale Q_s(x,A).

At a proposed Electron–Ion Collider (EIC) operating with electron–nucleus collisions in a kinematic regime that probes small x and moderate Q^2, with the capability of an e+A collision energy scan needed to extract F_L via the Rosenbluth-type separation, determine whether combined precision measurements of F_2(x,Q^2) and F_L(x,Q^2) over the accessible (x,Q^2) range have sufficient discriminating power to distinguish predictions of linear QCD evolution from those of nonlinear (saturation-based) QCD evolution. In particular, quantify the predicted relative differences ΔF_2/F_2 and ΔF_L/F_L between the two frameworks (after matching them in a control region where both are expected to be reliable) as functions of x, Q^2, and nuclear mass number A, and determine whether these differences exceed the projected combined experimental and theoretical uncertainties at the EIC, as is expected to be the case at the Large Hadron electron Collider (LHeC).

Recent phenomenological studies (e.g., Phys. Rev. D 105, 114017 (2022) and follow-up work) have computed F_2 and F_L within both linear collinear-factorization frameworks and nonlinear BK-based frameworks matched in a common region, finding that at EIC kinematics deviations in F_2 remain at the few-percent level while deviations in F_L can reach roughly 10%, indicating that F_L provides meaningful but not yet conclusive discriminating power. For a complex variable $s$, consider the ordinary Dirichlet polynomial
$$D_N(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} n^{-s}.$$
Let $H^1$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series, defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials with respect to the norm
$$\Big\|\sum_{n} a_n n^{-s}\Big\|_{H^1} = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n} a_n n^{-it}\Big|\,dt,$$
or equivalently, via the Bohr lift, as the $L^1$-norm on the infinite-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ of the corresponding multiplicative Fourier series. Equivalently, via Bohr's correspondence,
$$\|D_N\|_{H^1} \;=\; \mathbb{E}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(n)\Big|,$$
where $f$ is the Steinhaus random multiplicative function (i.e., $f(p)$ for primes $p$ are independent random variables uniformly distributed on the unit circle, extended completely multiplicatively).

Determine whether
$$\|D_N\|_{H^1} \;=\; o(\sqrt{N})\qquad \text{as } N\to\infty.$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Helson's problem was resolved affirmatively by A. J. Harper, who proved that $\mathbb{E}|\sum_{n\le N} f(n)| \asymp \sqrt{N}/(\log\log N)^{1/4}$ for the Steinhaus random multiplicative function $f$, which is equivalent (via Bohr lift) to $\|\sum_{n=1}^N n^{-s}\|_{H^1} \asymp \sqrt{N}/(\log\log N)^{1/4} = o(\sqrt{N})$. A short alternative proof was given by Gorodetsky (2024/2025).

For an integer N≥1 and integer m≥1, an m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomial of length N is a finite Dirichlet series of the form
   P(s) = Σ_{n≤N, Ω(n)=m} a_n n^{-s},
where Ω(n) denotes the number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity, and (a_n) are complex coefficients. For q≥1, define the L^q norm by
   ‖P‖_q = ( lim_{T→∞} (1/T) ∫_0^T |P(it)|^q dt )^{1/q}.
By orthogonality, ‖P‖_2^2 = Σ |a_n|^2.

Fix an integer k>1. Determine the range of m = m(N) (as N→∞) for which there exists a constant C = C(k) (independent of N and of the coefficients) such that
   ‖P‖_{2k} ≤ C ‖P‖_2
holds for every m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomial P of length N. Equivalently, characterize those m=m(N) for which the L^{2k} and L^2 norms are comparable on the space of m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials of length N.

representations.normalization_method: unicode-preserving newline and trailing-whitespace normalization v1
representations.normalized:
Consider exclusive diffractive vector-meson production in electron–nucleus scattering, e + A → e' + V + A', where V is a vector meson (e.g., J/ψ or φ), or, when the produced particle is a real photon, deeply virtual Compton scattering e + A → e' + γ + A'. Let t denote the square of the four-momentum transferred to the nuclear target. The coherent component of the cross section, in which the nucleus remains intact, is related by a two-dimensional Fourier transform in the transverse momentum to the spatial distribution (and correlations) of partons in the transverse plane of the nucleus. The incoherent component, in which the nucleus breaks up into its constituent nucleons, contributes a background that grows relative to the coherent signal at moderate and large |t|, and tends to obscure the diffractive minima and secondary maxima of dσ_coh/dt.

For diffractive J/ψ and φ production off a heavy nucleus such as gold, determine whether there exists an experimentally realizable procedure (for instance, vetoing on emitted nucleons, neutrons, or nuclear fragments, or otherwise tagging nuclear breakup) that suppresses the incoherent diffractive contribution to a level small enough, over the relevant range of |t|, that the first diffractive minimum and the subsequent maximum of the coherent t-distribution can be cleanly resolved. If such a procedure exists, quantify the required rejection efficiency, and demonstrate that the resulting measurement permits the extraction, via Fourier transformation in t, of the transverse spatial distribution and parton–parton transverse correlations in the nucleus.

The question concerns whether incoherent nuclear-breakup background can be suppressed enough at a future electron-ion collider to expose the first diffractive minimum/maximum in coherent J/ψ (and φ) production off heavy nuclei. EIC Yellow Report studies and subsequent simulations (e.g., using BeAGLE and zero-degree-calorimeter / forward-neutron vetoing) indicate this is considered feasible in principle, with rejection at the 1–2% level needed; however a definitive experimental demonstration awaits EIC operations, so the question remains open as of the present.

Let $\mathscr{P}$ denote the space of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$, where $s$ is a complex variable. For $0<p<\infty$, define the Hardy space norm
$$\|f\|_{H^p} \;=\; \left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T\Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p},$$
which makes $\mathscr{P}$ into a normed space whose completion is the Hardy space $H^p$ of Dirichlet series.

For each integer $N\ge 1$, consider the critically weighted Dirichlet polynomial
$$Z_N(s) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^N \frac{1}{n^{1/2+s}}.$$

Determine, for every exponent $0<p\le 1$, the precise asymptotic behavior of $\|Z_N\|_{H^p}$ as $N\to\infty$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A search of the recent literature on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (work of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman, Seip and collaborators, including subsequent papers on linear-space properties of $H^p$, contractive inequalities, and almost-periodic Hardy–Stein identities) does not turn up a determination of the asymptotics of $\|\sum_{n\le N} n^{-1/2-s}\|_{H^p}$ for $0<p\le 1$. The question is closely related to Helson-type problems on $H^1$ norms of partial sums of $\zeta$ on the critical line, which remain unresolved. No source surveyed reports a solution, so the problem appears to be still open.

For $0<p<\infty$, the Hardy space $H^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm
\[
\|f\|_{H^p} := \left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|f(it)|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p},
\]
equivalently realized via the Bohr correspondence as the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus.

Let $d(n)=\sum_{k\mid n}1$ denote the classical divisor function, and fix a real parameter $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$. For each integer $N\ge 1$, consider the weighted Dirichlet polynomial
\[
F_{N,\gamma}(s) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^{N} \bigl[d(n)\bigr]^{\gamma}\, n^{-1/2-s}.
\]

Determine, for every $0<p\le 1$, the precise asymptotic growth of $\|F_{N,\gamma}\|_{H^p}$ as $N\to\infty$, as a function of $N$, $\gamma$, and $p$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

For 1 < p < ∞, Helson's classical theorem gives boundedness of S_N on H^p. For p ∈ (0,1] and p = ∞, only upper and lower bounds are known (e.g. work of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman, Seip and others, supplementing Helson's result), with no matching precise asymptotic. Recent literature continues to refer to the exact asymptotic growth as an open problem.

representations.normalized: Let $\{\chi(p)\}_{p\text{ prime}}$ be a family of independent and identically distributed random variables, each uniformly distributed on the unit circle $\mathbb{T}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|=1\}$. Extend $\chi$ to a completely multiplicative function on the positive integers by setting $\chi(1)=1$ and, for $n=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_\ell^{k_\ell}$ with distinct primes $p_j$, $\chi(n)=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell}\chi(p_j)^{k_j}$. (This is the Steinhaus random multiplicative function.) Define the partial sums $S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\chi(n)$. Determine the almost sure growth rate of $|S_N|$ as $N\to\infty$; that is, find a deterministic function $\psi(N)$ such that $|S_N|/\psi(N)$ has a finite, nonzero (almost sure) limsup behavior, and quantify both the almost sure upper and lower asymptotic envelopes of $S_N$.

Extend $\chi$ to a completely multiplicative function on the positive integers by setting $\chi(1)=1$ and, for $n=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_\ell^{k_\ell}$ with distinct primes $p_j$, $\chi(n)=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell}\chi(p_j)^{k_j}$. (This is the Steinhaus random multiplicative function.) Define the partial sums $S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\chi(n)$. Determine the almost sure growth rate of $|S_N|$ as $N\to\infty$; that is, find a deterministic function $\psi(N)$ such that $|S_N|/\psi(N)$ has a finite, nonzero (almost sure) limsup behavior, and quantify both the almost sure upper and lower asymptotic envelopes of $S_N$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The exact almost sure growth rate remains undetermined. Harper (2020, IMRN 2023) proved that almost surely there exist arbitrarily large $x$ with $|\sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)|\ge \sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+o(1)}$, the first lower bound exceeding $\sqrt{x}$, and conjectured the exponent $1/4$ is sharp. Subsequent work (Caich 2023, and others on related models) has narrowed upper bounds toward $\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{C}$ but a matching tight almost sure asymptotic has not been established, so the problem is partially solved.

representations.normalized:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions (such as Au+Au at RHIC or Pb+Pb at the LHC), the early-time configuration of energy/entropy density deposited in the transverse plane—the "initial state"—fluctuates event by event due to nucleon positions, sub-nucleonic structure, and color-charge fluctuations. This initial state is then evolved by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics and hadronic transport to produce final-state observables such as the azimuthal flow harmonics v_n (Fourier coefficients of the single-particle azimuthal distribution) and multi-particle azimuthal correlations.

Formulate and identify the best physical model for this fluctuating initial state. Concretely:

(a) Within the broad space of candidate frameworks—including independent-nucleon Glauber Monte Carlo models, constituent-quark/sub-nucleonic Glauber variants, Color Glass Condensate–based descriptions (e.g., KLN, MC-KLN, IP-Glasma), parametric ansätze interpolating between wounded-nucleon and binary-collision scaling (e.g., reduced-thickness/TRENTo-type entropy depositions), and saturation-based pQCD minijet approaches (e.g., EKRT)—determine which choice of geometry, fluctuation spectrum, and entropy/energy deposition rule best reproduces measured observables across collision systems and energies.

(b) Quantify what constraints currently available flow data—including the centrality dependence of v_2, v_3, v_4, …, event-by-event v_n distributions, event-plane correlations, two- and multi-particle cumulants, and transverse-momentum-dependent correlations—place on (i) the eccentricity spectrum {ε_n} of the initial state, (ii) the granularity/correlation length of fluctuations, and (iii) the parameters (e.g., entropy-deposition exponent, nucleon width, sub-nucleonic structure) of such models, when convolved with viscous hydrodynamic response.

State the best-fitting model and the resulting allowed region of its parameters.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of identifying the best model of the fluctuating initial state in heavy-ion collisions, and of fully constraining it from flow and correlation data, remains an active research area. Bayesian inference studies (e.g., using TRENTo + viscous hydrodynamics) have substantially narrowed the allowed parameter space, and newer frameworks (IP-Glasma, MC-EKRT, sub-nucleonic Glauber) continue to be proposed and tested at Quark Matter 2025. No single model has been established as definitively "best"; multiple candidates remain compatible with data within current uncertainties, so the problem is partially constrained but still open.

Consider a relativistic heavy-ion collision modeled as follows. At an early proper time τ₀ after impact, the transverse energy-density profile e(x,y) of the produced matter is given on the transverse plane, and fluctuates from event to event. For each integer n ≥ 1, define the complex initial spatial anisotropy (eccentricity) of harmonic order n by

  ε_n e^{i n Φ_n} = − ( ∫ d²x⊥ r^n e^{i n φ} e(x,y) ) / ( ∫ d²x⊥ r^n e(x,y) ),

with (r,φ) polar coordinates centered at the energy-weighted center of mass. Let the subsequent evolution be governed by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a fixed equation of state and fixed transport coefficients (e.g., shear and bulk viscosities), followed by a standard particlization prescription on a freeze-out hypersurface. The final azimuthal single-particle distribution dN/dφ admits a Fourier decomposition

  dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_{n≥1} v_n cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)],

Consider a relativistic heavy-ion collision modeled as follows. At an early proper time τ₀ after impact, the transverse energy-density profile e(x,y) of the produced matter is given on the transverse plane, and fluctuates from event to event. For each integer n ≥ 1, define the complex initial spatial anisotropy (eccentricity) of harmonic order n by

  ε_n e^{i n Φ_n} = − ( ∫ d²x⊥ r^n e^{i n φ} e(x,y) ) / ( ∫ d²x⊥ r^n e(x,y) ),

with (r,φ) polar coordinates centered at the energy-weighted center of mass. Let the subsequent evolution be governed by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a fixed equation of state and fixed transport coefficients (e.g., shear and bulk viscosities), followed by a standard particlization prescription on a freeze-out hypersurface. The final azimuthal single-particle distribution dN/dφ admits a Fourier decomposition

  dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_{n≥1} v_n cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)],

defining the complex flow harmonics V_n = v_n e^{i n Ψ_n}.

  V_n = F_n( {ε_m e^{i m Φ_m}}, {⟨r^k⟩}, η/s, ζ/s, equation of state, … ),

that reproduces the output of full event-by-event viscous hydrodynamic simulations to controlled accuracy across centralities and harmonic orders, so that no separate hydrodynamic simulation is required for each candidate initial condition. In particular, characterize the regime of validity of a linear response relation V_n = κ_n ε_n e^{i n Φ_n}, identify and quantify the leading nonlinear and mode-mixing corrections (e.g., cubic response in ε_n and quadratic mixings such as ε_2 ε_3 contributing to V_5), and determine to what extent the response coefficients depend only on bulk medium properties rather than on details of the initial-state model.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Substantial progress has been made: for lower harmonics (n=2,3) and central/mid-central collisions, an approximately linear response V_n ≈ κ_n ε_n is well established, and explicit nonlinear/mode-mixing parametrizations (cubic response in ε_n, and quadratic mixings producing V_4, V_5, V_6 from ε_2, ε_3) have been formulated and tested against event-by-event viscous hydrodynamics with good but not perfect accuracy. A fully predictive, model-independent functional map covering all harmonics, all centralities, and all initial-condition models without running new simulations is not yet available, so the broader problem remains partially solved.

representations.normalized:
For a real parameter $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and a finite set of distinct positive integers $n_1,\dots,n_N$, consider the GCD sum
$$S_\alpha(n_1,\dots,n_N)=\sum_{k,\ell=1}^{N}\frac{(\gcd(n_k,n_\ell))^{2\alpha}}{(n_k n_\ell)^{\alpha}},$$
together with its optimized (weighted) variants. Such sums admit a representation as Poisson-type integrals on the infinite-dimensional polydisc $\mathbb{T}^\infty$, via Bohr's correspondence between Dirichlet series and power series in infinitely many variables. Let $\mathscr{H}^p$ ($1\le p\le\infty$) denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_n n^{-s}$, defined as the closure of Dirichlet polynomials under the norm
$$\|f\|_{\mathscr{H}^p}=\Bigl(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|f(it)|^p\,dt\Bigr)^{1/p}\qquad(1\le p<\infty),$$
which by Bohr's lift coincides with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite polydisc.

Establish a systematic correspondence between the sharp upper bounds (and lower bounds) for $S_\alpha$ and its optimized variants on the one hand, and the function-theoretic and operator-theoretic structure of the spaces $\mathscr{H}^p$ on the other. Concretely, develop analogues for $\mathscr{H}^p$ of classical phenomena such as:
(i) Poisson kernel representations and boundary behaviour,
(ii) bounded mean oscillation (BMO) and its duality with $\mathscr{H}^1$,
that recover, refine, or interpret the known GCD-sum estimates as quantitative statements about norms, embeddings, multipliers, or operators acting on $\mathscr{H}^p$.

The problem is a programmatic research direction asking to systematically tie GCD sum estimates to the function/operator theory of Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. representations.normalized:
For positive integers $n_1,\dots,n_N$, define the GCD sum
$$S_\alpha(n_1,\dots,n_N) \;=\; \sum_{j,k=1}^{N} \frac{(\gcd(n_j,n_k))^{2\alpha}}{(n_j n_k)^{\alpha}}, \qquad 0<\alpha\le 1,$$
and let
$$\Gamma_\alpha(N) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{ S_\alpha(n_1,\dots,n_N) : 1\le n_1<\dots<n_N \bigr\}.$$
Recent work has shown, via the resonance method of Soundararajan together with sharp estimates for $\Gamma_{1/2}(N)$, that
$$\max_{T^{1/2}\le t\le T} \bigl|\zeta\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}+it\bigr)\bigr| \;\ge\; \exp\!\left(\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}+o(1)\Bigr)\sqrt{\frac{\log T\,\log\log\log T}{\log\log T}}\right).$$
The problem is to develop further applications of GCD-sum estimates and the associated Dirichlet-series techniques to the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$, and to establish new structural links between such estimates and the behavior of $\zeta(s)$ on or near the critical line $\Re s = 1/2$. Concretely, one seeks:
(i) improved unconditional lower bounds for $\max_{t\in[T^\theta,T]} |\zeta(1/2+it)|$ for various $\theta\in[0,1)$, derived from refined bounds on $\Gamma_\alpha(N)$ or related multiplicative quadratic forms;
(ii) corresponding bounds for the imaginary part $\arg\zeta(1/2+it)$ and for $1/\zeta(1/2+it)$;
(iii) analogous applications to moments $\int_0^T |\zeta(1/2+it)|^{2k}\,dt$ and to the value distribution of $\zeta$ inside the critical strip;
(iv) a clarification of the precise relationship between the asymptotic order of $\Gamma_\alpha(N)$ as $N\to\infty$ and the maximal growth of $|\zeta(1/2+it)|$, including whether the constant $1/\sqrt 2$ above is optimal for the resonance-based approach.

Consider a relativistic heavy-ion collision modeled by viscous relativistic hydrodynamics, in which the produced quark-gluon plasma is described as a fluid with temperature-dependent specific shear viscosity η/s(T) and specific bulk viscosity ζ/s(T). The initial state of the fluid at proper time τ_0 is given by a (fluctuating) energy-density profile ε(x,y) determined by a chosen initial-condition model (e.g. Glauber, KLN, or IP-Glasma type), and the fluid evolves until freeze-out, after which produced hadrons are sampled and their azimuthal momentum distribution is analyzed. For each event, the anisotropic flow coefficients v_n (n = 2, 3, 4, …) are defined as the Fourier coefficients of the single-particle azimuthal distribution dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_n v_n cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)], and one further considers their event-by-event distributions, mixed cumulants, and correlations between event-plane angles Ψ_n.

(a) Given the family of physically admissible initial-state models and the freedom in η/s(T) and ζ/s(T), determine the present quantitative uncertainty (i.e. the range of values consistent with measured anisotropic-flow observables across collision systems and beam energies) in the transport coefficients η/s(T) and ζ/s(T) of the quark-gluon plasma inferred from anisotropic-flow data.

(b) Identify an optimal strategy — specifying which combinations of flow observables (e.g. v_n at multiple harmonics, event-by-event distributions, multi-particle cumulants, symmetric cumulants, event-plane correlations, system-size and beam-energy scans) and which model-comparison methodology — that would most effectively reduce the joint uncertainty on η/s(T) and ζ/s(T) by disentangling initial-state fluctuations from medium response.

Bayesian global analyses of heavy-ion data (e.g. Duke/JETSCAPE collaborations, 2019–2024) have constrained η/s(T) and ζ/s(T) of the QGP to within roughly a factor of 2–3, with sizable residual uncertainties driven by initial-state model ambiguity. The problem of fully separating initial-state fluctuations from transport is widely regarded as still open; ongoing work uses higher harmonics, symmetric cumulants, and event-plane correlations as discriminators, but no unique optimal strategy has been established.

representations.normalized:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the produced matter is modeled as a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) whose space-time evolution is commonly described by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with fluctuating initial conditions, followed by hadronic freeze-out. Standard final-state observables include the azimuthal anisotropic flow harmonics v_n (defined via the Fourier expansion dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_{n≥1} v_n cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)] of the single-particle azimuthal distribution about event-plane angles Ψ_n), event-by-event distributions P(v_n), event-plane correlations between Ψ_n at different harmonics, mixed-harmonic correlators, and multi-particle cumulants v_n{2k}. The initial state is characterized by eccentricities ε_n of the transverse energy- or entropy-density profile.

Address the following:

(a) Identify which combinations of the newly available observables (event-by-event v_n distributions, mixed-harmonic event-plane correlators ⟨cos(n_1 Ψ_{m_1} + ⋯ + n_k Ψ_{m_k})⟩, higher-order cumulants v_n{4}, v_n{6}, v_n{8}, factorization-breaking ratios in p_T and rapidity, and symmetric/asymmetric cumulants SC(m,n)) most tightly constrain (i) the shear and bulk viscosity to entropy density ratios η/s and ζ/s of the QGP as functions of temperature, (ii) the statistical properties of the fluctuating initial energy/entropy density (mean, variance, and non-Gaussianity of the ε_n distributions), and (iii) the pre-equilibrium dynamics linking the initial color-field stage to the hydrodynamic stage.

(b) Propose a minimal set of additional final-state observables, beyond those listed above, whose measurement would further disentangle initial-state fluctuations from medium response, and provide a precise mathematical definition of each proposed observable together with the specific theoretical degeneracy it is designed to break.

Let $\zeta$ denote the Riemann zeta function. Let $T>0$ and let $\omega$ be a random variable uniformly distributed on $[0,T]$ (so that $[0,T]$ is regarded as a probability space with normalized Lebesgue measure). Define the random variable
$$M(\omega,T) := \max_{h\in[0,1]} \log\bigl|\zeta\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}+i h + i\omega\bigr)\bigr|.$$
Prove or disprove: as $T\to\infty$,
$$M(\omega,T) = \log\log T - \tfrac{3}{4}\log\log\log T + E(\omega,T),$$
where the error term $E(\omega,T)$ is bounded in probability as $T\to\infty$ (i.e., for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $C_\varepsilon>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(|E(\omega,T)|>C_\varepsilon)<\varepsilon$ for all sufficiently large $T$).

This is the Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture for the maximum of |ζ(1/2+it)| on a typical short interval. Arguello-Bourgade and collaborators have established it in successive works ("The Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating Conjecture I" (2020) proving the tightness of the centered maximum, "II" (2023) proving the conjectured limiting law of the recentered maximum), and a 2024 preprint extends it to mesoscopic intervals. The leading two-term asymptotic with tightness of the error has been established, so the precise statement asked here (boundedness in probability of E) is essentially proved in the literature, although the original conjecture also predicts a specific limiting distribution which has been settled more recently.

For each prime $p$, let $\theta_p$ be independent random variables uniformly distributed on $[0,2\pi]$. Define the random field
$$X(x) \;=\; \sum_{p \text{ prime}} p^{-1/2}\bigl(\cos(x\log p)\cos\theta_p + \sin(x\log p)\sin\theta_p\bigr), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.$$
For a parameter $\beta>0$, consider the formal exponential $e^{\beta X(x)}$. Since the series defining $X$ does not converge pointwise, one must regularize it (for instance by truncating the sum to primes $p\le N$, obtaining $X_N$, and considering $e^{\beta X_N(x)}/\mathbb{E}[e^{\beta X_N(x)}]\,dx$) and study the resulting non-Gaussian multiplicative-chaos-type random measure as $N\to\infty$.

Investigate the properties of this non-Gaussian multiplicative chaos $\text{``}e^{\beta X(x)}\text{''}$: in particular, for which values of $\beta$ does the regularized measure converge to a nontrivial limit (subcritical phase), determine the critical value $\beta_c$, establish existence and uniqueness of the limiting measure independently of the regularization scheme, characterize the support and multifractal structure of the limit, and analyze the moments and the freezing/critical behavior at $\beta=\beta_c$.

representations.normalized:
In a relativistic heavy-ion collision, two nuclei collide at ultra-relativistic energies and produce a fireball of strongly interacting matter whose subsequent evolution can be modeled hydrodynamically. The azimuthal distribution of produced particles in the transverse plane is conventionally expanded in a Fourier series,

dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_{n≥1} v_n cos[ n(φ − Ψ_n) ],

where the harmonic flow coefficients v_n and event-plane angles Ψ_n fluctuate event by event. Two-particle azimuthal correlations are characterized by the harmonics V_{nΔ}(p_T^a, p_T^t) = ⟨cos[n(φ_a − φ_t)]⟩ as functions of the trigger and associated transverse momenta p_T^t and p_T^a. These correlations may originate either from initial-state geometric and quantum fluctuations of the colliding nuclei (e.g., fluctuating positions of nucleons, color-charge fluctuations, gluon-saturation effects encoded in spatial eccentricities ε_n) or from the collective final-state evolution of the produced medium (hydrodynamic response converting initial spatial anisotropies into momentum-space anisotropies v_n).

Formulate and analyze observables and theoretical procedures that can unambiguously separate these two sources of correlation. Specifically:

(a) Identify a set of measurable correlation functions (including factorization tests of V_{nΔ}(p_T^a, p_T^t) into a product v_n(p_T^a) v_n(p_T^t), multi-particle cumulants v_n{2k}, event-by-event distributions P(v_n), symmetric cumulants SC(m,n), and event-plane correlations ⟨cos(m Ψ_m + n Ψ_n + …)⟩) whose values discriminate between an initial-state-only origin and a collective hydrodynamic origin.

(b) Determine theoretically, within a chosen initial-condition model (e.g., Glauber, KLN, IP-Glasma) coupled to a hydrodynamic + hadronic-cascade description, which features of these observables are robust signatures of final-state collectivity rather than artifacts of initial-state correlations.

(c) Establish quantitative criteria (e.g., breakdown of factorization, system-size dependence, multiplicity dependence in small collision systems such as p+p and p+Pb) under which collective behavior can be claimed to dominate over initial-state correlations.

representations.normalized:
In a relativistic heavy-ion collision, the initial state of the produced fireball varies from event to event due to several distinct stochastic mechanisms. Consider the following sources of event-by-event fluctuations in the initial conditions:

(1) Fluctuations in the transverse positions of the nucleons (or constituent quarks) inside the colliding nuclei, together with the stochastic pattern of their binary interactions (which nucleon pairs scatter inelastically).

(2) The finite spatial extent of individual nucleons, modeled by a smooth profile and accompanied by a correspondingly adjusted Woods–Saxon nuclear density distribution.

(3) Fluctuations in the initial transverse momentum distribution of the produced matter (initial flow), independent of the geometric energy-density profile.

(4) Local fluctuations in the energy deposition and/or particle production at each transverse point, beyond what is dictated by the nucleon positions.

Each of these mechanisms imprints itself on observable final-state event-by-event quantities such as the harmonic flow coefficients v_n, their probability distributions P(v_n), event-plane correlations, and the correlations between flow harmonics of different orders.

Problem. Devise a set of observables, or a procedure, that uniquely disentangles the contributions of mechanisms (1)–(4) from one another using only measurable final-state correlations. More precisely: do there exist final-state observables whose dependence on these four sources is sufficiently independent that, given experimental measurements of those observables, one can separately determine (or place quantitative constraints on) the magnitude of each fluctuation source individually?

Let $\Lambda_{q,t} = \mathbb{Q}(q,t)\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}}\Lambda$ denote the algebra of symmetric functions in variables $x = (x_1,x_2,\dots)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$, with Schur basis $\{s_\lambda\}$. Recall the elliptic Hall algebra $\mathcal{E}_{q,t}$ of Burban–Schiffmann and its standard action on $\Lambda_{q,t}$: for each pair of coprime integers $(a,b)$ with $a,b\ge 1$, there is an embedding
$$\Theta_{a,b}\colon \Lambda_{q,t}\longrightarrow \mathrm{End}\bigl(\Lambda_{q,t}\bigr),$$
sending a symmetric function $f_d$ of degree $d$ to an operator $\Theta_{a,b}(f_d)$ on $\Lambda_{q,t}$, in such a way that $\Theta_{1,0}$ recovers multiplication operators, $\Theta_{0,1}$ recovers the Macdonald eigenoperators (so that $\Theta_{0,1}(e_n)$ is, up to normalization, the operator $\nabla$ on the modified Macdonald basis), and $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ acts by automorphisms cycling these slopes.

For every symmetric function $f_d$ of degree $d$ define
$$f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) \;:=\; \Theta_{a,b}(f_d)(1) \;\in\; \Lambda_{q,t}.$$

For a partition $\mu$ of $d$ let $\iota(\mu) := \sum_i \binom{\mu_i}{2}$ (or, equivalently, $n(\mu')$ in the standard notation), and consider the normalized Schur image
$$\widetilde{s}_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) \;:=\; (-qt)^{-\iota(\mu)}\, s_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t).$$

Prove or disprove: for every $d\ge 1$, every partition $\mu \vdash d$, and every coprime pair of integers $a,b\ge 1$, the symmetric function $\widetilde{s}_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t)$ is Schur-positive, i.e. its expansion in the Schur basis has all coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$. Furthermore, give a representation-theoretic interpretation of this positivity in terms of bigraded $S_n$-subrepresentations of the module of generalized diagonal harmonics.

The conjectural Schur positivity of the normalized images of Schur functions under the elliptic-Hall-algebra slope-$(a,b)$ operators (a rational/(a,b)-generalization of the classical $\nabla s_\mu$ Schur-positivity conjecture of Bergeron–Garsia–Haiman–Tesler) appears to remain open in general. Recent work (e.g., Blasiak–Haiman–Morse–Pun–Seelinger on Catalanimals and LLT positivity, and Negut/Mellit-style results) has established related positivity statements and the shuffle/rational shuffle theorem at the level of $\Theta_{a,b}(p_n)$ and $\Theta_{a,b}(e_n)$, but a general proof for arbitrary Schur seeds $s_\mu$ and arbitrary coprime $(a,b)$, together with the representation-theoretic interpretation via bigraded subrepresentations of generalized diagonal harmonics, has not been reported.

In the framework of 3+1-dimensional viscous relativistic hydrodynamic simulations of ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions, the transverse profile of fluctuating initial conditions has been extensively studied, while the modeling of the longitudinal direction (along the beam axis, parametrized by spacetime rapidity η) remains far less constrained. Develop and constrain a model of the longitudinal structure of the fluctuating initial energy/entropy density (and any associated initial flow profile) such that:

1. The model specifies, on an event-by-event basis, the η-dependence of the local energy density and the correlations between transverse fluctuations at different values of η (including any rapidity-dependent decorrelation of the transverse geometry).
2. The model is implemented as initial data for a 3+1-dimensional viscous hydrodynamic evolution with realistic transport coefficients and a hadronic freeze-out prescription.
3. The resulting predictions for pseudorapidity-dependent particle correlations — in particular the single-particle pseudorapidity distribution dN/dη, two-particle correlations C(η₁, η₂) and their dependence on the rapidity gap Δη = η₁ − η₂, and the longitudinal decorrelation of anisotropic flow harmonics vₙ between separated pseudorapidity windows — are quantitatively reproduced and used to fix the parameters of the longitudinal initial-state model.

Provide such a model together with the constraints on its parameters extracted from η- and Δη-dependent observables, and a comprehensive characterization of longitudinal initial-state fluctuations within 3+1-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics.

representations.normalized:
Consider the early, far-from-equilibrium stage of an ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collision modeled as a classical-statistical SU(3) Yang–Mills field theory in 3+1 spacetime dimensions. The classical color fields are evolved from initial conditions motivated by the Color Glass Condensate, and quantum fluctuations are incorporated by sampling initial-field perturbations (e.g., with a spectrum determined by the JIMWLK/CGC framework or by linearized fluctuations on top of the classical background) and then propagating them under the full nonlinear SU(3) Yang–Mills equations on a 3+1-dimensional lattice.

Within this classical-statistical SU(3) Yang–Mills framework with quantum fluctuations included in a fully 3+1-dimensional simulation, determine whether the gauge-field system undergoes rapid thermalization on a timescale compatible with the short hydrodynamization times (of order 1 fm/c or less) inferred from heavy-ion phenomenology. Specifically, establish whether the local energy-momentum tensor isotropizes (longitudinal pressure approaching transverse pressure) and whether the gluon occupation numbers approach a thermal (Bose–Einstein) distribution rapidly, or whether the dynamics instead remain anisotropic and/or relax only on parametrically longer timescales.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of rapid thermalization in classical-statistical SU(3) Yang–Mills simulations with quantum fluctuations in full 3+1D remains an active research area. Subsequent works have shown isotropization via chromo-Weibel-like instabilities and filamentation, but classical field theory suffers from Rayleigh–Jeans divergence and does not reach quantum thermal distributions, leaving full quantum thermalization unresolved. No definitive demonstration of rapid quantum thermalization in this framework has been established.

For coprime integers $a,b\ge 1$, let $\Theta_{a,b}$ denote the plethystic symmetric-function operator (acting on the ring of symmetric functions in variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$) associated with the rational $(a,b)$-shuffle setup; for a symmetric function $f$, define
$$f^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) := \Theta_{a,b}(f)(1).$$
For nonnegative integers $j,k$, let $s_{(j\mid k)}$ be the hook Schur function indexed by the hook partition with one row of length $j+1$ and $k$ additional rows of length $1$ (so the hook has $j+k+1$ cells). For positive integers $m,n$, let $e_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ and $h_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ be the symmetric functions obtained by applying $\Theta_{a,b}$ (with $(a,b)=(m/d,n/d)$, $d=\gcd(m,n)$) to the elementary, respectively complete homogeneous, symmetric functions of degree $d$, evaluated at $1$.

Write $f \preceq_s g$ to mean that $g-f$ is Schur-positive, i.e., expands in the basis of Schur functions with coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$.

Let $\beta = \beta(m,n)$ be the integer equal to the number of lattice points strictly between the staircase lattice paths from $(0,n)$ to $(m,0)$ that arise in the standard combinatorial interpretation of $e_{m,n}$ and $h_{m,n}$.

Prove (or disprove) that for all coprime $a,b\ge 1$, all $j,k\ge 0$ with $k\ge 1$, and all $m,n\ge 1$:
$$q\cdot(-1)^{j}\, s_{(j+1\mid k-1)}^{(a,b)}(x;q,t)\ \preceq_s\ (-1)^{j-1}\, s_{(j\mid k)}^{(a,b)}(x;q,t),$$
$$q^{\beta}\, e_{m-1,n}(x;q,t)\ \preceq_s\ (-qt)^{1-d}\, h_{m,n}(x;q,t),\qquad d=\gcd(m,n).$$
Furthermore, exhibit inclusions of bigraded representations whose graded characters realize these Schur-positive differences.

representations.normalized:
Let $\Lambda_{q,t}$ denote the ring of symmetric functions in variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\dots)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. For coprime-or-general positive integers $m,n$, let $e_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ and $h_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ denote the rational-shuffle symmetric functions defined by the elliptic Hall / shuffle algebra action: $e_{m,n} = Q_{m,n}(1)$ and $h_{m,n}$ its dual analogue, where $Q_{m,n}$ is the standard generator of the $(GL)$ shuffle algebra acting on $\Lambda_{q,t}$. (Equivalently, $e_{n,1}=e_n$ and $h_{1,n}=h_n$, and $e_{m,n}$ is the symmetric function appearing in the rational shuffle theorem.)

For two symmetric functions $f,g\in\Lambda_{q,t}$, write $f \preceq_s g$ ("$g$ Schur-dominates $f$") if $g-f$ expands as a $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$-linear combination of Schur functions $s_\lambda(x)$ — that is, every coefficient in the Schur expansion of $g-f$ is a polynomial in $q,t$ with nonnegative integer coefficients.

Define the following exponents associated to a pair $(m,n)$ with $m,n\ge 1$ and $d=\gcd(m,n)$:
- The minimal $(m,n)$-staircase is the lattice path from $(0,0)$ to $(m,n)$ that stays as close as possible to (and weakly above) the line segment from $(0,0)$ to $(m,n)$. The $(m,n-1)$-staircase path is defined analogously for the pair $(m,n-1)$.
- Let $\alpha'=\alpha'(m,n)$ be the number of integer lattice points lying strictly between the $(m,n-1)$-staircase path and the minimal $(m,n)$-staircase.
- Let $\beta'=\beta'(m,n)$ be the analogous count obtained from the transposed (column-strict) version of the staircase construction.

Prove or disprove: for all integers $m,n\ge 1$,
$$ q^{\alpha'}\, e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t) \;\preceq_s\; e_{m,n}(x;q,t), $$
and
$$ q^{\beta'}\, e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t) \;\preceq_s\; (-qt)^{1-d}\, h_{m,n}(x;q,t). $$

Equivalently, exhibit inclusions of bigraded $\mathbb{S}_N$-modules realizing these Schur-positive inequalities.

representations.normalized:
Consider a relativistic heavy-ion collision in which a hydrodynamic description of the produced quark–gluon medium is initialized at some proper time τ₀ from a pre-equilibrium stage. The full local energy–momentum tensor T^{μν}(x) at τ₀ admits a Landau decomposition

T^{μν} = ε u^μ u^ν − (P + Π)(g^{μν} − u^μ u^ν) + π^{μν},

where ε is the energy density, u^μ is the timelike flow four-velocity (the unique timelike eigenvector of T^{μν}), P(ε) is the equilibrium pressure given by an equation of state, Π is the bulk viscous pressure, and π^{μν} is the symmetric, traceless, transverse shear-stress tensor (u_μ π^{μν} = 0, π^μ_μ = 0).

Pre-equilibrium dynamics generically generate at τ₀ a nontrivial transverse flow velocity field u^μ(x) (the "initial flow") and nonzero dissipative components π^{μν}(x), Π(x), in addition to the energy density ε(x).

Quantify the magnitude and dynamical importance of the initial flow field u^μ at τ₀, and determine how the complete energy–momentum tensor T^{μν}—including its shear-stress components π^{μν} (and bulk Π)—should be used to initialize subsequent viscous hydrodynamic evolution, in such a way that final-state observables (in particular anisotropic flow coefficients v_n and their event-by-event distributions) are correctly reproduced. Specifically:

(a) Estimate the typical size of the transverse components of u^μ at τ₀ relative to the local speed of sound, and characterize their spatial structure on an event-by-event basis.

(b) Determine the quantitative impact on the final flow harmonics v_n of including, versus neglecting, (i) the initial transverse flow u^μ and (ii) the initial shear-stress tensor π^{μν}, when initializing hydrodynamics.

(c) Provide a prescription for matching pre-equilibrium dynamics to hydrodynamics that consistently transfers all components of T^{μν} at τ₀.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Significant progress has been made: pre-equilibrium frameworks (e.g., KøMPøST and QCD kinetic theory matching) now provide initial conditions for all second-order hydrodynamic variables, including initial flow and shear stress, and recent linear-response frameworks (e.g., 2024 work on initial energy-momentum to final flow) systematically quantify how each component of T^{μν} at τ₀ contributes to final flow harmonics. However, a full consensus on the precise size and importance of initial flow across all collision systems (especially small systems vs. AA) is still being refined, so the question is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

Work in the ring $\Lambda = \Lambda(x)\otimes\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$ of symmetric functions in variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\dots)$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. For a partition $\mu$, let $\bar\mu$ denote the partition obtained from $\mu$ by removing its first column, and define a $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$-linear map $\overline{(\cdot)}:\Lambda\to\Lambda$ by $\overline{s_\mu(x)} := s_{\bar\mu}(x)$ on the Schur basis, extended linearly.

For symmetric functions $F,G\in\Lambda$, write $F\preceq_s G$ (Schur-smaller than) if $G-F$ expands in the Schur basis with coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$.

Assume given, for each pair of coprime positive integers $(a,b)$ with $b\geq a\geq 1$ and each integer $d\geq 1$, an operator $\Theta_{a,b}$ on $\Lambda$ and a "seed" symmetric function $f_d\in\Lambda$ such that the expression
$$f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) := \Theta_{a,b}(f_d)\big|_{\text{evaluated at }1}$$
is Schur-positive (i.e., expands in the Schur basis with coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$); here $f_d^{(a,b)}$ is a homogeneous symmetric function of degree $bd$, while $f_d^{(b,a)}$ is homogeneous of degree $ad$.

Question: Is it true that for every such Schur-positive seed $f_d$ and every pair of coprime integers $b\geq a\geq 1$,
$$\overline{f_d^{(b,a)}(x;q,t)} \preceq_s \overline{f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,t)}\,?$$

representations.normalized:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the spatial profile of energy or entropy density deposited just after the collision fluctuates event by event. Models of these initial-state fluctuations are typically parametrized by a length scale (such as the transverse radius of color flux tubes, the Gaussian smearing width assigned to participant nucleons or partons, or a two-point correlation length of the deposited density) and an amplitude (the variance of the local density fluctuations).

Formulate and carry out a quantitative program with the following requirements:

(a) Fix a definite physical assumption about the microscopic origin of the fluctuations (for example: independent Gaussian sources centered on participant nucleons; color-charge fluctuations in a Color-Glass-Condensate / Glasma flux-tube picture with a transverse scale set by the saturation momentum Q_s; or a hot-spot picture based on constituent quarks).

(b) Within that assumption, define precisely the fluctuation scale parameter σ (e.g. flux-tube radius, Gaussian width, or correlation length) and the fluctuation amplitude parameter A (e.g. the relative variance of the deposited density at a point).

(c) Identify a set of experimental observables in heavy-ion collisions (such as the centrality dependence of anisotropic flow harmonics v_n{2}, v_n{4}, event-by-event v_n distributions, mixed harmonic correlators / symmetric cumulants, or correlations between flow magnitudes and mean transverse momentum) whose dependence on σ and A is monotonic and distinguishable from the dependence on subsequent hydrodynamic transport coefficients (shear and bulk viscosity).

In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the spatial profile of energy or entropy density deposited just after the collision fluctuates event by event. Models of these initial-state fluctuations are typically parametrized by a length scale (such as the transverse radius of color flux tubes, the Gaussian smearing width assigned to participant nucleons or partons, or a two-point correlation length of the deposited density) and an amplitude (the variance of the local density fluctuations).

Formulate and carry out a quantitative program with the following requirements:

(a) Fix a definite physical assumption about the microscopic origin of the fluctuations (for example: independent Gaussian sources centered on participant nucleons; color-charge fluctuations in a Color-Glass-Condensate / Glasma flux-tube picture with a transverse scale set by the saturation momentum Q_s; or a hot-spot picture based on constituent quarks).

(b) Within that assumption, define precisely the fluctuation scale parameter σ (e.g. flux-tube radius, Gaussian width, or correlation length) and the fluctuation amplitude parameter A (e.g. the relative variance of the deposited density at a point).

(c) Identify a set of experimental observables in heavy-ion collisions (such as the centrality dependence of anisotropic flow harmonics v_n{2}, v_n{4}, event-by-event v_n distributions, mixed harmonic correlators / symmetric cumulants, or correlations between flow magnitudes and mean transverse momentum) whose dependence on σ and A is monotonic and distinguishable from the dependence on subsequent hydrodynamic transport coefficients (shear and bulk viscosity).

(d) Determine, by combining these observables with viscous hydrodynamic evolution, quantitative confidence regions for σ and A that are consistent with the data, and demonstrate to what extent these constraints depend on, or remain robust against, the choice of physical assumption in (a).

The problem is to provide such a constraint procedure and to state the resulting allowed ranges of σ and A together with their dependence on the underlying physical picture.

C 89, 064907 and the Duke/JETSCAPE Bayesian programs), yielding constraints on nucleon Gaussian widths and sub-nucleon hot-spot scales. Setup. Work in the ring $\Lambda_{q,t}$ of symmetric functions in variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\dots)$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. Let $\{e_\lambda\}$, $\{h_\lambda\}$, $\{s_\lambda\}$ denote, respectively, the elementary, complete homogeneous, and Schur bases indexed by partitions $\lambda$. For an integer $d\ge 1$ and integers $j,k\ge 0$ with $j+k=d-1$, let $s_{(j\,|\,k)}$ denote the hook Schur function indexed by the hook partition with arm $j$ and leg $k$, i.e.\ the partition $(j+1,1^{k})$.

For each pair of coprime positive integers $(a,b)$, let $\Theta_{a,b}\colon \Lambda_{q,t}\to\Lambda_{q,t}$ be the rectangular Catalan/Theta operator associated with the slope $b/a$ (the operator $\nabla$-type operator producing the conjectural Schur-positive symmetric function for the rectangular shuffle theorem in the $(a,b)$ case), and write $\Theta_{a,b}(f)(1)$ for the result of applying $\Theta_{a,b}$ to $f$ and then setting an auxiliary specialization parameter to $1$. Define
$$h_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) := \Theta_{a,b}(h_d)(1), \qquad s_{(j\,|\,k)}^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) := \Theta_{a,b}(s_{(j\,|\,k)})(1).$$

Notation. For $f,g\in\Lambda_{q,t}$, write $0\le_e f$ if every coefficient of $f$ in the elementary basis $\{e_\lambda\}$ lies in $\mathbb{N}[q,r]$ (i.e.\ is a polynomial in $q$ and $r$ with nonnegative integer coefficients), and write $g\le_e f$ if $0\le_e f-g$.

Question. Prove or disprove: for every integer $d\ge 1$, every pair of nonnegative integers $j,k$ with $j+k=d-1$, and every pair of coprime positive integers $a,b\ge 1$, both of the following $e$-positivity statements hold after substituting $t=1+r$:
$$0 \le_e (-1)^{1-k}\, h_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,1+r),$$
$$q\,(-1)^{j}\, s_{(j+1\,|\,k-1)}^{(a,b)}(x;q,1+r) \;\le_e\; (-1)^{j-1}\, s_{(j\,|\,k)}^{(a,b)}(x;q,1+r).$$

Let $\Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)}$ denote the ring of symmetric functions over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$, with the usual bases $\{m_\mu\}$ (monomial), $\{e_\mu\}$ (elementary), and $\{p_\mu\}$ (power sum) indexed by integer partitions. For coprime positive integers $a,b\ge 1$, there is a family of "rational" symmetric functions $m_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t)$, defined for each partition $\mu$ of $d$, satisfying $m_\mu^{(1,1)}(x;q,t)=m_\mu(x)$ and arising as the images of monomial seeds under the $(a,b)$-rational analogue of the nabla-style operator (equivalently, via the elliptic Hall algebra action on symmetric functions). Concretely, $m_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t)$ may be characterized via the operator on $\Lambda$ whose eigenvectors are the modified Macdonald polynomials $\widetilde H_\lambda(x;q,t)$ with eigenvalues that are $(a,b)$-rational analogues of $\prod_{s\in\lambda} q^{a\cdot a'(s)} t^{b\cdot \ell'(s)}$, applied to the monomial $m_\mu$ (the precise normalization is that of the standard $(a,b)$-rational shuffle setup, so that $m_\mu^{(1,0)}=m_\mu$ and the construction reduces to nabla applied to $m_\mu$ when $(a,b)=(1,1)$).

Specialize the parameter $t$ to $1+r$, where $r$ is a formal indeterminate, and define
$$F_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,r)\;=\;(-1)^{d-\ell(\mu)}\, m_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,1+r),$$
where $\ell(\mu)$ is the number of parts of $\mu$.

Prove or disprove: for every partition $\mu$ of every $d\ge 1$ and every pair of coprime integers $a,b\ge 1$, the symmetric function $F_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,r)$ is $e$-positive in the strong sense that
$$F_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,r)\;=\;\sum_{\lambda\vdash d} c_{\mu,\lambda}^{(a,b)}(q,r)\, e_\lambda(x)$$
with all coefficients $c_{\mu,\lambda}^{(a,b)}(q,r)\in\mathbb{N}[q,r]$.

Furthermore, find a combinatorial model — in the spirit of weighted enumerations of lattice paths in the $a\times b$ rectangle (e.g.\ rational Dyck paths with statistics such as area and a $q$-weight) — that gives a manifestly nonnegative formula for the coefficients $c_{\mu,\lambda}^{(a,b)}(q,r)$.

In ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions, the colliding nuclei produce a hot, dense fireball whose subsequent evolution is well described by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics. The initial state of the fireball, just after the collision, exhibits event-by-event fluctuations of the energy/entropy density in the transverse plane. These fluctuations can be characterized by spatial cumulants such as the eccentricities ε_n e^{i n Φ_n} = − ⟨r^n e^{i n φ}⟩ / ⟨r^n⟩ (n ≥ 2), as well as by higher-order radial and azimuthal cumulants and by finer-grained measures of small-scale structure. After hydrodynamic evolution and freeze-out, the produced hadrons exhibit final-state correlations encoded in the complex anisotropic flow harmonics V_n = v_n e^{i n Ψ_n}, where dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_n v_n cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)], together with their event-by-event distributions, mixed harmonic correlators, symmetric cumulants, principal-component decompositions of p_T-differential flow, and event-plane decorrelation observables.

(a) For each such final-state observable O, determine quantitatively the aspects of the initial state (which spatial cumulant, which length scale, which radial weight, or which combination thereof) to which O is most sensitive, in the sense of providing a response map from initial-state characterizations to O that is approximately linear, weakly contaminated by other modes, and stable across model variations.

(b) Develop a general characterization of the hydrodynamic medium response — i.e., a parameter-independent or controllably parameter-dependent map from initial-state fluctuations to final-state observables — that is precise enough to allow simultaneous quantitative constraints on (i) the properties of the initial conditions (e.g., scale of fluctuations, granularity, geometric cumulants) and (ii) the transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma (e.g., shear viscosity to entropy density ratio η/s, bulk viscosity ζ/s, and equation of state).

Provide such a sensitivity classification and general medium-response framework, or prove that no such characterization with the required precision exists.

Substantial progress has been made on characterizing the hydrodynamic medium response and on identifying which initial-state features dominate each flow observable. Linear and nonlinear response coefficients V_n = κ_n ε_n + ... are now well established for low harmonics, principal-component analyses connect higher-order cumulants of the initial geometry to subleading flow modes, and Bayesian global analyses simultaneously constrain QGP transport coefficients and initial-condition parameters. However, a fully general, model-independent characterization of medium response sufficient to tightly disentangle initial conditions from QGP properties remains an active research goal, with recent works (2023–2025) still proposing new statistical decompositions and using nuclear-structure information to break degeneracies. The problem is therefore partially solved.

Consider a relativistic heavy-ion collision modeled as follows. In each event, the transverse density of the initial-state fireball is characterized by a set of complex eccentricities
  ε_n e^{i n Φ_n} = − ⟨ r^n e^{i n φ} ⟩ / ⟨ r^n ⟩,  for n = 2, 3, 4, …,
computed from the energy density at mid-rapidity (with ⟨·⟩ the energy-density-weighted average in the transverse plane after recentering). The final-state azimuthal particle distribution dN/dφ is described by complex flow harmonics
  V_n = v_n e^{i n Ψ_n},  n = 2, 3, 4, …,
which in principle are obtained by solving the event-by-event relativistic viscous hydrodynamic equations on each fluctuating initial condition and computing the Cooper–Frye particle spectrum.

A simplified, non-event-by-event "response" model attempts to predict V_n directly from the initial eccentricities through a fixed (event-independent) functional relation, e.g. a polynomial of the form
  V_n = κ_n ε_n e^{i n Φ_n} + ∑_{m,k} χ^{(n)}_{m,k} (ε_m e^{i m Φ_m})(ε_k e^{i k Φ_k}) δ_{m+k,n} + (higher-order terms),
with response coefficients κ_n, χ^{(n)}_{m,k}, … determined once (e.g. from a small set of smooth/averaged hydrodynamic runs) and then applied event-by-event to the fluctuating eccentricities.

Question. Determine the ultimate scope of such simplified response relations for reproducing mixed-harmonic event-plane correlations, defined for integer coefficients (c_2, c_3, …) with ∑ n c_n = 0 by
  ⟨ cos( ∑_n c_n n Ψ_n ) ⟩_events.
Specifically: does there exist a closed-form, event-independent map V_n = F_n(ε_2, Φ_2, ε_3, Φ_3, …) (of polynomial type or otherwise) that, applied event-by-event to a realistic ensemble of fluctuating initial conditions, reproduces all mixed-harmonic event-plane correlations measured in heavy-ion collisions to within experimental precision, thereby eliminating the need for brute-force event-by-event hydrodynamic simulation? If such a map exists, exhibit it and characterize its accuracy and domain of validity (collision system, centrality, harmonic order); if not, identify which correlators provably cannot be captured by any such response ansatz and require full event-by-event hydrodynamic evolution.

Subsequent work has shown that a substantial set of mixed-harmonic event-plane correlations can indeed be reproduced by simplified linear-plus-nonlinear (mode-coupled) response relations applied to fluctuating initial eccentricities, including single-shot and cumulant-based predictions matching ATLAS/ALICE data and RHIC predictions. Thus the program has been partially successful—linear response captures v2, v3 and many correlations involving Ψ2, Ψ3, while polynomial/mode-coupling expansions capture leading higher-harmonic correlators. However, full quantitative agreement for all correlators across systems and centralities still relies on event-by-event hydrodynamic simulations, and no proof exists that a universal closed-form response map suffices. Setup. Let $\Lambda$ denote the ring of symmetric functions in variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\dots)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$, with elementary basis $\{e_\lambda\}$ and complete homogeneous basis $\{h_\lambda\}$. For coprime-or-not pairs of positive integers $(m,n)$, let $e_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ and $h_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ denote the symmetric functions produced by the elliptic Hall algebra / rational shuffle construction (so that $e_{1,n}$ and $h_{1,n}$ recover the usual modified Macdonald-style operators applied to $1$, and $e_{m,n}$, $h_{m,n}$ are the images of the standard generators $e_{m,n}^{\mathrm{EHA}}$, $h_{m,n}^{\mathrm{EHA}}$ under the Schiffmann–Vasserot action on $\Lambda$).

For two symmetric functions $f,g \in \Lambda$, write $f \le_e g$ to mean that $g-f$ has nonnegative coefficients when expanded in the elementary basis $\{e_\lambda\}$ (with coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$, i.e. polynomials in $q,t$ with nonnegative integer coefficients).

Assume that the following two "$e$-positivity" inequalities are known at $t=1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists an exponent $\alpha=\alpha(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ (the staircase-path exponent) such that
\[ q^{\alpha}\,e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1) \;\le_e\; e_{m,n}(x;q,1); \]
\item there exists an exponent $\beta=\beta(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ (the $h$-vs-$e$ exponent) such that
\[ q^{\beta}\,e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1) \;\le_e\; (-q)^{1-d}\,h_{m,n}(x;q,1), \qquad d=\gcd(m,n). \]
\end{enumerate}

Question. For every nonnegative integer $r$ and all integers $m,n\ge 1$, do the strengthened inequalities
\[ q^{\alpha}\,e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) \;\le_e\; e_{m,n}(x;q,1+r), \]
\[ q^{\beta}\,e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) \;\le_e\; (-q(1+r))^{1-d}\,h_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) \]
hold (with the same exponents $\alpha,\beta$), and is there a combinatorial proof or interpretation of these inequalities (e.g.\ via an injection on labeled rational Dyck paths or on the corresponding parking-function combinatorics)?
