Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of real quaternions with standard basis $1, i, j, k$, and write a quaternion as $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$. For a differentiable function $f : \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{H}$, define the left Cauchy–Fueter operator by
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar{q}} = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_3}.$$
A differentiable function $f : \mathbb{H}^n \to \mathbb{H}$ in variables $q_1, \dots, q_n \in \mathbb{H}$ is called (left) regular if it satisfies the Cauchy–Fueter equation in each variable separately, i.e.
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar{q}_i} = 0, \qquad i = 1, \dots, n.$$
In the one-variable case ($n = 1$), Fueter's theorem states that every regular function $f$ defined on a suitable neighborhood of the origin admits a Taylor-type expansion
$$f(q) = \sum_{\nu} P_\nu(q)\, a_\nu,$$
where $\{P_\nu\}$ is the family of homogeneous regular polynomials in $q$ and $a_\nu \in \mathbb{H}$. A key ingredient enabling the construction and multiplication of regular functions in this one-variable theory is the Cauchy–Kowalewski (C–K) product, which assigns to two entire regular functions a new entire regular function and which restricts to the usual product on the subspace $\{q : x_0 = 0\}$.

The Cauchy–Fueter operator in the variable $q_\ell$ is
$$\frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{q}_\ell} \;=\; \frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,0}} + i\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,1}} + j\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,2}} + k\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\ell,3}}.$$
Let $\mathcal{R}$ be the polynomial ring (or its appropriate Fourier-transformed analogue) modeling these $n$ Cauchy–Fueter operators, and let $P_1$ be the matrix representing the operator $f \mapsto (\partial f/\partial \bar{q}_1, \ldots, \partial f/\partial \bar{q}_n)$. The Cauchy–Fueter module is $M_n = \operatorname{coker} P_1^t$. In a minimal free resolution
$$\cdots \longrightarrow \mathcal{R}^{a_2} \xrightarrow{P_2} \mathcal{R}^{a_1} \xrightarrow{P_1} \mathcal{R}^{a_0} \longrightarrow M_n \longrightarrow 0,$$
the matrix $P_2$ of first syzygies encodes the compatibility conditions that an $n$-tuple $(g_1, \ldots, g_n)$ of quaternion-valued functions must satisfy in order for the non-homogeneous system
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar{q}_\ell} \;=\; g_\ell, \qquad \ell = 1, \ldots, n,$$
to admit a solution $f$. For $n = 2$ these compatibility conditions admit a simple quaternionic expression; for $n = 3$ one obtains a $12 \times 40$ matrix encoding ten quaternionic second-order compatibility conditions whose analytic/geometric meaning is not transparent.

Problem. Give an analytic interpretation, valid uniformly for every $n \geq 2$, of the matrix $P_2$ of first syzygies in the free resolution of the Cauchy–Fueter module $M_n$ — that is, describe the compatibility conditions imposed by $P_2$ on the right-hand side $(g_1, \ldots, g_n)$ in a conceptual analytic form (analogous to the way curl-type conditions arise in the several complex variables $\bar\partial$-problem).

Let $\Sigma$ and $\Delta$ be finite alphabets, and let $h, g : \Sigma^* \to \Delta^*$ be two morphisms (i.e., a Post Correspondence Problem instance $(h, g)$). For words $x, y \in \Delta^*$, write $x \bowtie y$ to mean that $x$ and $y$ are comparable as prefixes, that is, $x$ is a prefix of $y$ or $y$ is a prefix of $x$.

The instance $(h, g)$ is said to have the unique equality continuation property if, for every word $u \in \Sigma^*$ and every pair of distinct letters $a, b \in \Sigma$ with $a \neq b$, the conditions
$$h(ua) \bowtie g(ua) \quad \text{and} \quad h(ub) \bowtie g(ub)$$
together imply
$$h(u) = g(u).$$

Question: Is there an algorithm which, given as input an arbitrary PCP instance $(h, g)$, decides whether $(h, g)$ has the unique equality continuation property?

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the quaternions with basis $1,i,j,k$. For $n\geq 1$ and quaternionic variables $q_\ell = x_{\ell,0}+ix_{\ell,1}+jx_{\ell,2}+kx_{\ell,3}$, $\ell=1,\dots,n$, the Cauchy–Fueter operator in the $\ell$-th variable is
$$\partial_{\bar q_\ell} = \partial_{x_{\ell,0}} + i\,\partial_{x_{\ell,1}} + j\,\partial_{x_{\ell,2}} + k\,\partial_{x_{\ell,3}}.$$
After identifying $\mathbb{H}\cong\mathbb{C}^2$, the operator $\partial_{\bar q_\ell}$ corresponds to a $2\times 2$ matrix of first-order constant-coefficient differential operators with polynomial symbol $P_\ell\in \operatorname{Mat}_{2\times 2}(R)$, where $R = \mathbb{C}[z_{\ell,\alpha}\colon \ell=1,\dots,n,\ \alpha=1,2,3,4]$ is a polynomial ring with $4n$ indeterminates corresponding to the Fourier symbols of the $4n$ real partial derivatives.

Let $P\in \operatorname{Mat}_{2n\times 2}(R)$ be the column matrix obtained by stacking $P_1,\dots,P_n$, and let $M_n = \operatorname{coker}(P^T\colon R^{2n}\to R^{2})^{\vee}$ be the associated Cauchy–Fueter module (viewed as the $R$-module whose minimal free resolution computes the syzygies of $P$). There exists a minimal graded free resolution
$$0\to R^{b_N}\xrightarrow{P_N}\cdots\xrightarrow{P_3} R^{b_2}\xrightarrow{P_2} R^{b_1}\xrightarrow{P_1} R^{b_0}\to M_n\to 0.$$

Prove or disprove: for every $n\geq 2$ and every $i\in\{1,3,4,\dots,N\}$ (that is, for every matrix in the resolution other than $P_2$), all nonzero entries of the matrix $P_i$ are homogeneous polynomials of degree exactly one in $R$.

Let $G$ be a finite, connected graph. A perfect matching of $G$ is a set of edges that covers every vertex exactly once. The graph $G$ is matching covered if it is connected, has at least one edge, and every edge of $G$ lies in some perfect matching of $G$.

A cut $\partial(X)$ of $G$ is the set of edges with exactly one endpoint in $X \subseteq V(G)$. The set $X$ and its complement $\overline{X}=V(G)\setminus X$ are called the shores of the cut. A cut $\partial(X)$ is trivial if $|X|=1$ or $|\overline{X}|=1$. A cut $\partial(X)$ is tight if every perfect matching of $G$ contains exactly one edge of $\partial(X)$. A cut $\partial(X)$ is separating if both graphs $G/X$ and $G/\overline{X}$ obtained from $G$ by contracting one shore to a single vertex are matching covered.

A brick is a non-bipartite matching covered graph that has no non-trivial tight cuts. A matching covered graph is solid if every separating cut is tight; equivalently, a brick is solid if and only if it has no non-trivial separating cuts.

Address the following:

(a) Provide a complete structural characterization of all solid bricks.

(b) Determine the computational complexity of the decision problem: given a brick $G$, decide whether $G$ is solid. In particular, decide whether this problem is in NP, and whether it is solvable in polynomial time.

The complete characterization of solid bricks and the complexity status of recognizing solid bricks remain open as of 2026. Partial results exist: claw-free solid bricks have been characterized (Graphs and Combinatorics, 2025), the only simple planar solid bricks are odd wheels, and the perfect matching polytope of a brick can be described without odd-set constraints iff it is solid. A SIAM J. Discrete Math. paper "On Two Unsolved Problems Concerning Matching Covered Graphs" addresses these problems but does not resolve them in general.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions and consider $\mathbb{H}^n$ with coordinates $q_\ell = x_{0\ell} + i x_{1\ell} + j x_{2\ell} + k x_{3\ell}$, $\ell = 1,\dots,n$. The Cauchy–Fueter operator in the $\ell$-th variable is
$$\partial_\ell = \partial_{x_{0\ell}} + i\,\partial_{x_{1\ell}} + j\,\partial_{x_{2\ell}} + k\,\partial_{x_{3\ell}}.$$
A function $f:\Omega\subset\mathbb{H}^n\to\mathbb{H}$ is (left) Cauchy–Fueter regular if $\partial_\ell f = 0$ for all $\ell$. Writing the system in matrix form $P\,f=0$ where $P$ is the $n\times 1$ column of Fueter operators (after identifying $\mathbb{H}\cong\mathbb{R}^4$), one obtains a finite free resolution of the associated module over the polynomial ring $\mathbb{R}[x_{\mu\ell}]$:
$$0 \to F_N \xrightarrow{Q} F_{N-1} \to \cdots \to F_1 \xrightarrow{P} F_0,$$
in which $Q$ denotes the last (highest) syzygy matrix in the Cauchy–Fueter complex. Let $\mathcal{R}$ be the sheaf on $\mathbb{H}^n$ of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions (the sheaf of solutions of $P$), and let $\mathcal{B}^Q$ be the sheaf of hyperfunction solutions of the system defined by $Q$. For $n=2$, $Q$ is again a Cauchy–Fueter-type operator and $\mathcal{B}^Q$ may be identified with the sheaf of anti-regular hyperfunctions. For $n\ge 3$, $P$ and $Q$ have the same characteristic variety but $Q$ is no longer a simple Fueter-type operator.

Problem: For every $n\ge 2$, describe explicitly the relationship between the sheaves $\mathcal{R}$ and $\mathcal{B}^Q$ on $\mathbb{H}^n$.

Definitions. Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A perfect matching of $G$ is a set of edges such that every vertex is incident to exactly one edge of the set. A graph $G$ with at least one edge is matching covered if it is connected and every edge of $G$ lies in some perfect matching. A nontrivial edge cut $C$ of a matching covered graph $G$ is tight if every perfect matching of $G$ contains exactly one edge of $C$. A matching covered graph is a brace if it is bipartite and has no nontrivial tight cut, and a brick if it is non-bipartite, 3-connected, and has no nontrivial tight cut other than the trivial cuts $\partial(v)$ at vertices. Equivalently (by a theorem of Edmonds, Lovász, and Pulleyblank), a 3-connected non-bipartite matching covered graph is a brick iff for every two distinct vertices $u, v$, the graph $G - \{u, v\}$ has a perfect matching. A brick $G$ is solid if for every two vertex-disjoint odd cycles $C_1, C_2$ of $G$, the graph $G - V(C_1) - V(C_2)$ has no perfect matching. A graph is cubic (3-regular) if every vertex has degree exactly 3. A graph is odd-intercyclic if every two odd cycles in it share at least one common vertex.

Question. Is every cubic solid brick odd-intercyclic? That is, does there exist a 3-regular solid brick containing two vertex-disjoint odd cycles, or must every such graph have the property that every pair of odd cycles meets in at least one vertex?

Let $\mathbb{H}^n \cong \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ denote the space of $n$-tuples of quaternions, and let $\mathcal{R}$ be the sheaf on $\mathbb{H}^n$ of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions, i.e. functions $f:\mathbb{H}^n\to\mathbb{H}$ that are annihilated coordinate-wise by the Cauchy–Fueter operator $\partial_{\bar q_i}=\partial_{x_i^0}+i\,\partial_{x_i^1}+j\,\partial_{x_i^2}+k\,\partial_{x_i^3}$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. For a closed subset $S\subset\mathbb{H}^n$, let $\mathcal{H}^j_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R})$ denote the $j$-th local cohomology of $\mathcal{R}$ with support in $S$.

Construct a real-analytic (or semi-analytic) subvariety $S\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ of real dimension $2n+1$ such that
$$\mathcal{H}^j_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R}) = 0 \quad \text{for all } j\neq 2n-1, \qquad \mathcal{H}^{2n-1}_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R}) \neq 0.$$

This is the quaternionic analogue of the classical purity result stating that $\mathbb{R}^n\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is purely $n$-codimensional with respect to the sheaf $\mathcal{O}$ of holomorphic functions.

The case $n=2$ (i.e. 5-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^2$) has been addressed by Colombo–Damiano–Sabadini–Struppa, who constructed quaternionic hyperfunctions on certain 5-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^2$ realizing the expected pure codimensionality with respect to $\mathcal{R}$. Background and definitions. A graph $G$ is called matching covered if it is connected, has at least one edge, and every edge of $G$ lies in some perfect matching. A 3-connected matching covered graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge 4$ is called a brick if, for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V(G)$, the graph $G-\{u,v\}$ has a perfect matching.

Given matching covered graphs $G$ and $J$, we say that $J$ is a conformal minor of $G$ if a graph isomorphic to $J$ can be obtained from $G$ by a sequence of the following operations applied so that the resulting graph remains matching covered at every step: (i) deleting an edge whose two endpoints are matched to each other in some perfect matching together with another perfect matching avoiding that edge (more precisely, taking a "conformal" subgraph: a subgraph $H$ such that $G-V(H)$ has a perfect matching), and (ii) bicontracting a degree-two vertex (replacing a vertex of degree two by an edge joining its two neighbors). Equivalently, $J$ is a conformal minor of $G$ if and only if $G$ contains a matching covered subgraph $H$ with $V(G)\setminus V(H)$ admitting a perfect matching, and $J$ can be obtained from $H$ by repeatedly bicontracting degree-two vertices.

For a fixed matching covered graph $J$, a matching covered graph $G$ is called $J$-based if $J$ is a conformal minor of $G$, and $J$-free otherwise.

Let $K_4$ denote the complete graph on $4$ vertices.

Problem. Give a complete structural characterization of all $K_4$-free bricks, i.e., describe all bricks $G$ such that $K_4$ is not a conformal minor of $G$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The general characterization of K4-free bricks remains open. Kothari and Murty characterized K4-free planar bricks (a planar brick is K4-free iff it has exactly two odd faces), and partial results exist for special classes (e.g., PM-compact K4-free bricks, claw-free solid bricks, essentially 4-edge-connected cubic bricks, K4-free planar minimal bricks). The nonplanar case is explicitly noted as unsolved in subsequent literature.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions, and consider $\mathbb{H}^2$ as an 8-dimensional real vector space. A smooth $\mathbb{H}$-valued function $f$ on an open set $U\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ with quaternionic coordinates $q_1=x_0^{(1)}+ix_1^{(1)}+jx_2^{(1)}+kx_3^{(1)}$ and $q_2=x_0^{(2)}+ix_1^{(2)}+jx_2^{(2)}+kx_3^{(2)}$ is called (left) Cauchy–Fueter regular if it satisfies the system
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0^{(\ell)}}+i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1^{(\ell)}}+j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2^{(\ell)}}+k\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_3^{(\ell)}}=0,\qquad \ell=1,2.$$

A compact subset $K\subset U$ is said to be a removable singularity for Cauchy–Fueter regular functions if every Cauchy–Fueter regular function on $U\setminus K$ extends to a Cauchy–Fueter regular function on all of $U$.

It is known that any compact subset $K$ contained in a real affine subspace of $\mathbb{H}^2$ of (real) dimension $6$, $7$, or $8$ is removable, while real dimension $4$ does not allow such a removability statement. The dimension $5$ case is not accessible by purely algebraic methods (Ext-module computations on the associated module over the Cauchy–Fueter complex).

Question: Is it true that every compact subset $K\subset U\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ contained in a $5$-dimensional real affine subspace of $\mathbb{H}^2$ is a removable singularity for Cauchy–Fueter regular functions?

Background and definitions:
- A graph is matching covered if it is connected, has at least one edge, and every edge belongs to some perfect matching.
- A brick is a 3-connected matching covered graph G such that for any two distinct vertices u and v, the graph G − {u, v} has a perfect matching (equivalently, a non-bipartite matching covered graph that is free of nontrivial tight cuts).
- For a matching covered graph G with a perfect matching, a subgraph H of G is conformal in G if G − V(H) has a perfect matching.
- Given matching covered graphs J and G, J is a conformal minor of G if G has a conformal subgraph that can be obtained from a subdivision of J by bi-subdividing some edges (i.e., subdividing an edge an even number of times so that subdivisions can be absorbed by perfect matchings).
- For a fixed matching covered graph J, a matching covered graph G is called J-based if J is a conformal minor of G; otherwise G is called J-free.
- Let C6 denote the triangular prism, that is, the complement of the 6-cycle, equivalently the 3-prism K3 □ K2.

Problem: Provide a complete structural characterization of all bricks G such that the triangular prism C6 is not a conformal minor of G; equivalently, describe explicitly the class of C6-free bricks.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions and consider the Cauchy–Fueter operator in $n$ variables. For a quaternionic variable $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$, define
$$\bar\partial_{CF} = \frac{\partial}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial}{\partial x_3}.$$
For $n$ quaternionic variables $q_1,\dots,q_n$, let $P(D)$ be the linear constant-coefficient differential operator (with values in a suitable free $\mathbb{H}$-module) whose components are $\bar\partial_{CF,\ell}$ ($\ell=1,\dots,n$), so that the homogeneous system $P(D)f = 0$ on an open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ characterizes regular (Fueter-regular) functions of several quaternionic variables.

Recall that, in the Ehrenpreis–Palamodov theory of systems of linear partial differential operators with constant coefficients, an open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is called $P$-convex (for the system $P$) if the cohomology of the associated complex on $\Omega$ vanishes in the appropriate degrees—equivalently, the exactness theorem that holds for convex $\Omega$ continues to hold for $\Omega$. $P$-convexity is strictly weaker than ordinary convexity and is expected to reflect a compatibility between the system $P$ and the topology/geometry of $\Omega$.

Problem. Give a purely geometric characterization of the open sets $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ that are $P$-convex for the Cauchy–Fueter system in $n$ quaternionic variables.

A homogeneous Riemannian manifold is a connected Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ on which a Lie group $G$ acts transitively by isometries; equivalently $M = G/H$ for some closed subgroup $H \le G$ and $g$ is a $G$-invariant Riemannian metric. A geodesic $\gamma$ of $(M,g)$ is called homogeneous (or a $G$-orbit geodesic) if there exist a point $o \in M$, a nonzero element $X$ of the Lie algebra of $G$, and an affine reparametrization $t \mapsto at+b$ such that
$$\gamma(at+b) = \exp(tX)\cdot o \qquad \text{for all } t \in \mathbb{R}.$$
The pair $(G/H, g)$ is called a $G$-g.o. space (geodesic orbit space) if every geodesic of $(M,g)$ is homogeneous in this sense.

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to local isometry, of all homogeneous Riemannian g.o. spaces $(G/H, g)$ of dimension $n$, in the following two cases:
(a) $n = 7$;
(b) $n \ge 8$ (i.e., produce a classification valid in every dimension greater than seven).

In each case the desired output is a complete list of the isometry types (or, equivalently, of the admissible triples consisting of a connected Lie group $G$, a closed subgroup $H$, and an invariant Riemannian metric $g$ on $G/H$) that yield Riemannian g.o. spaces of the given dimension, together with proofs that the list is exhaustive.

$$\overline{\partial}_\ell =  rac{\partial}{\partial x_0^{(\ell)}} + i rac{\partial}{\partial x_1^{(\ell)}} + j rac{\partial}{\partial x_2^{(\ell)}} + k rac{\partial}{\partial x_3^{(\ell)}},\qquad \ell=1,\dots,n,$$
and let $\mathcal{F}(U)$ denote the corresponding space of quaternionic hyperfunctions on $U$.

Construct an associative $\mathbb{R}$-algebra $A_1(\mathbb{H})=\mathbb{H}[x,\partial]$, called the quaternionic Weyl algebra, generated by quaternionic ``variables'' $x_1,\dots,x_n$ and quaternionic ``derivations'' $\partial_1,\dots,\partial_n$ together with quaternionic scalar coefficients, such that:

(i) the algebra correctly encodes the double noncommutativity inherent in the situation, namely the noncommutativity of the quaternionic coefficients and the noncommutativity between the variables and the differential operators;

(ii) the algebra acts naturally on $\mathcal{R}(U)$ and on $\mathcal{F}(U)$, endowing each of them with the structure of an $A_1(\mathbb{H})$-module;

(iii) the algebra is suitable for the algebraic analysis of overdetermined systems of linear differential equations with quaternionic coefficients in the sense of Ehrenpreis–Palamodov, so that homological methods (resolutions, syzygies, Ext-modules) can be developed within it.

Let $(M=G/H, g)$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a point $o\in M$. A geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ through $o$ is called a homogeneous geodesic (or a geodesic orbit of $G$) if it is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$, that is, $\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\cdot o$ for some $X\in\mathfrak g=\mathrm{Lie}(G)$. Such an $X$ is called a geodesic vector. The space $(M,g)$ is called a geodesic orbit space (g.o. space) if every geodesic of $(M,g)$ is homogeneous; otherwise it is non-g.o.

Standard algebraic criteria (e.g. the geodesic lemma of Kowalski–Vanhecke) reduce the determination of geodesic vectors to solving a system of polynomial equations on $\mathfrak g$ (or on a reductive complement $\mathfrak m$ with $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak m$), but solving these equations and enumerating all homogeneous geodesics in concrete non-g.o. examples is computationally expensive.

Problem: For a homogeneous Riemannian manifold $(G/H,g)$ that is not a geodesic orbit space, provide an explicit (closed-form) description of all its homogeneous geodesics through the origin — i.e., an explicit characterization of the set of geodesic vectors $X\in\mathfrak g$ — that goes beyond merely reducing the question to the algebraic system given by the geodesic lemma and beyond brute-force computational searches.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions, and let $f:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{H}$ be (left) regular in the sense of Cauchy–Fueter, i.e. it satisfies
$$\overline{D}f := \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_3} = 0.$$
For each multi-index $\nu$, let $P_\nu(q)$ denote the Fueter homogeneous regular polynomials (the symmetrized products of the Fueter variables $\zeta_\ell = x_\ell - x_0 e_\ell$, $\ell=1,2,3$), and let
$$E(q,\xi) := \sum_{\nu} P_\nu(q)\,\frac{(i\xi)^{|\nu|}}{|\nu|!}\cdot(\text{coefficients})$$
be the regular quaternionic exponential built from the $P_\nu$. The space of $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions on an open set $U\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is defined as boundary values, modulo regular functions, of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions on appropriate complex neighbourhoods, yielding a sheaf analogous to Sato's hyperfunctions but built from the kernel of $\overline{D}$.

Define the regular Fourier transform $\widehat{T}(\xi)$ of a compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunction $T$ by
$$\widehat{T}(\xi) := \langle T_q, E(q,\xi)\rangle,\qquad \xi\in\mathbb{H}.$$

Problem. Establish a Paley–Wiener theorem characterizing the image of the space of compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions under this regular Fourier transform: namely, identify $\widehat{T}$ with an explicitly described space of $\mathbb{H}$-valued entire functions on $\mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{C}}$ of exponential type, with the type bounded by the radius of a ball containing the support of $T$, together with appropriate growth conditions on the real axis reflecting that $T$ is a hyperfunction (rather than a distribution).

Let $(M=G/K, g)$ be a connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively and almost effectively by isometries on $M$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a point $o \in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{k}$ denote the Lie algebras of $G$ and $K$, and let $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ be a reductive decomposition, i.e.\ an $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement $\mathfrak{m}$ of $\mathfrak{k}$ in $\mathfrak{g}$, identified with $T_o M$.

Recall:
\begin{itemize}
\item $(M,g)$ is called a \emph{geodesic orbit space} (g.o.\ space) with respect to $G$ if every geodesic of $(M,g)$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$, equivalently, for every $X \in \mathfrak{m}$ there exists $A \in \mathfrak{k}$ such that $[A+X, Y]_{\mathfrak{m}} \cdot \langle X, X\rangle$-related geodesic-orbit condition holds, namely $\langle [A+X,Y]_{\mathfrak{m}}, X\rangle = 0$ for all $Y \in \mathfrak{m}$.
\item $(M,g)$ is called \emph{naturally reductive} with respect to the pair $(G,\mathfrak{m})$ if there exists a reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ such that $\langle [X,Y]_{\mathfrak{m}}, Z\rangle + \langle Y, [X,Z]_{\mathfrak{m}}\rangle = 0$ for all $X,Y,Z \in \mathfrak{m}$.
\item $(M,g)$ is said to be \emph{naturally reductive in some presentation} if there exists some transitive group $G'$ of isometries of $(M,g)$, with isotropy $K'$ and reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g}' = \mathfrak{k}' \oplus \mathfrak{m}'$, with respect to which $(M,g)$ is naturally reductive.
\end{itemize}

Both the g.o.\ property and the naturally reductive property a priori depend on the chosen coset presentation $M = G/K$ and the chosen $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$.

Problem. Develop a representation-independent criterion, formulated intrinsically on $(M,g)$ (i.e.\ not referring to a particular choice of transitive isometry group $G$ or of reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$), proving that the geodesic-orbit property of $(M,g)$ is independent of:
(a) the choice of transitive group of isometries $G$ presenting $M$ as a coset space $G/K$, and
(b) the choice of $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$.

In particular, give an intrinsic obstruction that certifies that a given homogeneous Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is in no way naturally reductive (i.e.\ not naturally reductive with respect to any presentation $G'/K'$ and any reductive decomposition), while still being a g.o.\ space with respect to some presentation.

The general classification of Riemannian geodesic orbit manifolds is a longstanding open problem, and the literature consistently emphasizes that the g.o.\ and naturally reductive properties are studied relative to a fixed presentation $G/K$ and reductive decomposition; representation-independent criteria are typically established only case-by-case (e.g.\ for specific spaces or families like compact rank-two Lie groups, simple isotropy, or nilmanifolds). Background. A quaternion-valued function f of a quaternionic variable q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k is called (left) Cauchy–Fueter regular on an open set U ⊂ H if it is C^1 and satisfies the Cauchy–Fueter equation
    (∂/∂x_0 + i ∂/∂x_1 + j ∂/∂x_2 + k ∂/∂x_3) f = 0   on U.
Building on this notion, one can develop a theory of quaternionic hyperfunctions: a hyperfunction on a real domain Ω ⊂ R^n (n ≤ 4) embedded in H is represented as an equivalence class of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions defined on a complex/quaternionic neighborhood minus Ω, modulo regular functions on the full neighborhood, so that every such hyperfunction admits an interpretation as a boundary value of a regular quaternionic function.

In quaternionic quantum mechanics, observable quantities (in particular the entries of the scattering matrix S) are quaternion-valued, and physicists construct S via a formal series analogue of the complex exponential exp(z) = Σ z^n / n!, applied to a quaternionic "Hamiltonian" expression. The resulting formal quaternionic exponential is not, in general, a Cauchy–Fueter regular function of its quaternionic argument.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following: every entry of the quaternionic scattering matrix in quaternionic quantum mechanics can be realized as the boundary value of a Cauchy–Fueter regular quaternionic function in the sense of quaternionic hyperfunctions. In particular, decide whether the non-regularity of the formal quaternionic exponential used to construct S is a genuine obstruction or can be circumvented by an alternative regular representation.

Let $(M = G/K, g)$ be a pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, $K$ is a closed subgroup with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{k}$, and $g$ is a $G$-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metric on $M$. Fix a reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ (so $\mathrm{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m} \subseteq \mathfrak{m}$), and let $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ denote the (possibly indefinite) $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant scalar product on $\mathfrak{m}$ induced by $g_o$ at the origin $o = eK$. Define the associated operator $\Lambda : \mathfrak{m} \to \mathfrak{m}$ by the relation
$$\langle \Lambda x, y \rangle = \tfrac{1}{2}\langle x, [a,y]_{\mathfrak{m}} \rangle + \tfrac{1}{2}\langle [a,x]_{\mathfrak{m}}, y \rangle$$
suitably extended so that the standard Riemannian formula relating $\Lambda$ to the Levi-Civita connection holds in the pseudo-Riemannian setting.

Address the following two questions.

(1) (Single exponential factor.) For $a \in \mathfrak{k}$ and $x \in \mathfrak{m}$, prove or disprove: the orbit $\gamma(t) = \exp(t(a+x)) \cdot o$ is a geodesic of $(M, g)$ if and only if
$$[a+x, \Lambda x] \in \mathfrak{k}.$$

(2) (Product of three exponential factors.) For $X, Y, Z \in \mathfrak{m}$, let
$$\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\exp(tY)\exp(tZ) \cdot o,$$
and let $T : \mathbb{R} \to \mathrm{Aut}(\mathfrak{g})$ be defined by $T(t) = \mathrm{Ad}(\exp(-tZ)\exp(-tY))$. Determine whether $\gamma$ is a geodesic of $(M, g)$ through $o$ if and only if, for every $W \in \mathfrak{m}$, the analogue $G_W(t)$ of the corresponding Riemannian function (built from $\langle \cdot, \cdot\rangle$, $T(t)$, and the brackets of $X, Y, Z$) vanishes identically in $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

In other words: extend the Lie-algebraic geodesic-orbit characterizations valid for Riemannian homogeneous manifolds to arbitrary pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifolds $(G/K, g)$, identifying any modifications needed when $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is indefinite.

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

There is active research on geodesic orbit pseudo-Riemannian manifolds (Lorentz, trans-Lorentz, and H-type signatures), and Lie-algebraic characterizations have been extended in several special cases (e.g., nilmanifolds of signature (n−2,2), Clifford-module H-type nilmanifolds). However, no single source clearly establishes the precise pseudo-Riemannian analogues of both the one-parameter-subgroup criterion $[a+x,\Lambda x]\in\mathfrak{k}$ and the three-factor product geodesic criterion in full generality. The general extension appears to be partially addressed but not definitively settled.

Let $(M=G/H, g)$ be a Riemannian homogeneous space, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries and $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a point $o\in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ denote the Lie algebra of $G$ and $\pi:G\to G/H$ the natural projection. A smooth curve $\gamma$ in $M$ through $o$ is called a homogeneous geodesic if it is a geodesic of $(M,g)$ and admits a parametrization of the form $\gamma(t)=\pi(\exp(tX))$ for some $X\in\mathfrak{g}$. More generally, for an integer $k\ge 2$, call a curve a $k$-step homogeneous geodesic if it is a geodesic of $(M,g)$ that admits, up to affine reparametrization, a representation of the form
$$\gamma(t)=\pi\big(\exp(tX_1)\exp(tX_2)\cdots\exp(tX_k)\big)$$
for some $X_1,\dots,X_k\in\mathfrak{g}$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: For every Riemannian homogeneous space $(G/H,g)$ and every integer $k\ge 3$, the existence problem for $k$-step homogeneous geodesics reduces to that of $2$-step homogeneous geodesics, in the sense that any geodesic representable as a product of $k\ge 3$ one-parameter exponential factors as above is also representable (up to affine reparametrization) as a $2$-step homogeneous geodesic, so no essentially new geodesics arise from allowing three or more exponential factors.

The reduction of $k$-step ($k\ge 3$) homogeneous geodesics to the two-step case is stated as a conjecture in the literature on two-step homogeneous geodesics in Riemannian and Finsler homogeneous spaces. Subsequent works (e.g., on two-step homogeneous geodesics in homogeneous Finsler manifolds) continue to study the two-step setting without reporting a proof or counterexample to the higher-step reduction, suggesting the question remains open.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the real algebra of quaternions with basis $1,i,j,k$, and consider functions $f=f_0+if_1+jf_2+kf_3:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{H}$ of three real variables $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$. The Moisil–Theodoresco operator is the first-order linear differential operator
$$ M f \;=\; i\,\partial_{x_1} f + j\,\partial_{x_2} f + k\,\partial_{x_3} f, $$
and a function $f$ is called Moisil–Theodoresco regular when $Mf=0$. For several variables, consider $N$ copies $(x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(N)})\in(\mathbb{R}^3)^N$ with corresponding operators $M_1,\dots,M_N$, and let $\mathcal{R}$ denote the system $M_1 f = \dots = M_N f = 0$ acting on $\mathbb{H}$-valued functions of $3N$ real variables. Viewing $\mathcal{R}$ as a left module over the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{R}[\xi^{(1)},\dots,\xi^{(N)}]$ obtained by symbol/Fourier transform (so $\partial_{x_\ell^{(m)}}\mapsto \xi_\ell^{(m)}$), perform the full algebraic analysis of this system. Specifically:

(i) Determine a minimal free resolution of the $R$-module $M_N := R^r / R^s A$ associated with the Moisil–Theodoresco system in $N$ variables, and identify the syzygies and compatibility conditions of the system.

(ii) Compute the Ext groups $\operatorname{Ext}^p_R(M_N,R)$ for all $p\geq 0$, and characterize the cohomological dimension and the projective dimension of $M_N$.

(iii) Use the resulting resolution to deduce the analytic properties of regular functions of several Moisil–Theodoresco variables: removability of compact singularities, Hartogs-type extension phenomena, the structure of the sheaf of solutions, and the dimensions of cohomology groups on suitable domains in $(\mathbb{R}^3)^N$.

(iv) Compare the results with those known for the Cauchy–Fueter system in several quaternionic variables, and describe explicitly the natural regular extensions of solutions to $\mathbb{H}^N$-valued Cauchy–Fueter regular functions.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Structural results for the Moisil–Theodoresco system in a single ℝ³ variable (resolution, structure theorem for solutions, right inverse, div-rot solvability) have been obtained, e.g., by Reyes (2008) and by Colombo–Luna-Elizarrarás–Sabadini–Shapiro–Struppa. Parts of the algebraic-analysis program (syzygies, Ext modules, cohomology) have been carried out in the one-variable case, but a complete several-variables treatment parallel to the Cauchy–Fueter system program does not appear to be fully published.

Setup. Work in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with coordinates $(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)$. The (left) Cauchy–Fueter operator acting on quaternion-valued functions $f = f_0 + f_1 i + f_2 j + f_3 k$ is
$$D_{CF} f \;=\; \partial_{x_0} f + i\,\partial_{x_1} f + j\,\partial_{x_2} f + k\,\partial_{x_3} f,$$
and a function is (left) Fueter regular when $D_{CF}f=0$. In several quaternionic variables $q^{(1)},\dots,q^{(n)} \in \mathbb{H}$, the Cauchy–Fueter system is the overdetermined system $D^{(\ell)}_{CF} f = 0$ for $\ell=1,\dots,n$, where $D^{(\ell)}_{CF}$ is the Cauchy–Fueter operator in the $\ell$-th quaternionic variable.

The Moisil–Theodoresco system in $\mathbb{R}^3$ acts on functions $W:\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}\oplus \mathbb{R}^3$, $W = W_0 + W_1 e_1 + W_2 e_2 + W_3 e_3$, by
$$\partial W \;=\; \big(e_1\partial_{x_1} + e_2\partial_{x_2} + e_3\partial_{x_3}\big) W \;=\; 0,$$
equivalently $\operatorname{div}\vec W=0$ and $\operatorname{grad}W_0+\operatorname{curl}\vec W=0$. Its several-variables version is the overdetermined system obtained by imposing this Dirac-type equation in each of $n$ groups of three real variables.

By "algebraic analysis" of such an overdetermined system one means the study, via commutative algebra and $\mathcal{D}$-module techniques, of the associated module $M = \mathcal{R}^p/\mathcal{R}^q P$ over the polynomial ring $\mathcal{R} = \mathbb{C}[\xi]$ (or the corresponding ring of differential operators), including its syzygies, its free resolution, the cohomology of the resulting complex, the characteristic variety, and the resulting compatibility conditions, removable singularities theorems, Hartogs-type phenomena, and Ext-module obstructions.

Problem. Determine whether information obtained by applying algebraic analysis (free resolutions, syzygies, characteristic varieties, Ext-modules, and the associated cohomological invariants) to the Moisil–Theodoresco system in several variables can be transferred to yield analogous information about the Cauchy–Fueter system in several quaternionic variables. Concretely, exhibit either:
(a) a functorial/algebraic correspondence between the $\mathcal{R}$-modules associated to the two systems that transports free resolutions and Ext-modules from one to the other, together with the resulting analytic consequences (e.g. removable singularities, Hartogs phenomena, structure of compatibility conditions) for Cauchy–Fueter; or
(b) an obstruction proving that no such transfer is possible.

representations.normalized:
Consider the single-machine scheduling problem defined as follows. There is a single machine that can process at most one job at a time, and a set J of n jobs. Each job j ∈ J has:
- a processing time p_j ∈ ℕ,
- a due date d_j ∈ ℕ, and
- a nonnegative weight w_j ∈ ℕ.

A schedule assigns to each job j a completion time C_j so that the jobs do not overlap on the machine and no job is preempted (each job is processed contiguously for p_j time units). The tardiness of job j is T_j := max{0, C_j − d_j}, and the objective is to minimize the total weighted tardiness

    Σ_{j ∈ J} w_j · T_j.

Let p_max := max_{j ∈ J} p_j denote the maximum processing time among the jobs.

Question: Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max? Equivalently, does there exist a computable function f and a constant c such that an optimal schedule can be computed in time f(p_max) · n^c on every input of size n?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A literature search did not turn up any FPT algorithm for 1||Σw_jT_j parameterized by p_max. Lawler's classical pseudopolynomial algorithm runs in time O(n^4 · Σp_j) ⊆ O(n^5 · p_max), placing the problem in XP for this parameter, but this does not yield fixed-parameter tractability. Recent surveys on the parameterized complexity of single-machine scheduling continue to list FPT-status with respect to p_max for the weighted tardiness objective among the unresolved questions, so the problem appears to still be open.

Let $A$ be a hypercomplex algebra, i.e., a finite-dimensional unital real algebra equipped with a basis $\{e_0=1,e_1,\dots,e_{n}\}$ satisfying prescribed multiplication relations (examples include the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$, the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes\mathbb{C}$, and the octonions $\mathbb{O}$). For functions $f:\mathbb{R}^{p,q}	o A$ on a (possibly indefinite) real space, consider first-order linear differential operators of the form
$$D=\sum_{j=0}^{m} a_j\,\partial_{x_j},\qquad a_j\in A,$$
or more generally finite families $(D_1,\dots,D_r)$ of such operators with coefficients in $A$. representations.normalized:
Consider the single-machine scheduling problem with precedence constraints and weighted sum of completion times, denoted 1|prec|∑ w_j C_j. The input consists of a set of jobs J = {1, …, n}, where each job j has a positive integer processing time p_j and a positive integer weight w_j, together with a partial order ≺ on J expressing precedence constraints. A feasible schedule is a sequence of the jobs on a single machine that processes them non-preemptively, one at a time, and respects the precedence: if i ≺ j then job i must complete before job j starts. The completion time C_j of job j in a schedule is the time at which the machine finishes processing j. The objective value of a schedule is ∑_{j∈J} w_j C_j, and OPT denotes the minimum objective value over all feasible schedules.

The natural linear programming relaxation of this problem is the completion-time LP:
  minimize ∑_{j∈J} w_j C_j
  subject to
   C_j ≥ p_j for all j ∈ J,
   C_j ≥ C_i + p_j whenever i ≺ j,
   for every subset S ⊆ J, ∑_{j∈S} p_j C_j ≥ (1/2)·[(∑_{j∈S} p_j)^2 + ∑_{j∈S} p_j^2].
Let LP denote the optimal value of this relaxation, and define the parameter k := OPT − LP (a non-negative integer when inputs are integral, after suitable rounding).

A kernelization for a parameterized problem is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given an instance I with parameter k, outputs an equivalent instance I' (with parameter k' ≤ k) whose total bit-size is bounded by some computable function of k alone; the kernel has polynomial size if this bound is a polynomial in k.

Question: Does 1|prec|∑ w_j C_j, parameterized by k = OPT − LP, admit a polynomial kernel?

representations.normalized:
Consider first-order linear constant-coefficient differential operators $D$ acting on functions $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to A^k$ taking values in a real associative *-algebra $A$ (for example, the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$ or a Clifford algebra) with the property that $D$ "linearizes" a wave-type operator, in the sense that there exists a companion operator $\overline{D}$ such that the composition $\overline{D}\,D$ equals (a scalar multiple of) a wave operator
$$\Box = -\partial_{t}^{2} + \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\varepsilon_j\,\partial_{x_j}^{2},\qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\},$$
on $\mathbb{R}^{1,n-1}$. Such operators arise as hypercomplex/Clifford-algebraic square roots of indefinite-signature Laplacians (Cauchy–Fueter–type operators in Lorentzian or split signatures).

The problem is twofold:

(a) Construct an explicit fundamental solution $E$ of $D$, i.e., an $A$-valued distribution on $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying $D E = \delta_0$, in a form analogous to the Cauchy–Fueter kernel of the elliptic case.

(b) Derive integral representation formulas (of Cauchy type) reproducing every sufficiently regular function $f$ in the kernel $\ker D$ on a suitable domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ from its boundary values, via an integral kernel built from $E$.

representations.normalized:
Consider the following single-machine scheduling problems. We are given a set J of n jobs, where each job j ∈ J has a processing time p_j ∈ ℕ, a release date r_j ∈ ℕ (job j cannot start before time r_j), a due date d_j ∈ ℕ, and (in the weighted version) a weight w_j ∈ ℕ. A schedule assigns each job a non-preemptive starting time s_j ≥ r_j on a single machine such that the time intervals [s_j, s_j + p_j) are pairwise disjoint. Let C_j = s_j + p_j be the completion time of job j, and define the indicator U_j = 0 if C_j ≤ d_j and U_j = 1 otherwise.

The two problems of interest are:
(a) 1|r_j|∑U_j: minimize ∑_{j∈J} U_j (the number of late jobs);
(b) 1|r_j|∑w_j U_j: minimize ∑_{j∈J} w_j U_j (the weighted number of late jobs).

Let p_max = max_{j∈J} p_j. Determine whether problems (a) and (b), when parameterized by p_max, are W[1]-hard.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional real hypercomplex algebra (i.e., a unital associative real algebra generated by a finite set of "imaginary" units, such as the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$, the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C}$, or a Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q)$). Suppose one has fixed a notion of $A$-regularity for functions $f:\Omega\subset A^n\to A$, meaning a first-order constant-coefficient linear differential operator $D_A^{(n)}$ (a Cauchy–Fueter type operator) such that the $A$-regular functions of $n$ variables are exactly the solutions of $D_A^{(n)} f=0$.

Problem. Find a hypercomplex algebra $C$ (depending on $A$ and $n$) together with a Cauchy–Fueter–type operator $D_C^{(1)}$ defining a notion of $C$-regularity for functions $g:\Omega'\subset C\to C$ of a single $C$-variable, and an embedding/identification
$$\iota:A^n \hookrightarrow C, \qquad \pi:C\to A,$$
such that every $A$-regular function $f:\Omega\to A$ of $n$ variables arises as $f = \pi\circ g\circ \iota$ for some $C$-regular function $g$ of one $C$-variable, and conversely the pullback of every $C$-regular $g$ yields an $A$-regular $f$.

As motivating instances, one requires that:
(i) when $A=\mathbb{H}$ and $n=2$, the algebra $C$ may be taken to be the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C}$, with an appropriate one-variable regularity;
(ii) alternatively, $C$ may be taken to be a suitable Clifford algebra, again with a one-variable Cauchy–Fueter–type regularity recovering the two-quaternionic-variable Fueter-regular functions.

Determine such an algebra $C$ and one-variable regularity for general $A$ and $n\ge 2$.

Consider the following single-machine scheduling problem. We are given a set of jobs $J = \{1,2,\dots,n\}$, where each job $j \in J$ has a positive integer processing time $p_j$. A schedule assigns to each job $j$ a start time $S_j \ge 0$ such that the jobs are processed non-preemptively on a single machine without overlap; the completion time of job $j$ is $C_j = S_j + p_j$. We are also given a set $F = \{t_1, t_2, \dots, t_\tau\}$ of $\tau$ nonnegative integers, called forbidden instants. A schedule is feasible if and only if, for every job $j \in J$ and every $t \in F$, $S_j \ne t$ and $C_j \ne t$ (i.e., no job may start at a forbidden instant and no job may complete at a forbidden instant). The objective is to minimize the makespan $C_{\max} = \max_{j \in J} C_j$.

Question: Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by $\tau$? Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm solving every instance in time $f(\tau) \cdot \mathrm{poly}(|I|)$ for some computable function $f$, where $|I|$ is the input size?

Let $\mathbb{O}$ denote the algebra of octonions, a real non-associative normed division algebra of dimension $8$ with standard basis $\{e_0=1,e_1,\dots,e_7\}$. A smooth function $f:\mathbb{R}^8\cong\mathbb{O}\to\mathbb{O}$ is called (left) octonionic regular if it lies in the kernel of the Cauchy–Fueter–Cayley operator
$$D = \sum_{i=0}^{7} e_i\,\partial_{x_i}.$$
For $n\ge 2$, consider functions $f:\mathbb{O}^n\to\mathbb{O}$ of several octonion variables and the system $D_1 f = \cdots = D_n f = 0$, where $D_k$ is the Cauchy–Fueter–Cayley operator applied to the $k$-th octonion variable.

(a) Develop a coherent theory of regular functions of several octonion variables based on the overdetermined system above (define an appropriate sheaf $\mathcal{R}$ of such regular functions on $\mathbb{O}^n$ and establish its basic homological/analytic properties).

(b) Compute the flabby dimension of the sheaf $\mathcal{R}$, i.e., the smallest integer $d\ge 0$ such that $\mathcal{R}$ admits a resolution of length $d$ by flabby sheaves.

(c) Construct an analogue of the Moisil–Theodoresco operator in this several-variable octonionic setting and identify regular functions as solutions of the corresponding first-order system.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Consider the scheduling problem P||C_max defined as follows. There are m identical parallel machines and a collection of jobs to be assigned to machines so that each job is processed on exactly one machine without interruption, and each machine processes at most one job at a time. The makespan of a schedule is the maximum, over all machines, of the total processing time of jobs assigned to that machine; the goal is to minimize the makespan.

An instance is specified in high-multiplicity encoding: there are p distinct processing-time values p_1, p_2, ..., p_p ∈ ℕ, and for each i ∈ {1, ..., p} a multiplicity n_i ∈ ℕ giving the number of jobs with processing time p_i. The number m of machines and all values p_i and n_i are encoded in binary, so the input size is O(p · (log m + max_i log p_i + max_i log n_i)).

Question: Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p? Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm that, given any such instance, computes an optimal makespan in time f(p) · |I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f, where |I| denotes the binary input length?

Consider the scheduling problem defined as follows. We are given a set of n jobs, each with unit processing time (p_j = 1), and a partial order ≺ on the jobs encoding precedence constraints: a job j may start only after every job i with i ≺ j has been completed. The jobs must be scheduled non-preemptively on exactly three identical parallel machines, where each machine processes at most one job per time unit and each job must be assigned to a single machine. The objective is to minimize the makespan C_max, i.e., the completion time of the last job.

The width w of a partial order is the maximum size of an antichain, that is, the largest set of pairwise incomparable jobs.

Question: Is the decision version of this scheduling problem (given an integer T, decide whether there is a feasible schedule with C_max ≤ T) fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the width w of the precedence partial order? Equivalently, does there exist a computable function f and a constant c such that the problem can be solved in time f(w) · n^c?

Define a ternary decision diagram (TDD) as a rooted directed acyclic graph in which each nonterminal node is labeled by a Boolean input variable and has exactly three outgoing edges, labeled 0, 1, and *; terminal nodes are labeled 0 or 1. On an input x ∈ {0,1}^n, computation proceeds nondeterministically from the root: at a node labeled x_i, the computation may follow either the edge labeled with the value of x_i or the edge labeled *. The diagram accepts x if at least one such nondeterministic path reaches a terminal labeled 1. (Equivalently, such a TDD represents a sum-of-products formula, where each root-to-1 path corresponds to a product term in which a 0- or 1-edge from a node labeled x_i contributes the literal ¬x_i or x_i and a *-edge from x_i contributes no literal involving x_i.)

Let PolyTDD_SOP denote the class of Boolean function families (f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1}) that are computed by a family of TDDs of size n^{O(1)} in the sense above.

Let l-NL denote the class of languages decidable by nondeterministic Turing machines with a one-way (read-once, left-to-right) input tape and O(log n) work-space.

Address the following:

(a) Provide structural improvements to the standard approach for proving PolyTDD_SOP = l-NL; in particular, establish suitable closure properties of PolyTDD_SOP under logspace-style reductions sufficient to derive the equality, or show such closure cannot hold.

(b) If PolyTDD_SOP ≠ l-NL, exhibit an explicit language L ∈ l-NL (or L ∈ PolyTDD_SOP) that witnesses the separation, i.e., a language whose membership in one class but not the other can be supported.

Consider the following parallel identical machine scheduling setting. We are given m identical machines (all of the same speed) and n jobs. All jobs share a common processing time p ∈ ℕ; that is, each job j requires exactly p time units on whichever machine processes it. Each job j additionally has a release date r_j ∈ ℕ (it cannot be started before time r_j), a due date d_j ∈ ℕ, and (in the weighted version) a weight w_j ∈ ℕ. A schedule assigns each job to exactly one machine and to a start time s_j ≥ r_j; each machine processes at most one job at a time, and once started, a job runs without preemption for p time units. A job j is tardy if s_j + p > d_j, in which case U_j = 1; otherwise U_j = 0.

Define the two decision/optimization problems:
  (A) P | r_j, p_j = p | Σ w_j U_j: minimize Σ_j w_j U_j over all feasible schedules.
  (B) P | r_j, p_j = p | Σ U_j: the unweighted special case, minimizing Σ_j U_j.

A problem is said to be fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) parameterized by k if it can be solved in time f(k) · |I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f, where |I| is the size of the instance.

Question: Are problems (A) and (B), parameterized by the number m of machines, fixed-parameter tractable?

A 2024 paper by Heeger and Molter ("Minimizing the Number of Tardy Jobs with Uniform Processing Times on Parallel Machines", arXiv:2404.14208) shows that the unweighted variant P | r_j, p_j=p | Σ U_j is W[2]-hard when parameterized by the number of machines, hence not FPT under standard complexity assumptions. This resolves the open problem in the negative for both variants (the weighted case (A) generalizes (B)). Positive FPT results are obtained for other parameterizations (e.g., number of machines plus processing time, or number of distinct release/due dates).

Definitions.

(a) A Boolean circuit on n input variables x_1,...,x_n is a directed acyclic graph whose sources (in‑degree 0) are labelled by input variables or constants ("input gates") and whose internal nodes are labelled by Boolean gates from a fixed finite basis. A linear arrangement of the circuit is a bijection of its nodes onto {1,2,...,N}; the cutwidth of a linear arrangement is the maximum, over all i, of the number of edges (u,v) with arrangement‑position(u) ≤ i < arrangement‑position(v). The graph cutwidth of the circuit is the minimum cutwidth over all linear arrangements.

(b) Let l-LogCut denote the class of Boolean functions f = (f_n)_{n≥1} such that there exists a family (C_n) of Boolean circuits of size polynomial in n computing f_n with the following properties:
   (i) each input variable x_i is read by at most one input gate of C_n;
   (ii) there exists a linear arrangement of C_n attaining cutwidth O(log n) in which the input gates appear in the prescribed order x_1, x_2, ..., x_n;
hence "l" indicates the restriction to such ordered linear arrangements with at most one input gate per variable.

(c) A ternary decision diagram (TDD) on variables x_1,...,x_n is a rooted directed acyclic graph in which every internal node is labelled by a variable and has exactly three outgoing edges labelled 0, 1, and *, and every sink is labelled 0 or 1. The function computed by a TDD is defined in the natural way, with the *-edge being followed when the label may be either 0 or 1. A TDD is said to represent a sum‑of‑products (SOP) formula F = T_1 ∨ T_2 ∨ ... ∨ T_m (each T_j a conjunction of literals) if its accepting paths from the root to the 1-sink, read as partial assignments via {0,1,*}, are exactly the terms T_1,...,T_m. Let PolyTDD_SOP denote the class of Boolean functions computed by families (D_n) of TDDs of size polynomial in n that represent some sum‑of‑products formula for the function.

Question. Determine the inclusion relationship between the classes l-LogCut and PolyTDD_SOP. Specifically, decide whether l-LogCut ⊆ PolyTDD_SOP, whether PolyTDD_SOP ⊆ l-LogCut, whether the two classes coincide, or whether they are incomparable.

Consider scheduling on identical parallel machines with preemption. An instance consists of a set $J=\{1,\dots,n\}$ of jobs and $m$ identical parallel machines. Each job $j$ has a processing time $p_j\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, and (depending on the variant below) a release date $r_j\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ and/or a due date $d_j\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$. A preemptive schedule assigns each job to time intervals (possibly on different machines, but never two simultaneously for the same job and never two jobs simultaneously on the same machine) so that the total length of the intervals assigned to job $j$ equals $p_j$, and (when release dates are present) no part of job $j$ is processed before $r_j$. For a schedule, $C_j$ is the completion time of job $j$, $U_j=1$ if $C_j>d_j$ and $0$ otherwise, and the tardiness is $T_j=\max\{0,C_j-d_j\}$.

Let $p$ denote the number of distinct values appearing in $\{p_1,\dots,p_n\}$. For each of the following three problems, decide whether it is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by $p$, i.e., whether it can be solved in time $f(p)\cdot |I|^{O(1)}$ for some computable function $f$, where $|I|$ is the input size:

(a) $P\mid pmtn, r_j\mid \sum_j C_j$: minimize $\sum_{j} C_j$ subject to release dates and preemption.

(b) $P\mid pmtn\mid \sum_j U_j$: minimize the number of late jobs $\sum_j U_j$ with due dates and preemption.

(c) $P\mid pmtn\mid \sum_j T_j$: minimize the total tardiness $\sum_j T_j$ with due dates and preemption.

Define the complexity class SL (symmetric logspace) as the class of languages accepted by symmetric Turing machines using O(log n) work tape space, where a symmetric Turing machine is a nondeterministic Turing machine whose transition relation is symmetric: for every allowed transition between two configurations, the reverse transition is also allowed.

Define the complexity class l-LogCut as the ordered-input version of the class of languages decided by polynomial-size Boolean circuit families {C_n} of cutwidth O(log n). Here the cutwidth of a Boolean circuit (viewed as a directed acyclic graph with input gates, internal gates, and one output gate, drawn with all gates placed on a horizontal line in some order) is the maximum, over all vertical cuts of the line, of the number of wires crossing the cut; "ordered-input" means that for each n the input bits x_1, …, x_n appear at fixed positions in this left-to-right order at the leftmost end of the layout.

Determine the inclusion relationship between SL and l-LogCut: prove one of the following statements, or show that the question is independent of standard assumptions:
(a) SL ⊆ l-LogCut,
(b) l-LogCut ⊆ SL,
(c) SL = l-LogCut,
(d) SL and l-LogCut are incomparable under inclusion.

Consider Turing machines with a read-only input tape and a separate work tape of size O(log n) on inputs of length n. Call such a machine one-way-input if its input head can only move left-to-right (it never moves leftwards along the input tape).

Define the following nonuniform complexity classes:
- NL: the class of languages decided by nondeterministic logarithmic-space Turing machines (with standard two-way input access), where a string is accepted iff at least one computation path reaches an accepting state.
- ⊕L: the class of languages decided by nondeterministic logarithmic-space Turing machines under parity acceptance, where a string is accepted iff an odd number of computation paths reach an accepting state.
- l-NL: the one-way-input analogue of NL, i.e., languages decided by one-way-input nondeterministic logarithmic-space machines under existential acceptance.
- l-⊕L: the one-way-input analogue of ⊕L, i.e., languages decided by one-way-input nondeterministic logarithmic-space machines under parity acceptance.

It is known (in the nonuniform setting) that NL ⊆ ⊕L. The question is: does the analogous inclusion hold in the one-way-input model? Specifically, prove or disprove the inclusion
        l-NL ⊆ l-⊕L.

Three-machine flow-shop scheduling with makespan objective, denoted F3 || C_max, is the following problem. We are given a set of n jobs J = {1, ..., n} and three machines M_1, M_2, M_3 arranged in series. Each job j has three nonnegative integer processing times p_{1,j}, p_{2,j}, p_{3,j}, where p_{i,j} is the time job j must be processed on machine M_i. Every job must be processed first on M_1, then on M_2, then on M_3 (the same order for all jobs). At any moment, each machine processes at most one job, each job is processed by at most one machine, and operations are non-preemptive. A schedule assigns starting times so that for every job j the operation on M_{i+1} starts no earlier than the completion of its operation on M_i. The makespan C_max of a schedule is the latest completion time over all jobs. The goal is to decide, given an input and a target T, whether there exists a feasible schedule with C_max ≤ T.

Let p_max = max_{i,j} p_{i,j} denote the maximum processing time appearing in the instance.

Question: Is F3 || C_max fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max? Equivalently, does there exist a computable function f and a constant c such that the problem can be solved in time f(p_max) · (n + log T)^c?

For a Boolean function f : {0,1}^n → {0,1}, define the following formula sizes:

• A sum-of-products (SOP) formula for f is an OR of ANDs of literals (variables or their negations). Its size is the total number of literal occurrences.
• A product-of-sums (POS) formula for f is an AND of ORs of literals; size is again counted by literal occurrences.
• An exclusive-or sum-of-products (ESOP) formula for f is an XOR of ANDs of literals; size is counted by literal occurrences.

For a family of Boolean functions {f_n}_{n≥1} with f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1}, say that:
• {f_n} ∈ PolySOP if there exist SOP formulas computing f_n of size bounded by a polynomial in n;
• {f_n} ∈ PolyPOS if there exist POS formulas computing f_n of size bounded by a polynomial in n;
• {f_n} ∈ PolyESOP if there exist ESOP formulas computing f_n of size bounded by a polynomial in n.

Note that PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS equals the class often denoted AC^0_1 of families computable by depth-2 unbounded fan-in AND/OR circuits of polynomial size.

Determine the inclusion relations among the classes PolySOP, PolyPOS, PolyESOP, and PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS. In particular:

(a) Is PolyESOP contained in PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS, or does there exist a family of Boolean functions with polynomial-size ESOP formulas but no polynomial-size SOP formula and no polynomial-size POS formula?
(b) Conversely, is PolySOP ∪ PolyPOS contained in PolyESOP, or does there exist a family with polynomial-size SOP (or POS) formulas but requiring superpolynomial-size ESOP formulas?
(c) More generally, give a complexity-theoretic comparison of the expressive power of SOP and ESOP representations as a function of the number of variables.

Consider the job-shop scheduling problem J||C_max defined as follows. We are given m machines M_1,...,M_m and n jobs J_1,...,J_n. Each job J_j consists of a finite ordered sequence of operations (O_{j,1}, O_{j,2}, ..., O_{j,n_j}); each operation O_{j,k} must be processed on a specified machine μ(j,k) ∈ {M_1,...,M_m} for a specified positive integer length p_{j,k}, and the operations of each job must be processed in the given order. A schedule assigns a starting time to each operation such that (i) operations of the same job do not overlap and respect their job order, and (ii) at any moment each machine processes at most one operation. The makespan C_max of a schedule is the largest completion time over all operations. Let OPT denote the minimum makespan over all feasible schedules.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm A and a computable function f such that, for every instance with m machines, n jobs, and every ε > 0, the algorithm A produces a feasible schedule of makespan at most (1+ε)·OPT in running time f(m, ε) · poly(N), where N denotes the bit-length of the input encoding (so the dependence on the input size is polynomial, while m and ε appear only inside f)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A PTAS is known for J||C_max when both the number of machines m and the maximum number of operations per job μ are fixed (Jansen–Solis-Oba–Sviridenko), and strong inapproximability is known when m is part of the input (Mastrolilli–Svensson). Consider the open-shop scheduling problem defined as follows. There are n jobs and m machines. Each job j must be processed on every machine, and each operation (job j on machine i) has unit processing time p_{ij} = 1. The order in which the operations of a job are processed on the machines is not fixed in advance and is part of the decision; at any time each machine processes at most one operation and each job is processed on at most one machine.

The set of jobs is partitioned into g batches B_1, …, B_g. For each ordered pair of batches (p, q) with p ≠ q, a nonnegative sequence-dependent setup time s_{pq} is given. On each machine, whenever the machine finishes processing an operation belonging to a job of batch p and next processes an operation belonging to a job of batch q ≠ p, a setup of length s_{pq} must be inserted between these two operations. No setup is required between consecutive operations of jobs from the same batch (and no setup is required before the first operation on a machine).

The objective is to minimize the makespan C_max, i.e. the time at which all operations (and required setups) are completed.

Question: Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number g of batches? Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm that, on every input, computes an optimal schedule in time f(g) · (n + m)^{O(1)} for some computable function f?

Consider the Cauchy problem for the Einstein vacuum equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$ on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold $(\mathcal{M}, g)$. An initial data set consists of a 3-manifold $\Sigma$ together with a Riemannian metric $\bar g$ and a symmetric 2-tensor $K$ on $\Sigma$ satisfying the Einstein constraint equations
\[ R(\bar g) + (\mathrm{tr}_{\bar g} K)^2 - |K|_{\bar g}^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_{\bar g} K - d(\mathrm{tr}_{\bar g} K) = 0. \]
Such an initial data set is called asymptotically flat if $\Sigma$ contains an end diffeomorphic to the complement of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$, on which, in the induced Cartesian coordinates, $\bar g_{ij} - \delta_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ decay to zero at infinity at suitable rates. Given such initial data, the maximal globally hyperbolic Cauchy development $(\mathcal{M}, g)$ is the unique (up to isometry) maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum spacetime containing $(\Sigma,\bar g, K)$ as a Cauchy hypersurface.

The maximal development is said to possess a naked singularity if its future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ (defined via conformal compactification) is incomplete, i.e., the spacetime fails to be future-causally-geodesically complete in a manner visible from infinity, equivalently, if the closure of the causal past of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in $\mathcal{M}$ does not coincide with $\mathcal{M}$ in the appropriate conformal sense.

Prove the following weak cosmic censorship conjecture: there exists a generic class (in a suitable topology, e.g., an open and dense, or a residual, subset) of asymptotically flat vacuum initial data $(\Sigma, \bar g, K)$ such that the maximal globally hyperbolic development of every member of this class has a complete future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$; equivalently, naked singularities do not occur for generic asymptotically flat initial data.

The weak cosmic censorship conjecture, formulated by Penrose in 1969, remains one of the central open problems in mathematical general relativity. While there are partial results (e.g., for spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field by Christodoulou, and recent constructions of naked singularities by Rodnianski–Shlapentokh-Rothman showing the borderline nature of genericity), the conjecture is open in the general asymptotically flat vacuum setting as of 2026.

Let $M$ be a smooth compact $3$-dimensional manifold. A vacuum initial data set on $M$ consists of a Riemannian metric $g$ and a symmetric $2$-tensor $K$ on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
\[
R_g - |K|_g^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0,
\]
where $R_g$ is the scalar curvature of $g$. Given such initial data, the maximal vacuum Cauchy development is the (unique up to isometry) maximal globally hyperbolic Lorentzian $4$-manifold $(\mathcal{D},\mathbf{g})$ solving the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(\mathbf{g})=0$ into which $(M,g,K)$ embeds as a Cauchy hypersurface with induced metric $g$ and second fundamental form $K$. A vacuum extension of $(M,g,K)$ is any vacuum Lorentzian $4$-manifold $(\mathcal{E},\mathbf{g}')$ into which $(M,g,K)$ embeds with induced metric $g$ and second fundamental form $K$, with $(\mathcal{D},\mathbf{g})$ embedding isometrically into $(\mathcal{E},\mathbf{g}')$; a maximal vacuum extension is a vacuum extension that is maximal with respect to isometric inclusion.

Prove that for generic vacuum initial data $(g,K)$ on $M$ (in a suitable topology on the space of such data), the maximal vacuum Cauchy development of $(M,g,K)$ coincides with the maximal vacuum extension of $(M,g,K)$. Equivalently, prove that generic vacuum spacetimes with compact Cauchy hypersurface $M$ cannot be continued as vacuum solutions beyond their maximal globally hyperbolic Cauchy development.

Consider the Einstein–Vlasov system, in which a spacetime $(M,g)$ of dimension $4$ with Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is coupled to a collisionless ensemble of particles described by a non-negative distribution function $f$ on the mass shell $P\subset T^*M$ (or $TM$). The matter satisfies the Vlasov (collisionless Boltzmann) equation
$$X(f)=0,$$
where $X$ is the geodesic spray on $P$, and the metric satisfies Einstein's equations
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g)-\tfrac{1}{2}R(g)\,g+\Lambda g=8\pi T[f],$$
with stress–energy tensor
$$T_{\alpha\beta}(x)=\int_{P_x} f(x,p)\,p_\alpha p_\beta\,\mu_{P_x}(p),$$
the integration being over the fiber of the mass shell with its induced measure. (One may consider the massive or massless case, with or without a cosmological constant $\Lambda$.) Initial data consist of a Riemannian $3$-manifold $(\Sigma,h)$, a symmetric $2$-tensor $K$ (second fundamental form) satisfying the constraint equations, together with a non-negative initial distribution $f_0$ on the appropriate bundle over $\Sigma$.

Establish the following:

(a) (Small-data inhomogeneous global existence.) Prove that for initial data sufficiently close (in a suitable Sobolev or weighted norm) to a reference solution (e.g.\ Minkowski space, or a chosen homogeneous cosmological background), without assuming any spatial symmetry, the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the data exists for all time and the resulting classical solution $(g,f)$ is geodesically complete (in the appropriate time direction) with quantitative decay.

(b) (Spatially homogeneous theory, including Bianchi IX.) For spatially homogeneous initial data on Bianchi-type Lie groups, including Bianchi type IX (where $\Sigma$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathrm{SU}(2)$), prove a general existence and uniqueness theorem for solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov system, characterize the maximal time interval of existence, and analyze the asymptotic behavior of large initial data solutions toward both the past and future (curvature singularities, recollapse, completeness, attractors).

The two parts have seen significant progress but the full statement is not completely resolved. The small-data global nonlinear stability of Minkowski space for the massless Einstein–Vlasov system was proved by Taylor (2017) and for the massive case by Lindblad–Taylor and Fajman–Joudioux–Smulevici (around 2017–2021), and several small-data results around cosmological backgrounds (e.g. with positive cosmological constant) are known. For the homogeneous case, many Bianchi types are well understood (Rendall, Rein, Lee and others), but Bianchi IX with Vlasov matter—particularly large-data dynamics, recollapse, and BKL-type oscillatory behavior—remains incompletely understood. Thus the problem is partially solved.

Let $(M, g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian 4-manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g + \Lambda g = 8\pi T$, where $T$ is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor (the energy–momentum tensor) satisfying the dominant energy condition. By a "test particle" one informally means a small massive body whose own contribution to the curvature of spacetime is negligible.

Formulate and prove a precise mathematical theorem within general relativity asserting the geodesic hypothesis: any ideal test particle of negligible (but positive) rest mass traces a timelike curve $\gamma : I \to M$ that is a geodesic of $(M, g)$, i.e.
$$\nabla_{\dot\gamma} \dot\gamma = 0.$$

The task is to give a rigorous derivation in which "test particle" is given a precise mathematical meaning (e.g., as a one-parameter family of energy–momentum tensors $T_\varepsilon$ supported in a shrinking world-tube, satisfying $\nabla^a T_{ab} = 0$ together with appropriate energy and size conditions, or as a suitable limit of extended bodies) and to deduce the geodesic equation as a theorem from the Einstein equations together with the chosen hypotheses, without postulating it as an independent axiom.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Partial results exist. The Geroch–Jang theorem (1975) shows that curves traced by energy–momentum tensors satisfying the dominant energy condition and supported in arbitrarily thin tubes must be geodesics. Ehlers and Geroch (2004) extended this to allow the body to back-react on the metric, again concluding geodesic motion under averaged energy conditions and technical hypotheses. However, philosophers of physics (e.g. Malament, Weatherall) and mathematical relativists note that a fully general, assumption-free derivation remains debated, and singular/self-gravitating cases are not fully settled. The problem is therefore best classified as partially solved rather than fully resolved.

Consider $(d+1)$-dimensional Anti–de Sitter spacetime $\mathrm{AdS}_{d+1}$ ($d\ge 3$), the maximally symmetric solution of the vacuum Einstein equations with negative cosmological constant $\Lambda=-d(d-1)/(2L^2)$, equipped with reflecting boundary conditions at conformal infinity. The AdS nonlinear instability conjecture asserts that for generic arbitrarily small smooth perturbations of AdS, the resulting solution of the Einstein equations (possibly coupled to matter) develops, through a weakly turbulent transfer of energy to ever higher frequencies, a region of arbitrarily large curvature, leading to gravitational collapse and black hole formation. This conjecture is supported by extensive numerical and perturbative evidence in the spherically symmetric Einstein–massless-scalar-field model, and has been proven by Moschidis for the spherically symmetric Einstein–null-dust and Einstein–massless-Vlasov systems.

Problem. Determine whether the qualitative picture of nonlinear AdS instability — namely, the existence of a turbulent cascade to high frequencies driving generic small perturbations toward black hole formation — persists, is modified, or fails in settings beyond spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse. In particular:

(a) For pure vacuum gravitational perturbations of $\mathrm{AdS}_{d+1}$ (which necessarily break spherical symmetry for $d\ge 3$), is AdS nonlinearly unstable, and if so, does the instability proceed via the same weakly turbulent resonant cascade mechanism as in the spherical scalar case, or is it qualitatively different (for instance, are there obstructions from non-resonant spectra, or families of globally regular time-periodic geons that act as islands of stability)?

(b) Identify the precise mechanism by which gravitational mode resonances at third (and higher) perturbative order organize the energy transfer, and decide whether the existence of single-mode and multi-mode horizonless time-periodic solutions of the Einstein equations in AdS implies the existence of an open set of small initial data whose evolution remains globally regular.

State and prove a rigorous result settling, in at least one such non-spherically-symmetric Einstein-matter or vacuum model, whether AdS is nonlinearly stable or unstable.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The conjecture is unresolved in full generality. In spherical symmetry it has been rigorously established for the Einstein–null-dust and Einstein–massless-Vlasov systems (Moschidis), and is supported by strong numerical/perturbative evidence for the spherical Einstein–scalar-field model. Beyond spherical symmetry, perturbative work (e.g., Dias–Santos and collaborators) shows that the gravitational sector behaves qualitatively differently from the spherical scalar one: not all gravitational normal modes extend to periodic horizonless solutions, and resonance structures differ. No rigorous proof of nonlinear (in)stability of vacuum AdS beyond spherical symmetry is currently known, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

Consider, in $D \geq 5$ spacetime dimensions, the family of asymptotically flat, vacuum (or electrovacuum) black hole solutions of the Einstein equations, including the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini solution, the Myers–Perry rotating black holes (with one or more independent angular momenta), and the black ring/black string/black saturn families. Study the linearized gravitational perturbations of these backgrounds (and, where applicable, fully nonlinear evolutions) and determine, for each family and each region of its parameter space (mass, angular momenta, charges):

(a) Whether the solution is mode-stable, i.e., whether the linearized vacuum Einstein equations admit no smooth, finite-energy, exponentially growing solutions on the exterior region with appropriate boundary conditions at the horizon and at infinity.

(b) Whether the solution is linearly stable in a stronger sense (uniform boundedness and decay of perturbations).

(c) Whether the solution is nonlinearly stable.

In particular, identify and characterize instabilities that have no analogue in four-dimensional general relativity, such as the Gregory–Laflamme instability of black strings and ultraspinning instabilities of higher-dimensional rotating black holes, and determine the precise thresholds (in terms of mass, spin parameters, horizon geometry) at which such instabilities set in. Provide a complete classification of which higher-dimensional black hole solutions are stable and which are unstable under gravitational perturbations.

representations.normalized:
In loop quantum gravity (LQG), one quantizes general relativity using holonomies of an SU(2) connection and fluxes of a densitized triad as basic variables, producing a kinematical Hilbert space on which geometric operators (area, volume) have discrete spectra. When this quantization program is applied to symmetry-reduced models — in particular to spatially homogeneous (e.g. FLRW and Bianchi) cosmologies, giving loop quantum cosmology — one finds that classical curvature singularities (such as the big bang) are generically resolved: the effective dynamics replace the singularity by a regular bounce, and strong curvature singularities are absent on physical states.

Problem. Determine whether the singularity-resolution results established for spatially homogeneous spacetimes in loop quantum cosmology extend to a substantially more general setting that goes beyond symmetry-reduced models. Concretely: formulate and prove (or disprove) a theorem in full (or midi-superspace) loop quantum gravity stating that, for a class of spacetimes strictly larger than the spatially homogeneous ones — for example inhomogeneous cosmological models, Gowdy spacetimes, spherically symmetric gravitational collapse, or generic globally hyperbolic quantum geometries — every classical curvature singularity (in a precise sense, e.g. strong curvature singularities along physically admissible evolutions) is resolved by the LQG quantum dynamics.
