Consider neutral-current (NC) induced single-photon emission off nucleons and nuclei, in which an incoming neutrino scatters off a nucleon or nuclear target via Z-boson exchange and produces an outgoing photon together with the recoiling hadronic system. At low energies such processes can be described within a chiral effective field theory expansion, where the hadronic amplitude is built from (i) Born terms with electromagnetic and weak nucleon form factors, (ii) baryon-resonance contributions (most importantly the Δ(1232) and higher resonances) parametrized by NC and electromagnetic transition form factors, and (iii) contact terms required by chiral symmetry and gauge invariance.

Develop a hadronic model of NC photon emission, valid up to neutrino energies of order 1–2 GeV, that satisfies the following requirements:

1. Specify the complete set of electroweak transition form factors (vector, axial, and possible pseudoscalar pieces) for the nucleon and for each baryon resonance R included in the model, together with their Q²-dependence and the constraints used to fix them (e.g. PCAC, vector-meson dominance, lattice or experimental input).

2. Determine the higher-order corrections — in particular loop contributions and higher-order contact terms — that must be added so that the resulting amplitude respects partial-wave unitarity bounds for νN → νNγ and coherent/incoherent νA → νAγ throughout the kinematic region considered.

3. Show explicitly how the inclusion of these loop and contact contributions cancels the unphysical high-energy growth of the tree-level resonance amplitudes, and quantify the residual theoretical uncertainty on the inclusive and differential cross sections arising from the poorly known form factors.

State and justify the minimal such set of form factors and higher-order terms, or prove that no finite truncation within this effective-theory framework can simultaneously satisfy unitarity and reproduce known low-energy constraints.

The problem of constructing a unitarity-respecting model of NC single-photon emission with reliable form factors at intermediate neutrino energies remains an active open question in neutrino-nucleus interaction physics. While several effective-field-theory and resonance-model calculations exist (Hill; Wang, Serot, Zhang; Rosner; etc.), no consensus framework with fully constrained form factors and demonstrably unitary loop+contact corrections at GeV energies has been established, and it is repeatedly listed as an open theoretical issue relevant to MiniBooNE-like excesses and MicroBooNE/SBN analyses.

Let H be a (real) Hilbert space, and let C_1, C_2 ⊂ H be compact convex sets. For x ∈ H and a closed convex set C ⊂ H, denote by P_C(x) the metric projection of x onto C (the unique nearest point of C to x). Recall that for a convex set C and a continuous linear functional f on H, a point p ∈ C is said to be strongly exposed by f if f(p) = sup_{y ∈ C} f(y) and every sequence (x_k) ⊂ C with f(x_k) → sup_{y ∈ C} f(y) satisfies x_k → p in norm. For x ∈ H and i ∈ {1,2}, set p_i := P_{C_i}(x); then the linear functional f_i(y) := ⟨x − p_i, y⟩ satisfies f_i(p_i) = sup_{y ∈ C_i} f_i(y), so p_i is exposed by f_i.

Prove or disprove: there always exists a point x ∈ H such that, with p_i := P_{C_i}(x) for i = 1, 2, the singleton {p_i} is strongly exposed in C_i by the functional y ↦ ⟨x − p_i, y⟩, for both i = 1 and i = 2 simultaneously.

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be (possibly nonconvex) proximal sets — that is, sets for which the metric projection $P_A(x) := \arg\min_{a\in A}\|x-a\|$ and $P_B(x)$ are well defined (single-valued almost everywhere). Assume $A\cap B \neq \emptyset$. For a parameter $\lambda \in (0,1]$, define the Douglas–Rachford operator
$$T_\lambda(x) := \big(\lambda(2P_B - \mathrm{Id})(2P_A - \mathrm{Id}) + (1-\lambda)\mathrm{Id}\big)x,$$
whose discrete-time iteration is $x_{k+1} \in T_\lambda x_k$. The associated continuous-time Douglas–Rachford flow is the vector field obtained as the limit $\lambda \to 0^+$, namely the (set-valued) ODE
$$\dot{x}(t) \in (2P_B - \mathrm{Id})(2P_A - \mathrm{Id})\,x(t) - x(t),$$
i.e. trajectories driven by $F(x) := (2P_B-\mathrm{Id})(2P_A-\mathrm{Id})x - x$.

Investigate the qualitative dynamics and convergence behavior of this continuous-time flow in the following two prototypical nonconvex feasibility settings:

(i) $A$ is an ellipse $\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2 : x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1\}$ (with $a>b>0$) and $B$ is an affine line in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that meets $A$ subtransversally;

(ii) $A$ is a $p$-sphere $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2 : |x_1|^p + |x_2|^p = 1\}$ for some $p>0$, $p\neq 2$, and $B$ is an affine line in $\mathbb{R}^2$ intersecting $A$.

Specifically, prove (or disprove) statements describing the basins of attraction of points in $A\cap B$, the existence and structure of equilibria, periodic orbits, or other invariant sets of the flow, and the relationship between the continuous-time dynamics and the known complicated global behavior of the discrete Douglas–Rachford iteration in these geometries.

Consider charged-current neutrino-induced single-pion production on nucleons, in particular the channel ν_μ p → μ^- p π^+ at intermediate neutrino energies (roughly 0.5–3 GeV), where the dominant mechanism is excitation of the Δ(1232) resonance. The hadronic amplitude depends on the N–Δ axial transition form factors C_3^A(Q^2), C_4^A(Q^2), C_5^A(Q^2), C_6^A(Q^2), whose Q^2 dependence and overall normalization (especially C_5^A(0)) must be fixed by experiment.

The two principal historical data sets used to constrain these form factors are the Argonne National Laboratory (ANL) 12-ft deuterium bubble chamber measurement and the Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) 7-ft deuterium bubble chamber measurement of the flux-averaged differential and total cross sections for ν_μ p → μ^- p π^+. The reported normalizations of these two data sets differ by approximately 30–40%, producing a corresponding uncertainty in the extracted N–Δ axial form factors and in theoretical predictions used by modern accelerator neutrino oscillation experiments.

Problem. Determine the true elementary cross sections σ(ν_μ p → μ^- p π^+) (and the related channels ν_μ n → μ^- p π^0 and ν_μ n → μ^- n π^+) on free nucleons as a function of neutrino energy, after correcting for nuclear (deuteron) effects, and decide which of the ANL and BNL data sets more faithfully reflects these elementary cross sections. Equivalently, extract the N–Δ(1232) axial transition form factors C_i^A(Q^2) (i = 3, 4, 5, 6) — in particular the value of C_5^A(0) and its Q^2 dependence — in a way that is consistent with both data sets within their stated uncertainties, and quantify the residual systematic uncertainty.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

A reanalysis of the ANL and BNL deuterium bubble-chamber pion-production data (Wilkinson et al., 2014; arXiv:1411.4482) showed that, once flux-independent ratios over multiple channels are used, the two data sets are consistent within experimental uncertainties, largely resolving the apparent normalization tension. Subsequent extractions of the N–Δ axial form factors (e.g., Hernández, Nieves, Valverde and follow-ups, arXiv:1001.4416, 1012.4260) have used the combined data to determine C_5^A(0) and its Q^2 dependence, finding a tension with the off-diagonal Goldberger–Treiman relation at roughly 2σ. The discrepancy between ANL and BNL is therefore considered largely resolved at the level of consistency, but the precise elementary cross sections and axial form factors still carry sizeable uncertainties and call for new hydrogen/deuterium measurements.

Consider neutrino-induced coherent single-pion production on an isoscalar nucleus (with equal numbers of protons and neutrons), in which the nucleus remains in its ground state and a single pion is produced in the forward direction. The two reactions of interest are the charged-current (CC) channel ν_μ A → μ^- A π^+ with cross section σ_{CC-COHπ+}, and the neutral-current (NC) channel ν_μ A → ν_μ A π^0 with cross section σ_{NC-COHπ0}. Under the standard theoretical approximations used to describe coherent pion production (PCAC dominance of the divergence of the axial current, isospin symmetry of the target, and dominance of the pion-pole / axial contribution), the cross sections satisfy

  σ_{CC-COHπ+} / σ_{NC-COHπ0} = 2.

For carbon (A = ^{12}C) at neutrino beam energies of order 1 GeV, an experimental measurement combining a search for CC coherent π^+ production (yielding only an upper limit) with a measurement of NC coherent π^0 production produces a ratio of approximately 0.14 (with uncertainties of order ±0.3), more than 4σ below the theoretical prediction of 2 and in tension with NC coherent π^0 measurements that indicate a sizeable cross section.

Provide a theoretical explanation, consistent with all known nuclear and hadronic physics, for why the measured CC-to-NC coherent pion-production ratio on carbon is so far below the value 2 that follows from the standard isoscalar-target relation, reconciling the apparent suppression of the CC channel with the observed NC channel rate.

Let $X$ be a real Euclidean space and let $a_1,\dots,a_m \in X$ be a finite set of points. Consider the minimax problem
$$\min_{x\in X}\;\max_{1\le i\le m}\|a_i-x\|,$$
whose unique minimizer $x^*$ is the center of the smallest closed Euclidean ball containing $\{a_1,\dots,a_m\}$.

(a) Provide an explicit closed-form formula or a clean structural characterization of $x^*$ in terms of $a_1,\dots,a_m$.

(b) More generally, suppose $X$ is an arbitrary normed (or metric) space, or replace $\max_{1\le i\le m}\|a_i-x\|$ by $N(\|a_1-x\|,\dots,\|a_m-x\|)$ for an arbitrary norm $N$ on $\mathbb{R}^m$. Describe the minimizer(s) of the corresponding problem
$$\min_{x\in X}\;N(\|a_1-x\|,\dots,\|a_m-x\|)$$
in an analogously explicit way (existence, uniqueness, and an explicit characterization).

The Euclidean smallest enclosing ball (1-center) problem is classical and has no known simple closed-form expression for its center in terms of the input points; it is typically solved via algorithms (e.g., Welzl's randomized linear-time algorithm) or as a convex/SOCP optimization. The general normed/metric-space and arbitrary-norm-aggregation versions are studied under "minisum/minimax facility location" but lack a unified explicit formula. No definitive resolution of the request for a "neat explicit formula" was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

Let $\Omega$ be a finite family of convex polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For each unit vector $g\in S^{n-1}$, define
$$C_\Omega(g) \;:=\; \operatorname{conv}\Bigl(\bigcup_{P\in\Omega}\operatorname{Argmax}_{x\in P}\langle x,g\rangle\Bigr),$$
i.e. the convex hull of the union of the support faces (in direction $g$) of all polytopes in $\Omega$. Define the converter
$$F(\Omega) \;:=\; \{\,C_\Omega(g) : g\in S^{n-1}\,\},$$
which is again a finite family of convex polytopes. Given an initial finite family $\Omega_0$, set $\Omega_i := F(\Omega_{i-1})$ for $i\ge 1$.

Provide a characterization of those initial finite families $\Omega_0\subset\{\text{convex polytopes in }\mathbb{R}^n\}$ for which the orbit $(\Omega_i)_{i\ge 0}$ eventually enters a $2$-cycle, that is, for which there exists an integer $N\ge 0$ such that
$$\Omega_{N+2} \;=\; \Omega_N.$$

The original Demyanov–Ryabova conjecture (that every orbit reaches a 2-cycle) was disproved by an explicit counterexample exhibiting a minimal cycle of length 4. Partial sufficient conditions guaranteeing 2-cycles have been obtained (e.g., when the family contains enough minimal polytopes with well-placed extreme points), but a full characterization of the initial families that eventually enter a 2-cycle remains open.

Consider charged-current single-pion production induced by muon neutrinos on a nuclear target (specifically CH2, as used in the MiniBooNE experiment), in the intermediate-energy regime (neutrino energies of order 1 GeV). Theoretical calculations of the inclusive and differential cross sections for this process incorporate (i) an elementary neutrino–nucleon pion-production amplitude (typically dominated by Δ(1232) excitation with non-resonant background) and (ii) a treatment of pion final-state interactions (FSI) inside the nucleus, which redistribute pion kinematics and absorb a fraction of produced pions. State-of-the-art calculations including FSI lie systematically below the MiniBooNE single-pion (π+ and π0) cross-section measurements by factors of roughly 1.5–2, while being broadly consistent with analogous data from MINERvA and T2K.

Determine which of the following is the dominant cause of the observed discrepancy between theory and the MiniBooNE single-pion production data:

(a) the theoretical modelling of pion final-state interactions in the nucleus is incorrect (e.g., it overestimates absorption or otherwise misrepresents the in-medium pion transport), so that a corrected FSI treatment would resolve the disagreement; or

(b) the FSI modelling is essentially correct, but the measured event sample contains additional dynamical mechanisms (such as multi-nucleon currents, or events whose true reaction channel differs from the assumed signal definition) whose origin has been misunderstood, so that the disagreement reflects a misidentification of the underlying reaction content rather than an FSI deficiency.

Provide a quantitative resolution distinguishing (a) from (b), or demonstrate that the discrepancy arises from a specific combination of the two.

Consider the simulation of neutrino-nucleus scattering in the intermediate-energy regime (neutrino energies roughly between a few hundred MeV and several GeV), as needed for precision accelerator-based neutrino oscillation experiments. A Monte Carlo event generator must produce, event by event, fully exclusive final states (lepton kinematics plus hadronic system) sampled from inclusive and semi-inclusive cross sections that incorporate the following physics ingredients consistently:

1. Realistic nuclear ground-state dynamics beyond the relativistic Fermi gas, including nucleon-nucleon correlations, spectral functions, and binding effects.
2. Quasielastic single-nucleon knockout with a controlled treatment of the nucleon axial form factor and Pauli blocking.
3. Two-body (and higher) current contributions producing multinucleon (np-nh, e.g. 2p2h) final states from meson-exchange currents and short-range correlations, including their interference with the one-body sector.
4. Resonant and non-resonant single- and multi-pion production on bound nucleons, including in-medium modifications of baryon resonance properties.
5. Deep-inelastic scattering and the transition region between resonance production and DIS (matching/duality).
6. Final-state interactions of the produced hadrons as they propagate through the residual nucleus (cascade, optical-potential, or transport-theory based).
7. Coherent pion production and other low-multiplicity exclusive channels.

Formulate a mathematically and computationally consistent framework — for example a unified hadronic tensor or transport equation together with a sampling algorithm — that:

(a) reproduces, within a single set of approximations and parameters, the inclusive double-differential cross section $d^2\sigma/(dE_\ell\, d\cos\theta_\ell)$ predicted by current state-of-the-art microscopic theoretical models in each of the above channels, with controlled (i.e., quantifiable) approximation errors;

(b) yields exclusive final states whose joint distribution is consistent with the inclusive prediction (so that integrating out the hadronic variables recovers the inclusive cross section to within the stated tolerance);

(c) is computationally efficient enough to be deployed in present and next-generation oscillation analyses (e.g. generating $\gtrsim 10^9$ events with reasonable resources);

(d) admits systematic, theoretically meaningful nuisance-parameter variations (rather than ad hoc reweighting of obsolete model parameters) so that experimental fits do not absorb genuine physics into unphysical tunings.

The problem is to construct such a framework, prove or quantitatively bound the consistency conditions in (a)–(b), and demonstrate the algorithm achieves (c)–(d); or, alternatively, to identify rigorous obstructions showing that no algorithm can simultaneously satisfy (a)–(d) within a prescribed tolerance.

Consider the simulation of neutrino-nucleus scattering in the intermediate-energy regime (neutrino energies roughly between a few hundred MeV and several GeV), as needed for precision accelerator-based neutrino oscillation experiments. A Monte Carlo event generator must produce, event by event, fully exclusive final states (lepton kinematics plus hadronic system) sampled from inclusive and semi-inclusive cross sections that incorporate the following physics ingredients consistently:

1. Realistic nuclear ground-state dynamics beyond the relativistic Fermi gas, including nucleon-nucleon correlations, spectral functions, and binding effects.
2. Quasielastic single-nucleon knockout with a controlled treatment of the nucleon axial form factor and Pauli blocking.
3. Two-body (and higher) current contributions producing multinucleon (np-nh, e.g. 2p2h) final states from meson-exchange currents and short-range correlations, including their interference with the one-body sector.
4. Resonant and non-resonant single- and multi-pion production on bound nucleons, including in-medium modifications of baryon resonance properties.
5. Deep-inelastic scattering and the transition region between resonance production and DIS (matching/duality).
6. Final-state interactions of the produced hadrons as they propagate through the residual nucleus (cascade, optical-potential, or transport-theory based).
7. Coherent pion production and other low-multiplicity exclusive channels.

Formulate a mathematically and computationally consistent framework — for example a unified hadronic tensor or transport equation together with a sampling algorithm — that:

(a) reproduces, within a single set of approximations and parameters, the inclusive double-differential cross section $d^2\sigma/(dE_\ell\, d\cos\theta_\ell)$ predicted by current state-of-the-art microscopic theoretical models in each of the above channels, with controlled (i.e., quantifiable) approximation errors;

(b) yields exclusive final states whose joint distribution is consistent with the inclusive prediction (so that integrating out the hadronic variables recovers the inclusive cross section to within the stated tolerance);

(c) is computationally efficient enough to be deployed in present and next-generation oscillation analyses (e.g. generating $\gtrsim 10^9$ events with reasonable resources);

(d) admits systematic, theoretically meaningful nuisance-parameter variations (rather than ad hoc reweighting of obsolete model parameters) so that experimental fits do not absorb genuine physics into unphysical tunings.

The problem is to construct such a framework, prove or quantitatively bound the consistency conditions in (a)–(b), and demonstrate the algorithm achieves (c)–(d); or, alternatively, to identify rigorous obstructions showing that no algorithm can simultaneously satisfy (a)–(d) within a prescribed tolerance.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is an ongoing program in neutrino physics rather than a single mathematical conjecture. Major generators (GENIE, NEUT, NuWro, GiBUU, ACHILLES) have actively been incorporating spectral functions, 2p2h/MEC models, improved pion production, and modern FSI treatments since 2014, but a fully consistent unified implementation matching state-of-the-art microscopic theory across all channels remains incomplete and is a recognized open challenge as of recent reviews (NuSTEC white paper 2018; Snowmass 2022; recent 2024–2025 generator development papers).

Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a convex 3-polytope with boundary surface $\partial P$. A *net* (or *edge unfolding*) of $P$ is obtained by choosing a spanning subset $E$ of the edges of $P$ such that cutting $\partial P$ along the edges in $E$ yields a connected surface that can be developed isometrically into the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ as a (possibly non-simple) planar polygon. The net is *nonoverlapping* if this planar development is a simple polygon, i.e., the images of the faces have pairwise disjoint interiors.

Prove or disprove: every convex 3-polytope $P$ admits a nonoverlapping net.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Dürer's conjecture (often attributed to Shephard, 1975) on the existence of a nonoverlapping edge unfolding of every convex 3-polytope remains open as of 2025. Partial results include Ghomi's theorem (2014) that every convex polytope has an affine image admitting a nonoverlapping net, and Barvinok–Ghomi's (2019) disproof of a pseudo-edge generalization. The problem is listed as open in the Open Problem Garden and recent surveys (e.g., Oberwolfach Snapshot 2/2025).

Let $S$ be a set and let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset. For a map $f : S \to S$ and a point $\alpha \in S$, define the return set
$$N_f(\alpha, T) := \{ n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} : f^n(\alpha) \in T \},$$
where $f^n$ denotes the $n$-fold iterate of $f$ (with $f^0$ the identity). A one-sided arithmetic progression is a set of the form $\{a + bn : n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\}$ for some $a \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ and $b \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ (where $b = 0$ gives a singleton).

Classify the maps $f : S \to S$ (together with the choice of subset $T \subseteq S$) such that for every $\alpha \in S$, the return set $N_f(\alpha, T)$ has a prescribed nice structure — for instance, that $N_f(\alpha, T)$ is the union of finitely many one-sided arithmetic progressions.

The question is a broad classification problem in arithmetic/abstract dynamics, generalizing the Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture. The DML conjecture itself remains open in general; it is known in special cases (étale endomorphisms by Bell–Ghioca–Tucker, endomorphisms of $\mathbb{A}^2$ over $\mathbb{C}$, polynomial maps, and others), but no full classification of abstract maps $f:S\to S$ producing finite unions of arithmetic progressions for all return sets is known. Recent surveys (e.g., on current trends and open problems in arithmetic dynamics) continue to list this as an active open area.

Consider antineutrino-induced charged-current production of strange hadrons on nucleon and nuclear targets at intermediate energies (roughly 1–20 GeV neutrino energy). Two classes of reactions are of interest:

1. Strangeness-changing (|ΔS| = 1) processes such as
   ν̄_ℓ + N → ℓ⁺ + Y + X,  where Y ∈ {Λ, Σ⁰, Σ⁻} and X may contain additional pions but no net strangeness;
   ν̄_ℓ + N → ℓ⁺ + K̄ + N' + X (associated antikaon production with no hyperon), and the analogous single-K̄ exclusive channels.

2. Strangeness-conserving (ΔS = 0) associated production
   ν̄_ℓ + N → ℓ⁺ + Y + K + X,
   in which a hyperon Y and a kaon K are produced together so that net strangeness is preserved.

Determine, both theoretically and experimentally, the inclusive and exclusive antineutrino-induced strange-particle production cross sections σ(E_ν̄) and the differential distributions (in Q², the hadronic invariant mass W, and the outgoing strange-hadron kinematics) for the channels above, on free nucleons and on nuclear targets relevant to accelerator-based oscillation experiments. In particular, provide measured cross sections for single-hyperon production (ν̄ + N → ℓ⁺ + Λ, Σ), for single antikaon production, and for associated YK production by antineutrinos, sufficient to constrain models of strangeness production used in event generators.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Some historical bubble-chamber measurements of antineutrino-induced neutral strange particle production exist (e.g., on neon and hydrogen/deuterium at high energies, with inclusive K⁰, Λ, Λ̄, Σ⁰ rates), but at intermediate energies relevant to modern oscillation experiments dedicated antineutrino strange-particle cross section data remain scarce. Recent MINERvA and MicroBooNE measurements of charged-current kaon production focus primarily on neutrino (not antineutrino) beams and on inclusive kaon production, so the broader program of antineutrino strangeness cross sections (especially exclusive YK associated production and antikaon production) is still incomplete.

representations.normalized:
Consider a sequential measurement scheme intended to model psychological/behavioral data such as opinion polls. At each trial, a "system" is in some state s belonging to a state space S, and a "question" (observable) a is drawn from a set A with each question a having a finite outcome set V_a. The scheme is specified by three functions:

  (i) F(v | s, a): the probability of observing outcome v ∈ V_a when question a is posed to a system in state s;
  (ii) G(s, a, v): the post-measurement state, i.e., the new state in S after question a has been asked of state s and outcome v has been observed;
  (iii) H(s, t): the inter-trial evolution mapping a state s to its state at a later moment t (between consecutive measurements).

Two specializations of (F, G, H) are well known:
  • Standard quantum mechanics with Hermitian observables: states are density operators, F is given by the Born rule with spectral projectors, G is the Lüders projection update, and H is unitary (or trivial).
  • Quantum mechanics with binary POVMs: F is given by tr(ρ E_v) for effects E_v with E_0 + E_1 = I, and G is the corresponding effect-update rule, with H as above.

For two binary questions a, b ∈ A with outcomes in {0,1}, consider the joint probability over two consecutive trials,
    h_{ab}(v, w) = Pr[outcome v on a in trial 1, then outcome w on b in trial 2].
Decompose h_{ab}(v,w) = f_{ab}(v,w) + g_{ab}(v,w) where
    f_{ab}(v,w) = f_{ba}(w,v)  (symmetric part),
    g_{ab}(v,w) = − g_{ab}(1−v, 1−w)  (antisymmetric part).
These imply the QQ equation
    h_{ab}(v,w) + h_{ab}(1−v,1−w) = h_{ba}(w,v) + h_{ba}(1−w,1−v).

Question. Does there exist a choice of the functions F, G, H — strictly more general than both the Hermitian-observable formalism and the binary-POVM formalism — that
  (a) automatically yields the symmetry/antisymmetry properties above (and hence the QQ equation) for binary question-pair data, and
  (b) provides a quantitatively or conceptually more profitable account of empirical opinion-polling data than the standard quantum-mechanical version, while remaining a coherent probabilistic measurement formalism?

Construct such a generalized formalism, or prove that no such generalization can outperform the existing quantum-mechanical model in this setting.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether a strictly more general (F, G, H) formalism can outperform standard QM and POVM-based models for opinion-polling data while satisfying the QQ equation appears still open. Subsequent work has explored extensions via quantum instruments and sharp repeatable non-projective measurements (e.g., Ozawa–Khrennikov 2018 and later papers) addressing combinations of question order and response replicability, but no result establishes a definitively superior generalized formalism for opinion polling, and the broader open question framed in terms of arbitrary F, G, H remains unresolved.

Let $N \geq 1$, $d \geq 2$, and $D \geq 1$ be fixed integers. For a number field $K$ and a morphism $f \colon \mathbb{P}^N \to \mathbb{P}^N$ defined over $K$, a point $P \in \mathbb{P}^N(K)$ is called preperiodic for $f$ if the forward orbit $\{P, f(P), f^2(P), \ldots\}$ is finite; let $\operatorname{PrePer}(f, \mathbb{P}^N(K))$ denote the set of all such $K$-rational preperiodic points.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $C(N, d, D)$, depending only on $N$, $d$, and $D$, such that for every number field $K$ with $[K : \mathbb{Q}] = D$ and every morphism $f \colon \mathbb{P}^N \to \mathbb{P}^N$ of degree $d$ defined over $K$,
$$\#\operatorname{PrePer}(f, \mathbb{P}^N(K)) \leq C(N, d, D).$$

This is the Morton–Silverman Dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture (1994). It remains widely open. Even the special case of the family $x^2 + c$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ (asking whether there is a uniform bound on rational preperiodic points) is unresolved, with only partial results bounding periods of small length and conditional results under abc-type hypotheses.

The conjecture remains open in general. Period 4 was ruled out unconditionally by Morton; period 5 by Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer; period 6 was ruled out by Stoll conditional on BSD. Consider a quantum-theoretic framework for modeling sequences of yes/no judgments by a human participant. Two classes of experiments are to be modeled within this framework:

(A) Psychophysical detection tasks, in which on each trial the participant is presented with a near-threshold stimulus and reports whether the stimulus was perceived.

(B) Opinion-polling tasks, in which on each trial the participant is asked a fixed question about an attitude, preference, or belief, and reports a binary answer.

In both cases the participant's mental state between trials may evolve, and the model assigns to the participant a (possibly mixed) state ρ on a Hilbert space H, with the answer on each trial generated by some measurement rule. Two natural ingredients in such a model are:

(i) An inter-trial state evolution: between successive trials, ρ is updated by a (possibly non-unitary) dynamical map, in addition to any post-measurement collapse.

(ii) A generalized measurement rule: instead of a projection-valued measure (a conventional self-adjoint observable), the binary outcome is governed by a positive operator-valued measure (POVM) {E, I − E} with 0 ≤ E ≤ I, possibly satisfying the Lüders property (i.e., the post-measurement state after outcome E is a function only of E and ρ, of the standard Lüders form).

Empirical regularities to be reproduced include:
- Property 2: certain stability/repeatability properties of repeated measurements observed in opinion polling.
- Property 3: question-order effects and other non-classical correlations observed in opinion polling.
- Analogous regularities in psychophysical detection that are known to require nontrivial inter-trial dynamics or POVM-valued measurements to be modeled consistently.

It can be shown that POVMs with the Lüders property reduce to conventional projective observables, so they cannot, by themselves, reconcile Properties 2 and 3 in the opinion-polling setting; meanwhile, in the psychophysical setting, inter-trial evolution and POVMs do appear to be indispensable.

Problem. Provide a principled, mathematically precise account that explains the following asymmetry: identify structural features of the state space, the measurement rule, or the inter-trial dynamics that make ingredients (i) and (ii) necessary and effective in modeling psychophysical detection tasks of type (A), yet ineffective or unnecessary—and in fact incapable of reconciling Properties 2 and 3—in modeling opinion-polling tasks of type (B). Equivalently, characterize what must be added to, removed from, or modified in the standard quantum measurement framework so that both types of experiments can be treated within a single coherent formalism, or prove that no such unified treatment exists under stated axioms.

For nonzero rational numbers $b,c \in \mathbb{Q}^{*}$, consider the degree-$2$ rational map
$$\varphi_{b,c}: \mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathbb{Q}) \longrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathbb{Q}), \qquad \varphi_{b,c}(x) = bx + \frac{c}{x}.$$
A point $P \in \mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathbb{Q})$ is called periodic for $\varphi_{b,c}$ if $\varphi_{b,c}^{n}(P) = P$ for some integer $n \ge 1$ (the smallest such $n$ being its exact period), and is called preperiodic if some forward iterate $\varphi_{b,c}^{m}(P)$ ($m \ge 0$) is periodic. Let
$$\operatorname{PrePer}(\varphi_{b,c}, \mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathbb{Q})) = \{P \in \mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathbb{Q}) : P \text{ is preperiodic for } \varphi_{b,c}\}.$$
Prove or disprove the following two assertions:
(a) Every $\mathbb{Q}$-rational periodic point of $\varphi_{b,c}$ has exact period $1$, $2$, or $4$.
(b) The supremum
$$\sup_{b,c \in \mathbb{Q}^{*}} \#\operatorname{PrePer}(\varphi_{b,c}, \mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathbb{Q}))$$
equals $12$.

Let $f: \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^1$ be a rational map of degree $2$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$. A point $P \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})$ is called periodic for $f$ if there exists an integer $n \geq 1$ such that $f^n(P) = P$, and the smallest such $n$ is the period of $P$. A point $P \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})$ is called preperiodic for $f$ if its forward orbit $O_f(P) = \{P, f(P), f^2(P), \dots\}$ is finite. Let $\mathrm{PrePer}(f, \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q}))$ denote the set of all rational preperiodic points of $f$. Prove or disprove the following statements (the constants are known to be attained, so the question is whether they are uniform upper bounds over all degree-2 rational maps $f$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$):

(a) Every periodic point $P \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})$ for $f$ has period at most $7$.

(b) For every preperiodic point $P \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})$, $\#O_f(P) \leq 9$.

(c) $\#\mathrm{PrePer}(f, \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})) \leq 14$.

The MiniBooNE experiment, a short-baseline accelerator neutrino experiment using a Cherenkov mineral-oil detector that cannot distinguish electrons from photons on an event-by-event basis, has reported a statistically significant excess of electron-like single-shower events at low reconstructed quasi-elastic neutrino energy E_ν^QE (roughly below 475 MeV) over the predicted background. One of the principal Standard Model background candidates considered for this excess is neutral-current single-photon emission (NCγ) induced by neutrino–nucleus scattering, in which a photon is radiated through processes such as nucleon excitation to the Δ(1232) and other baryon resonances followed by radiative decay, together with non-resonant and in-medium contributions on a nuclear (CH₂) target.

Assume that a careful theoretical evaluation of the NCγ cross section on the MiniBooNE target, including resonant, non-resonant, and nuclear-medium effects, yields a predicted NCγ event rate that is insufficient to account for the observed low-E_ν^QE excess of electron-like events. Under this assumption, identify and justify a physical mechanism — whether a Standard Model process not yet correctly modeled in the experimental simulation, or a beyond-Standard-Model phenomenon (for example, light sterile neutrino oscillations, heavy-neutrino decays, dark-sector mediators producing e⁺e⁻ pairs or photons, or non-standard neutrino interactions) — that quantitatively reproduces the observed excess of electron-like events at low reconstructed energy in MiniBooNE while remaining consistent with constraints from complementary short-baseline experiments.

Let $K$ be a number field with algebraic closure $\bar K$. Let $X$ and $S$ be varieties defined over $K$, let $\pi : X \to S$ be a morphism, and let $f : X \to X$ be an $S$-morphism (i.e., $\pi \circ f = \pi$). For each point $s \in S(\bar K)$, write $X_s := \pi^{-1}(s)$ for the fiber and $f_s : X_s \to X_s$ for the restriction of $f$ to $X_s$; thus $f$ is viewed as a family of self-maps parameterized by $S$. For a self-map $g : Y \to Y$ and a field $L$, define
$$\operatorname{PrePer}(g, Y(L)) := \{ y \in Y(L) : g^m(y) = g^n(y) \text{ for some integers } m > n \geq 0 \},$$
the set of $L$-rational preperiodic points of $g$.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $D \geq 1$,
$$\sup_{\substack{L/K \\ [L:K] = D}} \; \sup_{s \in S(L)} \; \# \operatorname{PrePer}(f_s, X_s(L)) \;<\; \infty,$$
where the outer supremum runs over all field extensions $L$ of $K$ of degree $D$.

This is a strong/uniform form of the Morton–Silverman dynamical uniform boundedness conjecture, formulated in the family setting by Poonen. It remains open in general over number fields. Setup. A field $K$ is called Hilbertian if Hilbert's irreducibility theorem holds over $K$: for every irreducible polynomial $F(T,X)\in K[T,X]$ that is separable in $X$, there exist infinitely many $t_0\in K$ such that $F(t_0,X)\in K[X]$ is irreducible.

Let $K$ be a Hilbertian field, fix an integer $d\ge 2$, let $f(X)\in K[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d$, and let $P\in K$. Write $f^{n}$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $f$. Assume that $f^{n}(X)-P$ is separable for every $n\ge 1$ (so the preimage tree below is well-defined). Define the inverse-image tree
$$T_\infty(f,P)\;=\;\bigsqcup_{n\ge 0}\,\{x\in\overline K : f^{n}(x)=P\},$$
with edges joining $\alpha$ at level $n+1$ to $f(\alpha)$ at level $n$. Since $f$ has degree $d$ and is separable on this tree, $T_\infty(f,P)$ is isomorphic as a rooted tree to the infinite complete $d$-ary rooted tree $T_\infty(d)$. The absolute Galois group $G_K=\mathrm{Gal}(\overline K/K)$ acts on $T_\infty(f,P)$ by tree automorphisms, giving the arboreal Galois representation
$$\rho_{f,P}:G_K\longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}\bigl(T_\infty(d)\bigr).$$
The Odoni index is defined as
$$\iota_K(f,P)\;=\;\bigl[\,\mathrm{Aut}(T_\infty(d))\;:\;\mathrm{Im}(\rho_{f,P})\,\bigr]\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\cup\{\infty\}.$$

Question. For every Hilbertian field $K$ and every integer $d\ge 2$, do there exist a monic polynomial $f(X)\in K[X]$ of degree $d$ and a point $P\in K$ such that $\rho_{f,P}$ is surjective, i.e.\ such that $\iota_K(f,P)=1$? (Strengthening when $K$ is a number field: can one furthermore require the coefficients of $f$ to lie in the ring of integers of $K$?)
representations.original:
Setup. A field $K$ is called Hilbertian if Hilbert's irreducibility theorem holds over $K$: for every irreducible polynomial $F(T,X)\in K[T,X]$ that is separable in $X$, there exist infinitely many $t_0\in K$ such that $F(t_0,X)\in K[X]$ is irreducible.

Let $K$ be a Hilbertian field, fix an integer $d\ge 2$, let $f(X)\in K[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d$, and let $P\in K$. Write $f^{n}$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $f$. Assume that $f^{n}(X)-P$ is separable for every $n\ge 1$ (so the preimage tree below is well-defined). Define the inverse-image tree
$$T_\infty(f,P)\;=\;\bigsqcup_{n\ge 0}\,\{x\in\overline K : f^{n}(x)=P\},$$
with edges joining $\alpha$ at level $n+1$ to $f(\alpha)$ at level $n$. Since $f$ has degree $d$ and is separable on this tree, $T_\infty(f,P)$ is isomorphic as a rooted tree to the infinite complete $d$-ary rooted tree $T_\infty(d)$. The absolute Galois group $G_K=\mathrm{Gal}(\overline K/K)$ acts on $T_\infty(f,P)$ by tree automorphisms, giving the arboreal Galois representation
$$\rho_{f,P}:G_K\longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}\bigl(T_\infty(d)\bigr).$$
The Odoni index is defined as
$$\iota_K(f,P)\;=\;\bigl[\,\mathrm{Aut}(T_\infty(d))\;:\;\mathrm{Im}(\rho_{f,P})\,\bigr]\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\cup\{\infty\}.$$

Question. For every Hilbertian field $K$ and every integer $d\ge 2$, do there exist a monic polynomial $f(X)\in K[X]$ of degree $d$ and a point $P\in K$ such that $\rho_{f,P}$ is surjective, i.e.\ such that $\iota_K(f,P)=1$? (Strengthening when $K$ is a number field: can one furthermore require the coefficients of $f$ to lie in the ring of integers of $K$?)

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The conjecture in its original form for all Hilbertian fields was disproved by Bary-Soroker, Entin, and Sofos (arXiv:2012.03076, 2020), who exhibited a Hilbertian (PAC) field over which every polynomial of degree d ≥ 2 yields an arboreal image of infinite index. However, the conjecture has been established for all number fields through work of Specter (arXiv:1803.00434), Benedetto–Juul, and Kadets, including the integer-coefficient strengthening for number fields.

representations.normalized:
Consider neutrino-induced coherent single-pion production on a nucleus,
   ν_ℓ(k) + A(p_A) → ℓ^-(k') + A(p_A) + π(k_π),
in which the target nucleus remains in its ground state. In the intermediate-energy regime relevant to accelerator neutrino oscillation experiments, this process is commonly modeled by exciting a Δ(1232) resonance on a bound nucleon, with the Δ then propagating in the nuclear medium and decaying into a pion that is subsequently distorted by its final-state interaction with the nucleus.

Within such a framework, write the Δ propagator in coordinate space as a nonlocal kernel G_Δ(x,x'), built from the in-medium Δ self-energy Σ_Δ(ρ(x)) (which encodes Pauli blocking, binding, and Δ-hole many-body absorption channels), and let the local approximation be defined by replacing G_Δ(x,x') by a δ-function-localized propagator evaluated at the production point. Couple this to a realistic treatment of: (i) nuclear-medium modifications of the elementary weak Nπ production amplitude, (ii) distortion of the outgoing pion (e.g., via a microscopic optical potential or a coupled-channels treatment based on the Δ-hole model), and (iii) distortion of the outgoing charged lepton in the Coulomb field of the nucleus where appropriate.

Quantify, for representative nuclear targets used in current oscillation experiments (e.g., ^12C, ^16O, ^40Ar) and for incoming neutrino energies in the range 0.5–5 GeV, the size of the corrections induced by retaining the full nonlocality of the Δ propagator G_Δ(x,x') compared with the local approximation, after all of the above realistic ingredients have been included consistently. In particular, determine whether the nonlocal corrections to the flux-averaged total and differential coherent-pion-production cross sections remain quantitatively important once full nuclear dynamics are accounted for, or whether they are largely absorbed into the in-medium Δ self-energy and pion distortion.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Existing studies (e.g., dynamical Δ-hole / Sato–Lee–based models and DWIA momentum-space calculations) have shown that the local approximation can overestimate coherent pion production cross sections by up to ~100%, and that in-medium Δ self-energy and pion distortion strongly reshape the cross section. However, a fully consistent realistic calculation that simultaneously incorporates full nonlocal Δ propagation, complete nuclear-medium renormalization, lepton/pion distortion, and other relevant nuclear dynamics—settling definitively the residual size of nonlocal effects—does not appear to have been carried out; the problem remains an open investigation in the literature.

representations.normalized:
Consider a single spinless impurity particle of mass $M$ immersed at zero temperature in a three-dimensional homogeneous polarized ideal Fermi gas of background atoms of mass $m$ with Fermi wavenumber $k_F$. The impurity interacts with the background fermions through a short-range $s$-wave interaction characterized by a tunable scattering length $a$ (with no interactions among the background atoms). As $1/(k_F a)$ is varied, the dressed ground state of the impurity is conventionally described by two candidate quasiparticle states: the "polaron," a single impurity dressed by particle-hole excitations of the Fermi sea, and the "dimeron," obtained by dressing the bound impurity-background dimer (existing for $a>0$) with particle-hole excitations. A polaron-to-dimeron transition is predicted to occur near $k_F a \sim 1$ at a critical coupling $1/(k_F a_c)$ that depends on the mass ratio $m/M$.

(a) Determine whether the polaron and dimeron are genuinely distinct energy branches of the many-body Hamiltonian, or whether they are instead the same branch connected continuously, i.e., whether the exact ground-state wave function is continuous as a function of $1/(k_F a)$ across the transition near $k_F a \sim 1$.

(b) In the regime of small $m/M$, where the polaron-to-dimeron transition is known to become continuous at fixed impurity, determine whether, as a function of the mass ratio $m/M$, the transition at the critical value $1/(k_F a_c)$ is smooth — for instance, with the discontinuities $\Delta E$ in the ground-state energy and $\Delta Z$ in the quasiparticle residue vanishing as power laws $\Delta E \sim (m/M - r_c)^\alpha$ and $\Delta Z \sim (m/M - r_c)^\beta$ with exponents $\alpha,\beta>0$ as $m/M$ approaches a critical mass ratio $r_c$ from above — or whether it instead remains discontinuous (first order) up to that mass ratio.

Provide a definitive theoretical argument, or at least a plausibility argument, settling these questions.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether polaron and dimeron are genuinely distinct branches of the single-impurity Fermi gas, and whether the small-m/M continuous transition meets the first-order regime smoothly, remains open as a rigorous theoretical question. A first-order polaron-to-molecule transition is predicted at zero temperature in the single-impurity limit, but recent experiments (e.g., PRX 10, 041019, 2020) observe a smooth crossover under finite-temperature/density conditions, and recent works unify polaron and molecule into a single variational framework. No rigorous proof of continuity/discontinuity of the exact ground state, nor of the smoothness of the transition as a function of m/M, has been established.

Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $f\in K(x)$ be a rational function of degree $2$, viewed as a self-map of $\mathbb{P}^1$. Fix a basepoint $P\in\mathbb{P}^1(K)$ that is not a periodic point under $f$ in trivial cases, and form the infinite preimage tree
$$T_{f,\infty}(P)=\bigsqcup_{n\ge 0} f^{-n}(P),$$
in which the edges connect each $Q\in f^{-(n+1)}(P)$ to $f(Q)\in f^{-n}(P)$. Let $K_n$ denote the field obtained by adjoining to $K$ all elements of $f^{-n}(P)$, and let $K_\infty=\bigcup_n K_n$. The absolute Galois group of $K$ acts on $T_{f,\infty}(P)$ by tree automorphisms, giving the arboreal representation
$$\rho_{f,P}\colon \mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(T_{f,\infty}(P)).$$
Define the arboreal index
$$\iota_K(f,P)=[\mathrm{Aut}(T_{f,\infty}(P)):\mathrm{Im}(\rho_{f,P})].$$

Prove or disprove: $\iota_K(f,P)=\infty$ if and only if at least one of the following four conditions holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] The map $f$ is post-critically finite, i.e., each of the two critical points of $f$ is preperiodic under $f$.
\item[(b)] There exists an integer $r\ge 2$ such that the two critical points $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ of $f$ satisfy $f^r(\gamma_1)=f^r(\gamma_2)$.
\item[(c)] The basepoint $P$ is periodic under $f$.
\item[(d)] There exists a non-trivial Möbius transformation $\varphi(x)=\frac{\alpha x+\beta}{\gamma x+\delta}$ defined over $K$ such that $\varphi\circ f=f\circ\varphi$ and $\varphi(P)=P$.
\end{enumerate}

The conjecture characterizing when the arboreal representation associated to a degree-2 rational function over a characteristic-zero field has infinite index appears to remain open in full generality. Recent work (e.g., results on PCF quadratic rational maps and on rational maps with few critical points, 2018–2024) has established partial results — for instance, that PCF maps yield infinite index, and conditional results under Vojta's and the abc conjecture for polynomial cases — but no unconditional proof of the full biconditional has been reported.

Consider neutrino-induced coherent single kaon production on a nucleus,
ν + A → ℓ⁻ + K⁺ + A,
in which the target nucleus A is left in its ground state. At low neutrino energies, this charged-current process is strongly suppressed both by Cabibbo mixing and by a kinematic suppression associated with the kaon mass m_K, leading to a small cross section. As the neutrino energy increases, larger kaon momenta become available, which is expected to reduce the kinematic suppression due to m_K and to produce a rapid rise of the cross section.

Determine, both qualitatively (energy dependence) and quantitatively (absolute size in cm² per nucleus, on a typical nuclear target such as carbon (CH)), the charged-current coherent K⁺ production cross section σ(E_ν) for muon-neutrino energies in the few-GeV range characteristic of an on-axis NuMI-like beam (mean E_ν of order 3–6 GeV). In particular, predict dσ/dT_K and the integrated σ as functions of E_ν in this regime, where low-energy chiral / single-kaon models are no longer directly applicable, and compare to the analogous coherent pion production cross section.

MINERvA reported the first evidence (3.0σ) for charged-current coherent K⁺ production in neutrino–nucleus scattering in Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 061802 (2016), with 6 candidates over 1.77 expected background, and a companion measurement of inclusive K⁺ production in Phys. Rev. D 94, 012002 (2016) including a differential cross section dσ/dT_K that is roughly flat between 0–500 MeV. This provides an experimental constraint on the size of the cross section at MINERvA energies but does not yet constitute a precise measurement of the energy dependence; theoretical models extending beyond the low-energy regime remain under development.

Consider a single impurity particle of mass $M$ interacting with identical (spin-polarized) fermions of mass $m$ in three dimensions via a zero-range, wide-resonance s-wave interaction characterized by a scattering length $a$. The interaction is modeled by the standard pseudopotential / Bethe–Peierls boundary condition: the $N$-body wavefunction $\Psi$ for one impurity at position $\mathbf{R}$ and fermions at positions $\mathbf{r}_1,\dots,\mathbf{r}_N$ satisfies, for each $i$, the short-distance condition
$$\Psi \;\sim\; \Big(\tfrac{1}{|\mathbf{r}_i-\mathbf{R}|} - \tfrac{1}{a}\Big)\,\phi_i(\mathbf{R};\{\mathbf{r}_j\}_{j\neq i}) \quad \text{as } |\mathbf{r}_i-\mathbf{R}|\to 0,$$
and is otherwise a free-particle eigenstate of the kinetic energy. Let $X$ be a projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $f\colon X\to X$ be a polarizable endomorphism, meaning that there exist an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$ and an integer $q>1$ such that $f^*L\cong L^{\otimes q}$. A point $x\in X$ is called preperiodic under $f$ if its forward orbit $\{x, f(x), f^2(x),\dots\}$ is finite, and we denote by $\mathrm{PrePer}_f(X)$ the set of all preperiodic points. A closed subvariety $Y\subseteq X$ is called preperiodic if there exist integers $a\ge 0$ and $b\ge 1$ such that $f^{a+b}(Y) = f^a(Y)$.

For each smooth point $x\in X$, write $T_{X,x}$ for the Zariski tangent space of $X$ at $x$, and let $\mathrm{Gr}_d(T_{X,x})$ denote the Grassmannian of $d$-dimensional linear subspaces of $T_{X,x}$. The differential $df_x$ induces a map between Grassmannians on the orbit of $x$, and we say a tangent subspace $V\subseteq T_{X,x}$ is preperiodic under this induced action if its forward iterates eventually become periodic.

Let $Y\subseteq X$ be a closed subvariety such that no irreducible component of $Y$ is contained entirely in the singular locus of $X$. Prove or disprove the following equivalence:

(a) $Y$ is preperiodic under $f$.

(b) The intersection $Y\cap \mathrm{PrePer}_f(X)$ contains a Zariski dense subset $S$ of points which are smooth points of both $X$ and $Y$ such that, for every $x\in S$, the tangent space $T_{Y,x}\subseteq T_{X,x}$ (viewed as a point of $\mathrm{Gr}_{\dim Y}(T_{X,x})$) is preperiodic under the induced action of $f$.

Let $N \geq 1$ and $d \geq 2$ be integers. For a number field $K$, a morphism $f : \mathbb{P}^N \to \mathbb{P}^N$ defined over $K$ of degree $d$ is said to have good reduction at a non-archimedean place $\mathfrak{p}$ of $K$ (in the naive sense) if $f$ can be written using homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ whose coefficients are $\mathfrak{p}$-integral and whose reduction modulo $\mathfrak{p}$ defines a morphism $\mathbb{P}^N \to \mathbb{P}^N$ over the residue field; otherwise $\mathfrak{p}$ is a place of bad reduction. Let
$$\mathrm{PrePer}(f, \mathbb{P}^N(K)) = \{P \in \mathbb{P}^N(K) : f^{m+n}(P) = f^m(P) \text{ for some } m \geq 0,\, n \geq 1\}$$
denote the set of $K$-rational preperiodic points of $f$.

Find an explicit function $C(N, d, D, s)$ of four nonnegative integer variables such that for every number field $K$ with $[K:\mathbb{Q}] \leq D$ and every degree-$d$ morphism $f : \mathbb{P}^N \to \mathbb{P}^N$ over $K$ having at most $s$ places of bad reduction, one has
$$\#\,\mathrm{PrePer}(f, \mathbb{P}^N(K)) \leq C(N, d, D, s).$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The full problem—finding an explicit bound $C(N,d,D,s)$ for arbitrary morphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ over number fields—remains open and is closely tied to the Morton–Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture. Partial results exist: Benedetto (2007) established a bound of order $d^3(D+s)\log(D+s)$ for polynomial maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$; Canci–Paladino (2014) and subsequent improvements (e.g., Canci–Troncoso, 2016) provide weaker bounds for rational maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$. No explicit $C(N,d,D,s)$ is known for $N \geq 2$.

Consider an opinion-polling setting in which a respondent is sequentially asked binary questions. Model each question as a measurement on a state in some Hilbert space, where the state may be updated after each measurement according to the rule prescribed by the chosen quantum formalism. Assume that the modeling family of measurements satisfies the following two empirical properties simultaneously, for a generic class of questions:

(P1) Response replicability: for any question A, if A is asked, answered, and then asked again, the same answer is returned with probability 1; moreover, if a different question B is asked and answered between the two askings of A, the answer to A is still repeated with probability 1.

(P2) Question-order effect: there exist questions A and B and an initial state such that the joint probability of the answer pair (a,b) when A is asked before B differs from the joint probability of (a,b) when B is asked before A.

Within standard quantum mechanics where each question is represented by a Hermitian observable (equivalently, a projection-valued measure) with the Lüders state-update rule, prove that (P1) and (P2) cannot hold together. More generally, within the formalism of binary positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) with their associated Lüders/Kraus state updates, show that (P1) forces each POVM to be projective, and hence (P1) and (P2) are again incompatible.

Problem: Identify and justify a set of principles that delimits the domain of applicability of the quantum-mechanical formalism (Hermitian observables and binary POVMs together with the standard state-update rules) to such cognitive measurements—that is, principles which specify under what conditions the formalism may legitimately be used to model sequential question-answer behavior, under what conditions it must not, and which explain on a conceptual basis why no model in this formalism can exhibit both (P1) and (P2). Alternatively, exhibit a principled extension of the formalism (beyond binary POVMs) that accommodates (P1) and (P2) jointly while reducing to standard quantum mechanics in appropriate limits.

Consider a single distinguishable impurity of mass M immersed in a non-interacting three-dimensional Fermi gas of identical particles of mass m at zero temperature with Fermi momentum k_F, interacting with the impurity through a short-range two-body potential characterized by an s-wave scattering length a. The exact ground state of the impurity dressed by the Fermi sea can be expanded as

|Ψ⟩ = α₀ c_p† |FS⟩ + Σ α_{kq} c_{p+q-k}† b_k† b_q |FS⟩ + Σ α_{kk'qq'} c_{p+q+q'-k-k'}† b_k† b_{k'}† b_q b_{q'} |FS⟩ + …,

where c† creates the impurity, b†, b are creation/annihilation operators of the bath fermions, and |FS⟩ is the filled Fermi sea. Truncating this expansion at the n-th particle–hole pair defines the n-th order Chevy ansatz; the first-order truncation (n=1) is the original Chevy ansatz.

Address the following:

(a) Provide a rigorous explanation for why the first-order Chevy ansatz reproduces the polaron ground-state energy E and quasiparticle residue Z to within a few percent of exact results across the full BCS–BEC crossover, including the strongly interacting regime |1/(k_F a)| ≲ 1 where naively strong multi-particle–hole correlations are expected.

(b) Determine whether the particle–hole-pair expansion possesses a hidden small parameter that controls the convergence of successive truncations, and identify this parameter explicitly as a function of the mass ratio m/M and the dimensionless interaction strength 1/(k_F a).

(c) Identify the regimes (values of m/M, 1/(k_F a), and possibly impurity momentum p) in which the particle–hole-pair expansion fails to converge or converges only slowly.

(d) Establish quantitative bounds on the truncation error |E_n − E_exact| and |Z_n − Z_exact| as functions of the truncation order n, the mass ratio m/M, and 1/(k_F a).

Recent work (e.g., 2024 papers extending the Chevy ansatz to arbitrarily many particle–hole excitations and comparing with exact diagrammatic theory) has provided a partial explanation: higher-order particle–hole channels interfere destructively, making the first-order Chevy ansatz accurate to ~1–2% at unitarity for the equal-mass 3D Fermi polaron. Fix a one-parameter family of rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$, for example $f_c(x)=x^2+c$, more generally $f_{m,c}(x)=x^m+c$ with $m\ge 2$, or $f_b(x)=bx+x^{-1}$. For an integer $n\ge 1$, let $\Phi_n(x,t)$ denote the $n$-th dynatomic polynomial of the family (the polynomial whose roots are the points of formal period $n$, defined by $\Phi_n(x,t)=\prod_{d\mid n}(f^d(x)-x)^{\mu(n/d)}$ where $t$ is the parameter). Let $Y_0^{\rm dyn}(n)$ be the affine dynamical modular curve over $\mathbb{Z}$ parametrizing pairs (parameter, $n$-cycle) and let $Y_1^{\rm dyn}(n)$ be the affine dynamical modular curve parametrizing pairs (parameter, point of formal period $n$); explicitly, $Y_1^{\rm dyn}(n)$ is cut out by $\Phi_n(x,t)=0$.

(a) Determine the set of primes of bad reduction of $Y_0^{\rm dyn}(n)$ and of $Y_1^{\rm dyn}(n)$, i.e., the primes $p$ at which the reduction modulo $p$ fails to be smooth.

(b) Give a precise definition of "sporadic" prime of bad reduction, intended to capture primes outside an obvious finite set associated with the family $f$ (such as primes dividing $n$, or primes dividing a fixed discriminant of the family), and provide a geometric/dynamical explanation of such sporadic primes. (For example, computational evidence suggests that for $f_{m,c}(x)=x^m+c$, the sporadic primes for $n$-periodic points should be those not dividing $2nm$.)

(c) Describe the primes $p$ for which the reduction modulo $p$ of $Y_0^{\rm dyn}(n)$ and/or $Y_1^{\rm dyn}(n)$ is geometrically irreducible. For $Y_1^{\rm dyn}(n)$ this amounts to characterizing the primes $p$ such that $\Phi_n(x,t)$ remains irreducible in $\overline{\mathbb{F}_p}[x,t]$.

Let $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ denote an algebraic closure of the field $\mathbb{Q}$ of rational numbers, and let $\mathbb{A}^N$ denote affine $N$-space. Let
$$f : \mathbb{A}^N \longrightarrow \mathbb{A}^N$$
be a morphism defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, given by polynomial coordinate functions $f = (f_1, \ldots, f_N)$ with $f_i \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}[x_1, \ldots, x_N]$. For a point $P \in \mathbb{A}^N(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$, the forward orbit of $P$ under $f$ is the set $\mathcal{O}_f(P) = \{P, f(P), f^2(P), f^3(P), \ldots\}$, where $f^n$ denotes the $n$-fold composition of $f$ with itself.

Assume that there does not exist any non-constant rational function $g \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}(x_1, \ldots, x_N)$ such that $g \circ f = g$ (i.e., $f$ admits no non-constant invariant rational function).

Prove or disprove: under this hypothesis, there exists a point $P \in \mathbb{A}^N(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ whose forward orbit $\mathcal{O}_f(P)$ is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^N$.

The Zariski Dense Orbit Conjecture (Medvedev–Scanlon; Amerik–Bogomolov–Rovinsky) is open in general. Proven cases relevant to this affine setting include: split polynomial maps on $\mathbb{A}^N$ (i.e., $(x_1,\dots,x_N)\mapsto(f_1(x_1),\dots,f_N(x_N))$) by Medvedev–Scanlon; endomorphisms of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$; smooth projective surfaces (Xie, with appendix by Tucker); and various tori/threefold cases. The general statement for arbitrary morphisms $f:\mathbb{A}^N\to\mathbb{A}^N$ over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ remains unresolved as of recent literature (2024).

Consider the framework of quantum probability applied to cognitive measurements. In this framework, a cognitive state is represented by a unit vector (or density operator) ψ in a complex Hilbert space H, and a yes/no question Q is represented by an orthogonal projector P_Q on H, so that the probability of the answer "yes" is ⟨ψ, P_Q ψ⟩, and the post-measurement state is given by Lüders' rule ψ ↦ P_Q ψ / ‖P_Q ψ‖ for a "yes" outcome (and analogously for "no"). Two questions Q_A, Q_B are modelled by projectors P_A, P_B which may or may not commute.

Two empirical phenomena are relevant:

(i) Question-order effects: for many pairs of questions A, B observed in surveys, the joint probability of answering "yes" to A and then "yes" to B differs from the joint probability of answering "yes" to B and then "yes" to A. Within the quantum framework this is reproduced precisely when [P_A, P_B] ≠ 0.

(ii) Response replicability: if the same question Q is asked twice in immediate succession (with no intervening question), the respondent gives the same answer with probability 1. In the standard projective model with Lüders updating this is automatic for a single Q, but if Q is asked, then a non-commuting Q' is asked, and then Q is asked again, the model generally predicts a non-zero probability of a different answer to the repeated Q, contrary to typical empirical findings.

Problem. Identify a minimal set of mathematical features of the quantum-probabilistic formalism — drawn from the list including (a) representation of states as vectors/density operators in a Hilbert space, (b) representation of questions as projectors versus more general POVMs, (c) non-commutativity of observables, (d) the Lüders state-update rule versus alternative update rules, (e) use of complex versus real Hilbert spaces, (f) interference between probability amplitudes, (g) contextuality in the Kochen–Specker sense — that are simultaneously:

  (1) necessary to reproduce the observed question-order effects (in the sense that omitting any one of them precludes a model from fitting the empirically observed asymmetry between Pr(A=yes, then B=yes) and Pr(B=yes, then A=yes) on standard survey data); and

  (2) compatible with exact response replicability, i.e. Pr(Q = x at time t_3 | Q = x at time t_1, Q' = y at time t_2) = 1 for every intervening question Q' and every answer y of positive probability.

Determine whether such a set of features exists, and if so characterise it; if not, prove an impossibility theorem showing that within the projective/Lüders quantum formalism the conjunction of (1) and (2) cannot be realised, and identify which feature must be modified or dropped.

The tension between non-commuting projectors (needed for question-order effects) and exact response replicability is a recognized open issue in quantum cognition. Consider a single impurity particle of bare mass $M$ immersed in an ideal (non-interacting) spin-polarized atomic Fermi gas of bath particles. Depending on the interaction strength and mass ratio, the impurity can bind one or more bath fermions to form composite few-body bound states in vacuum: a dimer (impurity + 1 bath fermion), a trimer (impurity + 2 bath fermions), a tetramer (impurity + 3 bath fermions), etc. Let $M_b$ denote the bare mass of such a composite bound state in vacuum (so for the dimer $M_b = M + m$, for the trimer $M_b = M + 2m$, etc., where $m$ is the bath atom mass).

When the Fermi sea is turned on, each such composite bound state becomes a dressed quasiparticle: the dimeron, trimeron, tetrameron, .... These dressed quasiparticles have a well-defined quasiparticle effective mass $M_b^*$ defined from the curvature of their dispersion at zero momentum.

Question: Is it true that, for every such composite dressed quasiparticle (dimeron, trimeron, tetrameron, and analogously for larger composites), the dressing by the Fermi sea cannot decrease the inertial mass, i.e.
$$\frac{M_b^*}{M_b} \;\ge\; 1\,?$$
Equivalently, prove or disprove that this inequality holds as a general bound (stronger than mere positivity of the effective mass) for all composite quasiparticles of an impurity in an ideal Fermi gas, across all coupling strengths and mass ratios for which the composite quasiparticle exists.

Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety defined over a number field $K$, and let $f\colon X\dashrightarrow X$ be a dominant rational self-map defined over $K$. Define the (first) dynamical degree of $f$ by
$$\delta_f \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\deg(f^n)\bigr)^{1/n},$$
where $\deg(f^n)$ denotes the degree of $f^n$ with respect to a fixed ample divisor on $X$ (the limit is independent of this choice). For a point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ whose forward orbit $\{P,f(P),f^2(P),\dots\}$ is well-defined, define the arithmetic degree of $f$ at $P$ by
$$\alpha_f(P) \;=\; \limsup_{n\to\infty} \max\bigl(1,\,h_X(f^n(P))\bigr)^{1/n},$$
where $h_X$ is a Weil height on $X$ associated to an ample divisor.

The following are known/conjectured for points $P\in X(\overline{K})$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(A)] (Existence/upper bound) The limsup defining $\alpha_f(P)$ is in fact a limit, and $\alpha_f(P)\le \delta_f$.
\item[(B)] (Equality conjecture) If the forward orbit of $P$ under $f$ is well-defined and Zariski dense in $X$, then $\alpha_f(P)=\delta_f$.
\end{itemize}

Question: To what extent do statements (A) and (B) remain valid if one restricts the point $P$ to lie in $X(K)$, the set of $K$-rational points of $X$, rather than allowing $P\in X(\overline{K})$? In particular, is the analogue of (A) known unconditionally for $P\in X(K)$, and for which classes of varieties $X$ and rational self-maps $f$ does the analogue of (B) hold for $P\in X(K)$ with Zariski dense $f$-orbit?

The upper bound part (A) was established in general by Kawaguchi–Silverman and Matsuzawa, and works equally well over a fixed number field K. The equality part (B), the Kawaguchi–Silverman conjecture, remains open in general as of 2024–2026. Many partial results are known (e.g., for surjective endomorphisms of projective surfaces, for abelian varieties, for varieties with sufficiently large irregularity, for certain automorphisms of threefolds, and for int-amplified endomorphisms), but the general case—whether stated over Q̄ or restricted to a number field K—is unresolved.

Let N ≥ 1 and let f : ℙ^N ⤏ ℙ^N be a dominant rational map defined over ℂ. Write f^n = f ∘ f ∘ ⋯ ∘ f for the n-th iterate (as a rational map), and let deg(f^n) denote the degree of f^n, i.e., the common degree of the homogeneous polynomials of minimal degree (with no common factor) defining f^n. The (first) dynamical degree of f is defined by

  δ_f := lim_{n→∞} deg(f^n)^{1/n},

a limit which is known to exist in [1, ∞).

Prove or disprove: for every dominant rational map f : ℙ^N ⤏ ℙ^N, the dynamical degree δ_f is an algebraic integer, i.e., a root of a monic polynomial with integer coefficients.

The Bellon–Viallet integrality conjecture has been disproved in general: Bell, Diller, and Jonsson (2021, published in Proc. London Math. Soc. 2024) constructed birational self-maps of ℙ^d for d ≥ 3 whose first dynamical degree is a transcendental number. The conjecture remains true in low-dimensional / special cases (e.g., birational surface maps by Diller–Favre 2001, polynomial maps of ℂ² by Favre–Jonsson 2007, monomial maps), but is false as stated for general dominant rational maps of ℙ^N.

Consider the use of quantum-mechanical (QM) formalism — Hilbert spaces, projection-valued observables, the Born rule, and non-commuting measurement operators — as a model for human responses in opinion polling, where empirical phenomena such as repeated-response stability and question-order effects are observed. Suppose these same phenomena admit alternative "traditional" psychological explanations, e.g.:
(i) memory of previous answers (a respondent recalls and reproduces the answer they just gave), and
(ii) ordinary context changes (the act of answering one question alters the cognitive context in which the next is interpreted).

Address the following two questions:
(A) If such traditional psychological mechanisms are admitted as explanations of repeated-response stability and order effects in opinion polling, identify a principled criterion that prevents these same mechanisms from intervening in physical situations where the QM formalism is regarded as successfully applicable (e.g., sequential measurements on microscopic systems). In particular, exhibit either a structural feature of the physical setting that excludes memory- and context-based explanations, or show that no such criterion exists.

(B) Determine whether the empirical regularities of repeated responses and question-order effects in opinion polling can be fully accounted for by traditional psychological mechanisms (memory plus context change) alone, so that the QM formalism is dispensable in this domain; or, conversely, exhibit a behavioral signature observable in opinion-polling data that is reproduced by the QM model but cannot be reproduced by any model based solely on such traditional mechanisms.

Subsequent literature continues to debate whether QM-style models for opinion polling provide genuine explanatory advantages over classical psychological mechanisms (memory, context), with no consensus resolution; the underlying issue remains an open foundational problem.

Let $N\ge 1$ and $k\ge 1$ be integers. For a dominant rational self-map $g:\mathbb{P}^N\dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^N$, let $\deg(g)$ denote the degree of $g$ (the common degree of the homogeneous polynomials defining $g$ in coprime form), and define the (first) dynamical degree of $g$ by
$$\delta(g)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\deg(g^n)\bigr)^{1/n},$$
where $g^n$ is the $n$-fold iterate of $g$ and the limit is known to exist.

Let $\{f_T:\mathbb{P}^N\dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^N\}$ be a family of dominant rational maps depending rationally on parameters $T=(T_1,\ldots,T_k)$; that is, the coordinates of $f_T$ are given by homogeneous polynomials in the coordinates of $\mathbb{P}^N$ whose coefficients are rational functions of $T$. Write $f_t$ for the specialization at $t\in\mathbb{C}^k$ (defined whenever the coefficients are regular at $t$ and $f_t$ remains dominant), and let $f$ denote the generic member, viewed over the function field $\mathbb{C}(T)$, with dynamical degree $\delta(f)$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every $\varepsilon>0$, the set
$$\bigl\{\,t\in\mathbb{C}^k : \delta(f_t)\le \delta(f)-\varepsilon\,\bigr\}$$
is not Zariski dense in $\mathbb{C}^k$. In particular, for one-parameter families ($k=1$), establish that this set is finite.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent work by Junyi Xie and others studies lower semicontinuity of dynamical degrees in families and proves related partial results (e.g., for mixed degrees and certain classes of maps), but the full conjecture that the locus of parameters where the dynamical degree drops by at least $\varepsilon$ is not Zariski dense (and is finite when $k=1$) does not appear to be settled in general.

Let $N\ge 1$ be an integer and let $f:\mathbb{P}^N\dashrightarrow\mathbb{P}^N$ be a dominant rational self-map of complex projective $N$-space. For each integer $n\ge 0$, let $f^n$ denote the $n$-th iterate of $f$ (as a rational map), and let $\deg(f^n)$ be its degree, defined as the degree of the homogeneous polynomials representing $f^n$ in any reduced expression (equivalently, the pullback degree on hyperplane classes). Set $f^0=\mathrm{id}$, so $\deg(f^0)=1$. The (first) dynamical degree of $f$ is
$$\delta(f)\;=\;\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\deg(f^n)\bigr)^{1/n},$$
which is known to exist and to satisfy $\delta(f)\le \deg(f^{n+1})/\deg(f^n)\cdot\bigl(\text{something}\bigr)$ in various weak senses, but in general $\delta(f)$ may be strictly less than $\deg(f)$ due to indeterminacies.

Prove or disprove the following statement: there exists a constant $\gamma_N>0$, depending only on $N$, such that for every dominant rational map $f:\mathbb{P}^N\dashrightarrow\mathbb{P}^N$ one has
$$\delta(f)\;\ge\;\gamma_N\cdot\min_{0\le n<N}\frac{\deg(f^{n+1})}{\deg(f^n)}.$$

Let $N\ge 1$ and let $f:\mathbb{P}^N\dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^N$ be a dominant rational map defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. For each integer $n\ge 0$ let $f^n$ denote the $n$-th iterate of $f$ (defined as a rational self-map of $\mathbb{P}^N$), and let $\deg(f^n)$ denote its degree. The (first) dynamical degree of $f$ is
$$\delta_f \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\deg(f^n)\bigr)^{1/n},$$
which is known to exist. Fix an absolute logarithmic Weil height $h:\mathbb{P}^N(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\to[0,\infty)$. For a point $P\in\mathbb{P}^N(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ whose forward orbit $\{f^n(P):n\ge 0\}$ is well-defined (i.e., no iterate lands in the indeterminacy locus of $f$), define the arithmetic degree
$$\alpha_f(P) \;=\; \limsup_{n\to\infty} h\bigl(f^n(P)\bigr)^{1/n}.$$

Question: Does there exist an integer $\ell_f$ with $0\le \ell_f\le N$, depending only on $f$, such that for every $P\in\mathbb{P}^N(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ with well-defined forward $f$-orbit one has the upper bound
$$h\bigl(f^n(P)\bigr) \;=\; O\!\left(\delta_f^{\,n}\, n^{\ell_f}\right)\qquad\text{as } n\to\infty,$$
and moreover such that for every $P$ whose forward orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^N$ the limit
$$\widehat{h}_f(P) \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{h(f^n(P))}{\delta_f^{\,n}\, n^{\ell_f}}$$
exists and is strictly positive?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question concerns the existence of an integer exponent $\ell_f$ governing the polynomial correction to the exponential growth $\delta_f^n$ of heights along orbits of a dominant rational self-map of $\mathbb{P}^N$. This is part of the Kawaguchi–Silverman circle of conjectures on dynamical/arithmetic degrees and canonical heights. While many partial cases are known (e.g., morphisms, surfaces, abelian varieties, certain product varieties), the general existence and finiteness of such an $\ell_f$ for arbitrary dominant rational self-maps of projective space remains open as of recent surveys.

Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $f\colon X \dashrightarrow X$ be a dominant rational map. For each integer $1 \le i \le N$, the $i$-th dynamical degree of $f$ is defined as
$$\delta_f^{(i)} \;=\; \lim_{n \to \infty} \bigl( (f^n)^{*} H^i \cdot H^{N-i} \bigr)^{1/n},$$
where $H$ is an ample divisor class on $X$ and $(f^n)^{*}$ denotes the pullback action on the cohomology group $H^{i,i}(X)$ (or equivalently on the Néron–Severi group when $i=1$); this limit exists, is independent of the choice of $H$, and is a birational invariant.

Question: Is it true that for every smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $N$ and every dominant rational self-map $f\colon X \dashrightarrow X$, all of the higher-order dynamical degrees $\delta_f^{(i)}$, $1 \le i \le N$, are algebraic integers?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Bell, Diller, and Jonsson constructed an explicit dominant rational self-map of $\mathbb{P}^2$ whose first dynamical degree is a transcendental number (published as "A transcendental dynamical degree"), and this was extended to birational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^d$ for $d \ge 3$ ("Birational maps with transcendental dynamical degree", Proc. London Math. Soc., 2024). These examples show that dynamical degrees need not even be algebraic numbers, hence not algebraic integers in general, answering the question in the negative.

representations.normalized:
Consider a quantum system in three-dimensional vacuum consisting of a single distinguishable impurity particle of mass M and N identical (spin-polarized) non-interacting fermions of mass m, where the impurity interacts with each fermion through a short-range, zero-range two-body interaction characterized by a positive s-wave scattering length a > 0, while the identical fermions do not interact with one another. Let the mass ratio satisfy m/M < 13.384, the threshold below which the three-body Efimov effect (heavy-heavy-light Efimov states for two heavy fermions plus one light impurity, or its analogue) does not occur, so that the spectrum of universal bound clusters is non-Efimovian. It is known that for suitable values of m/M and a > 0 there exist stable bound states of the impurity with two, three, and four identical fermions (the dimer, trimer, and tetramer).

Question: For which values of N ≥ 5 (pentamer, hexamer, and larger clusters consisting of one impurity bound to N identical fermions) and which mass ratios m/M < 13.384 do there exist stable, non-Efimovian few-body bound states in vacuum at positive scattering length a > 0? In particular, determine whether such larger bound clusters exist at all, and if so characterize the range of mass ratios for which each cluster size is bound.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has provided partial answers: a universal non-Efimovian (4+1) pentamer continuing the dimer–trimer–tetramer series has been established for sufficiently large mass ratio, while no (5+1) six-body bound state (hexamer) has been found in the explored mass-ratio range up to M/m ≲ 12, with the p-shell argument suggesting a qualitative change at N = 6. A complete classification of stable larger clusters for all m/M < 13.384 has not been established.
