representations.normalized:
Setting. Work in the algebra of symmetric functions in variables x = (x_1,x_2,...) over the field Q(q,t). For coprime positive integers a,b let e^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) and h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) denote the rectangular (q,t)-elementary and (q,t)-complete symmetric functions associated with the (ad,bd)-rectangle, defined as the images, under the operators of the elliptic Hall algebra acting on symmetric functions, of e_d and h_d via the natural slope-(b/a) action (so that for d=1 these reduce to the (a,b)-elementary and complete symmetric functions of rectangular Catalan combinatorics, and for (a,b) = (1,1) they specialize to the standard nabla-deformed e_d and h_d).

For arbitrary positive integers m,n with d = gcd(m,n) and m = ad, n = bd, set
   e_{m,n}(x;q,t) := e^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t),    h_{m,n}(x;q,t) := h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t).

Schur order. For two symmetric functions F,G ∈ Λ ⊗ Q(q,t) write F ⪯_s G iff G − F expands in the Schur basis with coefficients that are polynomials in q,t with nonnegative integer coefficients.

Staircase exponents. For positive integers m,n let the (m,n)-staircase be the lattice path from (0,n) to (m,0) lying just below the diagonal joining these two points; let α'(m,n) denote the number of integer points strictly between the (m,n−1)-staircase and the minimal (m,n)-staircase, and let β'(m,n) be the analogous count obtained by exchanging the roles of e and h (the count appropriate to the transpose/complete-homogeneous version below).

Problem. Prove that for every pair of integers m,n ≥ 1 the following Schur-positivity inequalities hold:
   (i)  q^{α'(m,n)} · e_{m,n−1}(x;q,t)  ⪯_s  e_{m,n}(x;q,t),
   (ii) q^{β'(m,n)} · e_{m,n−1}(x;q,t)  ⪯_s  (−qt)^{1−d} · h_{m,n}(x;q,t).

It is desired, moreover, to realize each inequality as the bigraded character identity coming from an explicit inclusion of bigraded S_N-modules (where N is the appropriate degree), so that the difference of the two sides is the bigraded Frobenius characteristic of an S_N-module quotient.

Setup. Let $\Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)}$ denote the ring of symmetric functions in variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. Assume one has, for each pair of coprime positive integers $(a,b)$, a family of linear operators
$$\Theta_{a,b}(f_d):\Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)}\longrightarrow \Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)},$$
indexed by "seed" symmetric functions $f_d$ of degree $d$ (the operators arise from the elliptic Hall algebra / rectangular Catalan combinatorics framework, generalizing the nabla operator). For a seed $f_d$ and coprime $a,b\ge 1$, define the symmetric function
$$f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) := \Theta_{a,b}(f_d)(1).$$

Question. Prove or disprove: for every seed $f_d$ and every pair of coprime integers $a,b\ge 1$, the specialization at $t=1$ of the operator $\Theta_{a,b}(f_d)$ acts on $\Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q)}$ as multiplication by the symmetric function $f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)$; that is,
$$\Theta_{a,b}(f_d)(g(x))\big|_{t=1} \;=\; f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)\cdot g(x)$$
for every symmetric function $g(x)$.

Equivalently, establish the multiplicativity identity
$$(f_d\, g_k)^{(a,b)}(x;q,1) \;=\; f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)\, g_k^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)$$
for all seeds $f_d, g_k$ and all coprime $a,b\ge 1$.

Let $\Lambda$ denote the ring of symmetric functions in infinitely many variables $x = (x_1, x_2, \ldots)$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. For a partition $\mu = (\mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots)$, let $m_\mu(x)$ denote the monomial symmetric function and $\ell(\mu)$ the number of (nonzero) parts of $\mu$, with $|\mu| = d$. For coprime integers $a, b \geq 1$, let $\Theta_{a,b}$ be the rectangular-Catalan symmetric-function operator on $\Lambda$ associated with the slope $b/a$ (the operator built from the modified Macdonald and nabla-type operators that conjecturally produces the rectangular $(a,b)$-Catalan symmetric function when applied to $1$). For a partition $\mu$ of $d$, define
$$m^{(a,b)}_\mu(x; q, t) \;:=\; \Theta_{a,b}(m_\mu)\big|_{1},$$
that is, the symmetric function in $\Lambda$ obtained by applying $\Theta_{a,b}(m_\mu)$ to the constant $1$. Substitute $t = 1 + r$ to obtain $m^{(a,b)}_\mu(x; q, 1+r) \in \Lambda \otimes \mathbb{Q}(q,r)$.

(i) Prove or disprove: for every partition $\mu \vdash d$ and every pair of coprime integers $a, b \geq 1$, the renormalized symmetric function
$$(-1)^{d - \ell(\mu)}\, m^{(a,b)}_\mu(x; q, 1+r)$$
is $e$-positive, meaning that when expanded in the basis $\{e_\lambda(x)\}_{\lambda \vdash d}$ of elementary symmetric functions, all coefficients lie in $\mathbb{N}[q, r]$.

(ii) If $e$-positivity holds, exhibit an explicit combinatorial interpretation of these coefficients as a weighted enumeration of lattice paths (in the style of a $q,t$-statistic on Dyck paths in the $a \times b$ rectangle) that explains the positivity.

The construction of a fully self-consistent global model for the electrodynamics of an obliquely rotating pulsar magnetosphere and wind remains an open problem. Force-free, MHD, and particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of oblique rotators (e.g., Philippov–Spitkovsky and successors, and radiative MHD treatments through 2022–2024) have made substantial progress in modeling global field structure and spin-down, but they rely on idealizations (force-free closure, prescribed pair injection, limited resolution of gaps) and have not produced a complete consistent description that simultaneously resolves the inductive field, displacement current, E_∥ ≠ 0 acceleration regions, and the global circuit without corotation assumptions. No widely accepted pulsar emission mechanism has been established.

Let $C$ be a smooth complex projective curve of genus $g$, and let $\mathrm{gon}(C)$ denote its gonality, i.e., the minimal degree of a non-constant morphism from $C$ to $\mathbb{P}^1$. Let $K_C$ be the canonical line bundle of $C$, and for $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ let $L_d$ be a line bundle on $C$ of degree $d$.

For a line bundle $L$ on $C$ and an auxiliary line bundle $B$, the Koszul cohomology group $K_{p,q}(C, B; L)$ is defined as the cohomology in the middle of the complex
$$\wedge^{p+1} H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C, B + (q-1)L) \to \wedge^p H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C, B + qL) \to \wedge^{p-1} H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C, B + (q+1)L).$$

Prove or disprove: there exists an integer $d_0$ (depending on $C$) such that for every line bundle $L_d$ on $C$ with $d \geq d_0$, and for every integer $p \geq 0$,
$$K_{p,1}(C, K_C; L_d) \neq 0 \iff \mathrm{gon}(C) \leq p+1.$$

Construct rational two-dimensional conformal field theories satisfying the geometric/categorical axioms of Kontsevich–Segal and the Moore–Seiberg axioms, or at least prove that such rational conformal field theories exist.

In more detail: a Segal-type two-dimensional conformal field theory is a symmetric monoidal projective functor from the category whose objects are disjoint unions of unit circles and whose morphisms are conformal equivalence classes of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary (composed by sewing) to the category of locally convex topological vector spaces, together with the additional analytic and modular data (modular functor, factorization on sewing of surfaces of all genera, modular invariance of partition and correlation functions, duality and crossing relations) singled out by Moore and Seiberg. A conformal field theory is called rational if the associated space of states decomposes as a finite direct sum of irreducible representations of a pair of commuting chiral algebras and the corresponding modular functor takes values in finite-dimensional vector spaces.

(a) Produce a mathematical construction of a class of such rational conformal field theories satisfying all of these axioms (genus-zero, genus-one, and higher-genus sewing, modular invariance, and the Moore–Seiberg consistency relations), or alternatively give a proof that such theories exist.

(b) In particular, carry this out for the Wess–Zumino–Witten models associated to a simple, simply connected compact Lie group G at every positive integer level k, and for the Virasoro minimal models with central charge c = 1 − 6(p−q)^2/(pq) for coprime integers p, q ≥ 2: construct them, or prove their existence, as rational conformal field theories satisfying the Kontsevich–Segal and Moore–Seiberg axioms.

A long-running program of Y.-Z. Huang has constructed rational closed conformal field theories from representations of vertex operator algebras, including the Wess–Zumino–Novikov–Witten models and the Virasoro minimal models, and has established as theorems many of the key required structures (operator product expansion, modular invariance, Verlinde formula, modular tensor category structure, full rational CFT). Let V be the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory in the sense of two-dimensional conformal field theory, so that V = ⨁_{n} V_{(n)} is a graded vector space equipped with intertwining operators producing the conformal-field correlation maps for genus-zero Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundaries. Suppose V carries an inner product (a nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form) that is compatible with — i.e. invariant under — the conformal fields constructed from these intertwining operators.

Two completions of V are considered:

(a) The locally convex topological completion V^{LC} obtained from V by adjoining elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces (i.e. the completion arising from the Kontsevich–Segal-type sewing of higher-genus surfaces, viewed as a locally convex topological vector space with the induced grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form).

(b) The Hilbert space completion V^{H} of V with respect to the norm associated to the given inner product, regarded as a locally convex topological vector space with its grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form.

Question: Are V^{LC} and V^{H} isomorphic as locally convex topological vector spaces equipped with grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form?

Let G be a compact connected semisimple Lie group and let K be the centralizer in G of a torus, so that the homogeneous space M = G/K is a generalized flag manifold. Fix an Ad(G)-invariant inner product on the Lie algebra g of G (e.g. the negative of the Killing form), and let m be the orthogonal complement of the Lie algebra k of K in g, so that the isotropy representation of K on m decomposes into a finite direct sum of pairwise inequivalent irreducible Ad(K)-submodules m = m_1 ⊕ m_2 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ m_s (the "isotropy summands"). A G-invariant Riemannian metric on M then corresponds, up to scaling on each summand, to a positive-definite diagonal form g = x_1 B|_{m_1} + ⋯ + x_s B|_{m_s} with x_i > 0, and the Einstein condition Ric(g) = c·g reduces to a polynomial system in the variables x_1, …, x_s.

Develop a general method, applicable to generalized flag manifolds with an arbitrary (in particular, large) number s of isotropy summands — most notably those associated with the classical Lie groups SO(n), SU(n), and Sp(n) — that determines, up to homothety and isometry, the exact total number of G-invariant Einstein metrics on M = G/K and provides a complete classification of these metrics (distinguishing Kähler-Einstein metrics from non-Kähler Einstein metrics).

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Complete classifications of G-invariant Einstein metrics on generalized flag manifolds are known when the number of isotropy summands is small (2, 3, 4, and 5 summands have been treated in full, and several families with 6 summands have been resolved). For flag manifolds of classical Lie groups with many isotropy summands, only partial results exist, due to the difficulty of computing structure constants and Gröbner bases of the resulting polynomial Einstein systems. A general classification method covering arbitrarily many isotropy summands remains open.

Consider the collection $\mathcal{M}$ of all (isomorphism classes of) two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs), where a two-dimensional CFT is understood in the standard mathematical sense (e.g., as a unitary full CFT consisting of a pair of vertex operator algebras for the chiral and anti-chiral sectors, together with a modular-invariant torus partition function and a consistent collection of correlation functions on Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus, or equivalently as a Segal-type functor from a category of Riemann surfaces with conformal structure to a category of Hilbert spaces). A CFT is called rational if its chiral algebra is a rational vertex operator algebra, i.e., it has finitely many irreducible modules and its category of modules is a modular tensor category.

(a) Endow $\mathcal{M}$ with a natural topology and a geometric structure (for instance, that of a (possibly infinite-dimensional, stratified) manifold or analytic space) such that continuous deformations of CFTs—e.g., exactly marginal deformations driven by exactly marginal operators—correspond to continuous paths, and such that the central charge and other natural invariants vary continuously.

(b) With respect to such a topology and geometric structure on $\mathcal{M}$, prove that every rational conformal field theory is an isolated point of $\mathcal{M}$, i.e., that no rational CFT admits a nontrivial continuous family of CFT deformations.

The problem of equipping the moduli space of 2D CFTs with topological/geometric structure and proving rational CFTs are isolated points remains open as a general mathematical statement. Partial results and supporting evidence exist: in physics literature it is widely believed that RCFTs are typically isolated (e.g., not dense in CFT moduli spaces of Calabi–Yau sigma models for n>2), and rational points have been studied in specific c=1, c=3/2 examples and via complex-multiplication criteria, but a general topological/geometric framework on the full moduli space and a proof of isolatedness in that setting has not been established.

Let $V=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}V_{(n)}$ be a simple vertex operator algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying:
(1) $V_{(0)}=\mathbb{C}\mathbf{1}$ and $V_{(n)}=0$ for $n<0$, and the contragredient module $V'$ is isomorphic to $V$ as a $V$-module;
(2) $V$ is $C_2$-cofinite, i.e. $\dim V/C_2(V)<\infty$, where $C_2(V)$ is the subspace of $V$ spanned by elements of the form $\operatorname{Res}_x x^{-2}Y(u,x)v$ for $u,v\in V$, with $Y:V\otimes V\to V[[x,x^{-1}]]$ the vertex operator map.

Under these hypotheses, the category of grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules carries a natural braided tensor category structure (the logarithmic vertex tensor category structure of Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang).

Prove or disprove: this braided tensor category is rigid, i.e., every object admits a left and a right dual in the tensor-categorical sense.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The conjecture is established in important special cases but remains open in full generality. Huang proved rigidity (and modularity) when $V$ is additionally rational. McRae has shown rigidity under the additional assumption that the modular $S$-transformation of the character of $V$ is a linear combination of characters of $V$-modules. Recent work (e.g., on $N=1$ super-Virasoro and Virasoro logarithmic minimal models) verifies rigidity in further specific $C_2$-cofinite (non-rational) examples, but no general proof for all simple, self-contragredient, $C_2$-cofinite VOAs is known.

Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $B$ be a line bundle on $C$. For each integer $d$, let $L_d$ be a line bundle on $C$ of degree $d$. Recall that for line bundles $L$ and $B$ on $C$, the Koszul cohomology group $K_{p,q}(C,B;L)$ is defined as the cohomology at the middle term of the complex
$$\wedge^{p+1} H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C,B \otimes L^{q-1}) \longrightarrow \wedge^p H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C,B \otimes L^q) \longrightarrow \wedge^{p-1} H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C,B \otimes L^{q+1}),$$
where the differentials are the standard Koszul differentials. Recall also that a line bundle $B$ on $C$ is called $p$-very ample if for every effective divisor $\xi$ on $C$ of degree $p+1$, the restriction map $H^0(C,B) \to H^0(C, B \otimes \mathcal{O}_\xi)$ is surjective.

Determine, in terms of $p$ and $B$, exactly those non-negative integers $p$ for which the weight-one Koszul cohomology group
$$K_{p,1}(C, B; L_d)$$
is nonzero for all sufficiently large $d$ (equivalently, characterize when it vanishes for $d \gg 0$).

For each $g \in G$, consider the category of grading-restricted generalized $g$-twisted $V$-modules, and the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators of types $\binom{W_3}{W_1\,W_2}$ where $W_i$ is a $g_i$-twisted $V$-module and $g_3 = g_1 g_2$.

(a) Determine sufficient (and, if possible, necessary) conditions on $V$ and on $G$ under which the system of all such twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the $g$-twisted $V$-modules for all $g \in G$ satisfies the associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance properties (analogous to those known for finite $G$ and for the untwisted logarithmic case).

Let $V$ be a rational vertex operator algebra (in particular, $V$ is assumed to be of CFT type, $C_2$-cofinite, and to have semisimple module category, so that the standard construction of chiral genus-zero correlation functions from intertwining operators among irreducible $V$-modules is available). For each pair of irreducible $V$-modules $W_i, W_j, W_k$ let $\mathcal{V}^{k}_{ij}$ denote the space of intertwining operators of type $\binom{W_k}{W_i\,W_j}$, viewed as formal series-valued maps $W_i\otimes W_j\to W_k\{z\}[\log z]$.

To construct chiral correlation functions on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\ge 1$ with marked points, one performs the following sewing/gluing procedure. Start from a (possibly disconnected, lower-genus or many-pointed) surface $\Sigma_0$ together with a chiral $n$-point function built as a (formal) sum
$$F(w_1,\dots,w_n;\,q_1,\dots,q_r) \;=\; \sum_{M_1,\dots,M_r}\; \mathrm{tr}_{M}\bigl(\mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1)\cdots \mathcal{Y}_n(w_n,z_n)\,q_1^{L(0)}\cdots\bigr)$$
of products and (pseudo-)$q$-traces of intertwining operators $\mathcal{Y}_\ell$, the sums ranging over complete sets of irreducible $V$-modules inserted at the nodes that are pinched to obtain $\Sigma$ from $\Sigma_0$ via the standard sewing of local coordinates with sewing parameters $q_1,\dots,q_r$.

Problem. Prove that for every choice of marked points, local coordinates, and module insertions $w_1,\dots,w_n$, the formal series $F$ defined above is absolutely convergent on a nonempty open subset of the parameter space (and in particular in a punctured polydisk in the sewing parameters $q_1,\dots,q_r$), so that this construction unambiguously defines higher-genus chiral correlation functions associated to a rational conformal field theory built from $V$.

Substantial progress has been made. Bin Gui (arXiv:2011.07450, published in Commun. Contemp. Math. 2023) proved convergence of Segal's sewing of conformal blocks for analytic families of pointed compact Riemann surfaces under $C_2$-cofiniteness. More recently, Gui and Hao Zhang (arXiv:2411.07707, 2024) established higher-genus convergence of sewing for $C_2$-cofinite (logarithmic) chiral CFTs and the convergence of higher-genus pseudo-$q$-traces. These results cover the rational case and a broad logarithmic generalization, but the general convergence problem for all higher-genus correlation functions built from intertwining operators in arbitrary settings is regarded as a long-standing problem with these recent advances representing major partial/affirmative answers in the rational and $C_2$-cofinite settings.

Let $V$ be a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra: a $\mathbb{Z}$-graded vector space $V=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} V_{(n)}$ with $\dim V_{(n)}<\infty$ and $V_{(n)}=0$ for $n$ sufficiently negative, equipped with a vertex operator map $Y:V\otimes V\to V((x))$, a vacuum vector $\mathbf{1}$, and a grading operator, satisfying the identity, creation and weak associativity axioms (but not necessarily skew-symmetry/commutativity, in contrast to an ordinary vertex algebra). A grading-restricted generalized $V$-bimodule is a doubly-graded vector space carrying compatible left and right vertex operator actions of $V$, with the usual grading restrictions. For each positive integer $n$, let $H^n(V,W)$ denote the $n$-th cohomology of $V$ with coefficients in such a bimodule $W$, defined via the cochain complex of grading-preserving maps satisfying the standard composability and convergence conditions for meromorphic open-string vertex algebras.

Prove or disprove: every grading-restricted generalized left $V$-module of finite length is completely reducible if and only if, for every positive integer $n$ and every grading-restricted generalized $V$-bimodule $W$, one has $H^n(V,W)=0$.

In particular, when $V$ is a grading-restricted (ordinary) vertex algebra regarded as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, decide whether complete reducibility of every grading-restricted generalized $V$-module of finite length is equivalent to the vanishing $H^n(V,W)=0$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ and every bimodule $W$ (where the left and right actions of $V$ on $W$ may differ).

Assume that for every Calabi–Yau manifold $X$ (a compact Kähler manifold with vanishing first Chern class) one can construct an associated $N=2$ vertex operator superalgebra $V_X$, that is, a $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded vertex operator superalgebra carrying an action of the $N=2$ superconformal algebra of central charge $c = 3\dim_{\mathbb C} X$, whose chiral data encode the geometry of $X$ (for instance via a sigma-model or chiral de Rham–type construction). Carry out the following program for such $V_X$:

1. Develop the representation theory of $V_X$: classify a suitable category of (admissible, grading-restricted, generalized) modules over $V_X$ and describe their fusion rules.

2. For triples of modules, construct the spaces of intertwining operators and prove the convergence and associativity of products of intertwining operators (i.e., the operator product expansion for intertwining operators among $V_X$-modules).

3. Prove modular invariance of the graded characters and, more generally, of the genus-one (pseudo-)trace functions associated to $V_X$-modules, including the action of $SL(2,\mathbb Z)$ on the space of conformal blocks on the torus.

4. Using (1)–(3), endow the module category of $V_X$ with the structure of a modular tensor category in an appropriately formulated sense (allowing for the supersymmetric and possibly non-rational, non-finite features inherent in Calabi–Yau models).

5. From this modular tensor category, construct a full $N=2$ superconformal field theory associated to $X$: a consistent assignment of correlation functions on Riemann surfaces of all genera, with a modular-invariant torus partition function and crossing-symmetric sphere correlators, realizing the chiral algebra $V_X$.

Provide the constructions and proofs above, or determine the obstructions that prevent such a program from being carried out for general Calabi–Yau $X$.

A vertex algebra is a vector space $V$ equipped with a vacuum vector $\mathbf{1}\in V$, a linear operator $D\colon V\to V$, and a vertex operator map $Y(\cdot,x)\colon V\to (\operatorname{End}V)[[x,x^{-1}]]$, $v\mapsto Y(v,x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}v_n x^{-n-1}$, satisfying the standard axioms (vacuum, translation, and the Jacobi identity). The algebra $V$ is called grading-restricted if it carries a $\mathbb{Z}$-grading $V=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}V_{(n)}$ such that $\dim V_{(n)}<\infty$ for every $n$ and $V_{(n)}=0$ for all sufficiently negative $n$, and such that the grading is compatible with the vertex algebra structure (i.e., $\mathbf{1}\in V_{(0)}$, $D$ raises degree by $1$, and $u_m V_{(n)}\subseteq V_{(n+\deg u-m-1)}$ for homogeneous $u$). A (grading-restricted generalized) $V$-module is a $\mathbb{C}$-graded vector space $W=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{C}}W_{[n]}$ with finite-dimensional homogeneous components, gradings bounded below in real part, and a vertex operator map $Y_W\colon V\to(\operatorname{End}W)[[x,x^{-1}]]$ satisfying the module axioms.

Problem. Formulate a criterion, expressed entirely in terms of intrinsic data of a grading-restricted vertex algebra $V$ itself (not in terms of a chosen category of modules), which is necessary and sufficient to ensure that every grading-restricted generalized $V$-module is completely reducible, i.e., decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible $V$-modules.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Yi-Zhi Huang has obtained cohomological criteria for complete reducibility of modules for grading-restricted vertex algebras: if the first cohomology $\hat{H}^{1}_{\infty}(V,M)$ equals a certain subspace $\hat{Z}^{1}_{\infty}(V,M)$ for every $\mathbb{Z}$-graded $V$-bimodule $M$ generated by a grading-restricted subspace, then suitable modules are completely reducible. This provides a criterion stated in terms of $V$ itself, but a fully intrinsic, easily verifiable characterization remains an active research direction.

representations.normalized:
Two mathematically rigorous frameworks for chiral two-dimensional conformal field theory are:

(1) Vertex operator algebras (VOAs): a vector space V with a vacuum 1, a conformal vector ω, and a state–field correspondence Y(·, z) : V → End(V)[[z, z^{-1}]] satisfying the Jacobi identity and Virasoro relations; together with a category Rep(V) of admissible V-modules, which for a rational (regular) VOA carries the structure of a modular tensor category (Huang's theorem).

(2) Conformal nets: an assignment I ↦ A(I) of von Neumann algebras to proper open intervals I of the unit circle S^1, satisfying isotony, locality, Möbius (or diffeomorphism) covariance, positivity of energy, existence of a vacuum, and the split property; for a completely rational conformal net A, the category Rep(A) of Doplicher–Haag–Roberts representations is a modular tensor category (Kawahigashi–Longo–Müger).

Problem. Construct a direct, canonical correspondence between these two approaches. Concretely:

(a) Define a natural procedure that to a suitable unitary VOA V associates a conformal net A_V on the Hilbert space completion of V, and conversely a procedure that recovers a VOA from a conformal net satisfying appropriate smoothness conditions, in such a way that the two procedures are mutually inverse on a large class of models.

(b) Show that, when V is a rational (unitary) vertex operator algebra and A_V is the associated conformal net, the modular tensor categories Rep(V) and Rep(A_V) are equivalent as (unitary) modular tensor categories.

Prove that, at least for rational conformal field theories, the VOA-based and conformal-net-based formulations are equivalent in this sense.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Carpi–Kawahigashi–Longo–Weiner (Mem. AMS 254, 2018; arXiv:1503.01260) gave a general procedure assigning a conformal net A_V to every strongly local unitary VOA V, providing a direct connection between the two frameworks. The full equivalence of modular tensor categories Rep(V) ≅ Rep(A_V) for all rational VOAs remains a conjecture, but substantial progress has been made: recent work (e.g. Gui and others) establishes the equivalence for WZW models, even lattice VOAs, parafermion VOAs, ADE discrete-series W-algebras, their tensor products, and regular cosets. Hence the problem is partially solved.

representations.normalized:
A grading-restricted vertex algebra is a vector space $V=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} V_{(n)}$ together with a vacuum vector $\mathbf{1}\in V_{(0)}$, a conformal vector $\omega$, and a vertex operator map $Y:V\otimes V\to V((x))$, $u\otimes v\mapsto Y(u,x)v=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} u_n v\, x^{-n-1}$, satisfying the standard axioms (vacuum, creation, $L(0)$-grading with $\dim V_{(n)}<\infty$ and $V_{(n)}=0$ for $n$ sufficiently negative, the Jacobi identity, and the Virasoro relations for the modes of $\omega$).

A formal deformation of $V$ over $\mathbb{C}[[t]]$ is a $\mathbb{C}[[t]]$-linear vertex-algebra structure on $V[[t]]$ whose reduction modulo $t$ recovers $V$; equivalently, it is a formal power series $Y_t(u,x)v=Y(u,x)v+\sum_{k\ge 1} t^k\, \Phi_k(u,x)v$ of vertex operator-valued maps satisfying the Jacobi identity order by order in $t$. An analytic deformation is a family $\{V_t\}$ of grading-restricted vertex algebras depending holomorphically on a complex parameter $t$ in a neighborhood of $0$, with $V_0=V$.

A genus-zero full conformal field theory (in the sense compatible with the sewing operation on the moduli space of genus-zero Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary components) is a state space $H$ equipped with correlation function maps that are real-analytic in the moduli, satisfy the appropriate sewing axioms, and combine a chiral and an antichiral structure compatible with modular invariance at genus zero.

Solve the following two problems:

(a) Determine sufficient conditions on a grading-restricted vertex algebra $V$ and on a formal deformation $Y_t$ of $V$ guaranteeing that the formal series $Y_t(u,x)v$ converges (in an appropriate topology) for $t$ in some nonempty open neighborhood of $0\in\mathbb{C}$, so that $Y_t$ defines an analytic deformation of $V$.

(b) Generalize the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras (formal and analytic) to a deformation theory of genus-zero full conformal field theories: formulate the cochain complex controlling deformations, identify the cohomology classes parametrizing infinitesimal and obstructed deformations, and establish convergence criteria for passing from formal to analytic deformations in this setting.

Recent work (2022–2025) by Huang and collaborators continues to develop the cohomology theory of grading-restricted vertex (super)algebras, including convergence questions and classification of formal deformations for certain classes of strongly generated vertex superalgebras. However, no general result giving sufficient conditions for formal deformations to converge to analytic ones, nor a full deformation theory of genus-zero full conformal field theories, appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open.

representations.normalized:
Setup. Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra (or more generally, a chiral algebra of a two-dimensional conformal field theory) which is not necessarily rational, so that its category $\mathcal{C}=\mathrm{Rep}(V)$ of suitable (e.g., grading-restricted generalized) modules carries the structure of a braided tensor category that need not be semisimple. Assume $\mathcal{C}$ is a finite, rigid, ribbon braided tensor category whose braiding is non-degenerate in an appropriate sense, but in which not every object is a direct sum of simples.

Problem.
(a) Formulate a definition of "modular tensor category" valid in the nonsemisimple setting, i.e., a notion of finite ribbon braided tensor category equipped with the additional structure/non-degeneracy condition needed to play the role traditionally played (in the semisimple case) by a modular tensor category in the sense of Reshetikhin–Turaev.
(b) Prove that the braided tensor category $\mathcal{C}=\mathrm{Rep}(V)$ described above carries the structure of a nonsemisimple modular tensor category in the sense of (a).
(c) Determine whether, given such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category, one can construct a three-dimensional topological quantum field theory and, in particular, invariants of (framed/oriented) knots, links, and closed 3-manifolds extending the Reshetikhin–Turaev construction.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Substantial progress has been made. Definitions of nonsemisimple modular tensor categories (finite, factorizable ribbon categories, following Lyubashenko, Kerler–Lyubashenko, Shimizu) are now standard, and 3-dimensional TQFTs as well as knot/3-manifold invariants have been constructed from them by De Renzi–Gainutdinov–Geer–Patureau-Mirand–Runkel (Selecta Math., 2022) and subsequent work, including extensions to quasi-Hopf settings and cochain-valued TQFTs (2025). Establishing the nonsemisimple modular tensor category structure on representation categories of specific (logarithmic) vertex operator algebras remains only partially proven; verification has been achieved in particular families (e.g., singlet/triplet $W$-algebras) but not in full generality.

The conjecture remains open in full generality, but partial results exist. It has been proved in the trivial-group case (the well-known untwisted theory) and when V is holomorphic with G a finite cyclic group. Subsequent work by Huang and collaborators (e.g., on twisted intertwining operators among twisted modules for not-necessarily-commuting automorphisms, and the 2024 paper on modular invariance of (logarithmic) intertwining operators, plus the 2025 work on tensor products of generalized twisted modules) has established components of the program (skew-symmetry, contragredient isomorphisms, P(z)-tensor product structure, modular invariance in special cases), but a complete proof of associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance for twisted intertwining operators for arbitrary finite G is not yet available.

Let $V = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} V_n$ be a vertex operator algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ (in the standard sense of Frenkel–Lepowsky–Meurman, with vacuum vector, conformal vector, and Virasoro action giving the grading by $L(0)$-eigenvalues) satisfying all three of the following conditions:

(1) The central charge of $V$ is $24$.

(2) The weight-one subspace is trivial, i.e. $V_1 = 0$.

(3) Every irreducible $V$-module is isomorphic to $V$ itself as a $V$-module, and every $V$-module is completely reducible (so $V$ is holomorphic/self-dual and rational in this sense).

Question: Must $V$ be isomorphic, as a vertex operator algebra, to the moonshine module vertex operator algebra $V^\natural$ of Frenkel–Lepowsky–Meurman?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The Frenkel–Lepowsky–Meurman uniqueness conjecture for the moonshine module under these hypotheses (central charge 24, $V_1=0$, holomorphic/self-dual rationality) is widely regarded as still open. Partial/weak versions have been established (e.g., Dong–Griess and subsequent work characterizing $V^\natural$ under additional assumptions), but the full conjecture remains unresolved.

Background and definitions.

(a) A Calabi-Yau manifold is a compact complex Kähler manifold $(X,J,g)$ of complex dimension $n$ with vanishing first Chern class admitting a Ricci-flat Kähler metric and a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic $n$-form. Morphisms in the category $\mathbf{CY}$ may be taken to be holomorphic maps preserving the chosen Calabi-Yau structure (or, more flexibly, an appropriate notion of equivalence including mirror partners and deformations of complex/Kähler structure).

(b) An N=2 vertex operator superalgebra is a $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded vertex operator superalgebra $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ equipped with four distinguished vectors generating the N=2 superconformal Lie algebra: a Virasoro element $L$ of central charge $c$, a Heisenberg current $J$, and two odd currents $G^\pm$ satisfying the standard N=2 superconformal operator product expansions. Morphisms are vertex superalgebra homomorphisms preserving the N=2 structure. Deformations of an N=2 superconformal field theory are governed by exactly marginal operators in the chiral and twisted-chiral rings.

(c) The Fermat quintic threefold is the Calabi-Yau threefold
$$Q=\{[z_0:z_1:z_2:z_3:z_4]\in\mathbb{P}^4 : z_0^5+z_1^5+z_2^5+z_3^5+z_4^5=0\}.$$

(d) The Gepner model associated to $Q$ is the N=2 superconformal field theory obtained as a specific GSO-projected tensor product of five copies of the N=2 minimal model at level $k=3$ (each of central charge $9/5$), yielding an N=2 vertex operator superalgebra of total central charge $c=9$.

Problem. Construct a functor
$$\mathcal{F}:\mathbf{CY}\longrightarrow \mathbf{VOSA}_{N=2}$$
from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N=2 vertex operator superalgebras with the following two properties:

(1) $\mathcal{F}(Q)$ is isomorphic, as an N=2 vertex operator superalgebra, to the Gepner model associated to the Fermat quintic threefold.

(2) The functor sends deformations of Calabi-Yau structures (variations of complex structure and complexified Kähler class) to deformations of the corresponding N=2 superconformal field theories by exactly marginal operators, in a manner compatible with the moduli spaces on both sides.

Working under the following hypotheses:

(H1) For every Calabi-Yau manifold X (a compact complex Kähler manifold with trivial canonical bundle), there exists an associated N=2 vertex operator superalgebra V_X — that is, a Z/2-graded vertex operator superalgebra equipped with an N=2 superconformal structure (a Virasoro vector together with two odd primary fields G^+, G^- of conformal weight 3/2 and an even primary U(1)-current J of weight 1, satisfying the N=2 superconformal OPEs) of central charge c = 3 dim_C X, naturally attached to X.

(H2) The basic representation theory of V_X has been developed: classification of irreducible modules, complete reducibility statements (rationality/C_2-cofiniteness when applicable), fusion rules, characters and modular transformation properties, intertwining operator algebra structure, and chiral/antichiral spectral flow.

(H3) From V_X (together with its anti-chiral counterpart) one can construct the full N=2 superconformal field theory associated with X as a mathematically rigorous full conformal field theory (e.g., a modular-invariant combination of left and right movers giving genus-g correlation functions satisfying sewing axioms).

Tasks. Using only the structures in (H1)–(H3) as input, give rigorous mathematical formulations and proofs of the following physicists' conjectures on Calabi-Yau manifolds:

(a) Quantum cohomology. Construct, from V_X and its modules, the small (and where appropriate big) quantum cohomology ring of X as a deformation of the classical cohomology ring H^*(X,C), and prove that this construction agrees with the Gromov-Witten quantum cohomology of X.

(b) Mirror symmetry. Define a mirror involution on the class of N=2 superconformal field theories arising from (H3) (for instance, by an automorphism reversing the sign of the U(1)-current J, exchanging chiral and antichiral rings), and prove that for a Calabi-Yau manifold X there exists a Calabi-Yau manifold X^∨ such that the full N=2 SCFT of X^∨ is isomorphic (as a full CFT) to the mirror of the full N=2 SCFT of X. Deduce the standard consequences: the exchange of Hodge numbers h^{p,q}(X) = h^{n-p,q}(X^∨), the identification of the A-model on X with the B-model on X^∨, and the equality of Gromov-Witten invariants of X with the appropriate period/variation-of-Hodge-structure invariants of X^∨.

Provide the full chain of definitions, theorems, and proofs realising this program.

Hilbert proved that every nonnegative homogeneous polynomial in three variables of degree four with real coefficients can be written as a sum of squares of real polynomials. Consider the ternary quartic
\[
P(x,y,z) \;=\; x^{2}(x-y)(x-z) + y^{2}(y-x)(y-z) + z^{2}(z-x)(z-y),
\]
which is nonnegative for all real $x,y,z$ (this is Schur's inequality with exponent $2$). Find an explicit representation of $P(x,y,z)$ as a sum of squares of real polynomials in $x,y,z$.

A multiple hypergeometric sum is a finite or infinite sum of the form
\[ S(n) \;=\; \sum_{k_1,\,k_2,\,\dots,\,k_r} F(n,k_1,k_2,\dots,k_r), \]
where the summand $F$ is a proper hypergeometric term, meaning that the ratios $F(\dots,k_i+1,\dots)/F(\dots,k_i,\dots)$ and $F(n+1,\dots)/F(n,\dots)$ are rational functions of all variables, and where the summand may also involve products and quotients of Pochhammer symbols, factorials, and binomial coefficients, including those that arise naturally from iterated integral representations such as connection-coefficient computations between families of orthogonal polynomials.

Develop a systematic algorithmic procedure that takes as input such a multi-index hypergeometric sum $S(n)$ and produces, when one exists, an equivalent expression of strictly lower nesting depth: ideally a single sum, or, when possible, a closed form expressible in terms of standard hypergeometric functions ${}_pF_q$, gamma functions, or similar recognized special functions. The procedure should:

(i) decide, in a constructive sense, whether such a reduction to lower-order summation exists;
(ii) when reduction exists, output an explicit lower-order representation;
(iii) combine algorithmic tools available for this setting, including holonomic-systems methods (creative telescoping, $\partial$-finite closure properties, Zeilberger-type algorithms in several variables) and difference-field methods (Karr's algorithm and its $\Pi\Sigma^*$-extensions), with whatever additional structural input (such as integral representations, contiguous relations, or symmetry of the summand) is required to identify the correct reduced form.

In particular, characterize a class of multiple hypergeometric sums for which a reduction to a single sum is guaranteed to be effectively computable, and provide an algorithm whose output on this class is a single-sum or closed-form representation of $S(n)$.

Let $u$ be a Leray–Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
\[
\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \Delta u + \nabla p = 0,\qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,
\]
on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times (0,T)$, and let its vorticity be $\omega = \nabla\times u$. For points $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and $t\in(0,T)$, let $\theta(x,y,t)$ denote the angle between the vectors $\omega(x,t)$ and $\omega(y,t)$. Assume that the direction of vorticity is $\beta$-Hölder continuous in space in the sense that there exist constants $c>0$ and $\beta\in(0,1/2)$ such that
\[
\sin\theta(x,y,t) \le c\,|x-y|^{\beta} \qquad \text{for all } (x,y,t)\in\mathbb{R}^3\times\mathbb{R}^3\times(0,T).
\]
For exponents $s,q\in[1,\infty]$, set $\lambda(s,q) = \tfrac{2}{s} + \tfrac{3}{q}$.

Question: Under the above hypothesis with some $\beta<1/2$, must there exist exponents $s$ and $q$ such that
\[
u \in L^s\bigl(0,T;\,L^q(\mathbb{R}^3)\bigr) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \lambda(s,q) = \tfrac{2}{s} + \tfrac{3}{q} < \tfrac{3}{2}\,?
\]

Let $M = G/K$ be a homogeneous space, where $G$ is a compact connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup of $G$. A Riemannian metric on $M$ is called $G$-invariant if $G$ acts by isometries, and is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor is a constant scalar multiple of the metric. Two $G$-invariant Einstein metrics are identified if they differ by an isometry and by a positive scaling factor.

Prove or disprove the following finiteness statement (Ziller's finiteness conjecture): the number of $G$-invariant Einstein metrics on $M = G/K$ (up to isometry and homothety) is finite whenever at least one of the following holds:

(a) $\operatorname{rank} G = \operatorname{rank} K$, or

(b) the isotropy representation of $K$ on $T_{eK}(G/K)$ decomposes into pairwise non-equivalent irreducible summands.

Let $G/K$ be a compact homogeneous space, where $G$ is a compact connected Lie group and $K\subset G$ is a closed subgroup, with reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ (so that $\mathrm{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}$). A Riemannian metric on $G/K$ is called $G$-invariant if it is induced by an $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant inner product on $\mathfrak{m}$. An invariant Einstein metric is a $G$-invariant Riemannian metric whose Ricci tensor is a constant multiple of the metric. Suppose that the isotropy representation $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{m}_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{m}_s$ of $K$ decomposes into irreducible $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-submodules among which at least two are equivalent as $K$-representations.

A distinguished family of such spaces are the real Stiefel manifolds $V_k(\mathbb{R}^n)=\mathrm{SO}(n)/\mathrm{SO}(n-k)$ of orthonormal $k$-frames in $\mathbb{R}^n$, whose isotropy representation contains equivalent summands whenever $k\ge 2$.

Determine, modulo homothety, whether the set of $G$-invariant Einstein metrics on such a homogeneous space $G/K$ (and in particular on $V_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$) is necessarily finite, or whether continuous one-parameter families of non-isometric $G$-invariant Einstein metrics can occur.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent work (e.g., Arvanitoyeorgos–Sakane–Statha and others, 2014–2021) has produced new families of invariant Einstein metrics on Stiefel manifolds $V_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and on related spaces with equivalent isotropy summands, typically by restricting to a smaller invariance group to make the Einstein system tractable. However, no general classification or finiteness theorem is known in the presence of equivalent isotropy summands, and the question of whether continuous one-parameter families of invariant Einstein metrics can occur on such spaces remains open.

Let $\{P_n(x)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials defined by the three-term recurrence
$$P_n(x) = (x-c_n)P_{n-1}(x) - \lambda_n P_{n-2}(x), \qquad n\ge 1,$$
with initial conditions $P_{-1}(x)=0$, $P_0(x)=1$, where the recurrence coefficients satisfy $c_n\in\mathbb{R}$, $\lambda_n>0$ for all $n$, and the "one-quarter class" conditions
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} c_n = \infty, \qquad \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\lambda_{n+1}}{c_n c_{n+1}} = \frac{1}{4}.$$
For each $n$, denote the zeros of $P_n$ by $x_{n,1}<x_{n,2}<\cdots<x_{n,n}$, and define
$$\xi_i = \lim_{n\to\infty} x_{n,i}, \qquad \eta_j = \lim_{n\to\infty} x_{n,n-j+1},$$
$$\sigma = \lim_{i\to\infty} \xi_i, \qquad \tau = \lim_{j\to\infty} \eta_j,$$
assuming these limits exist in $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$. Blumenthal's classical theorem asserts that, in the bounded case, the zeros of $\{P_n\}$ are dense in the interval $[\sigma,\tau]$, which equals the support of the orthogonality measure (up to a denumerable set). In the one-quarter class one always has $\tau=\infty$. In the case $\sigma=-\infty$ (so both endpoints are unbounded), formulate and establish an analogue of Blumenthal's theorem describing the limiting distribution of the zeros of $\{P_n\}$ in this doubly unbounded situation.

Recent work (notably by G. Świderski and collaborators) has established Blumenthal/Nevai-type results for the one-quarter class when σ is finite, showing that under a mild monotonicity condition the zeros are dense in [σ,∞) and this set is the essential spectrum. Define a sequence of polynomials $A_n(t) \in \mathbb{Q}[t^3]$ by the three-term recurrence
$$\bigl(n^3 - (-1)^n t^3\bigr) A_n(t) + (n+1)^2 (2n+1)\, A_{n+1}(t) + (n+2)^2 (n+1)\, A_{n+2}(t) = 0, \qquad n \ge 0,$$
together with the initial conditions $A_0(t) = 1$ and $A_1(t) = 0$. (Then $A_n(t)$ is a polynomial of degree $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ in $x = t^3$.) Define the partial-sum polynomials
$$\widetilde{A}_n(t) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} A_k(t).$$
Find an explicit closed-form representation of both $A_n(t)$ and $\widetilde{A}_n(t)$ as (finite) hypergeometric series, or prove that no such representation exists.

Let G=(V,E) be a planar graph. Each vertex v∈V is assigned a demand d(v) and a capacity c(v). In the unweighted, splittable-demand, hard-capacity Capacitated Domination Problem, a feasible solution consists of (i) a multiset D⊆V where each vertex is selected at most once (hard capacity), together with (ii) a fractional assignment f:V×V→ℝ_{≥0} such that f(u,v)>0 only if u=v or uv∈E and u∈D, ∑_{u} f(u,v) ≥ d(v) for every v∈V (all demand of v is covered, possibly split among multiple dominators), and ∑_{v} f(u,v) ≤ c(u) for every u∈D (capacity of each chosen dominator is not exceeded). The objective is to minimize |D|.

It is known that when demands and capacities are positive integers bounded by a fixed constant, this problem admits a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) on planar graphs. The question is:

Does the PTAS extend to either of the following more general settings on planar graphs, while preserving the same approximation guarantee?
(a) demands d(v) and capacities c(v) allowed to be arbitrary positive integers (not bounded by a constant);
(b) demands d(v) and capacities c(v) allowed to be bounded positive real numbers (rather than integers).

Determine whether such a PTAS exists in each of these settings.

Let G=(V,E) be a planar graph. Each vertex v∈V is given a non-negative real weight w(v) and a positive integer hard capacity c(v). A capacitated dominating set is a pair (D,f), where D⊆V and f: V∖D → D is an assignment mapping every non-selected vertex to a neighbor in D such that, for every u∈D, the number of vertices assigned to u satisfies |f^{-1}(u)| ≤ c(u). The cost of the solution is Σ_{v∈D} w(v).

A standard "smoothing" technique handles the unweighted case (w≡1) by performing local exchanges that trade capacity for weight in unit quantities; however, this approach does not obviously bound the weight contributed by an underfull selected vertex during reassignment when weights are arbitrary.

Question: Does the Capacitated Domination problem with hard capacities on planar graphs admit a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS), or otherwise an approximation algorithm matching the unweighted-case guarantees, in the fully weighted setting with arbitrary non-negative vertex weights w: V → ℝ_{≥0}?

Let G=(V,E) be a simple planar graph. For each vertex v ∈ V, let d(v) ∈ ℤ_{≥0} be a demand and c(v) ∈ ℤ_{≥0} be a (hard) capacity, and let w(v) ∈ ℝ_{≥0} be a cost. A capacitated dominating assignment is a pair (S, x) where S ⊆ V and x : V × V → ℤ_{≥0} is an assignment of demand units such that:
 (i) for every v ∈ V, ∑_{u ∈ N[v]} x(u,v) ≥ d(v) (every vertex's demand is covered by demand units routed from vertices in its closed neighborhood);
 (ii) for every u ∈ V, ∑_{v ∈ N[u]} x(u,v) ≤ c(u)·[u ∈ S] (hard-capacity constraint: only chosen vertices in S provide demand units, and never more than their capacity).
The cost of the assignment is ∑_{u ∈ S} w(u). The Capacitated Dominating Set problem with hard capacities asks for an assignment of minimum cost.

A bicriteria (α, β)-approximation with capacity violation is a polynomial-time algorithm that returns a feasible assignment when each capacity c(u) is replaced by β·c(u), having cost at most α·OPT, where OPT denotes the optimum of the original (non-violated) problem. Analogously, a bicriteria (α, γ)-approximation with demand under-coverage produces, in polynomial time, an assignment that satisfies ∑_{u ∈ N[v]} x(u,v) ≥ γ·d(v) for every v ∈ V (with 0 < γ ≤ 1) and has cost at most α·OPT.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial-time bicriteria approximation algorithm for Capacitated Dominating Set on planar graphs with hard capacities, achieving constant α together with either constant β > 1 (capacities may be exceeded by a bounded multiplicative factor) or constant γ < 1 close to 1 (demands may be under-covered by a bounded amount)?

Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple undirected graph. A capacity function is a map c:V→ℤ_{≥0}, and a demand function is a map d:V→ℤ_{≥0}. For an integer r≥1, the capacitated r-hop domination problem asks for a minimum-cardinality set S⊆V together with an assignment f:V→S such that:
(i) for every v∈V, the graph distance dist_G(v,f(v))≤r, and
(ii) for every s∈S, ∑_{v: f(v)=s} d(v) ≤ c(s).
The case r=1 is the standard capacitated dominating set problem (CDP).

For graphs of bounded branchwidth ω, CDP admits a dynamic-programming algorithm whose tables, at each edge of the branch decomposition, store "boundary configurations" that record, for each boundary vertex, whether it is in S and how much of its capacity has been consumed by vertices already assigned to it from within the processed cluster. The number of such configurations is bounded by a function of ω, yielding an exact algorithm for CDP on bounded-branchwidth graphs.

Problem. Determine whether this branchwidth dynamic program can be extended to capacitated r-hop domination for r≥2 with a comparable bound on the number of boundary configurations. Specifically: design a dynamic-programming algorithm over a branch decomposition of width ω that solves capacitated r-hop domination, and bound the number of distinct boundary configurations needed at each separator. The principal obstruction to overcome is that the demand of a non-boundary vertex inside a cluster may be served by a chosen vertex lying outside the cluster (at distance ≤ r through the boundary), so the dynamic program must encode the ways in which demand and coverage cross the cluster boundary without producing super-polynomial (in the branchwidth) configuration counts.

Specifically: design a dynamic-programming algorithm over a branch decomposition of width ω that solves capacitated r-hop domination, and bound the number of distinct boundary configurations needed at each separator. The principal obstruction to overcome is that the demand of a non-boundary vertex inside a cluster may be served by a chosen vertex lying outside the cluster (at distance ≤ r through the boundary), so the dynamic program must encode the ways in which demand and coverage cross the cluster boundary without producing super-polynomial (in the branchwidth) configuration counts.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has shown that capacitated r-domination on graphs of branchwidth ω can be solved exactly in n^{O(rω)} time, and that on planar graphs the problem admits subexponential FPT and PTAS-style results. Thus the extension of the bounded-branchwidth dynamic program to r-hop is known, but with a configuration count that grows with n (not purely a function of ω as in CDP), so a fully ω-bounded analogue has not been established.

Setup. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph and let $c:V\to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ be a capacity function. In the hard-capacitated Dominating Set problem one seeks a set $D\subseteq V$ (no repetitions of vertices are allowed, i.e. multiplicities are forbidden) together with an assignment $f:V\setminus D \to D$ such that:
(i) for every $u\in V\setminus D$, the image $f(u)$ is a neighbor of $u$ in $G$ (i.e. $f(u)v\in E$ where $v=u$ is dominated by $f(u)$), and
(ii) for every $v\in D$, $|f^{-1}(v)|\le c(v)$ (the hard-capacity constraint).
The objective is to minimize $|D|$.

It is known that on planar graphs the hard-capacitated Dominating Set problem admits structural / algorithmic techniques (constant-factor approximations and fixed-parameter tractable algorithms parameterized by solution size) that exploit planarity together with the no-multiplicity restriction.

Problem. Develop a general framework that extends these planar techniques for hard-capacitated Dominating Set to a broader class of hard-capacitated optimization problems on planar graphs in which multiplicities of the selected objects are forbidden (so that excess demand cannot be absorbed by duplicating chosen vertices/sets). Concretely, identify abstract structural conditions on a covering/domination-type problem $\Pi$ defined on planar graphs (with hard capacities and the no-multiplicity restriction) under which $\Pi$ admits:
(a) a constant-factor polynomial-time approximation algorithm, and
(b) a fixed-parameter tractable algorithm parameterized by the size of the solution.
As benchmark instances, the framework should encompass hard-capacitated Vertex Cover, hard-capacitated Set Cover (on planar incidence graphs), and related hard-capacitated covering problems on planar graphs, all without allowing multiplicities.

Consider the tree-level low-energy effective action of a closed string theory in (d+1)-dimensional spacetime, containing the spacetime metric g_{μν}, the dilaton φ, and a Ramond–Ramond p-form gauge potential A_p with field strength F_{p+1} = dA_p, with action (in the string frame)

  S = ∫ d^{d+1}x √(−g) [ e^{−2φ}(R + 4(∂φ)^2) − (1/2·(p+1)!) F_{p+1}^2 ].

Restrict to spatially homogeneous, anisotropic Bianchi-type cosmological ansätze of the form
  ds^2 = −dt^2 + Σ_{i=1}^{d} a_i(t)^2 (dx^i)^2,  φ = φ(t),
with a compatible homogeneous Ramond–Ramond field-strength configuration, and study the resulting autonomous system of ordinary differential equations for the logarithmic scale factors β_i = ln a_i, the dilaton φ, and the RR field-strength components.

(a) Determine the complete set of asymptotic regimes (as t approaches the cosmological singularity and as t → ∞) for the trajectories of this dynamical system. In particular, classify all asymptotic states and the corresponding Kasner-like exponents (p_1, …, p_d) that can be approached.

(b) For each known exact cosmological solution of the above system with non-trivial RR flux, determine whether the solution is asymptotically stable (i.e. an attractor on an open set of initial data) and whether it is asymptotically unique within its class.

(c) Identify and classify all asymptotic solutions that are subdominant — solutions that exist as exact trajectories of the system but whose contributions are exponentially or polynomially suppressed relative to the dominant asymptotic state — and determine the constraints these subdominant solutions impose on the spectrum of admissible singular asymptotic states.

Consider the cosmological dynamical systems arising from heterotic M-theory and from Hořava–Witten theory compactified on an interval, in the presence of nontrivial Ramond (form) field strengths. After dimensional reduction to a homogeneous (e.g. Bianchi-type or spatially flat FRW) cosmological ansatz with metric moduli (scale factors of the external space, the Calabi–Yau volume modulus, and the orbifold-interval modulus) coupled to dilaton/axion fields and to the Ramond form-field fluxes, one obtains an autonomous system of ordinary differential equations governing the time evolution of these moduli. Within this system there exist explicit exact cosmological solutions (the "basic regimes") parametrized by the flux data.

Tasks:
1. Determine the precise asymptotic role of these exact solutions as t → 0⁺ (initial singularity) and as t → ∞ (late-time regime): identify which trajectories of the full nonlinear system are attracted to, or repelled from, each exact solution, and characterize the leading-order asymptotic expansions of generic nearby trajectories.
2. Compute the dimension of the asymptotic attractor formed by these exact solutions inside the phase space of the reduced cosmological system, i.e. the dimension of the stable (or unstable) manifold consisting of all perturbations of the basic regimes that converge to the family of exact solutions in the chosen asymptotic limit.

Provide the dimension as a function of the discrete data of the model (number of moduli, rank of the flux configuration, and dimension of the orbit of exact solutions).

Consider the low-energy effective field equations of string and M-theory compactified to four spacetime dimensions, with bosonic content consisting of the spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$, the dilaton $\phi$, and form-field strengths (e.g. an axion or NS–NS three-form $H$). Within this setting, suppose one has identified a class of spatially homogeneous (e.g. Bianchi-type) cosmological solutions that are asymptotically stable, in the sense that small homogeneous perturbations of initial data on a Cauchy surface decay (or remain bounded) toward the cosmological singularity or toward future infinity.

Address the following:

1. Extend the stability analysis of these homogeneous solutions to fully inhomogeneous perturbations of the metric, dilaton, and form fields. Determine the asymptotic form of a generic inhomogeneous perturbation, including its dependence on spatial coordinates, in the chosen asymptotic regime (singularity or infinity).

2. Characterize, for the real-analytic category, the universal features that any generic analytic cosmological solution to the same field equations must share with these stable homogeneous solutions. Concretely, identify the leading asymptotic behaviour (e.g. Kasner-like exponents, scaling of the dilaton, decay or growth of form fields), the number of free functions of the spatial coordinates parametrizing the generic solution, and any constraints these free functions must satisfy.

3. Determine whether the generic analytic solution is BKL-like (governed pointwise by a homogeneous model) or, on the contrary, exhibits genuinely inhomogeneous asymptotic structure not captured by any homogeneous truncation.

Consider the tree-level string effective action in $D=4$ spacetime dimensions, written in the string frame as
$$S = -\tfrac{1}{2\lambda_s^{D-2}}\int d^D x\,\sqrt{-g}\,e^{-\phi}\bigl(R + (\nabla\phi)^2 + V(\phi)\bigr) + S_{\text{matter}},$$
where $\phi$ is the dilaton, $V(\phi)$ is a (possibly vanishing) dilaton potential, and $S_{\text{matter}}$ describes a perfect fluid coupled to the dilaton with energy density $\rho$, pressure $p=\gamma\rho$, and equation-of-state parameter $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$ left arbitrary. Allow generic higher-curvature/$\alpha'$ quantum corrections of the form
$$\Delta S = \tfrac{1}{2\lambda_s^{D-2}}\int d^Dx\,\sqrt{-g}\,e^{-\phi}\bigl[\alpha'\,c_1 R_{GB}^2 + \alpha'\,c_2(\nabla\phi)^4 + \cdots\bigr],$$
involving the Gauss–Bonnet term and dilaton kinetic corrections, with coefficients $c_i$ allowed in the standard string-theoretic range.

Restrict to spatially flat, homogeneous, isotropic cosmologies with metric $ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2\,d\mathbf{x}^2$, dilaton $\phi=\phi(t)$, and fluid variables depending only on $t$, satisfying the resulting nonlinear field equations together with the fluid conservation law $\dot\rho + DH(1+\gamma)\rho - \tfrac{1}{2}\dot\phi(1-D\gamma)\rho = 0$ (or the analogous covariant equation when the dilaton couples to matter).

Determine, as a function of the fluid parameter $\gamma$, all asymptotic solutions $(a(t),\phi(t),\rho(t))$ as $t\to\pm\infty$ that are stable (in the sense of late- or early-time attractors of the dynamical system obtained from the equations of motion). Equivalently, classify the stable fixed points and asymptotic regimes of the corresponding cosmological dynamical system over the full range of $\gamma$, in the presence of the quantum/$\alpha'$ corrections.

Consider a spatially curved Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker (FLRW) cosmology with metric

  ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 [ dr^2/(1 - k r^2) + r^2 (dθ^2 + sin^2θ dφ^2) ],   k ∈ {-1, 0, +1},

coupled to a dilaton field φ(t) and to a system of N interacting perfect fluids with energy densities ρ_i(t) and pressures p_i(t) = (γ_i - 1) ρ_i(t), i = 1, …, N, satisfying coupled conservation laws

  ρ̇_i + 3 H γ_i ρ_i = Q_i(ρ_1, …, ρ_N),     ∑_{i=1}^N Q_i = 0,

where H = ȧ/a is the Hubble rate and the interaction terms Q_i are smooth functions of the densities.

Take the low-energy effective string-frame action with leading α'-correction,

  S = ∫ d^4x √(-g) e^{-φ} [ R + (∇φ)^2 - V(φ) - α' c_1 R_GB^2 + … ] + S_matter,

where R_GB^2 = R^2 - 4 R_{μν} R^{μν} + R_{μνρσ} R^{μνρσ} is the Gauss–Bonnet term, c_1 is a constant, and α' > 0 is the string tension parameter. The resulting field equations form an autonomous dynamical system in the variables (H, φ̇, ρ_1, …, ρ_N) on which the spatial curvature term k/a^2 and the α'-correction enter as additional contributions.

Problem. Classify the asymptotic behavior, as t → +∞ and as t approaches any finite-time singularity, of all solutions of this system in terms of which contribution among
 (a) the spatial curvature term k/a^2,
 (b) the leading α' (Gauss–Bonnet) curvature correction, and
 (c) the interacting-fluid sector
is dominant and which is subdominant. In particular, determine, for every choice of k ∈ {-1, 0, +1}, of the barotropic indices γ_i, and of the interaction structure {Q_i}, the possible scaling exponents and stability properties of the asymptotic regimes that arise when the dominant contribution is the curvature term, the α'-correction, or the fluid sector, and identify the corrections induced by the subdominant terms.

Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity (the low-energy limit of M-theory) with bosonic field content consisting of a Lorentzian metric g on an 11-manifold and a 3-form gauge potential A with 4-form field strength F = dA, governed by the action

  S = (1/2κ²) ∫ d¹¹x √(−g) [ R − (1/2)|F|² ] − (1/12κ²) ∫ A ∧ F ∧ F,

augmented by the leading higher-curvature/quantum correction terms (schematically, an R⁴-type eight-derivative contribution together with its supersymmetric completion). On a spatially homogeneous Bianchi-type or product-of-flat-factors ansatz, the uncorrected theory admits "power-law" cosmological solutions in which each spatial scale factor evolves as a power of cosmic time t, supported by a suitable flux configuration; turning on the higher-derivative corrections produces a one-parameter family of "deformed power-law" cosmological solutions of the corrected equations of motion.

Question: Are these deformed power-law cosmological solutions of corrected eleven-dimensional supergravity asymptotically stable as t → ∞ under small homogeneous (and, more generally, inhomogeneous) perturbations of the metric and 4-form flux? In particular, does the basin of attraction include an open neighborhood of generic initial data, so that a phase of accelerated expansion (inflation) arising from such a solution is dynamically natural in M-theory cosmology?

Consider a five-dimensional bulk spacetime containing a codimension-one Robertson–Walker brane, with a perfect fluid energy–momentum tensor specified either in the bulk or induced on the brane. The bulk metric is taken to be regular (no curvature singularities or pathologies in the bulk geometry, away from the brane), and the induced geometry on the brane is a spatially homogeneous and isotropic Robertson–Walker spacetime. Two further requirements are imposed:

(i) Localization of gravity on the brane, i.e., the existence of a normalizable zero-mode of the linearized graviton fluctuations bound to the brane, reproducing four-dimensional Newtonian gravity at large distances on the brane.

(ii) The null energy condition in the bulk: T_{AB} k^A k^B \ge 0 for every null vector k^A, where T_{AB} is the bulk stress–energy tensor.

It is known that for a single perfect fluid in the bulk these three demands (regular bulk, gravity localization, and bulk null energy condition) cannot be simultaneously satisfied. The question is: does there exist a Robertson–Walker brane configuration sourced by a perfect fluid (in the bulk or on the brane) that admits a regular bulk solution while simultaneously localizing gravity on the brane and satisfying the null energy condition throughout the bulk?

Consider spatially homogeneous cosmological models in d+1 spacetime dimensions governed by the tree-level NS-NS gravi-dilaton effective string action

  S = (1/(2 λ_s^{d-1})) ∫ d^{d+1}x √(-g) e^{-φ} ( R + (∇φ)^2 - (1/12) H_{μνρ} H^{μνρ} ),

where g_{μν} is the spacetime metric with scalar curvature R, φ is the dilaton, and H = dB is the field strength of the Kalb–Ramond two-form B (truncating any massless gauge or matter fields and ignoring higher-derivative α' corrections and string-loop corrections). Restrict to homogeneous universes whose metric, dilaton and B-field depend only on cosmic time t, with spatial slices that are flat (or Bianchi-type homogeneous), so that the field equations reduce to a system of autonomous ODEs in t for the scale factors, the dilaton, and—via Hodge duality in d=3—an axion field σ defined by H^{μνρ} = e^{2φ} ε^{μνρλ} ∂_λ σ.

Two well-known exact solution families of this system are:

(i) the dilaton–moduli–vacuum solutions, in which H ≡ 0 (equivalently σ = const), each spatial scale factor evolves as a power of |t| with exponents satisfying a Kasner-like constraint, and the dilaton is logarithmic in |t|;

(ii) the axion solutions, in which σ is non-trivial and the system admits a one-parameter family of solutions interpolating between two asymptotic dilaton–moduli–vacuum branches.

Tasks:

(a) Provide a complete classification of the asymptotic limits (as t → 0^± and as t → ±∞, including pre– and post–big-bang regimes) of every solution of this homogeneous tree-level NS-NS system.

(b) Determine whether the dilaton–moduli–vacuum solutions and the axion solutions are asymptotically stable within this dynamical system, i.e. whether generic nearby homogeneous initial data converge to one of these exact solutions in the relevant asymptotic limit, and identify the basins of attraction in terms of the initial-data parameters.

Consider a five-dimensional braneworld model in which the bulk spacetime contains a four-dimensional brane whose induced geometry is of Robertson–Walker (spatially homogeneous and isotropic) type. Suppose that, near a distinguished value of the extra-dimensional coordinate (taken either at a finite location or asymptotically far from the brane), one has classified the leading-order asymptotic forms of the metric and matter fields that solve the coupled bulk–brane Einstein equations under the homogeneity and isotropy assumption, obtaining a finite collection of formal asymptotic families (some regular, some singular).

(a) Carry out a linear perturbation analysis around each such asymptotic family in which the perturbations are allowed to depend on all five spacetime coordinates (i.e., general inhomogeneous and anisotropic perturbations, not restricted to preserve the Robertson–Walker symmetry). Determine, for each family, whether the perturbation modes remain bounded (in a suitable norm) as one approaches the distinguished coordinate value, and hence decide which asymptotic families are stable and which are unstable under such generic perturbations.

(b) For each asymptotic family, perform a function-counting argument: count the number of independent arbitrary functions of the appropriate number of variables that parametrize the general solution of the linearized system whose leading behavior matches that family, and compare with the maximum number of arbitrary functions allowed by the full nonlinear system (after gauge fixing). Conclude from this counting which of the asymptotic families are general (depending on the maximal number of free functions and thus representing the generic behavior) and which are non-generic (of measure zero in the space of solutions).

Consider tree-level effective string cosmology actions in $D$ spacetime dimensions of the form
$$S = \int d^D x \, \sqrt{-g}\, e^{-\phi}\Bigl(R + (\nabla\phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{12} H_{\mu\nu\rho}H^{\mu\nu\rho}\Bigr) - \tfrac{1}{2}\int d^Dx\,\sqrt{-g}\,\sum_p \frac{1}{(p+2)!} F^{(p+2)}_{\mu_1\cdots \mu_{p+2}}F^{(p+2)\,\mu_1\cdots \mu_{p+2}},$$
where $\phi$ is the dilaton, $H = dB$ is the NS-NS three-form field strength of a two-form $B$, and the $F^{(p+2)}$ are RR field strengths. As background metric ansatz, take a spatially homogeneous Bianchi-type anisotropic cosmology
$$ds^2 = -dt^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{D-1} a_i(t)^2 (\sigma^i)^2,$$
with appropriately compatible homogeneous matter fields, so that the equations of motion reduce to an autonomous system of ODEs in the scale factors $a_i(t)$, the dilaton $\phi(t)$, and the matter degrees of freedom.

Investigate the asymptotic regimes (as $t\to 0^+$ and $t\to\infty$) of the corresponding dynamical system. Specifically:

(a) For each of the cases (i) only NS-NS fields turned on, (ii) only RR fields turned on, (iii) both NS-NS and RR fields turned on, classify all asymptotic regimes (in the sense of Kasner-like power-law behaviors, possible oscillatory regimes, and dilaton-driven regimes) of the anisotropic system.

(b) Determine all possible asymptotic decompositions of the vector field generating the flow, and identify the asymptotic cancellations among the various contributions (curvature, dilaton kinetic, NS-NS, RR) that can occur on each regime.

(c) Identify lower-dimensional attractor solutions, parametrized by fewer arbitrary constants than the generic solution, that asymptotically organize the full solution space, and prove that families of generic solutions converge to them.

Consider the heterotic M-theory effective description of the Ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmological scenarios, modeled by two boundary three-branes separated by an interval in an eleven-dimensional bulk. Working in the moduli-space approximation, the low-energy dynamics is governed by a four-dimensional effective action for the scale factor a(t) of the spatial sections together with the radion (inter-brane separation) modulus φ(t) and the Calabi–Yau volume modulus, supplemented by curvature corrections that arise as higher-order (in α' and in derivatives) terms beyond the leading two-derivative Einstein–scalar truncation.

A distinguished homogeneous, spatially flat solution of the leading-order equations is the Milne state: the brane configuration corresponding to a vanishing inter-brane velocity at past infinity with the four-dimensional metric tending to the flat Milne form ds² = −dt² + t² dx² as t → −∞ (equivalently, the empty Minkowski wedge realized as the past attractor of the moduli-space dynamics).

Now suppose that, in the regime of interest, the higher-order curvature/derivative corrections are not subdominant perturbations of the leading dynamics but instead enter the evolution equations dominantly, so that they govern the leading asymptotic behavior of the moduli (a, φ, …) as t → −∞.

Question. In this regime where the higher-order terms are asymptotically dominant, is the Milne state a globally asymptotically stable past attractor of the resulting moduli-space dynamical system? That is, do all initial data in an open neighborhood — and ideally in the full physically admissible phase space — of the Milne state evolve so that (a, φ, …) converge to the Milne configuration as t → −∞, with no other attracting solutions or runaway trajectories arising from the dominant higher-order corrections?

Consider the ambient cosmological construction in which a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M^4,g)$ is embedded as a hypersurface in a five-dimensional ambient space $(\widetilde{M}^5,\widetilde{g})$ carrying a perfect-fluid stress-energy content (rather than a pure cosmological constant $\Lambda$), with the embedding compatible with the conformal structure of $M^4$ at conformal infinity. On the twistor side, let $\mathbb{T}\cong\mathbb{C}^4$ denote twistor space equipped with the Hermitian form $\Sigma$ of signature $(2,2)$, and let $PN\subset P\mathbb{T}$ denote the null projective twistor 5-space, i.e., the real five-dimensional hypersurface of projective twistors $[Z]$ with $\Sigma(Z,Z)=0$, which is the space of null geodesics of conformally compactified Minkowski space. Recall further the nonlinear graviton / $\mathcal H$-space construction associating to suitable asymptotically flat (or self-dual) data a complex four-manifold of $\alpha$-planes.

(a) Determine whether there exists a canonical correspondence between the ambient 5-space $\widetilde{M}^5$ and $PN$ (or an appropriate deformation/$\mathcal H$-space generalization thereof) that intertwines the ambient fluid data with twistorial data, and if so describe this correspondence explicitly.

(b) Formulate and prove a precise asymptotic condition on $\widetilde{M}^5$ — replacing the cosmological-constant asymptotic conditions used in the $\Lambda$-case — under which the perfect-fluid ambient construction is well-posed and compatible with the proposed twistor correspondence.

(c) Give a precise mathematical meaning to "non-locality" of fields and observables on the ambient 5-space $\widetilde{M}^5$, and characterize how this non-locality is encoded on the twistor side (for example, via cohomological or contour-integral representations on $PN$ or its $\mathcal H$-space analogue).

Consider a (d+1)-dimensional Friedmann–Robertson–Walker spacetime with metric
  ds² = -dt² + a(t)² γ_ij dx^i dx^j,
where γ_ij is the metric of a maximally symmetric d-dimensional space with constant spatial curvature k ∈ {-1, 0, +1}, together with a spatially homogeneous dilaton field φ(t). Let H(t) = ȧ(t)/a(t) be the Hubble rate and let φ̇(t) denote the time derivative of the dilaton.

Take the gravi-dilaton effective action including the leading α′ (first-order in the inverse string tension) corrections,
  S = (1/(2λ_s^{d-1})) ∫ d^{d+1}x √(-g) e^{-φ} [ R + (∂φ)² - (1/12) H_{μνρ}H^{μνρ} + α′ ( a₁ R_{GB}² + a₂ (∂φ)⁴ + (couplings of the dilaton to the higher-curvature terms) ) + O(α′²) ],
with R_{GB}² = R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} - 4 R_{μν}R^{μν} + R² the Gauss–Bonnet density and the antisymmetric tensor field strength H_{μνρ} (and dilaton couplings to all higher-order curvature invariants) consistent with tree-level closed string theory.

Restricting to the cosmological ansatz above and to the vacuum sector (matter-free, with the H-field either set to zero or treated in its homogeneous reduction), derive the resulting autonomous system of ordinary differential equations for (H(t), φ̇(t)) (and, in the curved case, for a(t) itself), and:

(a) Identify all asymptotic regimes (fixed points, scaling solutions, and behavior as t → ±∞) of this system for k = 0 and for k = ±1.

(b) Determine the linear stability of each asymptotic regime, in particular of the vacuum solutions, including the effect of the dilaton coupling to the higher-curvature terms.

(c) Describe how the inclusion of the α′ dilaton-curvature couplings modifies the asymptotic and stability picture compared to the purely gravitational Gauss–Bonnet correction, and in particular characterize the stability of the trivial vacuum (H = 0, φ̇ = const) of the corrected effective action.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has made substantial progress on this problem. The Hohm–Zwiebach formulation (2019) provides O(d,d)-covariant gravi-dilaton cosmologies to all orders in α′, and explicit asymptotic and stability analyses for the flat FRW case have appeared (e.g., "α′-Cosmology: solutions and stability analysis", JHEP 2020; non-singular α′-corrected solutions, JHEP 2019; later FLRW/de Sitter constructions, 2023). However, a complete classification of asymptotic regimes and vacuum stability for both flat and curved FRW universes including the full first-order α′-corrected action with all dilaton couplings does not appear to be fully settled, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.
