Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth closed (compact, without boundary) orientable two-dimensional Riemannian manifold and let $V\colon M\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth function. Consider the natural Hamiltonian on the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ given, in local coordinates $(q,p)$, by
$$H(q,p)=\tfrac{1}{2}g^{ij}(q)\,p_i p_j+V(q).$$
A function $F\colon T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a polynomial integral of degree $n$ in the momenta if $F(q,p)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_{i_1\cdots i_k}(q)\,p^{i_1}\cdots p^{i_k}$ with smooth coefficients on $M$, and $\{H,F\}=0$ where $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ is the canonical Poisson bracket. The integral is called nontrivial if it is functionally independent of $H$.

Address the following:

(1) Construct new examples of pairs $(g,V)$ on a closed surface $M$ such that the associated natural Hamiltonian $H$ admits a nontrivial polynomial integral $F$ in the momenta, and describe and, if possible, classify such examples (in particular, beyond the cases of degree $\le 2$ and beyond the metrics/potentials currently known on the sphere $S^2$ and the torus $T^2$).

(2) Prove nonexistence results: under suitable additional assumptions on $(M,g,V)$, show that no nontrivial polynomial integral of a given degree (or of any degree) can exist.

The classification of natural Hamiltonian systems on closed surfaces admitting polynomial integrals in the momenta is a long-standing open problem. By Kolokoltsov's classical result, surfaces of genus $\ge 2$ admit no nontrivial polynomial integrals, but the cases of $S^2$ and $T^2$ remain unsettled in general degree. Let $T^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ be the flat two-dimensional torus with canonical coordinates $(q_1, q_2)$ and conjugate momenta $(p_1, p_2)$. Consider a natural Hamiltonian system on the cotangent bundle $T^*T^2$ with Hamiltonian
$$H(q,p) = \tfrac{1}{2}(p_1^2 + p_2^2) + V(q_1,q_2),$$
where $V: T^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is a smooth nonconstant potential. A function $F: T^*T^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is called a polynomial integral of degree $n$ in momenta if it Poisson-commutes with $H$ and has the form $F(q,p) = \sum_{i+j \le n} a_{ij}(q) p_1^i p_2^j$ with the homogeneous part of degree $n$ not identically zero. An integral is called nontrivial if it is functionally independent of $H$. Prove or disprove the following:

(a) If such a system admits a polynomial integral of odd degree in momenta, then it admits a nontrivial integral that is linear in momenta.

(b) If such a system admits a nontrivial polynomial integral of even degree in momenta, then it admits a nontrivial integral that is quadratic in momenta.

Fix integers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, and work over the field of complex numbers. Let V = C[x_1,...,x_n]_d denote the vector space of homogeneous forms of degree d in n variables, and let X_n^d ⊂ V be the open locus of forms with nonvanishing discriminant (smooth hypersurfaces). The group SL_n acts on V by linear substitution.

For f ∈ X_n^d, the gradient morphism ∇ : X_n^d → Z_n^{d-1} := (C[x_1,...,x_n]_{d-1})^n sends f to its tuple of partial derivatives (∂f/∂x_1, ..., ∂f/∂x_n). Passing to projectivizations and to the GIT quotients by SL_n (using the natural linearizations on the projective spaces and on Z_n^{d-1}), one obtains an induced map
   P∇|_{P X_n^d} : P X_n^d // SL_n  →  Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n.

Next, the "associated form" construction Ψ assigns to a tuple in Z_n^{d-1} a form of degree n(d-2) in the elementary symmetric polynomials e_1,...,e_n; this defines an SL_n-equivariant rational map Ψ : Z_n^{d-1} ⇢ P(C[e_1,...,e_n]_{n(d-2)}) (defined where the tuple has nonvanishing resultant). Taking GIT quotients yields an induced map
   PΨ : Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n  →  P(C[e_1,...,e_n]_{n(d-2)})^{ss} // SL_n.

Prove that for all integers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3 the following two conditions hold simultaneously:

(C1) P∇|_{P X_n^d} is a closed immersion, i.e., it is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n.

(C2) PΨ is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset of P(C[e_1,...,e_n]_{n(d-2)})^{ss} // SL_n.

Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote either the space of entire functions $h:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ or the space of holomorphic maps $h:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$. For $a\in\mathbb{C}$ and $h\in\mathcal{H}$, let $h_a(z):=h(z+a)$ denote the translate of $h$ by $a$. Define $\mathcal{U}\subset\mathcal{H}$ to be the set of maps $h\in\mathcal{H}$ such that the translation orbit $\{h_a : a\in\mathbb{C}\}$ is dense in $\mathcal{H}$; equivalently, for every $f\in\mathcal{H}$ there exists a sequence $(a_n)\subset\mathbb{C}$ with $h_{a_n}\to f$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$.

For $h\in\mathcal{H}$ (in the projective case), let $\omega$ denote the Fubini–Study Kähler form on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ (normalized so that $\int_{\mathbb{P}^1}\omega=1$), and define the Nevanlinna (Ahlfors–Shimizu) characteristic
$$T_h(r) := \int_0^r \frac{dt}{t}\int_{D(t)} h^{*}\omega, \qquad r>0,$$
where $D(t)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<t\}$. (In the entire case, replace $\omega$ by the pullback of the Fubini–Study form under $\mathbb{C}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1$.)

Determine the minimal possible growth rate of $T_h(r)$ as $r\to\infty$ over all $h\in\mathcal{U}$. More precisely, characterize the infimum, in the sense of growth orders, of the family $\{T_h : h\in\mathcal{U}\}$, and decide whether for every transcendental increasing function $\varphi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ there exists $h\in\mathcal{U}$ with $T_h(r)=O(\varphi(r))$ as $r\to\infty$.

Let $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{O}(\mathbb{C})$ denote the space of entire functions of one complex variable, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$ and the corresponding Borel $\sigma$-algebra. For each $a \in \mathbb{C}$, let $T_a : \mathcal{H} \to \mathcal{H}$ be the translation operator $(T_a h)(z) = h(z+a)$. A Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{H}$ is called translation-invariant if $\mu \circ T_a^{-1} = \mu$ for every $a \in \mathbb{C}$, and is called non-trivial if it is not the Dirac mass at a constant function.

Let $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathcal{H}$ denote the set of universal entire functions, i.e.\ those $h \in \mathcal{H}$ whose translation orbit $\{T_a h : a \in \mathbb{C}\}$ is dense in $\mathcal{H}$. (By a classical theorem of Birkhoff, $\mathcal{U}$ is non-empty; in fact it is a dense $G_\delta$ subset of $\mathcal{H}$.)

Problem. Given a non-trivial translation-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{H}$, determine what can be said about $\mu(\mathcal{U})$. In particular, decide whether $\mu(\mathcal{U})$ must equal $0$, must equal $1$, or whether each value in $[0,1]$ can occur for a suitable choice of $\mu$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has constructed non-trivial translation-invariant (in fact ergodic) probability measures on the space of entire functions whose support lies inside the set $\mathcal{U}$ of universal entire functions, showing that $\mu(\mathcal{U}) = 1$ can occur. Further results give sharp lower bounds on the growth of functions in the support of such measures and study tail decay. A complete classification of $\mu(\mathcal{U})$ for arbitrary non-trivial translation-invariant $\mu$ does not appear to be fully established, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

Let $n\ge 2$ and $d\ge 3$ be integers. Let $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]_d$ denote the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{C}$, equipped with the natural action of $SL_n(\mathbb{C})$. Let $e_1,\dots,e_n$ be the elementary symmetric polynomials in auxiliary variables, and consider the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[e_1,\dots,e_n]$ graded so that $\deg e_i=i$. Denote by $\mathbb{C}[e_1,\dots,e_n]_{n(d-2)}$ the homogeneous component of degree $n(d-2)$, on which $SL_n$ acts.

For a homogeneous form $f\in \mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]_d$ with isolated singularity at the origin (equivalently, with nonzero discriminant), the Milnor algebra $M_f=\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\partial f/\partial x_1,\dots,\partial f/\partial x_n)$ is a graded Gorenstein Artin algebra of socle degree $\nu:=n(d-2)$. The associated form construction assigns to such an $f$ a homogeneous polynomial $\mathbf{A}(f)\in \mathbb{C}[e_1,\dots,e_n]_{n(d-2)}$ (the Macaulay inverse system / dual socle generator of $M_f$, written in elementary-symmetric coordinates). Let $U_n^{n(d-2)}\subset \mathbb{C}[e_1,\dots,e_n]_{n(d-2)}$ denote the image of the morphism $f\mapsto \mathbf{A}(f)$ defined on the open locus of forms with nonzero discriminant.

Problem. Show that for all $n\ge 2$ and $d\ge 3$ there exists a homogeneous $SL_n$-invariant polynomial $J$ on $\mathbb{C}[e_1,\dots,e_n]_{n(d-2)}$ such that $U_n^{n(d-2)}$ is a closed subset of the open set $\{J\ne 0\}\subset \mathbb{C}[e_1,\dots,e_n]_{n(d-2)}$. Equivalently, exhibit such an invariant $J$ for each pair $(n,d)$.

A classical result of B. Weiss asserts that on the space $\mathcal{H}$ of entire functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets, there exist non-trivial Borel probability measures invariant under the action of the translation group $\mathbb{C}$ (i.e., measures not supported on constant functions).

Problem: Construct a non-trivial $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{M}$, that is, a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\mu(g \cdot A) = \mu(A)$ for every $g \in G$ and every Borel set $A \subseteq \mathcal{M}$, and such that $\mu$ is not supported on the set of constant maps. Equivalently, extend Weiss's construction of non-trivial invariant probability measures from the case of entire functions under translation to this general homogeneous setting.

Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a (possibly singular) holomorphic foliation on $X$ whose leaves have complex dimension $k > 1$. In the case $k=1$ (foliations by Riemann surfaces), the ergodic theory of $\mathcal{F}$ is built on the notion of a positive $dd^c$-closed current of bi-dimension $(1,1)$ directed by $\mathcal{F}$, i.e. a positive current $T$ on $X$ of bi-dimension $(1,1)$ such that $dd^c T = 0$ and such that, in flow boxes, $T$ is an average of integration currents along the local plaques against a transverse positive measure.

Problem: Identify the correct higher-dimensional analogue of such directed $dd^c$-closed $(1,1)$-currents for foliations with leaves of dimension $k>1$. More precisely, define a class of positive currents on $X$ associated to $\mathcal{F}$ — playing for $k$-dimensional leaves the same role that directed positive $dd^c$-closed $(1,1)$-currents play for $1$-dimensional leaves — such that this class supports the development of an ergodic theory (existence, uniqueness, and ergodic theorems for averages along leaves) for holomorphic foliations of leaf dimension greater than $1$ on compact Kähler manifolds.

Let $R$ be a finite-dimensional associative algebra over $\mathbb{R}$ equipped with an involution $\gamma\colon R\to R$ (an $\mathbb{R}$-linear map satisfying $\gamma(xy)=\gamma(y)\gamma(x)$ and $\gamma^2=\mathrm{id}$). Consider the ring $R[t]$ of left polynomials in a central indeterminate $t$, and extend $\gamma$ to $R[t]$ coefficientwise. For $C\in R[t]$, define the norm polynomial
$$\nu(C):=C\,\gamma(C)=\gamma(C)\,C,$$
and assume conditions on $C$ ensuring $\nu(C)\in R[t]$ (i.e., $\nu(C)$ has central, $\gamma$-invariant coefficients). One says $C$ admits a linear-factor factorization if there exist $c_n,h_1,\ldots,h_n\in R$ with
$$C=c_n(t-h_1)(t-h_2)\cdots(t-h_n),\qquad n=\deg C.$$

Restrict attention to the class of left polynomials $C\in R[t]$ with $\nu(C)=0$. Determine which such polynomials admit a linear-factor factorization, and give necessary and sufficient criteria, in terms of $R$, $\gamma$, and the coefficients of $C$, characterizing factorizability in this zero-norm case.

Let $\mathbb{P}^k$ denote complex projective space of dimension $k\ge 3$. A (singular) holomorphic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^k$ of dimension $d$, with $1<d<k$, is given by an integrable holomorphic subbundle (twisted by a line bundle) of the tangent bundle of $\mathbb{P}^k$ defined off an analytic subset $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$ of codimension at least $2$; equivalently, by a global twisted holomorphic $d$-vector field that is locally decomposable and integrable. The foliation $\mathcal{F}$ is called elementary if it admits a non-constant meromorphic first integral, or, more generally, if it is a pull-back of a foliation of the same dimension on a lower-dimensional projective manifold via a rational map, or is invariant under a non-trivial algebraic group action — i.e., if it can be reduced to a lower-dimensional or homogeneous situation. Otherwise $\mathcal{F}$ is said to be non-elementary.

Problem: Exhibit a non-elementary holomorphic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^k$ whose leaves have complex dimension strictly greater than $1$ and such that no leaf of $\mathcal{F}$ contains a compact (complex) algebraic curve.

Let $\mathbb{D}^k \subset \mathbb{C}^k$ denote the open unit polydisc, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a holomorphic foliation on $\mathbb{D}^k$ whose leaves have complex dimension $d$ with $d>1$. Assume $\mathcal{F}$ is given by $k-d$ holomorphic $(1,0)$-forms $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}$ on $\mathbb{D}^k$ that are linearly independent at a generic point and satisfy the Frobenius integrability condition
$$\partial \alpha_j = \sum_{l=1}^{k-d} \alpha_l \wedge \beta_{j,l}, \qquad j=1,\dots,k-d,$$
for some holomorphic $(1,0)$-forms $\beta_{j,l}$ on $\mathbb{D}^k$.

Question: Can each $\alpha_j$ be approximated, uniformly on every compact subset of $\mathbb{D}^k$, by holomorphic $(1,0)$-forms $\alpha_{j,n}$ defined on all of $\mathbb{C}^k$ (respectively, by polynomial $(1,0)$-forms, viewed as forms on $\mathbb{P}^k$) such that, for each $n$, the approximating forms $\alpha_{1,n},\dots,\alpha_{k-d,n}$ themselves satisfy a Frobenius condition
$$\partial \alpha_{j,n} = \sum_{l=1}^{k-d} \alpha_{l,n} \wedge \beta_{j,l,n}$$
for some holomorphic (respectively polynomial) $(1,0)$-forms $\beta_{j,l,n}$? Equivalently, can every such foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{D}^k$ be approximated by holomorphic foliations on $\mathbb{C}^k$ or $\mathbb{P}^k$?

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of real quaternions and $\mathbb{DH} = \mathbb{H}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ the algebra of dual quaternions, with conjugation extended from $\mathbb{H}$ by setting $\overline{\varepsilon} = \varepsilon$. For a polynomial $A = \sum_i a_i t^i \in \mathbb{H}[t]$ (the indeterminate $t$ commuting with all coefficients), write $\overline{A} = \sum_i \overline{a_i} t^i$ and define the norm polynomial $\nu(A) = A\overline{A} \in \mathbb{R}[t]$ when this product is real. The maximal real polynomial factor $\operatorname{mrpf} A$ of $A \in \mathbb{H}[t]$ is the (monic) polynomial in $\mathbb{R}[t]$ of largest degree dividing $A$ on the right (equivalently, on the left).

A polynomial $C = P + \varepsilon Q \in \mathbb{DH}[t]$ with $P, Q \in \mathbb{H}[t]$ is called a motion polynomial if its dual-quaternion norm $C\overline{C}$ lies in $\mathbb{R}[t]$ and $\nu(C) := P\overline{P} \neq 0$. A factorization of $C$ into linear factors is an expression
$$C = c\,(t - h_1)(t - h_2)\cdots(t - h_n), \qquad c \in \mathbb{DH},\ h_1,\dots,h_n \in \mathbb{DH},\ n = \deg C.$$
Such a $C$ is called generic if $\operatorname{mrpf} P = 1$; in that case it is known that $C$ always admits a factorization into linear factors. Call $C$ non-generic if $\operatorname{mrpf} P \neq 1$. It is also known that for any motion polynomial $C$ there exist $S \in \mathbb{R}[t]$ with $\deg S \leq \deg \operatorname{mrpf} P$, and (under boundedness hypotheses) $D \in \mathbb{H}[t]$, such that $CS$ or $CD$ admits a factorization into linear factors over $\mathbb{DH}$.

Problem: Formulate general necessary and sufficient criteria, in terms of $P$ and $Q$, that determine when a non-generic motion polynomial $C = P + \varepsilon Q \in \mathbb{DH}[t]$ itself (without multiplying by any auxiliary $S \in \mathbb{R}[t]$ or $D \in \mathbb{H}[t]$) admits a factorization into linear factors over $\mathbb{DH}$.

Let $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,1)$ denote the Clifford algebra with signature $(p,q,1)$, viewed as having a "primal part" (the quotient by the ideal generated by the degenerate generator) isomorphic to $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,0)$ and a "dual part" (the kernel of the projection to the primal part). The case $(p,q,1)=(0,2,1)$ recovers the dual quaternions $\mathbb{DH}$. For an indeterminate $t$ commuting with the algebra, consider the polynomial ring $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,1)[t]$.

Let $C \in \mathrm{Cl}(p,q,1)[t]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ whose primal part $A \in \mathrm{Cl}(p,q,0)[t]$ admits a factorization
$$A=(t-a_1)(t-a_2)\cdots(t-a_n), \qquad a_i \in \mathrm{Cl}(p,q,0).$$
Make the ansatz
$$C=(t-a_1-b_1)(t-a_2-b_2)\cdots(t-a_n-b_n),$$
where each $b_i \in \mathrm{Cl}(p,q,1)$ has vanishing primal part. Comparing coefficients yields a square system of $(m+1)n$ real linear equations in the $(m+1)n$ unknown real coordinates of $b_1,\ldots,b_n$, where $m+1$ is the real dimension of the dual part of $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,1)$.

(a) Provide sufficient algebraic/combinatorial criteria on $C$ (or on the chosen primal factorization $a_1,\ldots,a_n$) which guarantee that this linear system is solvable, and hence that $C$ admits a factorization into monic linear factors over $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,1)$.

(b) Characterize, in terms of the algebra of $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q,1)$ and (when applicable) the kinematic/geometric interpretation in $\mathbb{DH}[t]$, those $C$ for which the linear system has a unique solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution.

Let $(M^4,\omega)$ and $(M'^4,\omega')$ be connected symplectic 4-manifolds, and let $\varphi: M^4 \to B$ and $\varphi': M'^4 \to B'$ be Lagrangian fibrations, i.e., smooth surjective submersions (possibly with singular fibers in a controlled sense) whose generic fibers are Lagrangian submanifolds. By the Liouville–Arnold theorem, the regular part of each base carries a canonical integral affine structure (defined up to the action of $\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Z})\ltimes \mathbb{R}^n$ via action coordinates). Suppose that the bases $B$ and $B'$, equipped with these integral affine structures (extended over singularities in the natural sense), are affinely equivalent: there exists a diffeomorphism $\psi: B \to B'$ that preserves the integral affine structures.

Question: Does it follow that the Lagrangian fibrations $\varphi$ and $\varphi'$ are fiberwise symplectomorphic, i.e., does there exist a symplectomorphism $\Phi: (M,\omega) \to (M',\omega')$ such that $\varphi' \circ \Phi = \psi \circ \varphi$?

Consider an integrable Hamiltonian system with two degrees of freedom on a symplectic 4-manifold, given by a momentum map F = (F_1, F_2) whose components Poisson-commute. Restrict attention to "stable" (structurally stable) degenerate singularities of the associated Lagrangian fibration — for instance, parabolic orbits and cuspidal tori — for which, in a saturated neighbourhood of the singular fibre, one can introduce two action variables I_1 and I_2 such that I_1 is a smooth function of the original integrals while I_2 has a prescribed singular part determined by the topological type of the singularity (so that I_2 is singular but its non-singular remainder is smooth).

(a) Describe a complete set of semi-global symplectic invariants of such stable singularities, i.e. invariants that determine the singularity up to a fibre-preserving symplectomorphism in a saturated neighbourhood of the singular fibre.

(b) Decide whether the pair (I_1, I_2), viewed as germs of action variables (with their prescribed singular parts), is by itself sufficient for the symplectic classification of these stable singularities.

Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ equipped with an effective Hamiltonian action of the torus $(S^1)^{n-1}$, with momentum map $\mu=(f_1,\dots,f_{n-1}):M\to\mathbb R^{n-1}$. Such a triple $(M,\omega,\mu)$ is called a complexity-one space. Suppose there exists a smooth function $f_n:M\to\mathbb R$ such that $F=(f_1,\dots,f_{n-1},f_n):M\to\mathbb R^n$ is a completely integrable system, i.e. the components Poisson-commute and are almost-everywhere functionally independent. Assume further that every singular point $p\in M$ of $F$ is non-degenerate in the Williamson sense, and that the local symplectic normal form of $F$ at each singular point contains only elliptic and focus–focus blocks (no hyperbolic blocks).

When $n=2$ such a system is a semitoric system, and it is classified up to isomorphism by five symplectic invariants (the number of focus–focus singularities, the polygon invariant, the height invariant, the Taylor-series invariant at each focus–focus point, and the twisting-index invariant). On the other hand, complexity-one spaces in arbitrary dimension carry their own set of symplectic/topological invariants (the Karshon–Tolman invariants, multigraphs labeled by isotropy data, painted polytopes, etc.).

Problem: Determine an explicit correspondence between the invariants of the complexity-one space $(M,\omega,\mu)$ and the invariants of the integrable system $F=(\mu,f_n)$ viewed (when $n=2$) as a semitoric system, and more generally formulate and prove which complexity-one invariants extend to, or are recovered from, the symplectic invariants of the integrable system $F$ under the stated non-degeneracy and no-hyperbolic-block hypotheses.

Background. The classical pentagram map T acts on projective equivalence classes of (twisted) polygons in RP^2 by sending a polygon P with vertices (v_i) to the polygon whose i-th vertex is the intersection of the two consecutive "short" diagonals (v_{i-1} v_{i+1}) ∩ (v_i v_{i+2}). The leapfrog map is a one-dimensional analogue acting on configurations of points on a line (or on pairs of polygons in RP^1) via cross-ratio relations. Both admit higher-dimensional generalizations to twisted polygons in RP^d (the "higher pentagram maps"), and both are known to be completely integrable in the Liouville–Arnold sense: they admit invariant Poisson structures and a maximal family of Poisson-commuting integrals.

Replace the underlying field of scalars by a (not necessarily commutative) associative algebra A, using a noncommutative cross-ratio (e.g. the Gelfand–Retakh quasi-determinantal cross-ratio) to define the corresponding dynamical systems. Concretely:

(a) The noncommutative leapfrog map is the dynamical system on configurations of points with values in A obtained by replacing all cross-ratio relations defining the classical leapfrog map with their noncommutative cross-ratio counterparts. Establish its complete integrability: produce an invariant (noncommutative) Poisson/Hamiltonian structure together with a maximal collection of functionally independent integrals in involution, and prove Liouville-type integrability in the appropriate noncommutative sense.

(b) Define a noncommutative version of the pentagram map on twisted polygons in projective space over A, as well as noncommutative versions of the higher-dimensional pentagram maps (the maps on twisted polygons in RP^d obtained by intersecting suitable consecutive subspaces spanned by vertex tuples). For each of these noncommutative maps, establish complete integrability by exhibiting the requisite Lax/zero-curvature representation, invariant Poisson structure, and complete commuting family of integrals.

The noncommutative leapfrog map has been studied (Wang, J. London Math. Soc. 2025; arXiv:2310.01993): an explicit formula, a discrete zero-curvature representation, and a Poisson structure via noncommutative networks have been derived, giving substantial progress toward integrability of the leapfrog part. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $J = \{A + \lambda B : \lambda \in \mathbb{K}\cup\{\infty\}\}$ be a pencil of skew-symmetric bilinear forms on $V$ generated by two skew-symmetric forms $A, B$ on $V$. A subspace $L \subset V$ is called bi-Lagrangian (with respect to $J$) if $L$ is isotropic with respect to every form in the pencil $J$ and $\dim L$ is the maximum possible among such isotropic subspaces. The bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian $\mathrm{LG}(V, J)$ is the set of all bi-Lagrangian subspaces of $V$; it is a projective algebraic variety. Let $\mathrm{Aut}(V, J)$ denote the group of linear automorphisms of $V$ preserving the pencil $J$ (equivalently, preserving both $A$ and $B$ up to a change of basis of the pencil), which acts naturally on $\mathrm{LG}(V, J)$.

(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the pencil $J$ (equivalently, on its Jordan–Kronecker canonical form) under which $\mathrm{LG}(V, J)$ is a smooth algebraic variety.

(b) Describe explicitly the partition of $\mathrm{LG}(V, J)$ into orbits of the action of $\mathrm{Aut}(V, J)$.

Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$), and let $\mathfrak{g}^*$ denote its dual space. The Lie–Poisson bracket on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ is defined on linear functions $x,y \in \mathfrak{g} \subset C^\infty(\mathfrak{g}^*)$ by $\{x,y\}(\xi) = \langle \xi, [x,y]\rangle$ for $\xi \in \mathfrak{g}^*$, and extended by the Leibniz rule. For any fixed $a \in \mathfrak{g}^*$, the frozen-argument bracket $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_a$ is defined by $\{x,y\}_a(\xi) = \langle a, [x,y]\rangle$. The two brackets are compatible (their pencil is Poisson), and an element $a \in \mathfrak{g}^*$ is called regular if the dimension of its coadjoint orbit equals the maximal coadjoint orbit dimension in $\mathfrak{g}^*$.

A family $F \subset \mathbb{R}[\mathfrak{g}^*]$ of polynomials is said to be in bi-involution if its elements pairwise commute with respect to both $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ and $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_a$. The family is called complete if at a generic point $\xi \in \mathfrak{g}^*$ the differentials of its elements span a subspace of $T_\xi^*\mathfrak{g}^*$ of dimension $\tfrac{1}{2}(\dim \mathfrak{g} + \mathrm{ind}\,\mathfrak{g})$, where $\mathrm{ind}\,\mathfrak{g}$ is the index of $\mathfrak{g}$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and every regular element $a \in \mathfrak{g}^*$, there exists a complete family $G_a$ of polynomials on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ in bi-involution with respect to $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ and $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_a$.

The classical Mishchenko–Fomenko conjecture (existence of a complete commutative family on g*) was proved by Sadetov in 2004, but his construction does not in general yield a family in bi-involution with respect to the argument-shift pencil. The bi-Hamiltonian strengthening — existence of a complete family in bi-involution for every regular a — has been verified in many cases (semisimple Lie algebras via argument shift; low-dimensional solvable and nilpotent algebras) but remains open in general.

Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ (or $\mathbb{R}$) with dual space $\mathfrak{g}^*$, and let $\{\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\}$ denote the Lie–Poisson bracket on $\mathfrak{g}^*$, given on linear functions $x,y\in\mathfrak{g}\subset C^\infty(\mathfrak{g}^*)$ by $\{x,y\}(\xi)=\xi([x,y])$ for $\xi\in\mathfrak{g}^*$. For each $x\in\mathfrak{g}^*$ let $A_x$ denote the skew-symmetric matrix of the Lie–Poisson bracket at the point $x$, i.e. the operator on $\mathfrak{g}$ defined by $\langle A_x\,u,v\rangle = x([u,v])$ for $u,v\in\mathfrak{g}$. For a fixed regular element $a\in\mathfrak{g}^*$ consider the linear pencil of skew-symmetric forms
$$\mathcal{P}_{a}=\{A_x+\lambda A_a : \lambda\in\mathbb{C}\}, \qquad x\in\mathfrak{g}^*.$$
By the Jordan–Kronecker theorem, at a generic $x$ the pencil $A_x+\lambda A_a$ admits a canonical decomposition into Jordan blocks (with distinct or coinciding eigenvalues) and Kronecker (singular) blocks of various odd sizes; the multiset of these block types is called the algebraic type of the pencil at $x$.

Questions:
(1) Determine which algebraic types (i.e. which combinations of Jordan and Kronecker block structures) can occur as the Jordan–Kronecker type of a generic pencil $A_x+\lambda A_a$ associated with some finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and some regular $a\in\mathfrak{g}^*$. Are there nontrivial restrictions on the realisable algebraic types beyond those holding for arbitrary linear pencils of skew-symmetric forms?
(2) For each algebraic type that is not excluded a priori, construct a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and an element $a\in\mathfrak{g}^*$ that realises it, or prove that no such Lie algebra exists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The classification of realisable Jordan–Kronecker algebraic types for linear Poisson pencils on Lie coalgebras remains an active research problem. Partial results exist (e.g., computations of Jordan–Kronecker invariants for several series of Lie algebras by Bolsinov–Zhang and others, and results on three-dimensional Lie algebras admitting regular semisimple algebraic Nijenhuis operators in 2024), but no general classification or set of restrictions is known.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian (or pseudo-Riemannian) manifold of dimension $n \geq 3$, with cotangent bundle $T^*M$ equipped with its canonical symplectic form. For a smooth potential $V \colon M \to \mathbb{R}$, consider the natural Hamiltonian
$$H(q,p) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\, g^{ij}(q)\, p_i p_j \;+\; V(q), \qquad (q,p)\in T^*M,$$
and the associated Hamilton equations $\dot q^i = \partial H/\partial p_i$, $\dot p_i = -\partial H/\partial q^i$. A function $F \colon T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$ is called a polynomial-in-momenta integral of degree $k$ if, in any local canonical chart, $F(q,p) = \sum_{|\alpha|\le k} a_\alpha(q)\, p^\alpha$ and $\{H,F\}=0$, where $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ denotes the canonical Poisson bracket. The system $(M,g,V)$ is called Liouville integrable in the class of polynomial-in-momenta integrals if there exist $n$ functionally independent first integrals $F_1=H, F_2,\dots,F_n$ that pairwise Poisson-commute and are each polynomial in the momenta.

Problem. Construct new examples of natural Hamiltonian systems $(M,g,V)$ with $\dim M \geq 3$ that are Liouville integrable in the class of polynomial-in-momenta integrals, beyond those currently known (e.g. systems of Stäckel type, systems of geodesic type associated with Killing tensors on spaces of constant curvature, and direct products or known reductions thereof).

The construction of new integrable natural Hamiltonian systems with polynomial-in-momenta integrals on higher-dimensional manifolds is a longstanding research direction. While numerous examples and partial classifications exist in dimensions 2 and 3 (Stäckel systems, superintegrable systems, Killing-tensor methods), the general problem of producing genuinely new higher-dimensional examples remains an open and actively investigated challenge, with no comprehensive resolution reported.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$), and let $\{\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\}$ be a quadratic Poisson bracket on $V$, i.e., a Poisson bracket on the algebra of polynomial functions on $V$ such that for any two linear coordinate functions $x_i, x_j$ on $V$, the bracket $\{x_i, x_j\}$ is a homogeneous polynomial of degree $2$ in the coordinates. Equivalently, the Poisson tensor $\pi$ has matrix entries $\pi_{ij}(x) = \sum_{k,l} c_{ij}^{kl} x_k x_l$ that are quadratic in $x$, and the Jacobi identity $\{\{f,g\},h\} + \{\{g,h\},f\} + \{\{h,f\},g\} = 0$ holds for all polynomial functions $f,g,h$.

A polynomial integrable system on $(V, \{\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\})$ is a collection $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in \mathbb{R}[V]$ (or $\mathbb{C}[V]$) of polynomial functions, algebraically independent, pairwise in involution ($\{f_i, f_j\} = 0$ for all $i,j$), with $r$ equal to half the rank of the Poisson structure plus the number of independent Casimirs (so that $r = \dim V - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{rank}\,\pi$ generically), thereby producing a complete commutative family.

Question: Is it true that for every quadratic Poisson bracket on every finite-dimensional vector space $V$, there exists a polynomial integrable system?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A web search did not surface a published resolution of the general question. The analogous question for linear (Lie–Poisson) brackets is the well-known Mishchenko–Fomenko conjecture (resolved positively by Sadetov), but for general quadratic Poisson brackets on a vector space no such general existence theorem appears in the literature; only special families (e.g., associated to associative algebras with trace, R-matrix constructions, Lotka–Volterra systems) are known to admit polynomial integrable systems. The problem appears to remain open.

A (1,1)-tensor field L on a smooth manifold (with values in End(TM)) is called a Nijenhuis operator if its Nijenhuis torsion vanishes:
   N_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY] = 0
for all smooth vector fields X, Y. At each point p, the algebraic type of L(p) is encoded by its Segre characteristic, i.e., the unordered collection of sizes of Jordan blocks attached to each (possibly complex) eigenvalue in the Jordan normal form of L(p).

Say that L has compact support on R^n if L vanishes (i.e., L(p) = 0) outside some compact set K ⊂ R^n.

Question. Fix an algebraic type, that is, a Segre characteristic σ for an n×n linear operator. Does there exist a Nijenhuis operator L on R^n such that:
  (1) L has compact support, and
  (2) there exists a non-empty open domain U ⊂ R^n on which the algebraic type (Segre characteristic) of L(p) is constant and equal to σ for every p ∈ U?

Determine for which Segre characteristics σ such a compactly supported Nijenhuis operator exists, and either construct one or prove non-existence.

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

The problem belongs to the recently launched Nijenhuis geometry program of Bolsinov–Konyaev–Matveev. Several follow-up papers (e.g., on gl-regular Nijenhuis operators and on Nijenhuis operators with a unity / F-manifolds) develop tools relevant to constructing Nijenhuis operators with prescribed algebraic type, but none of the sources retrieved explicitly resolves the compact-support version of the question for an arbitrary Segre characteristic. No published solution was located, so the status is taken as unknown / likely still open.

\[
F(x,y)\;=\;f_x(x,y)\bigl(x-f_x(x,y)\bigr)\;-\;f(x,y)\,f_y(x,y),
\]
and assume that $F$ is locally smooth at the origin (more precisely, that it extends to a function which is smooth on a neighbourhood of $(0,0)$). Describe explicitly all such functions $f$, treating separately the two cases:

(a) the regular case $f_y(0,0)\neq 0$;

(b) the singular case $f_y(0,0)=0$.

In each case, give a complete normal-form description (up to an appropriate equivalence) of the set of admissible germs $f$ at the origin satisfying the smoothness condition on $F$.

Let $n\ge 1$ and consider $\mathbb{R}^n$ (or $\mathbb{C}^n$) with coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_n$. A linear operator field $L$ on this space is a $(1,1)$-tensor whose matrix entries $L^i_j(x)$ are linear (homogeneous of degree $1$) functions of $x_1,\dots,x_n$. Its Nijenhuis torsion is
\[
N_L(X,Y) \;=\; L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY],
\]
and $L$ is called a (linear) Nijenhuis operator if $N_L\equiv 0$.

For such an $L$, let $\chi_L(t)=\det(t\,\mathrm{Id}-L(x))=t^n-\sigma_1(x)t^{n-1}+\sigma_2(x)t^{n-2}-\dots+(-1)^n\sigma_n(x)$ be its characteristic polynomial. Then $\sigma_k$ is a homogeneous polynomial of degree $k$ in $x_1,\dots,x_n$.

Problem. Describe and classify all collections $(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n)$ of algebraically independent homogeneous polynomials in $x_1,\dots,x_n$ with $\deg\sigma_k=k$ that arise as the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of some linear Nijenhuis operator on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (equivalently, of some differentially non-degenerate left-symmetric algebra structure on $\mathbb{R}^n$).

Let $(M,\pi)$ be a Poisson manifold of dimension $n$ and let $\mathbf{F}=(f_1,\dots,f_s):M\to\mathbb{R}^s$ be an integrable system on $(M,\pi)$ in the non-commutative sense: the components $f_i$ Poisson-commute with $f_1,\dots,f_r$ (where $r$ is half the rank of $\pi$ at generic points) and the differentials $df_1,\dots,df_s$ are independent on a dense open set. Suppose that a connected compact regular fiber of $\mathbf{F}$ is a Liouville torus $T$, and assume that $T$ meets the singular locus of $\pi$, i.e. that the rank of the Poisson tensor $\pi$ drops on $T$ (or in every neighborhood of $T$).

Formulate and prove an action-angle theorem in a neighborhood of such a Liouville torus $T$ at singular points of the Poisson structure. That is, construct a system of coordinates $(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_r,p_1,\dots,p_r,z_1,\dots,z_{n-2r})$ defined in a saturated neighborhood of $T$ such that the $\theta_i\bmod 2\pi$ are angle coordinates parametrizing the tori, the $p_i$ are action coordinates, the remaining coordinates $z_j$ describe the transverse Poisson geometry, and the Poisson bracket is brought to a normal form that explicitly accounts for the singular behavior of $\pi$ along $T$. Determine, in particular, the precise normal form of $\pi$ near $T$ and the obstructions to the existence of such coordinates.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

An action-angle theorem in neighborhoods of Liouville tori on Poisson manifolds was established for regular points of the Poisson structure (Laurent-Gengoux–Miranda–Vanhaecke). Extensions to singular Poisson structures have been obtained in special cases, notably for b-Poisson/b-symplectic manifolds and for certain singular symplectic settings, where action-angle coordinates near tori on the singular locus have been constructed. A fully general extension to arbitrary singular points of the Poisson structure does not appear to be available, so the problem is partially solved.

Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field k (e.g. k = R or C), and let J : V → V be a linear endomorphism (thought of as the linearization of a Nijenhuis operator at a point). Define the automorphism group of the pair (V, J) by

    Aut(V, J) = { g ∈ GL(V) : g J = J g },

i.e. the group of invertible linear maps of V that commute with J.

(a) Describe the partition of V into orbits of the natural action of Aut(V, J) on V. In particular, give a complete set of invariants that distinguish the orbits, and provide canonical representatives.

(b) More generally, for each integer k with 1 ≤ k ≤ dim V, describe the action of Aut(V, J) on the Grassmannian Gr_k(V) of k-dimensional subspaces U ⊂ V: classify the orbits, exhibit a complete set of invariants, and characterize the fixed points of the action — that is, the Aut(V, J)-invariant k-dimensional subspaces of V.

(The fixed-point case is of particular interest because Aut(V, J)-invariant subspaces correspond to well-defined (co)distributions associated with the operator J in the setting of Poisson pencils.)

The problem is stated as an open problem in surveys on Nijenhuis geometry by Bolsinov and collaborators (e.g. lecture notes "Nijenhuis Geometry, Lecture 21: Open Problems", 2022). While the orbit problem on V itself reduces to a classical similarity/cyclic-decomposition question, the full classification of Aut(V, J)-orbits and invariants on the Grassmannian Gr_k(V), and the description of invariant subspaces, has not been completed in the literature located by search; subsequent work treats specific subclasses (e.g. bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian) but not the general case. Status appears to be open.

Let $(M,\{\,,\,\}_1,\{\,,\,\}_2)$ be a smooth manifold equipped with two compatible Poisson brackets (i.e., every linear combination $\lambda\{\,,\,\}_1+\mu\{\,,\,\}_2$ is again a Poisson bracket); call the family $\mathcal P=\{\lambda\{\,,\,\}_1+\mu\{\,,\,\}_2\}$ a Poisson pencil. At a generic point $x\in M$, the Jordan–Kronecker decomposition theorem associates to the pair of skew-symmetric forms induced by $\{\,,\,\}_1$ and $\{\,,\,\}_2$ on $T_x^*M$ a canonical algebraic invariant — its algebraic type — given by the multiset of Kronecker indices and Jordan blocks (with eigenvalues) appearing in the decomposition. The algebraic type is locally constant on an open dense subset of $M$.

A bi-integrable system on $(M,\{\,,\,\}_1,\{\,,\,\}_2)$ is a collection of smooth functions $f_1,\dots,f_n$ on $M$ that are functionally independent on a dense open set and that pairwise commute with respect to both Poisson brackets:
$$\{f_i,f_j\}_1=\{f_i,f_j\}_2=0\qquad\text{for all }i,j,$$
with $n$ equal to half the rank of a generic bracket in the pencil (so that they form a complete involutive family).

Question: Does there exist, for every algebraic type of Poisson pencil that can be realized at a generic point of some manifold, a bi-Hamiltonian manifold of that algebraic type carrying a bi-integrable system in the above sense (at least locally, in a neighbourhood of a generic point)?

The question concerns the existence of bi-integrable systems for every algebraic type of Poisson pencil (Jordan–Kronecker invariants). Surveys and research in bi-Hamiltonian geometry treat pure Kronecker and pure Jordan (symplectic) cases via known constructions, but note that for mixed algebraic types there is no canonical construction of involutive integrals. No source was found announcing a complete resolution of the existence question for arbitrary algebraic types, so the status appears unresolved/unknown.

The problem is the subject of active research with substantial partial progress. Jordan–Kronecker invariants have been computed for Lie algebras of small dimension (e.g., a 2023 paper by Kozlov in J. Math. Sci. and a 2023 article in Moscow University Math. Bulletin treating six-dimensional nilpotent cases), and general results on Lie algebra representations (relevant to case (a)) appeared in Transformation Groups (2021). New computational techniques (arXiv:2409.09535, 2024) and realization results (arXiv:2307.08642, 2023) further address parts of the problem, but a complete classification for Borel/parabolic subalgebras and centralizers of singular elements in simple Lie algebras has not been fully established.

Let $M$ be a smooth (or complex algebraic) manifold equipped with two compatible Poisson structures $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_1$ and $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_2$, meaning that every linear combination $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_\lambda := \{\cdot,\cdot\}_1 + \lambda\{\cdot,\cdot\}_2$ ($\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$) is again a Poisson bracket. Such a one‑parameter family $\mathcal{P} = \{\{\cdot,\cdot\}_\lambda\}$ is called a Poisson pencil. A pencil is said to be of "quadratic + linear" type if, in suitable coordinates $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ on $M = \mathbb{C}^n$ (or an affine subset), one bracket has structure functions that are homogeneous quadratic polynomials in the $x_i$ while the other has structure functions that are homogeneous linear polynomials in the $x_i$.

For such a pencil, the algebraic type at a point $p\in M$ is the equivalence class, under simultaneous $\mathrm{GL}$-action, of the pair of skew-symmetric bilinear forms on $T_p^* M$ given by the two brackets — equivalently, the Jordan–Kronecker normal form of the pencil of matrices $A_1(p) + \lambda A_2(p)$, where $A_i(p)$ are the Poisson tensors at $p$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{O}(M)$ of functions is said to be in bi-involution with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ if $\{f,g\}_1 = \{f,g\}_2 = 0$ for all $f,g\in\mathcal{F}$; the family is called complete if its dimension at a generic point equals $\tfrac{1}{2}(\dim M + \mathrm{corank}\,\{\cdot,\cdot\}_\lambda)$ for generic $\lambda$.

Tasks:
(a) Produce a list of natural examples of "quadratic + linear" Poisson pencils (e.g.\ those arising on duals of Lie algebras, on coadjoint orbits, from classical $R$-matrices, or from Nijenhuis-type constructions).
(b) For each such example, determine the algebraic type of the pencil at a generic point (its Jordan–Kronecker invariants).
(c) For each such example, construct an explicit complete family of polynomials on $M$ that are in bi-involution with respect to the pencil.

A web search shows ongoing research on Poisson pencils, Jordan–Kronecker invariants, and bi-involutive polynomial families (e.g. argument-shift pencils on Lie coalgebras, classifications of low-rank quadratic brackets, work on algebraic Nijenhuis operators and Kronecker pencils). Let $M$ be a smooth closed (compact, without boundary) manifold of dimension $n$. A Nijenhuis operator on $M$ is a smooth field $L$ of endomorphisms of the tangent bundle, i.e. a $(1,1)$-tensor field $L: TM \to TM$, whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]$$
vanishes identically for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ on $M$.

For each $x \in M$, the operator $L(x): T_xM \to T_xM$ is a linear endomorphism of the tangent space; call $L(x)$ algebraically regular if its centralizer in $\mathrm{End}(T_xM)$ has the minimal possible dimension $n$, equivalently, if for each eigenvalue of $L(x)$ (over $\mathbb{C}$) there is exactly one Jordan block in the Jordan canonical form of $L(x)$.

Problem: Describe (classify) all closed manifolds $M$ that admit a Nijenhuis operator $L$ such that $L(x)$ is algebraically regular at every point $x \in M$.

Recent work in "Nijenhuis Geometry" (Bolsinov, Konyaev, Matveev, 2019–2024) develops local normal forms and global obstructions (e.g., no non-constant complex eigenvalues on closed manifolds; no differentially non-degenerate singular points), but a full classification of closed manifolds admitting everywhere algebraically regular Nijenhuis operators does not appear to have been achieved. Background. Let $(M,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ equipped with an integrable system $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose singular points are non-degenerate in the sense of Williamson. Recall that, by the Eliasson–Miranda–Zung normal form theorem, every non-degenerate singularity is locally symplectomorphic to a product of elliptic ($\frac12(x_i^2+\xi_i^2)$), hyperbolic ($x_i\xi_i$), and focus-focus ($x_i\xi_{i+1}-x_{i+1}\xi_i,\ x_i\xi_i+x_{i+1}\xi_{i+1}$) blocks together with regular blocks $\xi_j$.

Assume $(M,\omega)$ is prequantizable, with prequantum line bundle $(L,\nabla)$ whose curvature is $\omega$. Let $\mathcal{P}\subset TM\otimes\mathbb{C}$ be the real (singular) polarization tangent to the level sets of $F$. The geometric quantization $\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P})$ is defined as the sheaf cohomology
$$\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P})=\bigoplus_{k\ge 0} H^k(M,\mathcal{J}),$$
where $\mathcal{J}$ is the sheaf of flat sections of $L$ along $\mathcal{P}$. For purely elliptic (toric) systems Kostant's theorem gives that this quantization is finite-dimensional and is concentrated on the Bohr–Sommerfeld leaves.

It is known that when the polarization has focus-focus or hyperbolic singularities the resulting cohomology may become infinite-dimensional (for instance, on a focus-focus fiber with $n$ nodes the model space takes the form $(C^\infty(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C}))^n$), even though only finitely many Bohr–Sommerfeld leaves contribute.

Problem. Construct a modification of the geometric quantization scheme above—e.g.\ by changing the sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, the polarization, the cohomology theory used, or by introducing a suitable functional-analytic completion or twisting—such that:

(i) when applied to integrable systems whose singularities include focus-focus and/or hyperbolic blocks, the resulting representation space is finite-dimensional;

(ii) the resulting finite-dimensional spaces still encode the symplectic invariants of the integrable system and of its singularities (Bohr–Sommerfeld data, Taylor series invariants of focus-focus singularities, monodromy, etc.);

(iii) the modification reduces to Kostant's geometric quantization in the purely regular/elliptic case.

Provide such a modified scheme and prove that it satisfies (i)–(iii).

Recall that, by the Eliasson–Miranda–Zung normal form theorem, every non-degenerate singularity is locally symplectomorphic to a product of elliptic ($\frac12(x_i^2+\xi_i^2)$), hyperbolic ($x_i\xi_i$), and focus-focus ($x_i\xi_{i+1}-x_{i+1}\xi_i,\ x_i\xi_i+x_{i+1}\xi_{i+1}$) blocks together with regular blocks $\xi_j$.

Assume $(M,\omega)$ is prequantizable, with prequantum line bundle $(L,\nabla)$ whose curvature is $\omega$. Let $\mathcal{P}\subset TM\otimes\mathbb{C}$ be the real (singular) polarization tangent to the level sets of $F$. The geometric quantization $\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P})$ is defined as the sheaf cohomology
$$\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P})=\bigoplus_{k\ge 0} H^k(M,\mathcal{J}),$$
where $\mathcal{J}$ is the sheaf of flat sections of $L$ along $\mathcal{P}$. For purely elliptic (toric) systems Kostant's theorem gives that this quantization is finite-dimensional and is concentrated on the Bohr–Sommerfeld leaves.

It is known that when the polarization has focus-focus or hyperbolic singularities the resulting cohomology may become infinite-dimensional (for instance, on a focus-focus fiber with $n$ nodes the model space takes the form $(C^\infty(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C}))^n$), even though only finitely many Bohr–Sommerfeld leaves contribute.

Problem. Construct a modification of the geometric quantization scheme above—e.g.\ by changing the sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, the polarization, the cohomology theory used, or by introducing a suitable functional-analytic completion or twisting—such that:

(i) when applied to integrable systems whose singularities include focus-focus and/or hyperbolic blocks, the resulting representation space is finite-dimensional;

(ii) the resulting finite-dimensional spaces still encode the symplectic invariants of the integrable system and of its singularities (Bohr–Sommerfeld data, Taylor series invariants of focus-focus singularities, monodromy, etc.);

(iii) the modification reduces to Kostant's geometric quantization in the purely regular/elliptic case.

Provide such a modified scheme and prove that it satisfies (i)–(iii).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of modifying the Kostant-type geometric quantization scheme so that focus-focus and hyperbolic singularities yield finite-dimensional representation spaces capturing the invariants of the system appears to remain open. Subsequent work (e.g., Hamilton–Miranda and Miranda–Presas–Solha on semitoric/almost toric manifolds, and Miranda–Solha on cotangent models) computes the relevant cohomologies and confirms that they are typically infinite-dimensional in the focus-focus/hyperbolic case, but no published modification has been found that simultaneously yields finite-dimensional spaces and retains the singular invariants in full generality.

A Nijenhuis operator on a smooth manifold $M$ is a $(1,1)$-tensor field $L:TM\to TM$ whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$
N_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]
$$
vanishes identically for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ on $M$.

Construct explicit real analytic examples of Nijenhuis operators $L$ on closed (compact, without boundary) two-dimensional real analytic surfaces $M$ with the following properties:
1. At every point $p\in M$, the endomorphism $L_p:T_pM\to T_pM$ has only real eigenvalues;
2. On an open dense subset of $M$, the two eigenvalues of $L_p$ are distinct.

Provide such operators on as many topological types of closed surfaces as possible (e.g. the sphere $S^2$, the torus $T^2$, and higher-genus surfaces, both orientable and non-orientable).

Consider a population of asexually reproducing organisms whose fitness landscape depends on a time-varying biotic and abiotic environment $E(t)$ that fluctuates on a wide range of time scales. Let the per-generation fitness of genotype $g$ be $W(g, E(t))$, and model the population dynamics by the standard Wright–Fisher or Moran process with mutation rate $\mu$ and population size $N$. In contrast, consider the same population evolving in a fixed environment $E_0$ (e.g., a constant laboratory condition or a simplified two-species host–pathogen coevolutionary system), where quantities such as the fixation probability of beneficial mutations, the rate of adaptation, the distribution of fitness effects of fixed mutations, and the structure of the substitution process can be derived analytically or measured experimentally.

Determine the precise extent to which quantitative predictions for adaptation in the stable environment $E_0$ — including the rate of adaptation, the probability and time to fixation of beneficial mutations, the effective strength of selection, and the statistics of substitution trajectories — remain valid predictors of the corresponding quantities in the time-varying environment $E(t)$. Specifically, identify the regimes of environmental fluctuation time scales (relative to mutation supply $N\mu$ and selection coefficients $s$) under which the stable-environment results provide accurate approximations, and characterize the corrections or qualitatively new phenomena that appear when these regimes are violated.

Let $U(0)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be an open neighbourhood of the origin and let
$$\Phi=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n):U(0)\to\mathbb{R}^n$$
be a smooth map. Assume that $0$ is a singular point of $\Phi$, i.e. $\operatorname{rank} d\Phi(0)<n$, but that the set of regular points (points $x$ where $d\Phi(x)$ is invertible) is dense in $U(0)$.

At every regular point $x\in U(0)$ define a $(1,1)$-tensor field $L(x)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ by requiring that the differentials $d\sigma_1,\dots,d\sigma_n$ form an eigen-coframe of $L^{*}$ with eigenvalues $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n$ respectively, i.e.
$$L^{*}(x)\,d\sigma_i(x)=\sigma_i(x)\,d\sigma_i(x),\qquad i=1,\dots,n.$$
Equivalently, in the standard coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_n$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$L(x)=\bigl(d\Phi(x)\bigr)^{-1}\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\sigma_1(x),\dots,\sigma_n(x)\bigr)\,d\Phi(x).$$
This operator $L$ is well defined and smooth at every regular point of $\Phi$, and (when smooth) it is automatically a Nijenhuis operator (its Nijenhuis torsion vanishes).

Problem. Give necessary and sufficient conditions on the smooth map $\Phi$ under which all components of $L(x)$ admit a smooth extension from the set of regular points to the whole neighbourhood $U(0)$, and describe explicitly the class of maps $\Phi$ for which this smooth extendability holds.

Consider a sample of $n$ genomes drawn from a recombining population. Tracing the ancestry of these genomes backward in time, segments of the genomes are inherited together until a recombination event separates linked loci, after which the affected segments have distinct (but correlated) genealogical histories. The ancestral recombination graph (ARG) of the sample is the structure that encodes, for every position along the genome, the marginal genealogical tree relating the $n$ sampled sequences, together with the connections between neighboring trees induced by recombination events.

Given aligned genomic sequence data from $n$ sampled individuals (with $n$ on the order of $10^3$ or larger, well beyond a few dozen), develop and analyze an algorithm that infers the ARG of the sample, i.e., reconstructs the sequence of marginal genealogies along the genome together with the recombination events linking them. Specify the computational complexity (in $n$ and in genome length $L$), the statistical accuracy under a standard coalescent-with-recombination model, and conditions under which the inferred ARG converges to the true ARG as more data are observed.

Substantial progress has been made since 2018. Methods such as Relate, tsinfer/tsdate, ARG-Needle, Threads, and SINGER now scale ARG inference from a few dozen to hundreds of thousands of genomes (e.g., the full UK Biobank with ~500,000 samples). However, these methods involve heuristic approximations and trade-offs between scalability, statistical accuracy, and uncertainty quantification; fully accurate, statistically principled, and uncertainty-aware ARG inference at biobank scale remains an active research area, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

Let $(M^{2n},\omega_1,\omega_2)$ be a smooth bi-Hamiltonian manifold, i.e. a $2n$-dimensional manifold equipped with two compatible symplectic forms (so that $\omega_1+\omega_2$, or equivalently the pencil of Poisson structures defined by their inverses, is again Poisson). Let $R:TM\to TM$ be the associated recursion (Nijenhuis) operator, defined by $\omega_2(X,Y)=\omega_1(RX,Y)$, so that the Nijenhuis torsion of $R$ vanishes. Assume that at a generic point of $M$ the operator $R$ is semisimple with $n$ distinct eigenvalues, each of algebraic multiplicity $2$. Let $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n$ be the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of $R$ (or equivalently a complete set of functionally independent traces of powers of $R$ generating the bi-Hamiltonian integrals), and consider the momentum-type map
$$\Phi=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n):M\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^n.$$
At each point $p\in M$ where $R$ fails to have the generic algebraic type, the linearisation of $R$ at $p$ endows the tangent space $T_pM$ (or a suitable quotient) with the structure of a left-symmetric (pre-Lie) algebra.

Recall that a singular point $p$ of an integrable Hamiltonian system on a symplectic manifold is called non-degenerate in the sense of Eliasson if the linearisations of the commuting Hamiltonians at $p$ span a Cartan subalgebra of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sp}(T_pM,\omega_1|_p)$ of quadratic Hamiltonians.

Problem. Describe the structure of the singularities of the map $\Phi$ in terms of:
(i) the singular points of the recursion operator $R$,
(ii) the linearisations of $R$ at those points, and
(iii) the corresponding left-symmetric algebras.

In particular, give sufficient and/or necessary conditions, in terms of the algebraic and analytic data (i)–(iii), under which a singular point of $\Phi$ is non-degenerate in the sense of Eliasson.

representations.normalized:
Consider the process of B-cell affinity maturation in a germinal center, modeled as a Darwinian evolutionary dynamics on a population of B-cell clones. Each B-cell clone is characterized by a B-cell receptor (BCR) whose binding affinities to a panel of distinct epitopes (receptor-binding regions) of a complex antigen are described by a vector of nonnegative real numbers. During maturation, clones proliferate, mutate (somatic hypermutation in BCR sequence), and are selected based on their binding affinities, eventually contributing to a memory pool.

Empirical observations to be explained by a mathematical/dynamical model satisfying the following constraints:
(i) The mean binding affinity of the surviving clones to the antigen increases with time.
(ii) The clonal diversity (e.g., effective number of distinct lineages, measured by Shannon or Simpson indices on the lineage distribution) does not decrease, and in fact increases with time, as initially rare but higher-affinity clones rise in frequency alongside abundant early winners.
(iii) The clones retained in the final memory pool are not necessarily those with the highest measured binding affinity; clones whose affinity to the antigen is orders of magnitude lower than the strongest binders can survive selection.
(iv) Spatial segregation/mixing of clones within the germinal center and recruitment of new naive B-cells from outside are explicitly excluded as mechanisms.

Tasks:
(a) Construct an explicit stochastic population-dynamics model (selection + mutation + finite-size effects, on a fitness landscape determined jointly by the multi-epitope affinity vectors) that simultaneously reproduces (i)–(iii) under constraint (iv), and identify the mechanism within the model responsible for the maintenance of high diversity together with rising mean affinity.

(b) Quantify, within the model, how the multiplicity of epitopes and the heterogeneity (orders-of-magnitude variation) of clone-to-epitope affinities contribute to sustained diversity, beyond the trivial contribution coming merely from the number of epitopes.

(c) Derive, within the model, the consequences of the resulting broad (high-diversity) memory repertoire for protection against future antigenic challenges, in particular against mutated or escaped variants of the original antigen, compared to the alternative outcome of a narrow high-affinity repertoire.

Let $(M,\Pi)$ be a smooth Poisson manifold of dimension $n$, and let $\mathcal{F}=(f_1,\dots,f_s)$ be an integrable system on $(M,\Pi)$ in the sense that the functions $f_1,\dots,f_s$ pairwise Poisson commute and the rank condition for integrability on a Poisson manifold is satisfied (so that generic common level sets that are compact and connected are Liouville tori). Let $m\in M$ be a point where the Poisson structure $\Pi$ is singular (i.e. its rank drops), and let $S$ be the symplectic leaf through $m$, with a transverse Poisson structure $\Pi_N$ on a transversal $N$ to $S$ at $m$. Call the integrable system $\mathcal{F}$ "splittable at $m$" if, on a neighbourhood of $m$, it decomposes as a product of an integrable system $\mathcal{F}_S$ on the symplectic leaf $S$ and an integrable system $\mathcal{F}_N$ on the transverse Poisson manifold $(N,\Pi_N)$.

Assume that the common level set of $\mathcal{F}$ through $m$ contains a compact connected Liouville torus $T$. Establish an action-angle coordinate theorem in a neighbourhood of $T$ in $M$ for splittable integrable systems on Poisson manifolds at points where $\Pi$ is singular: produce coordinates consisting of action variables, angle variables (along the torus), and additional transverse coordinates, and describe in these coordinates both the Poisson structure $\Pi$ and the integrals $f_1,\dots,f_s$, generalizing the Liouville–Arnold–Mineur theorem and the regular Poisson action-angle theorem to this singular splittable setting.

Consider a co-evolving system consisting of a viral population and a host immune repertoire. Let the viral population at time t be described by a probability distribution x_t over a (large) genotype space G of strains, evolving under mutation, selection by host immunity, and stochastic drift; let the immune state I_t describe the distribution of antibody/T-cell specificities in the host population, evolving in response to circulating strains. Standard predictive frameworks (e.g., fitness-based ranking schemes such as those used to anticipate future influenza strains) take as input the set of strains S_t = { g in G : x_t(g) >= ε } that are already present at relatively high frequency ε, and output a ranking or probability distribution over S_t indicating which currently-circulating strain is most likely to dominate at a future time t + Δ. 

Develop and rigorously analyze a predictive model P that goes strictly beyond this paradigm in the following sense: given only data available up to time t (genomic surveillance of strains, immune repertoire data, and biophysical/epidemiological parameters), P must output a probability measure μ_{t+Δ} on the full genotype space G — not restricted to S_t — assigning calibrated, non-trivial probabilities to genotypes g ∉ S_t (i.e., new mutations not yet present at high frequency) of becoming prevalent by time t + Δ. 

Specifically:
(a) Construct such a model P and prove that, on a suitable stochastic model of viral–immune co-evolution, its predictions for novel (currently rare or absent) genotypes are calibrated and strictly more informative (in a precise information-theoretic sense, e.g., expected log-score or KL divergence to the true future distribution) than any predictor whose support is restricted to S_t.
(b) Quantify the intrinsic predictability of the co-evolutionary process: derive sharp upper bounds on the achievable predictive accuracy (for example, in terms of mutual information between observables at time t and the future state at time t + Δ, or in terms of the entropy rate of the process) as a function of Δ, mutation rate, selection strength, and immune-pressure parameters, and identify the regime (a "predictability horizon") beyond which no predictor can outperform the climatological baseline.
(c) Characterize the failure modes — i.e., the structural features of the co-evolutionary dynamics (e.g., neutral plateaus, clonal interference, antigenic jumps) that saturate these bounds — thereby exhibiting natural limits to evolutionary predictability.

Consider a microbial population (such as the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus) modeled in the framework of population genetics with the following parameters: effective population size on the order of N = 10^13, per-base mutation rate μ ≈ 10^-7 per generation, and strong, spatially and temporally heterogeneous environmental selection. Empirical observations indicate that (i) no genome-wide selective sweeps have been recorded, and (ii) the standing genomic diversity within coexisting subpopulations is extremely large (hundreds of distinct genomic backbones coexisting in a given ecosystem).

Classical population-genetic predictions (Wright–Fisher / Moran-type models with strong directional selection) predict that, under such large N and strong selection, beneficial mutations should fix rapidly via genome-wide sweeps and reduce diversity. Provide a quantitative theoretical explanation, supported by an analyzable mathematical model, for the persistence of large genomic diversity. Specifically:

1. Formulate a stochastic evolutionary model incorporating one or more of the following ingredients: (a) co-evolution with bacteriophage predators (e.g., Lotka–Volterra–type host–parasite dynamics coupled to allele frequencies), (b) homologous recombination at rate r per site, allowing gene-specific rather than genome-wide sweeps, (c) fluctuating or fine-grained ecological niches that impose negative frequency-dependent or balancing selection, (d) explicit spatial/metapopulation structure with migration rate m, and/or (e) selection acting on multi-species ecosystem-level units rather than individual genomes.

2. Derive, within this model, conditions on the parameters (N, μ, r, m, selection coefficients, and predator/niche parameters) under which the equilibrium number of coexisting genomic types scales as observed (hundreds to thousands) while the probability of a genome-wide sweep over relevant timescales is negligible.

3. Identify which combination(s) of mechanisms (a)–(e) are necessary and/or sufficient to reconcile the observations with population-genetic theory.

The question of how Prochlorococcus maintains very large coexisting genomic diversity despite huge population size and strong selection, with no observed genome-wide sweeps, remains an active open problem. Recent work (Kashtan et al., Science 2014; Larkin & Martiny, ISME J 2017; studies on gene-specific sweeps) documents the diversity and proposes gene-specific sweeps via recombination, but recombination-to-mutation ratios in Prochlorococcus (≈1–3) are noted to be too low to fully explain the pattern, and no consensus quantitative theory reconciles all observations.

Consider biological diversity organized across four hierarchical levels: (i) the molecular level (e.g. sequence variation, protein structure and function), (ii) the genomic level (e.g. gene content, regulatory architecture, genome organization), (iii) the organismal level (e.g. phenotypic traits, life-history variation), and (iv) the ecological level (e.g. species composition and interactions in communities). Suppose an evolutionary phenomenon (such as the emergence and maintenance of diversity in a microbial community) is observed and modelled mathematically. Address the following questions in a precise, model-based way:

1. Construct or identify a unified mathematical framework that simultaneously captures dynamics at all four levels above and is capable of reproducing the observed phenomenon. Specify the state space at each level, the coupling operators between levels, and the dynamical rules.

2. Determine whether the dynamics at any single level can be described autonomously, i.e. whether there exists a closed effective dynamical system on one level (with effective parameters obtained by averaging or projecting out the others) whose trajectories accurately approximate those of the full multi-level system. Equivalently, decide whether a separation-of-scales decomposition exists in which different levels evolve on well-separated time scales and can be analyzed independently.

3. Alternatively, determine whether the levels are inseparably coupled, in the sense that no closed effective single-level description exists and the joint dynamics cannot be approximated by independent level-wise dynamics, or whether instead a cascade structure holds in which the levels can be ordered so that each level is driven by the preceding one but does not feed back on it.

Provide either a general theorem characterizing which of these regimes (autonomous single level, separated scales, fully interconnected, or one-way cascade) applies to a given multi-level evolutionary model, or explicit examples illustrating each regime together with criteria distinguishing them.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $\hbar \in (0, \hbar_0]$ be a semiclassical parameter. Consider a tuple $P_1(\hbar), \dots, P_n(\hbar)$ of semiclassical pseudodifferential operators on $M$ (or, more generally, $\hbar$-pseudodifferential operators acting on a suitable Hilbert space) with principal symbols $p_1, \dots, p_n \in C^\infty(T^*M)$, satisfying:

1. (Self-adjointness) $P_j^* = P_j$ for $j = 1, \dots, n$;
2. (Commutativity) $[P_i, P_j] = 0$ for all $i, j$.

Such a tuple has a well-defined joint spectrum
$$\Sigma(\hbar) = \{ \lambda = (\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n : \exists\, \psi \neq 0 \text{ with } P_j \psi = \lambda_j \psi \text{ for all } j \},$$
together with associated joint eigenfunctions.

The tuple is said to define a quantum integrable system when, in addition, the principal symbols are almost everywhere independent, meaning that the differentials $dp_1, \dots, dp_n$ are linearly independent at almost every point of $T^*M$ (equivalently, the map $(p_1, \dots, p_n) : T^*M \to \mathbb{R}^n$ has maximal rank $n$ on a dense open set of full measure).

Question: Given only the spectral data of the family $(P_1(\hbar), \dots, P_n(\hbar))$ — for instance, the asymptotic behavior as $\hbar \to 0$ of the joint eigenvalues in $\Sigma(\hbar)$ and/or of the joint eigenfunctions — does there exist a procedure that determines whether the independence condition on the principal symbols holds almost everywhere? In other words, can the almost-everywhere independence of $dp_1, \dots, dp_n$ on $T^*M$ be detected purely from spectral asymptotics, without direct access to the symbols themselves?

Recent work on inverse spectral theory for semiclassical quantum integrable systems (e.g., results on semitoric and Jaynes–Cummings systems, and on asymptotic lattices and good labellings) shows partial progress on recovering symbol-level information from joint spectra in special classes, particularly in two degrees of freedom. Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. Recall that:

- $X$ is called uniruled if there exists a variety $Y$ of dimension $\dim X - 1$ and a dominant rational map $Y \times \mathbb{P}^1 \dashrightarrow X$.
- A normal projective variety $X_{\min}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial if every Weil divisor on $X_{\min}$ has an integer multiple that is Cartier.
- $X_{\min}$ has only terminal singularities if there exists a resolution $f : \widetilde{X} \to X_{\min}$ such that $K_{X_{\min}}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and, writing $K_{\widetilde{X}} = f^{*}K_{X_{\min}} + \sum a_i E_i$ for the exceptional divisors $E_i$, all discrepancies satisfy $a_i > 0$.
- A $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor $D$ on a projective variety is nef if $D \cdot C \geq 0$ for every irreducible projective curve $C$.

Prove or disprove: at least one of the following two alternatives must hold.
(1) $X$ is uniruled.
(2) There exists a projective variety $X_{\min}$ birational to $X$ such that $X_{\min}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial, has only terminal singularities, and the canonical divisor $K_{X_{\min}}$ is nef.

$$\kappa_-(K_X+D) \;=\; \limsup_{m \to \infty,\; m(K_X+D)\ \text{Cartier}} \frac{\log h^0\!\bigl(X, m(K_X+D)\bigr)}{\log m},$$

Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected 4-dimensional symplectic manifold and let $F=(J,H)\colon M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a completely integrable system whose components Poisson-commute and satisfy: (i) $J$ is the momentum map of an effective Hamiltonian $S^1$-action on $M$ and is proper, and (ii) all critical points of $F$ are non-degenerate without hyperbolic blocks. Such a system is called semitoric. The singularities of $F$ are then of elliptic-elliptic, elliptic-regular, or focus-focus type; assume $m\in M$ is a focus-focus critical point with critical value $c=F(m)\in\mathbb{R}^2$.

Associated with such a focus-focus singularity is the Taylor series symplectic invariant $(S)^\infty\in\mathbb{R}[[X,Y]]/(2\pi\mathbb{Z}\cdot X)$ (with vanishing constant term), introduced as a complete local symplectic invariant for the singular Lagrangian fibration of $F$ near the focus-focus fiber $F^{-1}(c)$.

Now let $\hat J,\hat H$ be a pair of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical pseudodifferential (or Berezin–Toeplitz) operators that quantize $J,H$ as $\hbar\to 0$, and let $\Sigma(\hbar)\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ denote the joint spectrum of $(\hat J,\hat H)$.

Problem. Give an explicit algorithm that, taking as input the joint spectrum $\Sigma(\hbar)$ in an arbitrarily small neighbourhood of the focus-focus critical value $c$ (in the limit $\hbar\to 0$), computes the Taylor series invariant $(S)^\infty$ of the underlying classical semitoric system at $m$ to all orders.

Let $f: X \to S$ be a surjective proper Kähler morphism with connected fibers between connected complex manifolds, and let $S^o \subseteq S$ denote the locus over which $f$ is smooth. Let $(L, h_L)$ be a singular Hermitian $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle on $X$ whose curvature current is semipositive, and assume that for every $s \in S^o$ the restriction $(L, h_L)|_{X_s}$ is well defined, the pair $(X_s, L|_{X_s})$ is Kawamata log terminal (i.e., the local weights $\varphi$ of $h_L$ satisfy $e^{-\varphi} \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ on $X_s$), and $K_{X_s} + L|_{X_s}$ is pseudoeffective.

For each $s \in S^o$, define the relative maximal volume form $dV_{\max, X/S}(L, h_L)$ fiberwise by
$$dV_{\max, X_s}(L|_{X_s}, h_L|_{X_s}) = \sup\bigl\{\,|\sigma|^{2/m}\,h_L^{1/m} : m \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0},\ \sigma \in H^0(X_s, m(K_{X_s}+L|_{X_s})\otimes \mathcal{I}(h_L^m|_{X_s})),\ \tfrac{1}{m}\!\int_{X_s}\!|\sigma|^{2/m}h_L^{1/m} \leq 1\,\bigr\},$$
where the supremum is taken in the sense of upper envelopes of singular volume forms, and let $h_{\min, X/S}(L, h_L)$ be the associated singular Hermitian metric on $(K_{X/S} + L)|_{f^{-1}(S^o)}$ determined by $dV_{\max, X/S}(L, h_L)$ in the usual way (so that the curvature of $h_{\min, X/S}(L, h_L)$ on $f^{-1}(S^o)$ is semipositive).

Question: does $h_{\min, X/S}(L, h_L)$ extend from $f^{-1}(S^o)$ to a singular Hermitian metric on the line bundle $K_{X/S} + L$ over all of $X$ whose curvature current is semipositive?

Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $(L,h_L)$ be a singular Hermitian line bundle on $X$ that is pseudoeffective (i.e. the curvature current $\Theta_{h_L} = -\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial\log h_L \geq 0$) and Kawamata log terminal (KLT) in the sense that the multiplier ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}(h_L)$ equals $\mathcal{O}_X$. On the adjoint line bundle $K_X + L$ one can construct three canonical singular Hermitian metrics:

(i) The dynamical canonical metric $\hat h_{\mathrm{can}}(L,h_L)$, obtained as the limit of the normalized iteration
$$h_{m+1} = \left(K(mh_m \cdot h_L^{-1})\right)^{-1/m},$$
where $K(\cdot)$ denotes the diagonal of the Bergman kernel of $H^0(X, m(K_X+L))$ with respect to the indicated weight, started from any smooth positively curved initial metric.

(ii) The supercanonical (minimal-among-canonical) metric $\hat h_{\min}(L,h_L)$ defined as the upper envelope
$$\hat h_{\min}(L,h_L)^{-1}(x) = \sup\{|\sigma(x)|^2 : \sigma \in H^0(X, m(K_X+L)), \ m \geq 1,\ \tfrac{1}{m}\int_X |\sigma|^{2/m} h_L \leq 1\},$$
suitably normalized.

(iii) The minimal singular metric $h_{\min}(L,h_L)$ on $K_X+L$, namely a singular Hermitian metric with semipositive curvature current whose local weight is maximal (in the sense of the partial order of plurisubharmonic functions) among all such metrics on $K_X+L$.

Prove or disprove: for every such $X$ and every pseudoeffective KLT singular Hermitian line bundle $(L,h_L)$ on $X$, the identities
$$\hat h_{\mathrm{can}}(L,h_L) \;=\; \hat h_{\min}(L,h_L) \;=\; h_{\min}(L,h_L)$$
hold.

representations.normalized:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and let $D$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$ such that the pair $(X,D)$ is Kawamata log terminal (KLT); that is, for some (equivalently every) log resolution $\mu: Y \to X$ with $\mu^*(K_X+D) = K_Y + \sum a_i E_i$ over a simple normal crossing divisor, all coefficients satisfy $a_i < 1$.

Choose a nontrivial multivalued holomorphic section $\sigma_D$ of the $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle associated with $D$ whose divisor equals $D$, and set the (singular) Hermitian metric
$$h_D := |\sigma_D|^{-2}$$
on the $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$. A volume form $dV$ on $X$ with at worst KLT-type singularities along $D$ is called extremal with respect to $(D,h_D)$ if it has minimal singularities among (suitably normalized) singular volume forms whose associated curvature current
$$\sqrt{-1}\,\Theta_{dV^{-1}\cdot h_D}$$
representing $c_1(K_X+D)$ is a positive closed current.

Assume that $K_X+D$ is pseudoeffective. Prove or disprove:

(1) For every extremal volume form $dV$ with respect to $(D,h_D)$, the section $dV \otimes h_D^{-1}$ is generically pluriharmonic, in the sense that the absolutely continuous part of the curvature current $\sqrt{-1}\,\Theta_{dV^{-1}\cdot h_D}$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure, in the sense of Siu's decomposition) vanishes identically.

(2) $K_X+D$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-effective, i.e., some positive integral multiple $m(K_X+D)$ is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor.

Let $\Delta^* = \{ t \in \mathbb{C} : 0 < |t| < 1 \}$ be the punctured unit disk. The canonical line bundle $K_{\Delta^*}$ carries a canonical (singular) Hermitian metric $h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}$, defined as the supremum of all (semi-)positively curved Hermitian metrics on $K_{\Delta^*}$ with mass at most one, equivalently, the metric whose curvature current realizes the canonical $L^2$-extension/Bergman kernel construction on $\Delta^*$. Its inverse $h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}^{-1}$ is a (possibly singular) Hermitian metric on $K_{\Delta^*}^{-1}$, and may be viewed as a $(1,1)$-form (a section of $K_{\Delta^*}^{-1} \otimes \overline{K_{\Delta^*}^{-1}}$) on $\Delta^*$.

Prove or disprove: near the puncture $t = 0$, one has the asymptotic upper bound
$$
h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}^{-1} \;=\; O\!\left( \frac{\sqrt{-1}\, dt \wedge d\bar t}{|t|^2 (\log |t|)^2} \right),
$$
i.e., there exists a constant $C > 0$ and a neighborhood of $0$ in $\Delta^*$ on which
$$
h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}^{-1} \;\le\; C \cdot \frac{\sqrt{-1}\, dt \wedge d\bar t}{|t|^2 (\log |t|)^2}.
$$
